children.text: śriyaḥ pati śrīmati śāsituṃ jagajjagannivāso vasudevasadmani /
children.translated_text: In the auspicious abode of <s>Vasudeva</s>, the dwelling-place of the universe, where the Lord of <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) resided to rule the world,
<s>Hari</s> beheld descending from the sky the sage born from the body of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (Brahmā). // MSpv 1.01 //
The horizontal radiance of the chariot of rich essence, and the well-known upward flame of the oblation-eater (fire),

children.text: patatyadho dhāma visāri sarvataḥ kimedatityākulamīkṣitaṃ janaiḥ // MSpv_1.02 //
children.translated_text: a splendor falling downward and spreading in all directions—'What is this?'—people gazed in bewilderment. // MSpv 1.02 //
'It is a mass of stars,' was first determined; then, 'It is an embodied being,' with form discerned;

children.text: vibhurvibhaktāvayavaṃ pumāniti kramādamuṃ nārada ityabodhi saḥ // MSpv_1.03 //
children.translated_text: 'It is the all-pervading one, with distinct limbs, a person'—gradually he was recognized as <s>Nārada</s>. // MSpv 1.03 //
Passing below great rain-clouds, fresh, pale-white with diffused camphor-pollen,

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ kṣaṇotkṣiptagajendrakṛttinā sphuṭopamaṃ bhūtisitena śamghunā // MSpv_1.04 //
children.translated_text: at each moment resembling [the contrast with] <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva), white with sacred ash, momentarily lifting the elephant-hide. // MSpv 1.04 //
Bearing matted locks with the luster of lotus filaments and the radiance of autumn moonbeams,
like a line of ripened, lofty snow-field plants passing beyond the king of mountains. // MSpv 1.05 //
Wearing tawny <s>muñja</s>-grass girdle, with the fair complexion of <s>Arjuna</s> (white), clad in deerskin with the luster of food-offerings,
he seemed to mock the dark-clad body of [<s>Viṣṇu</s>], with his lower garment strung with golden thread. // MSpv 1.06 //
With long, golden creeper-like threads on his body, like the plumes of the king of birds (<s>Garuḍa</s>),

children.text: kṛtopavītaṃ himaśubhramuccakairghanaṃ ghanānte taṭitāṃ gaṇairiva // MSpv_1.07 //
children.translated_text: wearing the sacred thread, snow-white and high—like a dense [cloud] at the end of the rains, with streaks of lightning. // MSpv 1.07 //
With naturally bright, beautiful, fine eyelashes, and a body-companion that was a beautiful antelope-skin, white like cut lotus stalks,
he shone like <s>Indra</s>'s mount (<s>Airāvata</s>), with a cloth-covering. // MSpv 1.08 //
With the nail of his thumb, glowing from constantly striking the strings of the <s>vallakī</s> (lute),
he shone with a crystal rosary, half-filled as if with coral beads, sparkling. // MSpv 1.09 //
With tones that, sounding from the clash with the wind, separately penetrated the circles of musical intervals,
he was observing again and again the great <s>mūrcchanā</s> (melodic ascent) becoming manifest in the special <s>grāma</s> (musical mode). // MSpv 1.10 //
Having turned back the attendant gods who followed him, bowing respectfully, he, the treasure-house of <s>Indra</s>'s sacrificial knowledge,
reached the beautiful abode of the Discus-bearer (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), who had established [His rule] after subduing the wealth of the <s>daityas</s>. // MSpv 1.11 //
Until the treasure-house of austerity, resembling the falling sun, did not alight on the earth before Him,
until then, <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) rose swiftly and high from His throne, like lightning from a mountain. // MSpv 1.12 //
Then, when the hosts of serpents below somehow held [the earth] with their hoods bent down from the effort of upraising,

children.text: nyadhāyiṣātāmabhi devakīsutaṃ sutena dhātuścaraṇau bhuvastale // MSpv_1.13 //
children.translated_text: the son of the Creator (<s>Nārada</s>) placed his feet upon the surface of the earth before the son of <s>Devakī</s>. // MSpv 1.13 //
The Primal Person (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) duly honored him with the offering of welcome-water and other courtesies;

children.text: gṛhānupaituṃ praṇayādabhīpsavo bhavanti nāpuṇyakṛtāṃ manīṣiṇaḥ // MSpv_1.14 //
children.translated_text: 'Sages do not become desirous of visiting the homes of those who have not earned merit, out of affection.' // MSpv 1.14 //
As long as the people had not seen those two standing together, like the snowy and collyrium-dark mountains,
so long did the sage remain seated on the seat given by his own hand, for a long while. // MSpv 1.15 //

children.text: mahāmahānīlaśilārucaḥ puro niṣedivān kaṃsakṛṣaḥ sa viṣṭare /
children.translated_text: The slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, seated on his couch before [<s>Nārada</s>], with the luster of a great sapphire stone,
surpassed the beauty of the rising moon, high above the eastern mountain. // MSpv 1.16 //

children.text: vidhāya tasyāpacitiṃ praseduṣaḥ prakāmamaprīyata yajvanāṃ priyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having paid Him reverence, the one pleased—the beloved of sacrificers—was exceedingly delighted;
for the greatly fortunate are indeed eager to receive the worthy through service, again and again. // MSpv 1.17 //
Placing in His hand the water-pot bearing [waters] brought from all the <s>tīrthas</s> (sacred fords), extolled by the sages,
<s>Hari</s> received the waters, most efficacious in the rite of destroying the mass of sins, with His bowed head. // MSpv 1.18 //
When, by the sage's leave, He of the dark-as-fresh-raincloud body beheld [Himself] in the golden [seat],

children.text: jigāya jambūjanitaśriyaḥ śriyaṃ sumeruśṛṅgasya tadā tadāsanam // MSpv_1.19 //
children.translated_text: that seat then surpassed the glory born of <s>Jambū</s>-gold on the peak of <s>Sumeru</s>. // MSpv 1.19 //
He, with garments blazing like refined gold, with the hue of the marks of the mighty <s>Sudarśana</s> (discus),

children.text: vididyute bāḍavajātavedasaḥ śikhābhirāśliṣṭa ivāmbhasāṃ nidhiḥ // MSpv_1.20 //
children.translated_text: shone like the ocean embraced by the flames of the submarine fire. // MSpv 1.20 //
Enveloped by the array of radiance of the Discus-bearer, the sage's splendor shone forth
like rays of the moon at night, visible through gaps in moving foliage. // MSpv 1.21 //
By the radiance of [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], brilliant like blossoming <s>tamāla</s> flowers, and [<s>Nārada</s>'s], auspicious and pale as <s>saptacchada</s> (alstonia) pollen,

children.text: parampareṇa cchuritāmalacchavī tadekavarṇāviva tau babhūvatuḥ // MSpv_1.22 //
children.translated_text: sprinkled upon each other in succession, the two appeared as if of one color, spotlessly radiant. // MSpv 1.22 //
In that body of the enemy of <s>Kaiṭabha</s> (Viṣṇu), in whom at the time of cosmic dissolution the worlds with all their manifestations had been withdrawn,

children.text: tanau mamustatra na kaiṭabhadviṣastapodhanabhyāgamasaṃbhavā mudaḥ // MSpv_1.23 //
children.translated_text: the joys born of the sage's visit could not find room. // MSpv 1.23 //
With eyes bearing the splendor of one who has approached [a guest] with joy's full expansion,

children.text: vilocane bibhradadhiśritaśriṇī sa puṇḍarākākṣa iti sphuṭābhavat // MSpv_1.24 //
children.translated_text: like a light surpassing the brilliance of the summer sun, He became manifestly known as <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s> (Lotus-eyed). // MSpv 1.24 //

children.text: sitaṃsitimnā sutarāṃ munervapuḥ visāribhiḥ saudhamivātha lambhayan /
children.translated_text: Then, lending to the sage's body whiteness beyond its own whiteness—as moonbeams to the celestial palace—
by His spreading radiance, like rows of teeth, <s>Acyuta</s> spoke words [accompanied by] a pure smile: // MSpv 1.25 //

children.text: haratyaghaṃ saṃprati hetureṣyataḥ śubhasya pūrvācaritai kṛtarṃ śubhai /
children.translated_text: 'Your sight, which now destroys sin and was formerly accomplished through the cause of auspicious deeds,

children.text: śarīrabhājāṃ bhavadīyadarśanaṃ vyanakti kālatritaye 'pi yogyatām // MSpv_1.26 //
children.translated_text: reveals the worthiness of embodied beings across the three periods of time. // MSpv 1.26 //
That supreme darkness which could not be controlled by the sun, though his thousand rays suffice for the world—

children.text: prasahya tejobhirasaṃkhyatāṃ gatair adastvayā nunnamanuttamaṃ tamaḥ // MSpv_1.27 //
children.translated_text: that unsurpassed darkness was forcibly dispelled by you, with your radiances gone beyond numbering. // MSpv 1.27 //
Appointed by the Creator who labors for the welfare of his subjects, with a mind undisturbed in the bestowal [of knowledge] to worthy recipients,

children.text: sadopayoge 'pi gurustvamakṣayo nidhiḥ śrutīnāṃ dhanasaṃpadāmiva // MSpv_1.28 //
children.translated_text: you, though constantly drawn upon, are an inexhaustible treasure of the sacred texts, like [an inexhaustible treasure] of wealth. // MSpv 1.28 //

children.text: vilokanenaiva tavāmunā mune kṛtaḥ kṛtārthosmi nibarhitāṃhasā /
children.translated_text: By this very sight of yours, O sage, I am made fulfilled, with my sins extinguished;

children.text: tathāpiśuśrūṣurahaṃ garīyasīrgiro 'thavā śreyasi kena vā tṛpyate // MSpv_1.29 //
children.translated_text: yet I am eager to hear, for who indeed is satiated with what is most beneficial?' // MSpv 1.29 //
'Even though free from desire, he speaks the purpose of his coming'—she by whom [Speech] resolves to speak thus,

children.text: tanoti nastāmuditmagauravo gurustavaivāgama eva dhṛṣyatām // MSpv_1.30 //
children.translated_text: 'let the reason for the coming of you, our revered teacher, be boldly revealed to us, whose dignity He exalts.' // MSpv 1.30 //

children.text: itibruvantaṃ uvāca sa vratī na vācyamitthaṃ puruṣottama tvayā /
children.translated_text: To Him thus speaking, the vow-observing one replied: 'O Supreme Person, it should not be spoken thus by you;

children.text: tvameva sākṣātkaraṇīya ityataḥ kimasti kāryaṃ guru yogināmapi // MSpv_1.31 //
children.translated_text: you are indeed the one to be directly realized—therefore, what task is there even for the greatest yogins? // MSpv 1.31 //
You are the foremost form, the unfailing refuge, of those wise ones who have attained the path of liberation—
a path that resists the risen passions of people, and is exceedingly difficult due to being continuously untrodden. // MSpv 1.32 //
You, indifferent to all, somehow grasped by those who have restrained their minds and gained the inner vision,

children.text: bahirvikaraṃ prakṛteḥ pṛthagviduḥ purātanaṃ tvāṃ puruṣaṃ purāvidaḥ // MSpv_1.33 //
children.translated_text: the ancient knowers know you, the primeval <s>Puruṣa</s>, distinct from <s>Prakṛti</s>, beyond external transformation. // MSpv 1.33 //
You, the sole architect of the world, effortlessly established the canopy of the serpent-lord as [your] one abode,
high upon the excellent ground of the pillar-head of the lord of serpents (<s>Śeṣa</s>). // MSpv 1.34 //
Who alone can comprehend the greatness of you, the Primeval Form, who has no other superior?
Even in your human birth, you surpass gods and demons in qualities that destroy worldly existence. // MSpv 1.35 //
Indeed, to lighten this earth, overburdened and about to break, you descended from the triple heaven;

children.text: udūḍhalokatritayena sāṃprataṃ gururdharitrī kriyatetarāṃ tvayā // MSpv_1.36 //
children.translated_text: having now uplifted the three worlds, you make this earth, O Teacher, exceedingly heavy. // MSpv 1.36 //
If you had not desired to descend to the surface of the earth, to illuminate the world by your own splendor,

children.text: samāhitairapyanirūpitastataḥ padaṃ dṛśaḥ syāḥ katham īśa mādṛśām // MSpv_1.37 //
children.translated_text: then, unperceived even by the concentrated, how could you, O Lord, become an object of vision for the likes of us? // MSpv 1.37 //
You alone, O Upholder of the universe, are capable of protecting this world, inundated by the arrogant intoxicated ones;

children.text: ṛte raveḥ kṣālayituṃ kṣameta kaḥ kṣapātamaskāṇḍamalīmasaṃ tamaḥ // MSpv_1.38 //
children.translated_text: apart from the sun, who could cleanse the darkness, foul with the stain of the night's dark mass? // MSpv 1.38 //

children.text: karoti kaṃsādimahībhṛtāṃ vadhājjano mṛgāṇāmiva yattava stavam /
children.translated_text: The praise that people offer you for slaying <s>Kaṃsa</s> and other great kings, as though [praising the slaying] of deer—

children.text: hare hiraṇyākṣapuraḥsarāsuradvipadviṣaḥ pratyuta sā tiraskriyā // MSpv_1.39 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Hari</s>, that is rather a dishonor to you, the enemy of the bipeds (demons) led by <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, who assumed the <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> form. // MSpv 1.39 //

children.text: pravṛtta eva svayamujjhiśramaḥ krameṇa peṣṭuṃ bhuvanadvaṣāmasi /
children.translated_text: You are indeed already engaged, effortlessly, in gradually crushing the enemies of the worlds;

children.text: tathāpi vācālatayā yunakti māṃ mithastvadābhāṣaṇalolupaṃ manaḥ // MSpv_1.40 //
children.translated_text: nevertheless, my loquacious mind, eager for conversation with you, impels me. // MSpv 1.40 //
Therefore, O <s>Upendra</s>, let the message directed by <s>Indra</s>—words beneficial to all the world—be briefly told by me;
let it be heard by you, O enemy of the serpent, who has assumed the foremost role in all affairs. // MSpv 1.41 //
There was a son of <s>Diti</s>, the source of terror for all beings, with a body trembling with the lustre of agitated radiance—
him they call <s>Kaśipu</s> with the prefix '<s>Hiraṇya</s>' (Gold)—the one whose very name signifies the destruction of the meaning of the word '<s>Indra</s>' (Lord). // MSpv 1.42 //
That demon, who by his envy first gave reality to the designation 'enemy of the gods' (<s>asura</s>) long [before merely] in name,

children.text: bhayasyapūrvāvatarastarasvinā manastu yena dyusadāṃ nyadhīyata // MSpv_1.43 //
children.translated_text: by whose swiftness of unprecedented descent of terror the minds of the heaven-dwellers were subdued. // MSpv 1.43 //

children.text: diśāmadhīśāṃścaturo yataḥ surānapāsya taṃ rāgāhṛtāḥ siṣevire /
children.translated_text: Because the four lords of the directions, abandoning the gods, served him, seized by attachment,

children.text: avāpurārabhya tataścalā iti pravādamuccairayaśaskaraṃ śriyaḥ // MSpv_1.44 //
children.translated_text: the Glories (<s>Śrīs</s>) thereupon acquired the loud, ill-reputed saying that they are 'fickle.' // MSpv 1.44 //

children.text: purāṇi durgāṇi niśātamāyudhaṃ balāni śūrāṇi ghanāścakañcukāḥ /
children.translated_text: Impregnable cities, sharpened weapons, mighty armies, and thick armor—

children.text: svarūpaśobhaikaphalāni nākināṃ gaṇairyamāśaṅkya tadādi cakrire // MSpv_1.45 //
children.translated_text: whose sole fruit was the beauty of their own appearance—the hosts of heaven-dwellers then first fashioned, out of fear of him. // MSpv 1.45 //

children.text: sa saṃcariṣṇu bhuvanāntareṣu yāṃ yadṛcchayāśiśriyādāśrayaḥ śriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever direction he, the abode of <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), chose to grace by chance while roaming among the worlds,

children.text: akāri tasyai mukuṭopalaskhalatkaraistrisandhyaṃ tridaśairdiśe namaḥ // MSpv_1.46 //
children.translated_text: to that direction the gods offered their three-fold daily salutation, with hands from whose crowns jewels slipped. // MSpv 1.46 //

children.text: saṭācchaṭabhinnaghanena bibhratā nṛsiṃha saiṃhīmatanuṃ tanuṃ tvayā /
children.translated_text: By you, who assumed the leonine body of <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, bearing a form with mane-tufts that split the clouds,
his chest was torn open with nails that would have broken [even] at the touch of a tender woman's breast. // MSpv 1.47 //

children.text: vinodamicchannatha darpajanmano raṇena kaṇḍvāstridaśai samaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, seeking amusement through battle—born of arrogance—like an itch, [to be scratched] with the gods,

children.text: sa rāvaṇo nāma nikāmabhīṣaṇaṃ babhūva rakṣaḥ kṣatarakṣaṇaṃ divaḥ // MSpv_1.48 //
children.translated_text: there arose the <s>rākṣasa</s> named <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, dreadfully terrible, who destroyed the protection of heaven. // MSpv 1.48 //
He who desired to become lord of the three worlds, wishing to cut off his tenth head [as offering],
considered the grace of the Trident-bearer (<s>Śiva</s>)—befitting a favor—as an obstacle to the accomplishment of his wish. // MSpv 1.49 //

children.text: samutkṣipanyaḥ pṛthivībhṛtāṃ varaṃ varapradānasya cakāra śūlinaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who was tossing up the best of mountains made the Trident-bearer pay the price of granting his boon
through the pleasure of a self-embrace with the startled daughter of the snowy mountain (<s>Pārvatī</s>). // MSpv 1.50 //

children.text: purīmavaskanda lunīhi nandanaṃ muṣāṇa ratnāni harāmarāṅganāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Storm the city! Destroy <s>Nandana</s> grove! Steal the jewels! Seize the divine women!'—

children.text: vigṛhya cakre namucidviṣā balī ya itthamasvāsthyamahardivaṃ divaḥ // MSpv_1.51 //
children.translated_text: thus the mighty one, grappling with the enemy of <s>Namuci</s> (<s>Indra</s>), created such distress for heaven, day after day. // MSpv 1.51 //
The footsteps of <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s> (Indra's horse), which were effortlessly made without his master's whip,

children.text: anudrutaḥ saṃyati yena kevalaṃ balasya śatruḥ praśaśaṃsa śīghratām // MSpv_1.52 //
children.translated_text: when [<s>Rāvaṇa</s>] alone pursued him in battle, the enemy of <s>Bala</s> (Indra) praised only the [horse's] speed. // MSpv 1.52 //
Unable to endure his sight, which was like that of the thousand-rayed sun, with unsteady eyes,

children.text: praviśya hemādriguhāgṛhāntaraṃ nināya bibhyaddivasāni kauśikaḥ // MSpv_1.53 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kauśika</s> (Indra) entered the interior of the golden mountain cave-dwellings and fearfully spent his days. // MSpv 1.53 //
Of the enemy of the gods, whose broad and forceful throat-grasp scattered loose sparks of fire,
<s>Viṣṇu</s>'s discus, of the lord of the world, would not approach his excessively thick neck. // MSpv 1.54 //
With his conch broken, becoming agitated repeatedly with intoxication, like an elephant in rut observing human customs,

children.text: nirastaghāṃbhīryamapāstapuṣpakaṃ prakampayāmāsa na mānasaṃ na saḥ // MSpv_1.55 //
children.translated_text: he who had set aside [<s>Kubera</s>'s] dignity and seized <s>Puṣpaka</s> [chariot], shook—not <s>Mānasa</s> lake, but [<s>Kubera</s>'s] mind. // MSpv 1.55 //
The serpent-king's ropes, hurled by <s>Varuṇa</s> in battle, turned back by [<s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s] wrathful roar,

children.text: praharturevoragarājarajjavo javena kaṇṭhaṃ sabhayāḥ prapedire // MSpv_1.56 //
children.translated_text: fearfully wound themselves around the neck of their own sender, with great speed. // MSpv 1.56 //
The bull of that enemy-vanquisher, whose horn-circles had been uprooted [by the demon] to fashion a bow,

children.text: hṛte 'pibhāre mahatastrapābharāduvāha duḥkhena bhṛśānṛtaṃ śiraḥ // MSpv_1.57 //
children.translated_text: when its burden was taken, from the great weight of shame, bore its head with difficulty, as if in distress.
The night-prowler [<s>Rāhu</s>], suspicious of the moon even in the bright fortnight, with his finger-tips that are incomplete swallowers,
adorned his [<s>Indra</s>'s] face with pearls of perspiration-drops born of the heat of sin — the thief of the bride's modesty.
With the full digit that, refusing to release, was more skilled at agitating the passionate woman,
the moon, belonging to that dissolute one [<s>Rāhu</s>], spreading unrest, did not serve as a confidant of jesting.
Surely, desiring to fashion an arrow-letter suited to the amorous glances of the clever one — by this proud [<s>Rāhu</s>],

children.text: na jātu vaināyakamekamuddhṛtaṃ viṣāṇamadyāpi punaḥ prarohati // MSpv_1.60 //
children.translated_text: the single tusk of <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, once uprooted, has not grown back even to this day.
Though his sin was evident in shaking the garments of the women of the night-quarters, upon the thighs of him whose eyes roved —
the gods, afflicted by [<s>Indra</s>'s] beloved without [his] offense, sympathized through his trembling.
Overshadowed repeatedly by his glory — that of the greatest among the glorious, which humiliated the people —
[<s>Agni</s>] bore a doubled slender form through tears, his canopy of smoke from [unattended] oblations doubled by sorrows.
The serpent clans, straight-going, with ear-ornaments, whose forked-tongue fault was to pierce the vital points of the enemy,

children.text: tamiddhamārādhayituṃ sakarṇakaiḥ kulairna bheje phaṇināṃ bhujaṅgatā // MSpv_1.63 //
children.translated_text: did not adopt the nature of creeping creatures to propitiate him who was inflamed [with anger].
The directional elephants, from whose temple-regions the enemy-suppressing ichor had departed, shattered by the clash of his war-elephants' frontal globes,
never to return, having seized [their proper] directions — for a long time maintained their true [fixed] nature.
His body, though hot, was never cooled by the cool winds, fragrant with sandalwood-water drops,
that were like the sighs of <s>Indra</s>'s imprisoned panegyrists, breathed with warmth.

children.text: tapena varṣāḥ śaradā himāgamo vasantalakṣmyā śiśiraḥ sametya ca /
children.translated_text: The seasons — summer through the rains, autumn through the cool season, and winter with the beauty of spring — meeting together,

children.text: prasūnakḷptiṃ dadhataḥ sadartavaḥ purosya vāstavyakuṭumbitāṃ yayau // MSpv_1.66 //
children.translated_text: bearing the arrangement of flowers, assumed the householder-status of permanent residence before him.

children.text: amānavaṃ jātamajaṃ kule manoḥ prabhāvinaṃ bhāvinnamantamātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who was born superhuman, unborn, in the lineage of <s>Manu</s>, powerful, of a nature that was to be manifest, knowing himself to be infinite —

children.text: mumoca jānannapi jānakīṃ na yaḥ sadabhimānaikadhanā hi māninaḥ // MSpv_1.67 //
children.translated_text: did not release <s>Jānakī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>) even though he knew; for the proud have self-respect as their sole wealth.
Does the son of <s>Daśaratha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) now remember this one who abducted women from the forest-border?
He shall cross the ocean with its bridges of moving waters and destroy <s>Laṅkā</s> nearby!
Having obtained, through deception, another earthly role [as if] an actor,

children.text: tirohitātmā śiśupālasaṃjñayā pratīyate saṃprati sāpyasaḥ paraiḥ // MSpv_1.69 //
children.translated_text: he, with his true self concealed, is now perceived by others under the name <s>Śiśupāla</s>, and that [role] too is false.

children.text: sa bāla āsīdvapuṣā caturbhujo mukhena pūrṇendunibhastrilocanaḥ /
children.translated_text: As a child, he was four-armed in body, three-eyed with a face resembling the full moon;
now as a youth, he is undoubtedly the sun in splendor, having overleapt the mountaintops with his conquering stride.
The self-created Lord, the disposer of grace and wrath toward gods, demons, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>,
laughs at those like <s>Rāvaṇa</s> of ten faces, who have propitiated deities and descended with surpassing heroic power.
Even now, as before, he is obstructed by that one who desires to conquer the world, [though] his power [is overwhelming] —

children.text: satīva yoṣitprakṛtiḥ suniścalā pumāṃsaṃmabyeti bhavāntareṣvapi // MSpv_1.72 //
children.translated_text: like a chaste woman, [his] <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature), though utterly steadfast, follows the [same] man even in subsequent births.
Therefore, make him — who has transgressed the commands of the Creator — a guest in the abode of <s>Yama</s> (Death)!
Misfortunes arising from the ripening of wicked conduct are indeed to be destroyed; the wicked are to be uprooted by the virtuous.
May the heart of <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>), establishing unresisted, firm resolve,
again attain the capacity for tight embrace — pressed against the hardened breast-tips of <s>Pulomajā</s> (<s>Śacī</s>), bristling with goosebumps.

children.text: omityuktavato 'tha śāṅgiṇā iti vyāhṛtya vācaṃ nabhastasminnutpatite puraḥ suramunāvindoḥ śriyaṃ bibhrati /
children.translated_text: When the bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] had thus spoken 'Oṃ' and uttered this speech — when the divine sage [<s>Nārada</s>], bearing the beauty of the moon, had flown up into the sky before him — on his face, the frown-mark, portending the perpetual destruction of enemies, angry toward the <s>Caidya</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>), made a place for <s>Ketu</s> (the comet) in the sky as if in disguise.

children.text: śatruṇāmaniśa vināśapiśunaḥ kruddhasya caidyaṃ prati vyomni bhrakuṭicchalena vadane ketuśacakārāspadam // MSpv_1.75 //

children.translated_text: Then, summoned by <s>Arjuna</s> (<s>Pārtha</s>) who desired to perform a sacrifice — the slayer of <s>Mura</s>,
was about to set out against <s>Caidya</s> — he was agitated by the double task.
Then he sat in the assembly-hall together with <s>Uddhava</s> and the <s>Sātvatī</s> [warriors],
bearing the moonlit beauty of the sky, following the discourse of the teacher's poem.
Having come for the pacification of the world, blazing,
that threefold fire of men (<s>naraśikhitrayī</s>) shone on the assembly-platform.
Their reflections, transferred to the jeweled pillars, appeared
as though, even when alone, they were surrounded on all sides by attendants.
The golden thrones, lofty, upon which they sat —
on those, they appeared like [<s>Viṣṇu</s>], the enemy of <s>Keśāri</s>, mounted on the three peaks of <s>Trikūṭa</s>.
To the two weighty [matters] — of the two weighty tasks —
the wise one [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] reported to <s>Hari</s> [<s>Balarāma</s>] the contradiction.
With smiles that illuminated the interior of the assembly, [bright] like the tips of jasmine buds,
his <s>Sarasvatī</s> (speech), of pure sound, seemed to have been bathed.
'Our words are but a prelude to give opportunity for your speech —
a prologue to the dramatic subject at hand.
With kings made tributary by his brothers, the conquerors of the directions,
the son of austerity [<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>] is capable of performing the sacrifice even without us.
But a rising adversary should not be ignored by one who desires sovereignty;

children.text: samau hi śiṣṭairāmnātau vartsyantāvāmayaḥ sa ca // MSpv_2.10 //
children.translated_text: for the learned have declared that both — the growing [threat] and the disease — are equal.
It does not grieve me, the son of <s>Sātvatī</s> (<s>Devakī</s>), that he offends me;
but that the world is burning — that causes me distress.
For now, let my opinion be heard, and yours as well;
for even one who knows the essence [should consult], when the matter at hand is doubtful.
Having delivered this speech, whose every word served its purpose, <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)
fell silent; for the great are by nature sparing in speech.
Then, [<s>Balarāma</s>], with a quivering [of lips] from the memory of removing the enemy's wife, accompanied by regret,
with his lip — that lip coy for kissing the bimba-fruit lip of <s>Rāmā</s> (<s>Revatī</s>) —
conveying the speech of the expert in meaning, withdrawn at the very moment [of utterance],
brought the words of the son of <s>Pavana</s> (<s>Bhīma</s>) to the position of a rejoinder.
Rolling [his eyes], his radiance reddened by the intoxication of enjoying wine,
his two eyes purified by the remains [of the kiss] from <s>Revatī</s>'s face,
wilting the garland of forest-flowers with the hot breath of pride — that garland which bore witness to the hardness of the breasts of wives eager for embrace —
bearing drops of perspiration clinging to his limbs reddened by dyed garments, resembling
twinkling stars in the twilight-red sky,
making the luster of the ruby pendants set in the swinging earrings
appear as if [his body] wore the <s>Cauta</s> creeper with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s upper garment's sheen,
exhaling from his mouth a fragrance rendered sweeter by the wine,
which had obtained its seasoning from dwelling within the mouth of the <s>Kakudmī</s> princess,
driving away with the whiteness of his prominent teeth the bees
that fell around the lotus-disguise of his face, [attracted by] the nectar-like sweetness,
that which was spoken humbly by <s>Vāsudeva</s>, humbly though humbly uttered —
action alone was the proper response to his words.
'Even this brief speech is not surpassed by a more extensive one;
a fire, though fed with heaps of fuel, does not in brilliance exceed the sun.',
'Yet of this very sentence — brief but weighty in meaning —

children.text: suvistaratarā vāco bhūṣyabhūtā bhavantu mo // MSpv_2.24 //
children.translated_text: let more elaborate words, as ornaments, be mine.',
'Adversarial words make even the articulate mute;
but the words of the accomplished, following the intended meaning, make even the dull eloquent.',
'The six principles of policy, the three powers, the means of success, and the three occasions —
even the dull-witted can manage to expound these after studying the treatises.',
'The web of words of a speaker who has not thoroughly examined the matter at hand is futile —
like the prancing of an archer who aims at the wrong target.',
'In the entire body of political action, apart from the five limbs and the framework,
there is no other counsel for kings — just as, for the Buddhists, there is no other self.',
'Counsel, like an unsteady warrior, even when covered on all sides,

children.text: ciraṃ na sthātuṃ parebhyo bhedaśaṅkayā // MSpv_2.29 //
children.translated_text: cannot remain for long [hidden] from enemies, due to the suspicion of betrayal.',
'Self-advancement and the ruin of the adversary — these two, it is said, constitute statecraft.',
'Having acknowledged this, the accomplished extend the sovereignty of speech.',
'Great souls find no contentment even in the greatness of another;
the proof here is the great ocean, which, even when full, desires the rising of the moon.',
'He who, thinking [his] prosperity secure, becomes complacent with even a little —

children.text: kṛtakṛtyo vidhirmanye na vardhayanti tasya tām // MSpv_2.32 //
children.translated_text: the fates, I think, do not increase his [prosperity], considering his purpose already fulfilled.',
'The proud strike down their enemies to the root and do not merely suppress them;
the sun, which has utterly destroyed the darkness, is the example here.',
'Having made the adversary entirely [powerless], establishment is indeed difficult;
without reducing dust to mud, water does not stand firm.',
'As long as even a single enemy is maintained, how can there be happiness?

children.text: puraḥ klaśnāti somaṃ hi saiṃhikeyo 'suradruhām // MSpv_2.35 //
children.translated_text: Before their very eyes, <s>Rāhu</s>, the son of <s>Siṃhikā</s>, swallows the moon — though he is the enemy of the demons.',
'A greater friend, a smaller enemy — these two are artifices born of circumstances;
even naturally-born enemies and friends may become friends and enemies [respectively].',
'Alliance should be with the beneficent enemy, not with the harmful friend;
for benefit and harm are indeed the defining marks of these two.',
'<s>Caidya</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>) was offended by you when you abducted <s>Rukmiṇī</s> from <s>Hari</s>;
for women are the deep root of the great tree of enmity.',
'When you had gone to conquer <s>Bhauma</s> (<s>Naraka</s>), he tried to plunder this city —
as darkness [encroaches upon] the slope of <s>Meru</s> when the jewel among men has departed.',
'Enough of this, O brown-haired one — that he did not abduct our wives!
For even the talk of the wicked is sufficient to produce misfortune.',

children.text: virāddha evaṃ bhamatā virāddhā bahudhā ca naḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having been thus wronged by him who roams — and we have been wronged in many ways —

children.text: nirvatyate 'riḥ kriyayā sa śrutaśravasaḥ sutaḥ // MSpv_2.41 //
children.translated_text: the enemy is to be dealt with through action — he, the son of <s>Śrutaśravas</s>.',
'He who, having created enmity, sits idle before a resentful enemy —
throws a flame into dry grass and sleeps facing the wind.',

children.text: manāganabhyavṛtyā vā kāmaṃ kṣāmyatatu yaḥ kṣamī /
children.translated_text: 'Let the forbearing one forgive an offense committed through mere thoughtlessness, if he so desires;
but who would tolerate one who offends through deliberate, repeated assault?'

children.text: anyadā bhūṣaṇaṃ puṃsaḥ kṣamā lajjeva yoṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'At other times, forbearance is an ornament of a man, like modesty of a woman;
but valor in the face of insult is like ardor in love-making.',
'Let him not live who lives burnt by the fire of contempt from others!
Better that his mother had not given birth — to him who causes his mother distress.',
'That which, when kicked, rises up and mounts upon the head —
dust is better than a man who endures even when his honor is being stripped away.',
'For one who accomplishes nothing through birth, action, or qualities —
like the word 'accidental,' his birth serves merely as a name.',
'Height alone does not [make] a mountain impassable, nor depth alone the ocean;
both together make [them so] — so too the man of spirit.',
'For an equal offense, <s>Svarbhānu</s> (<s>Rāhu</s>) swallows the sun only after a long time,

children.text: himāṃśumāśu grasate tanmradimnaḥ sphuṭaṃ phalam // MSpv_2.49 //
children.translated_text: but the moon quickly — the clear fruit of [the moon's] softness.',
'A lightweight man, who submits even to the insignificant and approaches the other's power,
is an example of the worthless — like abundant grass [blown about].',
'A spirited man, even among the spirited, is counted, though far away;
among the five fires, the sun is the fifth, among all fires.',
'Without contemptuously placing one's foot high upon the heads of enemies,'
How can fame, without any support, ascend the sky? // MSpv_2.52 //
The moon, hare-marked, mounted upon [his] limbs,
is a lion, the lord of beasts, scattering herds of deer with ferocity. // MSpv_2.53 //
When the enemy is amenable only to the fourth expedient [force], conciliation is a waste;
what wise person sprinkles with water one who sweats from a fever that is not due to heat? // MSpv_2.54 //
Words of conciliation to one who is angry are rather like fuel [to fire],
like drops of water suddenly [thrown] on heated ghee. // MSpv_2.55 //
Those who, through misrepresentation of virtues, ruin the purpose,
bearing the guise of ministers — those, called enemies, are corrupting for kings. // MSpv_2.56 //
Some say the advance should come when one's own power increases, others when the enemy is in distress;
but you, seated [idle], are roused by both [circumstances]. // MSpv_2.57 //
Of you who desire to overstep the worlds, unoversteppable, not light [in power],
your forbearance, like a seashore, restrains the <s>Yādava</s> ocean. // MSpv_2.58 //
Let the army be appointed merely as a witness to your victory;
when the purpose is rightly assessed, [the army is] like enjoyment to the intellect that partakes of the fruit — in oneself. // MSpv_2.59 //
When the king who had two mothers was slain in battle by the enemy of <s>Hiḍimba</s>,
after a long time, he who gloats at the misfortune of [his] friend — <s>Sudāma</s>, the son of <s>Damaghoṣa</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>). // MSpv_2.60 //
Statecraft is something to be resorted to in adversity — that the other considers a humiliation [for us];
like the full moon for one who lacks the moon — he [<s>Śiśupāla</s>] finds that an occasion for celebration. // MSpv_2.61 //
One kind of spirit is unrestrained, another is disciplined by the scriptures;
how can there be a common ground between fire and darkness? // MSpv_2.62 //
For now, let the march to <s>Indraprastha</s> be undertaken — let the <s>Cedis</s> be restrained;
trees become dwarfed in the proximity of our elephants. // MSpv_2.63 //
Like cows [heading] to the pen, with the flow of their rut-juice stopped and checked,

children.text: uparundhantu dāśārhāḥ purīṃ māhiṣmatīṃ dviṣaḥ // MSpv_2.64 //
children.translated_text: let the <s>Dāśārhas</s> (Yādavas) besiege the city of <s>Māhiṣmatī</s> of the enemies. // MSpv_2.64 //
Let the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> sacrifice for heaven — let him who has <s>Indra</s> as his sacrificial priest [proceed];

children.text: vayaṃ hanāma dviṣataḥ sarvaḥ svārthaṃ samīhate // MSpv_2.65 //
children.translated_text: we shall slay the enemies — everyone strives for his own purpose. // MSpv_2.65 //
Let the wealth of lightnings be obtained from contact with the Sun's radiance,
with weapons drenched by the blood spurting from the severed heads of enemies. // MSpv_2.66 //
Thus, the words of the wrathful <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) — [as if] the painted deities,
with the echoes of the assembly-hall walls, repeated [his words] as if in fear. // MSpv_2.67 //
Having heard those [words], <s>Adhokṣaja</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), wishing to speak to the rest of the heroes,
indicated the opportunity to the disciple of the great ones with a glance, as a reply. // MSpv_2.68 //
Then <s>Uddhava</s>, having undertaken the weighty charge of speech, in a calm manner,
like <s>Utathya's</s> younger brother (<s>Bṛhaspati</s>), spoke truly before the elder brother of <s>Gadā</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>). // MSpv_2.69 //
When the Mace-wielder (<s>Balarāma</s>) has spoken what is inopportune at the present time,
the matter being determined — though certainly having spoken a spoken [truth] like a writing, certainly only a verbal one. // MSpv_2.70 //
Nevertheless, since even toward me you have the reverence due to a teacher,
that assumes the status of a prompting cause when I speak. // MSpv_2.71 //
Of language, composed of only a few syllables, like musical notes,
the variety is infinite, alas, like that of song! // MSpv_2.72 //
Although much may be said freely and at will, scattered [in discourse],
a composition with unbroken connection of meaning is hard to produce. // MSpv_2.73 //
The skillful extend their speech, though soft and dense,
composed of no small number of qualities, variegated — like a piece of cloth. // MSpv_2.74 //
That the treatise is taken up before you, who know distinctions,
is a means of confirming familiarity — it is merely the speaker's set of virtues [on display]. // MSpv_2.75 //
A master who possesses wisdom and energy should strive to establish [them] in himself;
for those two are the root of the self-wealth of one who aspires to conquer, that is about to arise. // MSpv_2.76 //

children.text: sopadhānāṃ dhiyaṃ dhīrāḥ stheyasīṃ khaṭvayanti ye /
children.translated_text: The wise who lay their well-founded, firm intellect upon a pillow,

children.text: tatrāniśaṃ niṣamṇṇāste jānate jātu na śramaṃm // MSpv_2.77 //
children.translated_text: constantly reclining thereon, never know fatigue. // MSpv_2.77 //
The sharp touch a little and penetrate within, like arrows;
those who are merely thick-skinned, though touching much, remain outside, like stones. // MSpv_2.78 //
The ignorant undertake only small [tasks] and are indeed agitated;
those of great undertakings, whose minds are made up, stand unperturbed. // MSpv_2.79 //
Even for one who has employed the right means, purposes perish if he is negligent;
a hunter lying in ambush does not kill deer if he is drowsy. // MSpv_2.80 //
Without abandoning his effort among the twelve [types of] kings, he who desires to conquer,
alone, is like the sun among the [twelve] <s>Ādityas</s> — destined to rise. // MSpv_2.81 //
With intellect as his weapon, ministers as his limbs, dense secrecy as his armor,

children.text: cārekṣaṇo dūtamukhaḥ papuruṣaḥ ko 'pi pārthivaḥ // MSpv_2.82 //
children.translated_text: spies as his eyes, envoys as his mouth — some sort of artificial person is the king. // MSpv_2.82 //

children.text: tejaḥ kṣamā vā naikāntaṃ kālajñasya mahīpateḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither valor alone nor forbearance alone suffices for a king who knows the right time;

children.text: naikamojaḥ prasādo vā rasabhāvavidaḥ kaveḥ // MSpv_2.83 //
children.translated_text: neither vigor alone nor sweetness alone suffices for a poet who knows the [right] sentiment (<s>rasa</s>). // MSpv_2.83 //
Even one against whom offenses have been committed, who does not reveal his agitation,

children.text: asādhyaḥ kurute vā rasabhāvavidaḥ kaveḥ // MSpv_2.84 //
children.translated_text: is unconquerable — or [rather], like a poet who knows the [right] sentiment. // MSpv_2.84 //
Valor, softly veiled, succeeds in accomplishing purposes;
a lamp absorbs oil through the wick placed within. // MSpv_2.85 //
He does not cling to rigid [principles], nor does he falter in manliness;
like a good poet [who regards] word and meaning, the wise one regards both [aspects]. // MSpv_2.86 //
As the transient emotions operate for the sake of the permanent emotion [in poetry],
so the many subordinate kings [operate] for the one dominant ruler, the mountain-bearing [king]. // MSpv_2.87 //
Governed by one who knows the warp and weft [of alliances], through strategic combinations, circles [of kings] are controlled;
enemies are as easily restrained by a supreme king as serpent-chiefs [by <s>Garuḍa</s>]. // MSpv_2.88 //
Lofty, with revenue gathered by hand, [demonstrating] the lord's manifest power,
the tree of energy, with a great root of wisdom and strength, bears fruit. // MSpv_2.89 //
Just as in music the other notes become subordinate to the [dominant] note because of their weakness or its strength,
so do the kings aspiring to conquer reduce [other] rulers to the status of attendants. // MSpv_2.90 //
Even for a lord who has not yet begun [action], purposes accomplished by others

children.text: vrajanti guṇatāmarthāḥ śabdā iva vihāyasaḥ // MSpv_2.91 //
children.translated_text: come to serve as his qualities, like sounds [that travel] through the sky. // MSpv_2.91 //
In the garland [of alliances] — the rear-guard and the rest — resplendent above all,
strung upon one thread of purpose, the leader leads. // MSpv_2.92 //
One should employ the sixfold policy as a tonic, according to one's power;
thus his limbs become stable and strong. // MSpv_2.93 //
For those who are tranquil, growth of the limbs [comes] through power in the right place;
an undertaking disproportionate to one's strength is the cause of the prosperity of ruin. // MSpv_2.94 //
Therefore, you should not look down upon that lord of the <s>Cedis</s>;
for the <s>udātta</s> (high-pitched accent), in one [syllabic] position, kills the other accents, as it were, slaying enemies. // MSpv_2.95 //
Do not think that he, the <s>Cedi</s> king, is merely one person to be conquered;

children.text: rājayakṣmeva rogāṇāṃ samūha sa mahībhṛtāṃ // MSpv_2.96 //
children.translated_text: he is like royal consumption (<s>rājayakṣma</s>) among diseases for the assembly of kings. // MSpv_2.96 //
His ally, who has accomplished his purpose, skilled in splitting the enemy,
like an arrow fitted to a bow with a bowstring, will come to [the act of] aiming. // MSpv_2.97 //

body.text:
ye cānye kālayavanaśālvarukmidrumādayaḥ /
tamaḥsvabhāvaste/pyenaṃ pradoṣamanuyāyinaḥ // MSpv_2.98 //
body.translated_text: And others — <s>Kālayavana</s>, <s>Śālva</s>, <s>Rukmin</s>, <s>Druma</s>, and the rest — dark by nature, they follow him like twilight follows [darkness]. // MSpv_2.98 //

children.translated_text: Subversion has been practiced by him upon those [allies] who are angry with you;
even a small [wind] quickly kindles those who have fire, like wind [kindles] firewood. // MSpv_2.99 //
Even a small one, with a great ally, reaches the end of the purpose;
a mountain stream, joining a great river, reaches the ocean. // MSpv_2.100 //

children.text: tasya mitrāṇyamitrāste ye ca ye cobhaye nṛpāḥ /
children.translated_text: His friends are your enemies, and whichever kings are on both sides;

children.text: abiyuktaṃ tvayainaṃ te gantārastvāmataḥ pare // MSpv_2.101 //
children.translated_text: those [now] attacked by you will go to him, and the rest [will come] to you. // MSpv_2.101 //
Having thus stirred up the entire royal assembly for the purpose of obstructing the sacrifice,
alas — you, the first enemy, have created [an enemy] for one who had been born without enemies. // MSpv_2.102 //
Esteeming you as one whose shoulder can bear the excessive burden, together with his kinsmen,
<s>Dharmarāja</s> (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>) desires [you] as a companion to bear the yoke of the sacrifice. // MSpv_2.103 //
Great souls favor even enemies who worship them;
rivers, [though] rushing to the sea, deliver to it [even] the tributaries that flow against them. // MSpv_2.104 //
Even after a long time, force against a powerful enemy [may work] for success;
[but] friends who have been slighted are hard to win back by following their whims. // MSpv_2.105 //
You think that slaying the enemy is good because it pleases the gods;
the eaters of the sacrificial cake desire that the desired sacrifice be completed, not disrupted. // MSpv_2.106 //
That which the righteous pour as nectar upon their mantra-tongues [in sacrifice] —
even the description of the churning of the ocean by <s>Mandara</s> is merely ornamental. // MSpv_2.107 //
'I shall endure a hundred offenses from your son' — that which was by you
promised in waiting to the aunt (<s>Śiśupāla's</s> mother), that [promise] is to be waited upon. // MSpv_2.108 //

children.text: tīkṣṇā nāruntudā buddhiḥ karma śāntaṃ pratāpavat /
children.translated_text: His intellect is sharp yet not wounding; his action is calm yet powerful;

children.text: nopatāpi manaḥ soṣamavāgekā vāgminaḥ sataḥ // MSpv_2.109 //
children.translated_text: his mind does not blaze, yet there is no lack of dryness — there is but one speech of the true eloquent man. // MSpv_2.109 //
Like the sun of a day whose grace is self-made,
without reaching the limit of the appointed time, even you are not [sufficient] for ending [it]. // MSpv_2.110 //
Let the spies, having established their footing at sacred fords, knowing the duties,
make known the depth of the great ocean of enemies. // MSpv_2.111 //
With every step placed along the line, with good conduct as its composition,
like the science of grammar, our statecraft shines, untouched [by error]. // MSpv_2.112 //
With faults unknown, by fault-knowers, of incorruptible double agents,
the enemy's allies should be split by means of openly proclaimed decrees. // MSpv_2.113 //
The doers have already come to the city of the one who was born without enemies;
your spies, knowing the expedients, have unified the royal purposes. // MSpv_2.114 //
When [<s>Dharmarāja</s>] extends his special devotion to the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>,
the fickle ones, inherently jealous, become hostile on their own. // MSpv_2.115 //

children.text: ya ihātmavido vipakṣamadhye saha saṃvṛddhiyujo 'pi bhūbhujaḥ syuḥ /
children.translated_text: Those self-knowing kings who, even among enemies, along with those who have prospered,
like well-nourished [vassals] from a powerful lineage — separately from this [<s>Śiśupāla</s>], they will soon be won over by them. // MSpv_2.116 //
Agitated by the impulsiveness of innate faults, grasping the support of a weak and wavering faction,
before your unapproachable valor, that band of bad friends will meet the fate of moths [before a flame]. // MSpv_2.117 //
Thus, having heard this speech of <s>Uddhava</s>, its meaning clearly analyzed, following the path of statecraft — a bolt against misrule,
he who had heard [it as if from] <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) seated on his broad and elevated chest, rose up with a joy that was manifest. // MSpv_2.118 //

children.text: kauberadigbhāgam apāsya mārgam āgastyam iva āśuḥ iva avatārṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Setting aside the path toward <s>Kubera's</s> quarter, descended like the swift [wind], like [the path] of <s>Agastya</s>,
his mind gentle, free from the obsession of battle, he then proceeded toward <s>Hariharaprastha</s>. // MSpv_3.1 //

children.text: jagatpavitraiḥ api taṃ na pādaiḥ spraṣṭuṃ jagatpūjyam ayujyata arkaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even the sun, with his world-purifying rays, was not fit to touch that world-worshipped one with [his] feet;
therefore he bore a great full-moon-beautiful parasol over him. // MSpv_3.2 //
He, standing between two waving <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks), [their handles] pure as lotus-fiber threads,
assumed on both sides the unprecedented splendor of the <s>Siddha-Sindhu</s> (Celestial Gaṅgā) at its fall. // MSpv_3.3 //
By the marvelous rays of the gems worn on the crowns of those above him,
the appearance of <s>Govardhana</s> mountain, streaked with many-hued minerals, was imitated. // MSpv_3.4 //
With the radiance of golden ear-ornaments, whose tips were studded with filigree of gold,
his chest attained [an appearance] as if adorned with peacock-feather crests befitting boyhood. // MSpv_3.5 //
The two arm-ornaments, by the enhanced brilliance of their gems from the friction against the peaks of <s>Mandara</s> mountain,
made him blaze with a vaster canopy of radiance. // MSpv_3.6 //
With the tips of his nails — naturally red, encircled by bracelets, streaked with rays of copper-colored gems —
his hands gleamed as if smeared with the blood gushing from wounds inflicted on the chest of the enemy of the gods. // MSpv_3.7 //
If in the sky two separate streams of the waters of the celestial <s>Gaṅgā</s> were to fall —
His chest, which has released strands of pearls, is compared to that one, dark as the <s>tamāla</s> tree // <s>MSpv</s> 3.8 //
By that, the ocean, whose essence is of the waters, bore a radiance illumined by the rays of gems,
wherein the world was seen directly, as if dwelling within, reflected in his body // <s>MSpv</s> 3.9 //
A garland of pearls, hanging from a necklace of geese, adorned him as it was being offered at his feet,
like the waters of the triple-coursed <s>Gaṅgā</s>, streaming upward continuously from between his big toe and little toe // <s>MSpv</s> 3.10 //
He, of dark-blue form like an <s>indranīla</s> gem set upon a dark surface, shone resplendent wearing garments tawny as camphor,
like the lord of <s>Yama</s>, variegated with the pollen scattered from lotuses // <s>MSpv</s> 3.11 //
That the beauty of this one who was adorned was different from that of his enemy—this is fitting,
for <s>Lakṣmī</s>, beloved of all the world, has no other lover, while the other one dwelt upon his chest alone // <s>MSpv</s> 3.12 //
Of him upon whose broad chest, delightful as a door-panel, the beautiful <s>Śrī</s> resided,
there was another <s>Lakṣmī</s> altogether, pervading all his limbs, who delighted all people // <s>MSpv</s> 3.13 //
By the nails of the lord of <s>Daityas</s>, which cut off life-breath, having attained the status of ornaments through the wound,

children.text: prakāśakārkaśyaguṇai dadhānāḥ stanau taruṇyaḥ parivrurenam // MSpv_3.14 //
children.translated_text: young women embraced him, displaying qualities of brilliance and hardness upon their breasts // <s>MSpv</s> 3.14 //
As if being pulled upward by the exceedingly slender waist and by the high-raised circle of breasts,
the middle of the women bent down, excessively weighed upon as if by something extremely heavy // <s>MSpv</s> 3.15 //

children.text: yāṃ yāṃ priyaḥ praikṣata kātarāśkṣīṃ sā sā hriyā namramukhī babhūva /
children.translated_text: Whichever timid-eyed beloved he gazed upon, she became one with downcast face from modesty;
meanwhile, without shame, others with steady jealousy seized him with sidelong glances // <s>MSpv</s> 3.16 //
Of him whose luster matched the <s>atasī</s> flower, with its circling garland of revolving rays,

children.text: cakreṇa reje yamunājalaughaḥ sphuranmahāgarta ivaikabāhuḥ // MSpv_3.17 //
children.translated_text: the one arm with the discus shone like a great whirlpool in the current of the <s>Yamunā</s> waters // <s>MSpv</s> 3.17 //
Like the embodied power, skilled in breaking the formations of adversaries, occasionally stumbling,

children.text: nityaṃ hareḥ saṃnihitā nikāmaṃ modayati sma cetaḥ // MSpv_3.18 //
children.translated_text: always closely attending <s>Hari</s>, she delighted the heart abundantly // <s>MSpv</s> 3.18 //

children.text: na kevalaṃ yaḥ svatayā murārerasādhāraṇatāṃ dadhānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Not only did it bear an exclusive relationship with <s>Murāri</s> by its own nature,

children.text: atyarthamudvejayitā pareṣāṃ nāmnāpi tasyaiva nandako 'bhūt // MSpv_3.19 //
children.translated_text: extremely terrifying to enemies—even by name it was indeed his: <s>Nandaka</s> ("the delighter") // <s>MSpv</s> 3.19 //
Never brought to submission by another, having attained the qualities that reach the ear in battles,

children.text: vidheyamasyā bhavadantikasthaṃ śārṅgaṃ dhanurmitramiva draḍhīyaḥ // MSpv_3.20 //
children.translated_text: obedient, standing near him—the bow <s>Śārṅga</s> was like a steadfast friend // <s>MSpv</s> 3.20 //
With the deep and resonant sound of a swollen cloud, a lone swan moving near the dark ocean that is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
appearing as if producing a sound filled by the wind, <s>Pāñcajanya</s> was heard // <s>MSpv</s> 3.21 //
The accomplisher of desired success shone forth on a path unpublished in all directions,

children.text: mahārathaḥ puṣyarathaṃ rathāṅgī kṣipraṃ kṣapānātha ivādhirūḍhaḥ // MSpv_3.22 //
children.translated_text: the great chariot-warrior, bearer of the discus, mounted upon <s>Puṣyaratha</s> swiftly, like the lord of night ascending // <s>MSpv</s> 3.22 //
Then the <s>Garuḍa</s>, blazing at the top of the banner, appeared to <s>Śauri</s>, his form transferred to the jeweled grounds,
as if wishing to speak to the underworld to frighten the hooded serpents // <s>MSpv</s> 3.23 //
As he wished to depart, the sound of the kettle-drum, more powerful than splitting mountain caverns,
made the intervals between sounds seem like intervals between waters, as in a great ocean flood // <s>MSpv</s> 3.24 //

children.text: yataḥ sa bhartā jagatāṃ jagāma dhartrā dharitryāḥ phaṇinātato 'dhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Wherever he, the lord of the worlds, went, from below, from <s>Śeṣa</s>, the bearer of the earth,
whose thousand heads were bent by the great burden, there flowed forth the exertion of his many arms // <s>MSpv</s> 3.25 //
Then the armies followed him who was devoted to righteous conduct, with their banners bowed in humility for fear of breaking against the high gateway arches,
like the fruits of good deeds following one who practices good policy // <s>MSpv</s> 3.26 //
The golden mountains were stirred by the dark-red rut-water of elephants,
and the masses of chariots, sunk to their axles, with the splendor of crushed peacock-feather dust, were jostled // <s>MSpv</s> 3.28 //
He did not step over the heads of great people, nor did he exhibit arrogance;
the dust of the chess-board earth, struck by his feet, did not stir—such was his dignity // <s>MSpv</s> 3.27 //
Being restrained by the <s>Yadus</s>, yet somehow repeatedly raising their forelegs,

children.text: dhruvaṃ gurūnmārgarudhaḥ karāndrānullaṅghya gantuṃ turagāstatīṣuḥ // MSpv_3.29 //
children.translated_text: the horses surely wished to go, leaping over the elders blocking the path // <s>MSpv</s> 3.29 //
In front, horses with extended reins, whose riders held them back with effort, were watched,
and mothers quickly came and carried their children away from the roads, along with the dust of their play // <s>MSpv</s> 3.30 //
Wishing to see, crowds of people went along the cross-streets toward the faultless slayer of <s>Mura</s>;

children.text: anekaśaḥ saṃstutamapyanalpā navaṃ navaṃ pratiraho karoti // MSpv_3.31 //
children.translated_text: though praised many times, great beauty ever makes itself seem new // <s>MSpv</s> 3.31 //
As people approached the road in unbroken streams, with breathless rows of armies,

children.text: rathasya tasyāṃ puri dattacakṣurvidvānvidāmāsa śanairna yātam // MSpv_3.32 //
children.translated_text: one who watched his chariot in that city with attentive eyes could barely discern that it moved slowly // <s>MSpv</s> 3.32 //
She who, making the quarters tawny, gleaming with the splendor of a golden rampart, amid the ocean,
burst through the water and leaped up, like a flame from fire emerging from the mouths of beautiful horse-faced ones // <s>MSpv</s> 3.33 //
She whose form was surrounded by ocean waters, established upon thousands of mountains,

children.text: anirvidā yā vidadhe vidhātrā pṛthivī pṛthivyāḥ pratiyātaneva // MSpv_3.34 //
children.translated_text: was fashioned without weariness by <s>Brahmā</s>—a counter-image, as it were, of the earth itself // <s>MSpv</s> 3.34 //
She was the limit of the expansion of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>'s skill, acquired through constant practice and mastery of all arts;
she appeared in the spotless mirror-surfaces of the waters like a reflection of the celestial ocean // <s>MSpv</s> 3.35 //
Of her who was given to the lord of the discus as a fresh bride, as if by her father,
the ocean lovingly bound garlands of jewels close to her limbs repeatedly // <s>MSpv</s> 3.36 //
Whose rampart, crowded with throngs of conch shells tossed up by the leaping waves of the restless ocean,
made even <s>Sumeru</s>, with its crests surrounded by celestial chariots moving around it, seem an imitation // <s>MSpv</s> 3.37 //
Where on the merchant roads, the ocean, robbing the jewels that were reflected with trembling rays
by waters arriving carried by currents, attained the status of a jewel-mine // <s>MSpv</s> 3.38 //
The ocean, having dropped heaps of soft gems, their luster veiled by foam,
seemed to spread out a bed for the sun to rest upon, with arms made of waves // <s>MSpv</s> 3.39 //
Whose mansion-peaks, in their aspiration to surpass, rose far above the ocean,
while the ocean's great waves, their ambitions thwarted, shrank back as if in shame when approaching near // <s>MSpv</s> 3.40 //
The rain-cloud, having approached swiftly out of curiosity, was suddenly blocked by the rampart wall;
it roared mightily outside her walls, raining torrents under the pretext of a downpour // <s>MSpv</s> 3.41 //
When <s>Apsarases</s>, desiring some distinguishing feature from the identical beauty of her women,

children.text: ārādhito 'ddhā manurapsarobhiścakre prajāḥ svāḥ sanimeṣacihnāḥ // MSpv_3.42 //
children.translated_text: worshipped <s>Manu</s>, he made his own offspring endowed with the mark of blinking // <s>MSpv</s> 3.42 //
With the nets of rays from the gleaming moon, concealing the rows of crystal pillars,

children.text: āruhya nāryaḥ kṣaṇadāsu yatra nabhogatā devya iva vyārājan // MSpv_3.43 //
children.translated_text: the women of that city, ascending them at night, appeared like celestial goddesses moving through the sky // <s>MSpv</s> 3.43 //
On the beautiful moonstone-paved floors of the palace terraces where
even the rain-clouds that fell from above were made to flow upward by the water-channels // <s>MSpv</s> 3.44 //
Where during lovemaking, wives, perceiving the lamps through lattice-windows from within the house,
were frightened by the moonbeam reflections on the <s>vaidūrya</s> gem walls, terrifying as cat's eyes // <s>MSpv</s> 3.45 //
Where in houses so exceedingly smooth that young men were unable to execute paintings,

children.text: cakruryuvānaḥ pratibimbitāṅgāḥ sajīvacitrā iva ratnabhittīḥ // MSpv_3.46 //
children.translated_text: they, with their bodies reflected, made the jeweled walls appear like living pictures // <s>MSpv</s> 3.46 //
Where on the golden pillars, the reflections of women's cheeks,

children.text: yasyāṃ kapolaiḥ kaladhautadhāmastambheṣu bheje maṇidarpaṇaśrīḥ // MSpv_3.47 //
children.translated_text: pale with love-sickness, arriving as if their own color-mates, attained the beauty of jeweled mirrors // <s>MSpv</s> 3.47 //
Where, on the thresholds of houses made of parrot-green and sapphire-blue gems, smeared with their luster,

children.text: yasyāmalindeṣu na cakrureva mugdhāṅganā gomayagomukhāni // MSpv_3.48 //
children.translated_text: innocent young women did not make auspicious cow-dung designs on the doorsteps // <s>MSpv</s> 3.48 //
Where houses, with the hanging tail-plumes of peacocks momentarily perched on the roof-beams,
shone as if adorned with thatched roofs charming with emerald-dark grass // <s>MSpv</s> 3.49 //
She who was splendid with houses broad yet with grand arched roofs, with canopies bound with garlands yet also with awnings,

children.text: reje vicitrairapi yā sacitraigṛhairviśālairapi bhūriśālai // MSpv_3.50 //
children.translated_text: variegated yet also having paintings, spacious yet also having many halls // <s>MSpv</s> 3.50 //
Where, out of a desire to pounce upon the rows of artificial birds in the pigeon-houses of dwellings,

children.text: mārjāramapyātaniścalāṅkaṃ yasyāṃ janaḥ kṛtrimameva mene // MSpv_3.51 //
children.translated_text: people considered even a real cat with motionless limbs to be artificial // <s>MSpv</s> 3.51 //
Where the women, though standing on the ground, with their lotus-faces put the moon to shame,
and he in vain climbed the palace peaks that surpassed the path of stars // <s>MSpv</s> 3.52 //

children.text: ramyā iti prāptavatīḥ patākā rāgaṃ viviktā iti vardhayantīḥ /
children.translated_text: Where young men courted the balconies equally with the brides—the balconies that had arrived at being "charming," that promoted "passion,"
and that had "bowing rows"—for the brides too were charming, passionate, and had bowing waistlines // <s>MSpv</s> 3.53 //
Where without any deliberate effort, fragrance is borne to delight men;
the honeys and the faces of beautiful women attained an interchange of their function of giving fragrance // <s>MSpv</s> 3.54 //
Where in the interiors of houses, between love-bouts, the flock of birds nesting in the balcony niches and ledges,
hearing the sounds, clearly became apprentices of the women // <s>MSpv</s> 3.55 //
Where, even when covered, the garments of women, upon their breast-circles more visible than the uncovered,

children.text: ākāśasāmyaṃ dadhurambarāṇi na nāmataḥ kevalamarthataḥ'pi // MSpv_3.56 //
children.translated_text: achieved equality with the sky—not merely in name but also in substance // <s>MSpv</s> 3.56 //
Where the straight, broad, long roads, whose boundaries the excessively extended ones never transgressed,
were called "well-mannered paths" in both senses, for the people too never stumbled upon them // <s>MSpv</s> 3.57 //
Where <s>Brahmā</s>, having created the city-women with mutually competing forms of surpassing beauty,
cleansed the blemish upon <s>Śrī</s>'s reputation of being the sole standard of comparison for beauty // <s>MSpv</s> 3.58 //
The wish-fulfilling trees within the heart bear the very fruit that is meditated upon;

children.text: adhyūṣuṣo yāmabhavañjanasya yāḥ sampadastā manaso 'pyagamyāḥ // MSpv_3.59 //
children.translated_text: the riches of those who dwelt in her were beyond even the mind's reach // <s>MSpv</s> 3.59 //
Bearing all arts in his own rays, illuminating the quarters with the whiteness of his mansions,

children.text: yāṃ revatījāniriyeṣa hātuṃ na rauhiṇīyo na ca rohiṇīśaḥ // MSpv_3.60 //
children.translated_text: the lord of <s>Revatī</s> wished to leave her—neither the son of <s>Rohiṇī</s> nor the lord of <s>Rohiṇī</s> did // <s>MSpv</s> 3.60 //
Having attained proximity to <s>Janārdana</s>, whose power of <s>Śambhu</s> was thwarted in the battle of arrows,

children.text: śarīriṇā jaitraśareṇa yatra niḥśaṅghamūṣe makaradhvajena // MSpv_3.61 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kāma</s>, the banner-bearer of the <s>makara</s>, dwelt there fearlessly, with his victorious arrow embodied // <s>MSpv</s> 3.61 //
Served by auspicious winds, inhabited by <s>Hari</s> for a long time,
she who surpassed <s>Amarāvatī</s> on <s>Meru</s>, in the ocean resplendent with rays of sprouting gems // <s>MSpv</s> 3.63 //
Of dark ointment-like luster, well-rounded, as if binding the eclipsed beauty of color,

children.text: viśeṣako vā viśiśeṣa yasyāḥ śriyantrilokītilakaḥ sa eva // MSpv_3.62 //
children.translated_text: the distinguishing mark—or rather what distinguished her <s>Śrī</s>—was he himself, the <s>tilaka</s> of the three worlds // <s>MSpv</s> 3.62 //
Gazing upon that city before him, he of incomparable valor reached the main avenue,
which, with the splendor of divine weapons blazing like <s>Vajra</s>'s radiance, was as unassailable by foes as <s>Devasenā</s> // <s>MSpv</s> 3.64 //
Like subjects from the lotus-naveled <s>Viṣṇu</s>, like waters from the crest of <s>Śambhu</s>'s matted locks,
like the <s>Vedas</s> from the mouth of <s>Brahmā</s>, the armies of the slayer of <s>Mura</s> issued forth from the city // <s>MSpv</s> 3.65 //
With horses pressing together, stumbling over each other's reins clashing at the meeting of their faces, restless,
their knees crushed against each other, the horse-troops passed through with difficulty // <s>MSpv</s> 3.66 //

children.text: nirantarāle 'pi vimucmāne dūraṃ pathi prāṇabhṛtāṃ gaṇena /
children.translated_text: Even though the way was cleared of people in between, on the road far ahead,
by those of great splendor, as darkness by lamps, it became unobstructed as if by islands of light // <s>MSpv</s> 3.67 //
The chariots were slowly brought down to earth from the descending path, without strain, by the elephants' toe-nails
with horses whose necks were curved forward, yoked to [chariots] with extended reins [held by] careful charioteers. (MŚpv 3.68)
With the waves of his army, the road-arms [streets] of her [<s>Dvārakā</s>], diminishing at every moment,
[seemed] like bangles; mostly, <s>Dvārakā</s> — you were not desired by any other than the discus-bearer (<s>Cakrapāṇi</s>), who departs. (MŚpv 3.69)
On the far shore of the ocean, the slayer of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Murāri</s>) saw heaps of dark-leaved [trees],
rows of forests, with the appearance of moss raised up every moment by thousands of budding flowers. (MŚpv 3.71)
The bearers of beauty, dwelling on the ocean shore, dark as rain-clouds, [like] the pair <s>Druma</s> and <s>Nāsa</s> —
joined with creeper-brides, he saw them ceaselessly, as if [they were] his own honored ones. (MŚpv 3.70)
Embracing the earth, resounding deeply, with tall waves like swaying banners,
foaming — that lord of rivers he suspected [to be] an epileptic in his raging. (MŚpv 3.72)
Having drunk greedily from the reservoir of waters, even in the swelling of itself, not reaching satiety,

children.text: kṣiptā ivendoḥ sa ruco 'dhivelaṃ muktāvalīrākalayāñcakāra // MSpv_3.73 //
children.translated_text: as if the rays of the moon were cast [into it] ceaselessly — it made strings of pearls. (MŚpv 3.73)
These [clouds], who will flood the earth completely, roaring constantly with fury —
he saw those waters of the ocean, gathered from one quarter, being drunk by the clouds. (MŚpv 3.74)
Having raised the very same water through clouds, like meanings properly conveyed by the foremost sages,
<s>Hari</s> beheld the rivers falling — like memory [falling] into the ocean. (MŚpv 3.75)
Having traded precious regional goods for excellent [merchandise], he, the obtainer of the finest gains,
welcomed the merchants on their ships with their considerable cargo returning from there. (MŚpv 3.76)
Desiring to leap up, with the exhalation-wind of the lord of rivers, exceedingly heavy,

children.text: payāṃsi bhaktyā garuḍadhvajasya dhvājānivoccikṣipire phaṇīndrāḥ // MSpv_3.77 //
children.translated_text: the lords of serpents raised the waters like banners, out of devotion to the one whose banner bears <s>Garuḍa</s>. (MŚpv 3.77)
Seeing him arrived — the friend of the end of an age (<s>Yuga</s>) — the ocean, whose pleasure is the lap-bed [of <s>Viṣṇu</s>],
rose up as if to greet [him], with wave-arms outstretched in great joy. (MŚpv 3.78)
The wind, carrying up droplets of water, wiped the ocean with its own leaves [wings];
as he traveled along the shore ceaselessly, the fragrance of the <s>melā</s>-creepers' blossoms struck [him]. (MŚpv 3.80)
With <s>ketakī</s> (screw-pine) flowers parted [as if in a hair-part] by the wind arising from the groves of tall <s>tāla</s> (palmyra) palms,

children.text: āsedire lāvaṇasaindhavīnāṃ camūcaraiḥ kacchabhuvāṃ pradeśāḥ // MSpv_3.79 //
children.translated_text: the coastal regions of the salt and <s>Sindhu</s> [seas] were reached by the army's scouts. (MŚpv 3.79)
Those [coastal people], wearing clove-garland ear-ornaments, drinking the water between coconut palms,
having tasted ginger and areca-nut, showed hospitality to him who had come from the sea. (MŚpv 3.81)

children.text: turagaśatākulasya paritaḥ paramekaturaṅgajanmanaḥ pramathitabhūbhṛtaḥ pratipathaṃ mathitasya bhṛśaṃ mahībhṛtā /
children.translated_text: Of [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], surrounded on all sides by hundreds of horses, born from the supreme single horse [<s>Uccaiḥśravas</s>], with [enemy] kings crushed, greatly churned on every path by the king [of mountains],

children.text: paricalataḥ balānujabalasya puraḥ satataṃ dhṛtaśriyaściravigataśriyo jalanidheśca tadābhavadadantaraṃ mahat // MSpv_3.82 //
children.translated_text: of the army of the younger brother of <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), proceeding before [him], constantly bearing prosperity — and of the ocean, long bereft of prosperity — the difference at that time became great. (MŚpv 3.82)
With the smoke of the exhalations, together with the splendor of gems upraised, as if the earth of the serpents [were rising],
he saw that mountain <s>Raivataka</s>, studded with diverse minerals of sapphire. (MŚpv 4.1)
Heavy rocks on all sides, above and above, with canopies of clouds

children.text: vindhyāyamānaṃ divasasya bhartumārgaṃ punā roddhumivonnamadbhiḥ // MSpv_4.2 //
children.translated_text: rising, as if striving to block again the path of the lord of day (<s>Sūrya</s>), vying with <s>Vindhya</s>. (MŚpv 4.2)
Traversed by charmingly darkened radiance, by creepers that invited swarms of bees —
resorted to by the charmingly dark rocks and creepers, [in turn] summoning bees. (MŚpv 4.3)

children.text: sahasrasaṃkhyair gaganaṃ pādair bhuvaṃ vyāpya vitiṣṭhamānam /
children.translated_text: Standing pervading the sky with a thousand feet and the earth,
[like] the golden-wombed one (<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the Sun) with the hot-rayed [sun] and the cool-rayed [moon] in place of eyes — excellent. (MŚpv 4.4)
In some places, pale white from the receding of waters, with the appearance of a washed upper garment,
bearing clouds, it resembled the enemy of <s>Smara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), his body smeared with ashes divided by limb-contacts. (MŚpv 4.5)
Providing shade for its own playfully languid women — the [peacocks], somewhat languid with passion,
doing so with the outspread feather-wings of birds [that were like] lotus-leaf-wings. (MŚpv 4.6)
With brilliant peacocks mounted on its shoulders — trees — with great serpent-lords clinging to their trunks,
causing many creeper-arms to dance at their tips — as if bearing many forms of <s>Rudra</s> (<s>Śiva</s>). (MŚpv 4.7)
With hanging blue-lotus ear-ornaments, with cheek-surfaces fair as <s>lodhra</s> [bark],
with the appearance of sandbanks adorned with fresh fruits of <s>Ulapāla</s> — bearing streams with pure water and moss. (MŚpv 4.8)
With bees restlessly [hovering over] rows of streaks [of flowers] and lotuses, dispelling heat with the shade of trees —
the beautiful-haired women of the gods, with tresses dark and lovely, it bore, [though] frightened by the <s>Rākṣasas</s>. (MŚpv 4.9)
For the delight of the slayer of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Murāri</s>), [peaks] brought by the immortals from <s>Sumeru</s> and added to its summits —
the descriptions of height and beauty by unbridled poets do not become false. (MŚpv 4.10)
From which, exceedingly precious [gems], borne on numerous, repeatedly elevated plateaus with high crests,
the world constantly took unlimited gems, as if from a wealthy merchant's shop. (MŚpv 4.11)
Though bearing a lotus-lake in which the sun of burning heat approaching from above was scorching,

children.text: bhṛṅgāvaliryasyataṭe nipītarasā namattāmarasā na mattā // MSpv_4.12 //
children.translated_text: the row of bees on its slope, having drunk the nectar, [found] the lotuses bowing — not intoxicated. (MŚpv 4.12)
Where, mounted on a tree with a thousand open flower-eyes, standing tall,
the silver-cheeked cliff performed the play of the great royal elephant presided over by the lord of the gods. (MŚpv 4.13)
By the elder brother of <s>Garuḍa</s>, of varied colors of <s>aguru</s> (aloe), with the rays of the sun all around, shining —

children.text: ratnaiḥ punaryatra rucaṃ svāmāninyire vaṃśakarīranīlaiḥ // MSpv_4.14 //
children.translated_text: the gems on that [mountain] again bore [their] own radiance, [like] bamboo-reeds dark with blue [light]. (MŚpv 4.14)
Where, by [fires that were] repeatedly released by the clouds, rising yet not rising —
the forest was troubled by the fire arising from the venom of the serpents — [fires] of extinguished serpents, not extinguished. (MŚpv 4.15)
With the sun-stones yielding [fire] from the touch of the hot-rayed [sun's] rays, emitting a slender radiance,
that [mountain] proclaimed, by the vessel-quality of its [stones], a transference of qualities surpassing the transferred qualities. (MŚpv 4.16)
Even though seen [before], that mountain repeatedly extended to the slayer of <s>Mura</s> a wonder as if unprecedented;
that which is not attained as 'new' in each moment — that alone is the true form of loveliness. (MŚpv 4.17)
Then, upon [the mountain] that bore slopes with bird-flocks resounding high, expert in pronunciation [of Vedic sounds] —

children.text: utkaṃ dharaṃ draṣṭumavekṣya śauriṇutkandharaṃ dāruka ityuvāca // MSpv_4.18 //
children.translated_text: observing [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], eager to see the mountain, <s>Dāruka</s> (the charioteer) raised his neck and said: (MŚpv 4.18)
'Having covered the vast sky above the earth, standing with its bold and broad peak,

children.text: mūrdhniskhalattuhinadīdhitikoṭimenam udvīkṣya ko bhuvi na vismayate nageśam // MSpv_4.19 //
children.translated_text: with the crescent moon-tip sliding on its crown — seeing this lord of mountains, who on earth is not astonished?' (MŚpv 4.19)
'When the wide-rayed sun rises, and when the cool-rayed moon sets,
this mountain bears the play of a lordly elephant garlanded by a pair of hanging garlands [sun and moon].' (MŚpv 4.20)

children.text: vahati yaḥ paritaḥ kanakasthalīḥ saharitā lasamānanavāṃśukaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who bears golden plateaus all around, with [new-green] garments shining alongside the green [vegetation],
this mountain shines among mountains like <s>Bhava</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), with garments [the color of] fresh orpiment.' (MŚpv 4.21)
'Those seated on the slopes here, in the western part, see the dense net of rays, calm and spotless,
of the moon — [resembling] the mirror obtained at the full [moon] by a woman — like a deer resting in its [the mountain's] lap.' (MŚpv 4.22)
'Having placed a non-male foot high upon the heads of the crags — for the <s>Bhṛgu</s>-sages —
the torrents of waterfalls, rising to the sky, render [the mountain] an ornament-washing for the bodies of heaven's love-afflicted women.' (MŚpv 4.23)
'These clouds, whose sounds allay the distress of <s>cātaka</s> birds, with lightning resembling a beloved's flash of gold —

children.text: jagatīrihasphuritacārucāmīkarāḥ savituḥ kacitkapiśayanti cāmī karāḥ // MSpv_4.24 //
children.translated_text: the rays of the sun here, displayed beautifully golden, make the regions tawny — these hands [of the sun] do [so].' (MŚpv 4.24)
'Propped up by the raised, uplifted white-rayed constellations on its high heads,
clearly the sky falls on its slopes everywhere, on the pretext of waterfall-streams.' (MŚpv 4.25)
'In one place, the waters are split by the rays of crystal cliffs — transparent; elsewhere, the waters are hard to [distinguish], broken by the gleam of sapphires —

children.text: kālindījalajanitaśriyaḥ śrayante vaidagdhīmiha saritaḥ surāpagāyāḥ // MSpv_4.26 //
children.translated_text: the rivers here assume the beauty born of the waters of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā) — the cleverness of the celestial <s>Gaṅgā</s>.' (MŚpv 4.26)
'Here and there on this [mountain] shine [beings] with affection equal to that of <s>Meru</s>'s jeweled peaks —

children.text: striyaśaca patyau surasundarībhiḥ samā navapremaṇisānurāgāḥ // MSpv_4.27 //
children.translated_text: women too, with their lord — equal in fresh love-jeweled affection to the divine beauties.' (MŚpv 4.27)
'This [mountain], highly adorned with rows of great silver [minerals], its surface of poor color [elsewhere] here [becomes] dense nectar-colored —
it assumes the beauty of the forehead of the enemy of <s>Smara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), pallid with ash, [adorned with] the ornament of the fire-eye.' (MŚpv 4.28)
'This [mountain] bears exceedingly aged, heavily massive, deeply pendulous cloud-breasted slopes —
of unattainable beauty always, like ripe female directional elephants.' (MŚpv 4.29)

children.text: dhūmākāraṃ dadhati puraḥ sauvarṇe varṇenāgneḥ sadṛśi taṭe paśyāmī /
children.translated_text: 'Behold! On the golden slope, of a color resembling fire, bearing a smoke-like appearance before [it] —

children.text: śyāmībhūtāḥ kusumasamūho 'līnāṃ līnāmālīmiha taravo bibhrāṇāḥ // MSpv_4.30 //
children.translated_text: trees bearing dark clusters of flowers [and] clinging rows of bees, as if wearing a garland of bees.' (MŚpv 4.30)
'Spreading sky-touching walls of gold, with the tawny luster of <s>campaka</s> flowers in full bloom —
by this [mountain], possessing the hip-beauty of <s>Meru</s>'s daughter, this <s>Bhārata</s>-land shines as if [it were] <s>Ilāvṛta</s>.' (MŚpv 4.31)
'With beautiful, colorfully barked trees, surrounded on all sides by swaying <s>priyaka</s>-groves,
this [mountain] shines with jeweled limbs, as if its body-parts had attained the power of movement.' (MŚpv 4.32)
'Here, the women of the water-abodes delight with lotuses, with cries resembling young elephants;
and it is sung by hosts of <s>Siddhas</s> (accomplished beings), with women, in sweetly youthful voices.' (MŚpv 4.33)
'Here, for the lord [Sun] who was seized by darkness from the decree of <s>Niyater</s> (Fate), who desires again the time of departure,
the great herbs bear the position of a wife — a place not overpowered by others.' (MŚpv 4.34)
'Here, the creepers, with young-coral-[colored] hands resting on the trunks of forest lords, [look] like young women;
or with half-opened bud-eyes, surrounded by swarms of bees, [performing] their vows.' (MŚpv 4.35)
'The birds here, fragrant with <s>kadamba</s> blossoms, make the cows musical, every moment, in many a melody;
and the wind, shaking the fresh <s>nīpa</s> groves, wanders constantly, never wandering [astray].' (MŚpv 4.36)
'Though heard and somehow explained by the learned ones, experts in scripture, [it remains] hard to grasp for others of uncertain intellect —

children.text: śreyāndvijātiriva hantumaghāni dakṣaṃ gūṭhārthameṣa nidhimantragaṇaṃ bibharti // MSpv_4.37 //
children.translated_text: this [mountain] bears a collection of hidden-meaning treasure-mantras, like the twice-born, capable of destroying sins, better [than all].' (MŚpv 4.37)

children.text: bimboṣṭhaṃ bahu manute turaṅgavaktraś cumbantaṃ mukhamiha kiṃnaraṃ priyāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The horse-faced <s>Kinnaras</s> here prize greatly [their] <s>bimba</s>-[fruit-red] lips, kissing the face of the beloved;
another [<s>Kinnara</s>] too, repeatedly embracing her — his own wife, whose waist is fearful of the burden of her high breasts.' (MŚpv 4.38)
'That which shines along the slopes of this [mountain] is a forest with innumerable <s>tamāla</s> trees and palms;
