children.text: na puṣpitātra sthagitārkarasmāvanāntatāne katamā latālam // MSpv_4.39 //
children.translated_text: among the blossoming [creepers] here, concealing the sun's rays — which creeper in the endless [forest] has not bloomed?' (MŚpv 4.39)
'With teeth gleaming, with girdles ending in pure gems, with fine-jeweled bracelets, with broad hips,
women with dense, smooth, cliff-like cheeks dwell fittingly on the plateaus of this [mountain].' (MŚpv 4.40)
'Resembling water recently abandoned by clouds, [yet] appearing as if of long-standing luminous rise —

children.text: viralavikīrṇavajraśakalā sakalām iha vidadhāti dhautakaladhautamahī // MSpv_4.41 //
children.translated_text: with scattered diamond-fragments, the washed golden earth here presents a complete [imitation].' (MŚpv 4.41)

children.text: varjayantyā janaiḥ saṃgamekāntatas tarkayantyā sukhaṃ saṅgame kāntataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Avoiding the company of [ordinary] people exclusively, imagining happiness in the company of [her] beloved only —
this [mountain] is served by many a woman with <s>Smara</s>-subdued side-glances, with bowed limbs.' (MŚpv 4.42)
The yak-cows, with minds anxious from stumbling, their single tail-hairs caught in the dense <s>kīcaka</s> bamboo groves,
do not venture to move here, as if [reluctant to leave] the pleasant sound of the wind's breath [blowing] through those hollow reeds. // MSpv 4.43 //
Here, the water, pearl-white like milk released by clouds, submerged within pools of great blue lotuses,
swiftly assumes the clear reflection of indigo-dye water, through the dark-as-blades rays. // MSpv 4.44 //

children.text: yā na yayau priyamanyavadhūbhyaḥ sāratarāgamanā yatamānam /
children.translated_text: She who did not go in love to another from [among] the co-wives, of most essential passion's course, despite [his] striving—

children.text: tena saheta bibharti rasaḥ strī sā ratarāgamanāyatānām // MSpv_4.45 //
children.translated_text: she, the passionate woman, bears the [enduring] sentiment, of the extended passion's course, of those [suitors]. // MSpv 4.45 //
Here, when the moon's rays, split by gem-radiances into high and low beams, approach a thousandfold [multiplication],

children.text: doṣāpi nūnamahimāṃśurasau kileti vyākośakokanadatāṃ dadhate nalinyaḥ // MSpv_4.46 //
children.translated_text: the lotus-pools open their day-lotuses, [thinking], 'Surely this one too is the Radiant One (the Sun), though without rays!' // MSpv 4.46 //
The young ones, accustomed to rolling fearlessly in [their parents'] laps, run forward to meet their father [returning];

children.text: anuroditīva karuṇena pattriṇāṃ virutena vatsalatayayaiṣa nimnagāḥ // MSpv_4.47 //
children.translated_text: while the rivers seem to weep, as if with the piteous cry of birds. // MSpv 4.47 //
Bearing rows of trees whose branches are bent down by bees, with branches bending low,
the riverbank gleams tawny, with the shedding pollen of its fully-ripe creepers. // MSpv 4.48 //
In the foothills to the east, the water falling from before, ornamented like the trunk of a great lordly elephant,
is seen pierced by various gem-rays, beautiful like <s>Indra</s>'s bow stretched upward. // MSpv 4.49 //
These mountain peaks, bearing peacock-crests, with garlands of long dangling tail-feathers,
appear as if garlanded with the blossoming flowers of the various wish-fulfilling trees. // MSpv 4.50 //
Happy with their wives on this [mountain], continually [enjoying] the delight of <s>Mandāra</s> flowers resembling celestial lotuses,
the gods, resembling celestial lotuses from <s>Mandāra</s>, continually do not attend to relishing [this place]. // MSpv 4.51 //
Covering a great canopy of flowers within, with cloud-layers resembling the necks of house-pigeons,

children.text: śasvaṅgāni dhūmarucimāguravīṃ dadhānair dhūpāyatīva paṭalairnīradānām // MSpv_4.52 //
children.translated_text: bearing the dusky luster of <s>aguru</s> (aloewood) incense, [the mountain] seems to fumigate itself. // MSpv 4.52 //
With varied rays from newly-born gems, beautiful in their mutual interplay,
it creates upon this [mountain] an amazed celestial assembly—a wall-less painting in the sky. // MSpv 4.53 //
Cool with breezes, dwelling well on the head, with curtains [of clouds] for those dwelling happily in the caves,
[the mountain] bears white cloud-rows that produce joy in the waters, free from impurity. // MSpv 4.54 //

Those who know the mental purification of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and the other [<s>brahmavihāras</s>], having accomplished the removal of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), having attained <s>sabīja-yoga</s> (meditation with seed),

children.text: khyātiṃ casattvapuruṣānyatayādhigamya vāñcanti tāmapi samādhibhṛtaḥ niroddhum // MSpv_4.55 //
children.translated_text: and having realized the distinction between <s>sattva</s> (consciousness) and <s>puruṣa</s> (Self), desire to restrain even that [distinction] through <s>samādhi</s> (absorption). // MSpv 4.55 //
On the emerald-like grounds, the rays of the sun falling through gaps in the tree-branches
impart here the beauty of the bowed blue-throated peacock's throat, with trembling motes of dust. // MSpv 4.56 //
She who bears a beauty surpassing the sound of the delicate <s>vallakī</s> (lute) strings, with excessive dark splendor—

children.text: nātra kāntamupagītayā tayā svānamānamati kālimālayā // MSpv_4.57 //
children.translated_text: here, by her who sings to her beloved, the beauty does not surpass the excess of dark splendor. // MSpv 4.57 //
In the evening, the ramparts, anointed with streams from moonstone melted by moonbeams,

children.text: arkopalollasitavahnibhirahni taptās tīvraṃ mahāvratamivātra caranati vaprāḥ // MSpv_4.58 //
children.translated_text: and scorched by day with fires kindled by sunstone, seem to perform a severe great vow here. // MSpv 4.58 //

children.text: etasminnadhikapayaḥśriyaṃ vahantyaḥ saṃkṣobhaṃ pavanabhuvā javena nītāḥ /
children.translated_text: In this [mountain], the great lakes, bearing the glory of abundant waters, swiftly agitated by the wind's son,

children.text: vālmīkerarahitarāmalakṣmaṇānāṃ sādharmyaṃ dadhati girāṃ mahāsarasyaḥ // MSpv_4.59 //
children.translated_text: attain the likeness of the words of <s>Vālmīki</s>, without <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>. // MSpv 4.59 //

children.text: iha muhurmuditaiḥ kalabhai ravaḥ pratidiśaṃ kriyate kalabhairavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, by joyful young elephants, the sound is made in every direction—a terrible [roar like] <s>Kalabhairava</s>;

children.text: sphurati cānuvanaṃ camarīcayaḥ kanakaratnabhuvāṃ ca marīcayaḥ // MSpv_4.60 //
children.translated_text: and in every forest, herds of yak-cows glitter, and rays [glitter] from birthplaces of gold and gems. // MSpv 4.60 //
In this [mountain], the wind, having obtained its song by filling the hollows of bark and reeds,

children.text: kastūrikāmṛgavimardasugandhireti rāgīva saktimadhikāṃ viṣayeṣu vāyuḥ // MSpv_4.61 //
children.translated_text: fragrant with the scent of rubbing against musk-deer, with body brushing their soft eyelashes, passes like a lover with excessive attachment to sense-objects. // MSpv 4.61 //

children.text: prītyai yūnāṃ vyavahitatapanāḥ prauḍhadvāntaṃ dinamiha jaladāḥ /
children.translated_text: For the delight of young couples, the rain-clouds here, hiding the sun, make the day deeply dark—
creating another night, [themselves being] skilled in relieving the fatigue and weariness of love-play. // MSpv 4.62 //

children.text: bhagne nivāso 'yamihāsya puṣpaiḥ sadānataḥ yena viṣāṇi nāgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the serpent, before whom [all] always bow, by whose flowers [his] dwelling is shattered,

children.text: tīvrāṇi tenojjhati kopito 'sau sasānatoyena viṣāṇi nāgaḥ // MSpv_4.63 //
children.translated_text: abandons even fierce poisons when angered—that serpent, by water mixed with poisons. // MSpv 4.63 //
Even the Lord (<s>Śiva</s>), the master of the cool, snowy mountain, rests here covered with a thick bearskin garment;

children.text: sarvartunivṛttikare nivasannupaiti na dvandvaduḥkhamiha kiñcidakiñcano 'pi // MSpv_4.64 //
children.translated_text: dwelling in a place that removes [the effects of] all seasons, even the possessionless one suffers no discomfort from the pairs of opposites. // MSpv 4.64 //
This mountain, with dark streaks like lines of young elephant-forest-paintings, fair [in hue],
with the crystal-bracelet ground performing a dance, with white ash-paste body-adornments of a serpent-girdled one, assumes the appearance of the Trident-bearer (<s>Śiva</s>). // MSpv 4.65 //
With fully-blooming water-lotuses of golden hue on both banks, their daytime fatigue dispelled, made lustrous by golden <s>jambū</s> fruits,

children.text: niṣevya madhu mādhavāḥ sarasamatra kādambaraṃ haranti rataye rahaḥ priyatamāṅgakādambaram // MSpv_4.66 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Mādhava</s> bees, having savored honey, relish the <s>kādambara</s> (mead) here, and carry off for pleasure in secret the embrace of their beloved's limbs, surrounded by <s>kadamba</s> [flowers]. // MSpv 4.66 //

children.text: darpaṇanirmalāsu patite ghanatimiramuṣi jyotiṣi raupyabhittiṣu puraḥ pratiphalati muhuḥ /
children.translated_text: When the radiance that steals dense darkness falls upon the mirror-clear silver walls, reflecting again and again before [them],

children.text: vrīḍamasaṃṃmukho 'pi ramaṇairapahṛtavasanāḥ khāñcanakandarāsu taruṇīriha nayati raviḥ // MSpv_4.67 //
children.translated_text: the sun brings modesty to young women here, even when not face-to-face with their lovers, [appearing] undressed in the golden caves. // MSpv 4.67 //
When you approach, adorned with glories that imitate its peak-clusters, this mountain seems to rise eagerly and high,
with dark-as-<s>Baladeva</s>'s-garment rain-clouds, swiftly driven upward by quick winds, rising playfully. // MSpv 4.68 //

children.text: itthaṃ vyalīkāḥ priyatamā iva so 'vyalīkaḥ śuśrāva sūtatanayasya tadā vyalīkāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, the son of the charioteer (<s>Dāruka</s>) recounted artful [praises] of the mountain, like false beloved ones, to him (Kṛṣṇa) who was artless;

children.text: rantuṃ nirantaramiyeṣa tato 'vasāne tāsāṃ girau ca vanarājipaṭaṃ vasāne // MSpv_5.1 //
children.translated_text: he then desired to sport unceasingly, in the end, on that mountain wearing its garment of forest-rows. // MSpv 5.1 //
That mountain, with peaks matchlessly lofty like great elephants, with soaring rows of banana-tree groves rising high—
the massive army, bearing the fortune of a rival mountain, blocking the earth's expanse, marched toward [it] and the mountain trembled. // MSpv 5.2 //
Within the sky, brilliant with the interplay of [sun]rays, as if bashful at the sight of the multitude,
the earth's dust, raised by the army, spreading in the air, tawny as a young camel's neck, covered [them]. // MSpv 5.3 //
The horses, spiraling, endowed with auspicious-fruit-giving whorls, bearing gem-ornaments filling [their] openings,

children.text: aśvāḥ pyadhurvasumatīmatirocamānās tūrṇaṃ payodhaya ivormibhirāpatatantaḥ // MSpv_5.4 //
children.translated_text: exceedingly radiant, struck the earth swiftly, like oceans rushing with waves. // MSpv 5.4 //

children.text: ārakṣamagnamavamatya sṛṇiṃ śitāgram ekaḥ palāyata javena kṛtārtanādaḥ /
children.translated_text: One [elephant], despising the goad sunk to its guard-ring, the sharp-pointed [goad], fled with great speed, making a cry of distress;
another, repeatedly leaping up, [trying to] arrest its weight—alas!—an elephant and a camel feared each other on the road. // MSpv 5.5 //
The people watched the horse going wearily, with restless fore-hooves, beautiful with its raised <s>cāmara</s> (fly-whisk) [tail];

children.text: nāgaṃ punarmṛdu salīlanimīlitākṣaṃ sarvaḥprayaḥ khalu bhavatayanurūpaceṣṭaḥ // MSpv_5.6 //
children.translated_text: while the elephant [went] gently, playfully half-closing its eyes—truly, every being acts in accordance with its nature. // MSpv 5.6 //
Then a frightened donkey, causing laughter among all people, made a violent leap from [near] a female elephant;
until a woman of the royal harem fell, her garment slipping from her swaying, unsteady-seated hips. // MSpv 5.7 //
Filled with dust from stones crushed on hard rock-surfaces by chariot-wheel rims falling on mountain obstacles,
the clouds of dust in the sky, joined with gathered rain-clouds, spread forth with a dusky-purple glow like <s>cakravāka</s> feathers. // MSpv 5.8 //
On the paths of the mountainside, strewn with stone slabs fallen from the earth-surface by the impact of the gods' [chariots], with rising sparks of fire,

children.text: parntavartmasu vcakramire mahāśvāḥ śailasya dardurapuṭāniva vādayantaḥ // MSpv_5.9 //
children.translated_text: the great horses trod, as if playing upon the rocky frog-bellied drums of the mountain. // MSpv 5.9 //
Controlled by a machine that maintained equilibrium in checking the force, properly harnessed with discrimination of three whips,
the Persian [horse] wonderfully made [its] step with a fierce, harsh fall from on high, through a half-gallop of great force. // MSpv 5.10 //
Making the eyelash-lines of young women's eyes appear doubly dense, soiled with frost-nets,

children.text: kṣuṇṇaḥ kṣaṇaṃ yadubalairdivamātitāṃsuḥ pāṃśurdisāṃ mukhamatutthayadutthito 'dreḥ // MSpv_5.11 //
children.translated_text: the dust, trampled by the <s>Yadu</s> forces for a moment, rose from the mountain and surpassed the sky, blocking the faces of the directions. // MSpv 5.11 //

children.text: ucchidya vidviṣa iva prasrabhaṃ mṛgendrān indrānujācarabhūtapatayo 'dhyavātsuḥ /
children.translated_text: Violently driving away lions as if they were enemies, the attendant lords of <s>Indra</s>'s younger brother (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) entered
the cave-dwellings, brilliant with scattered pearls from the claws dug into the heads of wild elephants. // MSpv 5.12 //
Some followed <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) with peacock-feathered crests bearing thick <s>yāvaka</s> (saffron) paste, tawny,
others with the flagstaff bearing the <s>Garuḍa</s> emblem, with a restless serpent bitten at the beak-tip as banner. // MSpv 5.13 //

children.text: chāyāmapāsya mahatīmapi vartamānām āgāminīṃ jagṛhire janatāsrūṇām /
children.translated_text: People abandoned even the great shade that was presently available and grasped [instead] the shade that was yet to come, of parasols;
for indeed, everyone resorts to a growing shelter, even if diminishing, rather than one that has arrived [but is passing]. // MSpv 5.14 //
As the vanguard, occupying a charming camp-site, was in confusion, driving away the rushing soldiers—

children.text: yānto 'nyataḥ plutakṛtasvaramāśu dūrād udbāhunā juhuvavire muhurātmavargyāḥ // MSpv_5.15 //
children.translated_text: those going elsewhere, with arms raised, calling out loudly from afar with leaping, improvised voices, repeatedly summoned their own retinue. // MSpv 5.15 //
The forest trees, as if sprinkled with nectar, then dispelled people's weariness;
beautiful with garments and ornaments hung upon their branches, they shone together with the wish-fulfilling trees bearing various fruits. // MSpv 5.16 //
The queens, being helped down from their carriages by attendants, with their <s>sauvidalla</s> (chamberlain) attendants agitated by the gaze of men,
their veiling cloths slipping, their curving beauty momentarily visible, were watched with fearful curiosity. // MSpv 5.17 //
Those appointed to help the newly-wed women of the royal harem dismount from their horses, their soft creeper-like arms clinging to [the horses'] necks—

children.text: āliṅganānyadhikṛtāḥ sphuṭamāpureva gaṇḍasthalīḥ śucitayā na cucumburāsām // MSpv_5.18 //
children.translated_text: they clearly obtained embraces, yet did not kiss their cheeks, out of propriety. // MSpv 5.18 //
Seeing the loosened hair of a young woman, with its heavy braid-ornaments fallen down and scattered,

children.text: prādudruvatsapadi candrakavāndrumāgrāt saṃgharṣiṇā saha guṇābhyadhikairdurāpam // MSpv_5.19 //
children.translated_text: a peacock immediately darted from the treetop, along with [its] rivals of superior qualities—[thinking it] an unattainable [tail]. // MSpv 5.19 //
With directions tinged golden by the rays of bright golden heaps, with bamboo flagpoles scratching the cloud-masses,

children.text: bhūbharturāyata nirantarasaṃnivṛṣṭāḥ pādā ivābhivabhurāvalayo rathānām // MSpv_5.20 //
children.translated_text: the rows of chariots of the earth's lord continuously assembled, like the feet [of a great being], tall. // MSpv 5.20 //
With shade-providing [tents], retaining their glory of beauty, towering high, with dense red mineral-color [decorations],
the encampments shone, even with [mere] cloth coverings of the princes, with elephants making noble star-row patterns. // MSpv 5.21 //
In the tent-chambers, on beds natural with <s>dūrvā</s> grass coverings, hidden behind drawn curtain-ends,

children.text: durvāpratānasahajāstaraṇeṣu bheje nidrasukhaṃ vasanasadmasu rājadāraiḥ // MSpv_5.22 //
children.translated_text: the royal women enjoyed the pleasure of sleep, their fatigue-sweat cooled by the breeze. // MSpv 5.22 //
Removing her bodice, stuck to her body with distinctive sweat-moisture, scratched by broken nails,
revealing the roots of her arms with forest-like breasts, the slender-waisted [woman] became a momentary festival for young men's eyes. // MSpv 5.23 //

children.text: yāvatsa eva samayaḥ samameva tāvad avyākulāḥ paṭamayānyabhito vitatya /
children.translated_text: At that very same time, simultaneously, calmly spreading their cloth [awnings] all around,
the merchants divided up their market-stalls, sufficient for the trading populace, full of priceless wares with counted prices. // MSpv 5.24 //
Pierced all around by clods of moist clay thrown with great effort for small purpose, rising up,
others quickly emerged from the midst of reed-hut roofs, collecting no small [amount of] thread. // MSpv 5.25 //

children.text: trāsākulaḥ paripatanparito niketān puṃbhirna kaiścidapi dhanvabhiranvabandhi /
children.translated_text: Fleeing in panic, running around the dwellings, not caught by any bowmen—

children.text: tasthau tathāpi na mṛgaḥ kvacidaṅganānām ākarṇapūrṇanayaneṣuhatekṣaṇaśrīḥ // MSpv_5.26 //
children.translated_text: Yet nowhere did the deer stand still — with the beauty of its glance slain by the eyes of the women, drawn to the ears [in sidelong glances]. // MSpv_5.26 //
The hospitality-folk, with beds spread and lodgings arranged in an instant, desiring to perform the new rites of welcome,
received the weary yet unwearied-minded men arriving, with courtesies as if long-established. // MSpv_5.27 //
They bathed in water, drank, washed their garments, ate lotus-stalks; [the women,] holding blossoming flowers,
the army-women wiped away the reproach of purposelessness against the enjoyment of the beauty of the river-women's limbs. // MSpv_5.28 //
The waters, their currents captured by the deep navel-pools, dammed by the broad hip-embankments of the women,
flowed slowly, stumbling against the high shore-like breasts — with the pleasant sound of <s>jalamūḍḍaka</s> (water-splashing). // MSpv_5.29 //
The elephant-stables were repeatedly sprinkled on all sides with showers of water from the waving trunk-tips;
as if with clusters of gems [swaying] on the heads of those [elephants] whose heat was drawn out by their panting, as their perspiration subsided. // MSpv_5.30 //
Those birds that first went to the ocean, and those whose wings were clipped by the thunderbolt-weapon in <s>Indra's</s> hand —
the mountain-lords came to plunge into the lakes, under the pretext of army-elephants whose banners and blankets had been thrown off. // MSpv_5.31 //

children.text: ātmānameva jaladheḥ pratibimbitāṅgam ūrmau mahatyabhimukhāpātitaṃ nirīkṣya /
children.translated_text: Seeing its own reflection in a great wave of the sea — its own image cast facing it —
in anger, a great elephant charged fearlessly to strike it, thinking it was another elephant attacking — how fitting! // MSpv_5.32 //
Unable to drink the rut-water released by another elephant, which was bitter, yet unwilling to leave the water though it shook off its goad,

children.text: ruddhe gajena saritaḥ saruṣāvatāre riktodapātrakaramāsta ciraṃ janaughaḥ // MSpv_5.33 //
children.translated_text: when the elephant blocked the angry descent to the river, the crowd of people stood long with their water-vessels empty. // MSpv_5.33 //

children.text: panthānamāśu vijahīhi puraḥ stanau te paśyanpratidvaradakumbhaviśaṅgicetāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Leave the path quickly! Before you, seeing her breasts, your mind wavering between them and the rival frontal globes of elephants' —

children.text: stamberamaḥ pāriṇinaṃsurāvupaiti ṣiṅgairagadyata sasaṃbhramameva kācit // MSpv_5.34 //
children.translated_text: a certain woman was addressed in great haste by the lowing elephant-bull approaching her husband. // MSpv_5.34 //
The water that was slowly poured along the temple-cheeks of many elephants, deeply plunged in for the relief of the heat of rut,
spraying up to the ears, gleaming like blossoming <s>kāśa</s> (silver-grass), attained the likeness of a white <s>cāmara</s> (fly-whisk). // MSpv_5.35 //
By the elephant that had expelled a mouthful of water in anger — having obtained the wind [of breath] from another elephant —
the water fell upon the dam of the ocean, its broad current checked by the dam-like portion of the reflected image, its rushing pestle-force stemmed. // MSpv_5.36 //
Even when the waters suddenly rise, given by the rut-fluid, who, with the means of crossing available, would try to remain?

children.text: yaddantinaḥ kaṭakaṭāhataṭānmimaṅkṣor maṅkṣūdapāti paritaḥ paṭalairasīnām // MSpv_5.37 //
children.translated_text: For from the elephant desiring to descend by the temple-pot banks, with the clatter of sword-clusters, the water cascades around in sheets at once. // MSpv_5.37 //
The elephant submerged within the mass of water — its temples below — for a moment, the swarms of bees, [like] the blue color having gone separately,

children.text: dravyaśrayeṣvapi gaṇeṣu rarāja nīlo varṇaḥ pṛthaggata ivāligaṇo gajasya // MSpv_5.38 //
children.translated_text: spreading their wings in the sky, shone in the groups [of bees] that depend on material supports — like the dark color detached from the elephant. // MSpv_5.38 //
With the red ochre-colored particles floating in the water, and with the lotus-pollen-juice clinging to their bodies,
the river and the great elephant, having enjoyed the play of sporting, performed as it were an exchange of garments. // MSpv_5.39 //

children.text: yāṃ candrakairmadajalasya mahānadīnāṃ netraśriyaṃ vikasato vidadhurgajendrāḥ /
children.translated_text: The splendor of the eyes of the great rivers, which the elephant-lords, with the eye-like circles of rut-water, had given while blooming,
they received back without delay upon emerging — through the garments of fresh blue lotuses clinging to their washed bodies. // MSpv_5.40 //
The [blood] of a rival elephant, flowing from the wound deeply pierced by the sharp goad, dripping as it moved,

children.text: roddhuṃ mahebhaparivraḍhimānamāgād ākrantito na vaśameti mahānparasya // MSpv_5.41 //
children.translated_text: came [to be checked] by the pride of the great elephant's strength; what is seized by force does not come under the control of another, however great. // MSpv_5.41 //
Though to be attended to with gentle caressing, the tree, perfumed by the rut-exudation of the wild elephant,

children.text: nābhāji kevalamabhāji gajena śākhī nānyasya gandhamapi mānabhataḥ sahante // MSpv_5.42 //
children.translated_text: was not merely visited but was broken by the [tame] elephant; the proud do not endure even another's scent. // MSpv_5.42 //
Of the forest tree that was rubbed by the temple-rub of the wild elephant roaming in mountain-groves, from whose rut-water [flowed down] —

children.text: senāgajena mathitasya nijaprasūnair mamle yathāgatamagāmi kulairalīnām // MSpv_5.43 //
children.translated_text: and was then crushed by the army-elephant, its own flowers [were dislodged] — the bee-swarms returned as they had come, by their families. // MSpv_5.43 //
When the elephants did not stand tall under the tree-canopies, then the riders directed them to the large root-branches;

children.text: bandhāya cicchiduribhāstarasātmanaiva naivātmanīnamatha vā kriyate madāndhaiḥ // MSpv_5.44 //
children.translated_text: the elephants tore [branches] to bind [themselves] by their own swiftness — or rather, what is not done by those blinded with rut? // MSpv_5.44 //
Those [elephants], hot, emitting hot moisture, of powerful internal heat, whose appearance resembled the interior of fully bloomed blue lotuses,
the men tied them, [all but] unable to be restrained, to <s>haricandana</s> (yellow sandalwood) [trees], on whose single-side [stood] towering heads. // MSpv_5.45 //

children.text: kaṇḍūyataḥ kaṭubhuvaṃ kariṇo madena skandhaṃ sugandhimanulīnavatā nagasya /
children.translated_text: When the elephant, scratching his sharp temple with rut-fluid, [rubbed against] the fragrant shoulder of the tree that he had leaned upon,
his neck received the quality of being a garland — through a soft necklace-like ring of massive lapis lazuli fragments. // MSpv_5.46 //
The driver, with a sequence of cajoling and threatening, gradually,

children.text: śikṣāvaśena śanakairvaśamānināya śāśtraṃ hi niścitadhiyāṃ kva na siddhameti // MSpv_5.47 //
children.translated_text: brought the leaping young one — even though having shaken off the rod — under control through disciplinary training; for where does the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise/goad) not succeed for those of determined minds? // MSpv_5.47 //

children.text: stambhaṃ mahāntamucitaṃ sahasā mumoca dānaṃ dadāvatitarāṃ sarasāgrahastaḥ /
children.translated_text: He suddenly released a great pillar; the elephant-king, whose trunk-tip was moist with excess rut-water, giving copiously,

children.text: baddhaparāṇi parito nigaḍāneyalāvīt svātantryamujvalamavāpa kareṇurājaḥ // MSpv_5.48 //
children.translated_text: loosened the fetters bound around [him] on all sides and attained brilliant freedom. // MSpv_5.48 //
It was recognized by the people, with half-closed eyes, even without taking [the food] —

children.text: gambhīravedini puraḥ kavalaṃ karīndre mando 'pi nāma na mahānavagṛhya sādhyaḥ // MSpv_5.49 //
children.translated_text: with the harsh urgings of the agitated elephant-keeper, the lord of elephants, deep-feeling, took the morsel in front; even a dull one is not manageable without understanding the great. // MSpv_5.49 //

children.text: kṣiptaṃ puro na jagṛhe muhurikṣukāṇḍaṃ nāpekṣate sma nikaṭopagatāṃ kareṇuṃ /
children.translated_text: The lord of elephants did not take the sugarcane stalk placed before him again and again, nor did he regard the cow-elephant that had approached nearby;
with half-closed eyes, he remembered the free roaming, the forest-dwelling, the great festivities of desire. // MSpv_5.50 //
With difficulty, the keeper was able to make the king of elephants eat and sleep, showing indifference to one of towering front-body and unyielding mind;
the love-oozing food-ball given by the raised palm bathed his tusk in its flowing oil. // MSpv_5.51 //
The palaces of kings, constructed with white-rayed [moonstones], with unbroken rays spread [throughout],
topped by the elephant-stable semicircles in crescent-moon shapes, appeared as if encircled by dark cloud-rows. // MSpv_5.52 //

children.text: gatyūnamargagatayo 'pi gatorumārgāḥ svairaṃ samācakṛṣire bhuvi vellanāya /
children.translated_text: Though going on paths too narrow for their gait, yet having traversed broad paths, the horses
freely pulled about on the ground for their exercise — their hoof-tracks traceable by the froth-water flowing from their pride-induced excitement. // MSpv_5.53 //
When the horse from <s>Bāhlīka</s> (Balkh) sniffed at [a man's] bowed head, the earth's dust,

children.text: nāsāvirokapavanollasitaṃ tanīyo romāñcatāmiva jagāma rajaḥ pṛthivyāḥ // MSpv_5.54 //
children.translated_text: stirred by the nose-breeze of [the mare] eager to experience the pleasure of union with that [stallion's] limbs, rose finer, as if into goosebumps. // MSpv_5.54 //

children.text: hemnaḥ sthalīṣu paritaḥ parivṛtya vājī dhunvanvapuḥ pravitatāyatakeśapaṅktiḥ /
children.translated_text: The stallion, wheeling around on the golden grounds on all sides, shaking its body with extended, outspread mane-rows,

children.text: jvalākaṇāruṇarucā nikareṇareṇoḥ śeṣeṇatejasaḥ ivollasatā rarāja // MSpv_5.55 //
children.translated_text: shone with the mass of dust, ruddy as flame-sparks — as if with the remainder of [its own] splendor, blazing. // MSpv_5.55 //
With his two hands steady on the horse's bridle-bar, half-risen like <s>Hari</s> (the Sun) from the summit of the rising mountain,

children.text: stokena nākramata vallabhapālamuccaiḥ śrīvṛkṣakī puruṣakonnamitāgrakāyaḥ // MSpv_5.56 //
children.translated_text: the chief groom, with body bent forward, barely mounted the stallion on high — the <s>Śrīvṛkṣakī</s> (man-plant). // MSpv_5.56 //
A horse, its body densely wet from bathing, shone — gazed upon with unblinking eyes by the people like gods;

children.text: śrīsaṃnidhānaramaṇīyataro 'śva uccair uccaiśravā jalanidheriva jātamātraḥ // MSpv_5.57 //
children.translated_text: more beautiful in the proximity of <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī), the horse on high [appeared] like <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s> just born from the ocean. // MSpv_5.57 //

children.text: aśrāvi bhūmipatibhiḥ kṣaṇavītanidrair aśnunpuro haritakaṃ mudamādadhānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Heard by the kings who were briefly free from sleep, the horse, chewing green [gram] in front and producing pleasure,
made a mixed sound of bells tinkling at the tip of his swaying neck and the crunching of [grain by] his teeth. // MSpv_5.58 //

children.text: utkhāya darpacalitena sahaiva rajjvā kīlaṃ prayatnaparamānavadurgraheṇa /
children.translated_text: Having uprooted the tethering-peg along with the rope, agitated by pride, by one hard to restrain even with utmost effort,

children.text: ākulyakāri kaṭakasturageṇa tūrṇam aśveti vidrutamanudrutāśvamanyam // MSpv_5.59 //
children.translated_text: the army-horse caused commotion; they ran after [it] swiftly [crying] 'Horse!' — [and others] ran after a different horse. // MSpv_5.59 //
Calmly and skillfully performing the subsequent duties, a certain [horseman], expert in the division of the reins,

children.text: siddhaṃ mukhe navasu vāthiṣu kaścidaśvaṃ valgāvibhāgakuśalo gamayāṃbabhūva // MSpv_5.60 //
children.translated_text: his appearance beyond confusion — having mastered in his mouth the nine gaits — made the horse go [through them]. // MSpv_5.60 //
Running about everywhere with loosened reins, pulling at the strings of the canopy awnings entangled [with them],
the horses moved with prancing, unsteady steps, restrained by angry attendants — slipping on the hem of the cloth. // MSpv_5.61 //
Beneath a tree, by a bull [that was] light though its burden had been unloaded, yet unable to bear the fullness of its over-nourished [body],
chewing the cud with slow-moving, heavy dewlap — [the bull] made a lazy, half-closed gaze [at the world]. // MSpv_5.62 //
The great bulls, with horns whose tips were capped with mud-balls, bearing a half-moon [mark], adorned on the horn-tips with the beauty [of strength], as if laughing,

children.text: ucchṛṅgitānyavṛṣabhā saritāṃ nadanto rodhāṃsi dhīramapacaskirire mahokṣāḥ // MSpv_5.63 //
children.translated_text: with horns raised, bellowing at the riverbanks, steadily pushed aside [the other cattle]. // MSpv_5.63 //
Having repeatedly defeated in battle the fearless rival bulls that approached the fat [cow], <s>Sarabha</s>-like,
the vigorous bull, victorious, with broad horns held high in triumph, went to the <s>Surabhī</s> (divine cow) without rival. // MSpv_5.65 //
Carrying its great length of neck not in vain, bestowing the finest pre-eminence,

children.text: loloṣṭramauṣṭrakamudagramukhaṃ tarūṇām abhraṃlihāni lilihe navapallavāni // MSpv_5.64 //
children.translated_text: the camel, with its lips moving upward, its face raised, licked the fresh sprouts of trees that touched the clouds. // MSpv_5.64 //
Together with suitable <s>picumarda</s> (neem) leaves, the tender mango-leaf that had entered between its jaws, softer [than the rest],

children.text: dāserakaḥsapadi saṃvalitaṃ niṣādair vipraṃ purā patagarāḍiva nirjagāra // MSpv_5.66 //
children.translated_text: the buffalo, at once swallowed — rolled up with the <s>niṣāda</s> (bitter-neem) leaves — like the king of birds [swallowing] a serpent of old. // MSpv_5.66 //

children.text: spaṣṭaṃ bahiḥ sthitavaterapi nivedayantaś ceṣṭāviśeṣamanujīvijanāya rājñām /
children.translated_text: Clearly revealing, even to the attendant-folk standing outside, the particular deeds of the kings through gestures,

children.text: vaitālikāḥ sphuṭapadaprakaṭārthamuccair bhogāvalīḥ kalagiro 'vasareṣu peṭhuḥ // MSpv_5.67 //
children.translated_text: the bards, with sweet voices, sang aloud songs of delight, with clear words and manifest meanings, at the appropriate times. // MSpv_5.67 //
That camp of the one whose fame was auspicious, adorned with tall pavilions of copper-colored cloth, teeming with dark elephant-herds,
shone, rivaling the beauty of the sky variegated by clouds broken apart at twilight. // MSpv_5.68 //

children.text: dharasyoddhartāsitvamitinanu sarvatra jagati pratītastatkiṃ māmatibharamadhaḥ prāpipāyiṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'You are the upholder of the earth!' — so indeed being known everywhere in the world, [the mountain asked:] 'Then why do you wish to bring me down under your excessive weight?'
Thus chided loudly, the mountain — this lord of <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) — was attacked by the army, [producing] sounds from the cracking of trampled elephants and uprooted trees. // MSpv_5.69 //
Then, to delight him who desired pleasure, on that mountain, adorned with the beauty of seasonal blossoms each in their proper [place],

children.text: ṛtugaṇena niṣevitumādadhe bhuvi padaṃ vipadantakṛtaṃ satāṃ // MSpv_6.1 //
children.translated_text: the group of seasons set foot on the earth — that [season] which destroys the adversities of the good. // MSpv_6.1 //
Before him, a forest of fresh <s>palāśa</s> (Flame-of-the-Forest) [trees], with lotuses whose pollen resembled broken crystal,
he beheld, fragrant with [flower-]burdens, with soft creeper-tips at the ends of creepers. // MSpv_6.2 //
Touching the perspiration born on the foreheads of the doe-eyed women, [causing] disarrangement of their disheveled locks,
the wind blew, making waves on the surface of the lakes, splitting apart the <s>kuvalaya</s> (blue lotus) [petals]. // MSpv_6.3 //
It equaled the stars of the eyes — in [the women] whose garlands were intertwined with <s>kurabaka</s> (red-amaranth) clusters;
in the <s>mālinī</s> (garland-maker women) of the spring women, quality acquired quality from a worthy support — like an ocean [that grows]. // MSpv_6.4 //
Splendidly, with the radiance of blazing gold, the <s>aśoka</s> (sorrowless) tree shone together with <s>campaka</s> (golden-champa) flowers;

children.text: virahiṇāṃ hṛdayasya bhidābhṛtaḥ kapiśitaṃ piśitaṃ madanāgninā // MSpv_6.5 //
children.translated_text: as if the heart of the love-lorn, which bore the splitting, had been browned — [its] flesh roasted by the fire of <s>Madana</s> (Love). // MSpv_6.5 //
The pollen-particles of the mango-grove, as if ground into powder by the fire of <s>Smara</s> (Love),

children.text: nipātitāḥ paritaḥ pathikavrajānupari te paritepurato bhṛśam // MSpv_6.6 //
children.translated_text: cast upon the groups of travelers on all sides, caused them severe burning. // MSpv_6.6 //
Like a female messenger of reconciliation sent by the lord of <s>Rati</s> (<s>Kāma</s>) to the beloved women pretending anger,
the row of bees went forth, melodious with the sound of <s>bakula</s>-flower nectar-liquor [humming]. // MSpv_6.7 //
Awakened [by the cuckoo] as if by a dear friend, speaking some desirable words like the <s>parapuṣṭā</s> (cuckoo) —
the women, out of jealousy toward the body most dear to their beloved, did not adorn themselves // <s>MSpv</s> 6.8 //
Like travelers reminded by bees that serve as slanderers, or by deer,
they fell under the power of the <s>vīṇā</s>-string, conquered by the sweetness of its voice // <s>MSpv</s> 6.9 //
Approached with delight by a woman desiring to gather flowers and embraced,
the forest tree did not bend down—in vain it stood tall, with a feigned dance, as if with a real dance // <s>MSpv</s> 6.10 //
"Cast aside this dispassionate swarm of bees upon the clusters of lotuses;
bowing with the weight of your breasts, which surpass flower-clusters, the vine turns toward you" // <s>MSpv</s> 6.11 //
"Bearing thirst for your fragrant breath and for your lips sweet as fresh nectar,

children.text: alamaleriva gandharasāvamū mama na saumanasau manaso mude // MSpv_6.12 //
children.translated_text: these two bees of scent and flavor are not enough, like jasmine flowers, for the delight of my heart" // <s>MSpv</s> 6.12 //
Thus as he spoke, the woman with breasts elevated by the rising of her pair of arms,
embraced her lover impetuously with the beauty of her bared stomach, as if out of fear of bees // <s>MSpv</s> 6.13 //
With her who moved with the beauty enhanced by the confusion of bees wandering about, attracted by the fragrance of her face-lotus,
she of restless glances, her girdle-bells tinkling, produced a melodious sound // <s>MSpv</s> 6.14 //

children.text: ajagaṇan gaṇaśaḥ priyamagrataḥ praṇatamapyabhimānitayā na yāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those women of the <s>Kukura</s> clan who, out of pride, did not acknowledge in groups their lover bowing before them—

children.text: sati madhāvabhavanmadanavyathā vidhuritā dhuritāḥ kukurastriyaḥ // MSpv_6.15 //
children.translated_text: when <s>Madhāva</s> (spring) arrived, the anguish of <s>Madana</s> (love) shook them and distressed them // <s>MSpv</s> 6.15 //
Other women, their bodies shattered by the swift arrows fitted to the flower-bow of <s>Kāma</s>,
even accepted death—what to speak of those who were repeatedly deprived of their husbands? // <s>MSpv</s> 6.16 //
"O slender one, to rival the beauty of your lotus-face, this ornament for a blemished forehead;

children.text: tadapi samprati sannihite madhāvadhigamaṃ dhigamaṅgalamaśruṇaḥ // MSpv_6.17 //
children.translated_text: but now that <s>Mādhava</s> is near, alas for this inauspicious tear!" // <s>MSpv</s> 6.17 //
"Alas, she will soon give up her life from the pain of separation"—spoken by anxious relatives

children.text: priyatayā gaditāstvayi bāndhavairavitathā vitathāḥ sakhi mā giraḥ // MSpv_6.18 //
children.translated_text: out of affection for you, O friend, those words were not false, though seemingly false // <s>MSpv</s> 6.18 //
"Surely this great one does not transgress even when gone far away"—hearing these words of kinsmen spoken out of affection,

children.text: praṇayino niśamayya vadhūrbahiḥ svaramṛtairamṛtairiva nirvavau // MSpv_6.19 //
children.translated_text: the bride outside was revived, as if by nectar, by those voice-nectars // <s>MSpv</s> 6.19 //
With a sweet intellect enriched by the abundance of honey from the <s>mādhavī</s> vine awakened by spring,
the female bee, filled with intoxicated humming, sang softly and quietly // <s>MSpv</s> 6.20 //
Making all the mountain forests ruddy repeatedly, causing travelers to suffer,
the mass of blossoming <s>kiṃśuka</s> trees carried aloft the beauty of a forest fire // <s>MSpv</s> 6.21 //
Where the dust of <s>śirīṣa</s> flowers bore comparison to the hair on the body of the sun's horses,
he arrived, bestowing upon the new <s>mallikā</s> jasmines their long-lasting wealth of fragrance // <s>MSpv</s> 6.22 //
When the wind blew, imitating the breath of his own bride, upon the opened soft <s>pāṭala</s> buds,
the intoxicated bee-swarm acquired the frenzy of amorous excitement // <s>MSpv</s> 6.23 //
The breasts, cool from the goosebumps raised by their momentary touch, were placed upon the beloved's chest,

children.text: sarasacandanareṇuranukṣaṇaṃ vicakare ca kareṇa varorubhiḥ // MSpv_6.24 //
children.translated_text: and moist sandal paste was applied again and again by the hand of the beautiful-thighed women // <s>MSpv</s> 6.24 //
Flashing with unsteady lightning-eyes, with cloud-like breasts that have poured forth upon the beloved,
the row of rain-clouds, not observing their proper season, reached the mountain lord // <s>MSpv</s> 6.25 //
Seeing high in the sky a fresh cloud, dark as a herd of elephants, against the sky,

children.text: abhisasāra na vallabhamaṅganā na cakame ca kamekarasaṃ rahaḥ // MSpv_6.26 //
children.translated_text: the woman did not go out to meet her beloved, nor did she desire the pleasure of love in private // <s>MSpv</s> 6.26 //
She followed the body of the rain-cloud shaking its limbs with bracelet-like motion,

children.text: dhutatanurvalayasya payomucaḥ śabalimā balimānamuṣo vapuḥ // MSpv_6.27 //
children.translated_text: enveloped in a garment colored by the radiance of various jeweled earrings, robbing the beauty of <s>Bali</s> // <s>MSpv</s> 6.27 //
The cluster of blossoms of the tree of the sky, dark as a bent <s>tamāla</s>,
momentarily glimpsed and then concealed by branches swaying in the swift wind, shone brightly through the clouds // <s>MSpv</s> 6.28 //
The traveler's wife, about to enter mortal danger at the sudden sight of the mass of rain-clouds,
gazed with eyes full of tears, with her friend, in agitation, at her beloved kinsman, charmingly distressed // <s>MSpv</s> 6.29 //
Greatly agitating the mind of the wife of the traveler, delighting with the trembling of the <s>kandala</s> plant,

children.text: namayati sma vanāni manasvinījananamano ghanamārutaḥ // MSpv_6.30 //
children.translated_text: the dense wind bent the forests and bowed the minds of noble women // <s>MSpv</s> 6.30 //
The row of clouds made the intoxicated, sweetly-crying flock of peacocks dance,
having surpassed the sound of the drum's circle with its own wealth of thunder // <s>MSpv</s> 6.31 //
Fresh kadamba-born pollen, reddening the sky, fragrant as mushrooms, O lady of the city,
inspired passion in the hearts of the passionate, ever-new, by forest breezes // <s>MSpv</s> 6.32 //
With their heat subdued and the great dust removed, by the first sparse drops of water from the rain-clouds,

children.text: praviralairacalāṅganamaṅganājanasugaṃ na sugandhi na cakrire // MSpv_6.33 //
children.translated_text: they did not make the mountain-slopes fragrant or pleasant for the company of women // <s>MSpv</s> 6.33 //
The <s>ketaka</s> flower, with its barely visible glimmer of buzzing bees, was indistinguishable from an elephant's trunk;

children.text: ghanaghanaughavighaṭṭanayā divaḥ kṛśasikhaṃ śaśikhaṇḍamiva cyutam // MSpv_6.34 //
children.translated_text: like a crescent moon fallen from the sky by the collision of dense rain-clouds, with its slender tip // <s>MSpv</s> 6.34 //
Whitened by crushed pearl-powder, beautiful with the spray of gushing waterfalls,
the particles of <s>kuṭaja</s> flower-pollen clearly made a mockery of mountain-dust // <s>MSpv</s> 6.35 //
By bees, resembling the moon, clinging constantly to the continuous garlands of <s>mālatī</s> blossoms soft with fresh rain-drops,
paleness was produced, carrying the burden of pure pollen // <s>MSpv</s> 6.36 //
The row of fresh <s>nīpa</s> trees, as if scattering its own pollen like a garment of cloth,
upon the quarters holding cloud-like garments, for the hearts of women separated from their beloveds // <s>MSpv</s> 6.37 //
Though bearing the anger of love and turning their faces away, at the sudden fearful roar of the clouds,
the women with slender waists turned around to embrace their lovers // <s>MSpv</s> 6.38 //

children.text: vigatarāgaguṇo 'pi jano na kaścalati vāti payodanabhasvati /
children.translated_text: Even a person bereft of the quality of passion does not remain still when the wind blows with cloud-laden breezes;
as if thus addressed by the bees, the fresh sprouts danced exuberantly on high // <s>MSpv</s> 6.39 //
Young women of the <s>Yadu</s> lords, soft-spoken with love, delighted the company,
being reluctant to depart out of fear of the sudden brightness, from the house, that <s>Kāma</s> himself // <s>MSpv</s> 6.40 //
Providing shelter-like darkness that conceals the sun's rays for the bird-families,
the rainy season, experienced without awareness, distressed the quarters—then <s>Hari</s>, bearer of the discus weapon // <s>MSpv</s> 6.41 //
He gazed upon autumn with its wide-open lotus-eyes, like a beloved resting upon the mountain's lap,
he whose fame destroys sins, of those whose wealth is pure, clear, and with garments fallen away // <s>MSpv</s> 6.42 //
In the world the cool-rayed moon with its beams at night, in the sky the mass of clouds forming darkness,

children.text: jalajarājiṣu naindramadidravanna mahatāmahatāḥ kva ca nārayaḥ // MSpv_6.43 //
children.translated_text: the rainbow dissolved in the waters of ponds—where are the glories of the great if not opposed? // <s>MSpv</s> 6.43 //

children.text: samaya eva karoti balābalaṃ praṇigatavanta itīva śarīriṇām /
children.translated_text: As if proclaiming that "circumstance alone creates strength and weakness" to embodied beings,
in autumn the calls of geese, having harshened the voices of peacocks, attained loveliness // <s>MSpv</s> 6.44 //
Previously conquering the sounds of the body-hair with the cooing of white-winged birds,

children.text: jagalurakṣamayeva śikhaṇḍinaḥ paribhavo 'ribhavo hi suduḥsahaḥ // MSpv_6.45 //
children.translated_text: the peacocks dropped their tails; indeed, insult from enemies is very hard to bear // <s>MSpv</s> 6.45 //
Forest after forest, on the faces of the forest-row brides, beautiful with thick redness on the lips below,
the opened <s>bāṇa</s> flower-bracelets shone exceedingly—those coquettish glances of beauty // <s>MSpv</s> 6.46 //
With leaves tawny as broken gold, beautiful with saffron filaments reddish with pollen,
the rejection of the anger of proud women insulted by their lovers proved not to be fruitless // <s>MSpv</s> 6.47 //
From where the lotus imitated the lotus-face complexion, rosy with intoxication, of the <s>cakora</s>-eyed women,
bearing fresh sunshade, the lotus therefore out of anxiety did not leave the water // <s>MSpv</s> 6.48 //
The cowherd-woman threshing the rice free of grain did not chase the deer-herd;
hearing the soft singing voice uttered by them, she stood before them with unblinking gaze // <s>MSpv</s> 6.49 //
As if declaring that the rutting elephant has bewildered the three worlds,
the winds blew, fragrant with flower-cluster bouquets, with bees continuously singing in accompaniment // <s>MSpv</s> 6.50 //
Freed from the veil of rain-clouds, the quarters appeared in some places bright white,
in some places clad in the elephant-hide of <s>Indra</s>—in autumn, the waterless, tearless sky-god's directions // <s>MSpv</s> 6.51 //
The autumn-maiden, with her new lotus-filament-born dust scattered by the winds,
playfully tossed it upward like <s>Hari</s>'s wife playfully throwing dust in jest // <s>MSpv</s> 6.52 //
Like a garland made of green leaves by the <s>Marut</s> hosts, with beautiful sprouts bound together,

children.text: madhuriporabhitāmramukhī mudaṃ divi tatā vitatāna śukāvaliḥ // MSpv_6.53 //
children.translated_text: the row of parrots, with faces coppery before the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>, spread delight across the sky // <s>MSpv</s> 6.53 //
Perceiving the sky with its smile-like lotuses, eye-like lakes, its limbs exceedingly white, its bird-like laughter,

children.text: akalayan muditāmiva sarvataḥ sa śaradanturadihmukhām // MSpv_6.54 //
children.translated_text: he regarded autumn as if she were a delighted woman, her face turned in all directions // <s>MSpv</s> 6.54 //
Though the lord of deer also bestowed frost upon the rivers and even golden-hued ones,
he attenuated the continuous flow of water from the eyes of bee-women, causing sorrow to their sight // <s>MSpv</s> 6.55 //
"Alas, how unfitting, O great lord, that the wind at other times reminds one of love's
breasts warm with the heat of remembered youth, yet with frost destroys the love-sick" // <s>MSpv</s> 6.56 //

children.text: priyatamena yayā saruṣā sthitaṃ na saha sā sahasā parirabhya tam /
children.translated_text: She who had stood angrily without her beloved—she could not for a moment

children.text: ślathayituṃ kṣaṇamakṣamatāmaṅganā na saha sā sahasā kṛtavepathuḥ // MSpv_6.57 //
children.translated_text: loosen her embrace of him, suddenly seized by trembling, that woman // <s>MSpv</s> 6.57 //
Greatly pained was she whose lip-petal wound was unshielded from the frost-bearing winds;

children.text: daśanaraśmipaṭena ca sītkṛtairnivāsiteva sitena sunirvavau // MSpv_6.58 //
children.translated_text: and she breathed out gently with hissing sounds, as if veiled by the white cloth of her tooth-rays // <s>MSpv</s> 6.58 //
By the wound-bearing one of beautiful body, the ray of teeth in a half-formed smile was held
as if it were clearly a covering from the cold winds, by the soft, messenger-like lower lip // <s>MSpv</s> 6.59 //
The gestures of threatening with vine-like fingers at the frost-bearing wind

children.text: pṛthu nirantaramiṣṭabhujāntaraṃ vanitayānitayā na viṣehire // MSpv_6.60 //
children.translated_text: were not endured by the woman who was not brought to the broad, uninterrupted space between the beloved's arms // <s>MSpv</s> 6.60 //

children.text: himaṛtāvapi tāḥ sma bhṛśasvido yuvatayaḥ sutarāmupakāriṇau /
children.translated_text: Even in the winter season, those young women perspired greatly—extremely helpful
in revealing natural passion, <s>Kāma</s>-filled, they delighted their lovers // <s>MSpv</s> 6.61 //
Making trees bloom and fruit, with blossoming vines and without the hum of bees,
the winter wind reproached the garden, and the women separated from lovers // <s>MSpv</s> 6.62 //
Even the powerful one falls into impotence when others are ascendant, by the force of time;
the sun with feeble rays was not terrified, nor did the great mass of frost grow less // <s>MSpv</s> 6.63 //
He who wishes to anoint the worlds as if with love—the heap of <s>lodhra</s> blossoms declared this;
whitened by the pale dust of the stirred army, this radiance veiled the quarters and appeared on the horizon // <s>MSpv</s> 6.64 //

children.text: śiśiramāsamapāsya guṇosya naḥ ka iva śītaharasya kucoṣmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Having set aside the cold season, who indeed is the remover of cold for us but the warmth of breasts?"

children.text: iti dhiyāstaruṣaḥ parirebhire ghanamato namato 'numatān priyāḥ // MSpv_6.65 //
children.translated_text: Thus thinking, with eager affection, the beloveds warmly embraced their lovers who bowed with consent // <s>MSpv</s> 6.65 //
Over the clove trees, more reddened with pollen, the flower-petal rows aligned with fragrant dust;

children.text: sphuṭamiti prasavena puro 'hasatsapadi kundalatā dalatālinaḥ // MSpv_6.66 //
children.translated_text: clearly thus, with blossoming, the <s>kundalatā</s> vine laughed before them, splitting its petal-rows suddenly // <s>MSpv</s> 6.66 //
The exceedingly fragrant <s>santānaka</s> tree, resplendent with the beauty of its flowers, did not diminish in delicacy;

children.text: taruṇaparabhṛtaḥ svanaṃ rāgiṇāmatanuta rataye vasantānakaḥ // MSpv_6.67 //
children.translated_text: the young cuckoo extended its song, for the delight of the passionate, like the vernal conclusion // <s>MSpv</s> 6.67 //
Not abandoning the hearts of young women in the pleasures of the season of honey and spring,
the mango garland, out of excessive passion for the bees, failed to grasp the essence of the honey-season. (MŚpv 6.68)
'These [banana plants] are the victorious slim [warriors] in the army of <s>Smara</s>'s (Love's) prowess, [meant] to conquer the world' —

children.text: ityasya tene kadalīrmadhuśrīḥ prabhāvanī ketanavaijayantīḥ // MSpv_6.69 //
children.translated_text: thus, the beauty of spring gave him banana plants as victorious banners of prowess. (MŚpv 6.69)
The darkness of the body, consisting of <s>Smara</s>'s (Love's) passion, was spread around, beyond the sun's control;

children.text: priyamāpa divāpi kokile strī paritastārarave rasatvaśyam // MSpv_6.70 //
children.translated_text: the female <s>kokila</s> (cuckoo), even by day, found her beloved — in the continuous resounding, she attained the essence of passion. (MŚpv 6.70)
Her body, [as if enjoying] a water-sport, with a pure [complexion], beautiful — more lovely — moving [gracefully],
by her lover, the beautiful ray-creeper of radiance was delighted — her passion measured [in beauty]. (MŚpv 6.71)

children.text: mudamabdabhuvāmapāṃ mayūrāḥ sahasāyanta nadī papāṭa lābhe /
children.translated_text: The peacocks, [born] of the joy of cloud-born waters, suddenly went to the river that had split open in [its own] gain;

children.text: alinā ratamālinī śillīndhre saha sāyantanadīpapāṭalābhe // MSpv_6.72 //
children.translated_text: the garlanded [woman], in love, with a bee, on the <s>śilīndhra</s> [mushroom] — going to the river at evening, [amid] the gain of <s>pāṭala</s> [blossoms]. (MŚpv 6.72)

children.text: kuṭajāni vīkṣya śikhibhiḥ śikharīndraṃ samayāvanau ghanamadabhramarāṇi /
children.translated_text: Seeing the <s>kuṭaja</s> blossoms, by the peacocks [who thought it was] the peak of the mountain-lord — in the season, in the forest, [there were] abundant dense intoxicated bees;

children.text: gaganaṃ ca gītaninadasya giroccaiḥ samayā vanaughanamadabhramarāṇi // MSpv_6.73 //
children.translated_text: the sky too, [resounding] with the high sound of song from the mountain — in the season, the forest-flood [had] abundant, not-few, intoxicated bees. (MŚpv 6.73)

children.text: abhīṣṭhamāsādya cirāya kāle samuddhṛtāśāṃ kamanī cakāśe /
children.translated_text: Having obtained the desired [thing] after a long time, the beautiful one shone with raised hopes;
at the joyous rise of <s>Manmatha</s> (Love) for women, she shone with the going of raised limbs [i.e., goosebumps]. (MŚpv 6.74)

children.text: stanayoḥ samayena yāṅganānāmabhinaddhārasamā na sā rasena /
children.translated_text: By the season, the nipples of women were not bound [covered] equally with that liquid [sweat];
the taste of the pleasure of embrace of waters was not [equaled by] the bound <s>Mānasasaras</s> [lake]-essence. (MŚpv 6.75)
The woman, whose affection has arisen, sweet, [singing] throughout the forest's end, in love, to her beloved — that amorous one, who would not do [thus]?

children.text: tatsamparka prāpya purā mohanalīlāṃ kāmekānte sā rasikā kā kurute na // MSpv_6.76 //
children.translated_text: Having obtained that union, formerly, [performing] the play of enchantment, in love, alone with the beloved — that amorous woman, who would not do [thus]? (MŚpv 6.76)

children.text: kāntājanena rahasi prasabhaṃ gṛhītakeśe rate smarasahāsavatopitena /
children.translated_text: With hair forcibly seized in private by the people of the beloved, in the pleasure [of love], by him who is emboldened by <s>Smara</s>'s (Love's) laughter —

children.text: premṇā manastu rajanīṣvapi haimanīṣu ke śerate sma rasahāsavatopitena // MSpv_6.77 //
children.translated_text: whose mind, even in the wintry nights, with love, emboldened by the laughter of passion — who would sleep? (MŚpv 6.77)
Even those who had gone beyond wonder, with high [expectations], with the play of the complete, spotless, young shoot —
the row of bees' words, repeatedly, with the play of the flawless tender sprout, [attained] the essence. (MŚpv 6.78)

children.text: kurvantamityatibhareṇa nagānavācaḥ puṣpaivirāmamalināṃ ca na gānavācaḥ /
children.translated_text: Making the mountains speechless with excessive burden of flowers, and also songs unsullied by cessation —

children.text: śrīmānsamastamanusānu girauvihartu bibhratyacodi sa mayūragirā vihartum // MSpv_6.79 //
children.translated_text: the glorious [mountain], bearing [all this] along every slope, with the voices of the peacocks, delighted in wandering. (MŚpv 6.79)
Then, to behold the beauty of the forest's interior, being extended by the seasons following the [mountain-] songs,

children.text: niragamadabhirāddhumadṛtānāṃ bhavati mahatsu na niṣphalaḥ prayāsaḥ // MSpv_7.1 //
children.translated_text: he set out — for the great ones, the effort to honor the intent of the devoted is not fruitless. (MŚpv 7.1)

children.text: dadhati sumanaso vanāni bahvīryuvatiyutā yadavaḥ prayātumīṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: The forests bear many flowers; the <s>Yādavas</s>, accompanied by young women, wished to go forth;
thinking [otherwise] in their minds, these [people] would not have been able to endure the five-flower [arrows] of the great weapon [of <s>Kāma</s>]. (MŚpv 7.2)
Approaching him involuntarily, stealing the heart, with effortlessly radiant forms,
the women then placed [their] feet on the ground, depositing the wealth of their charms among the women. (MŚpv 7.3)
With a nail-lustrous rainbow [of beauty], maintaining a come-and-go [swaying motion] in her graceful gait,

children.text: mukharitavalayaṃ pṛthau nitambe bhujalatikā muhuraskhalattaruṇyāḥ // MSpv_7.4 //
children.translated_text: the arm-creeper of the young woman repeatedly slipped on her broad hip, jingling her bracelets. (MŚpv 7.4)
On the canopy of excessive girth, with abundant small bells attached,
on the heavy hip-region of another woman, the waist-girdle's cluster made an excessive, sweet sound. (MŚpv 7.5)
Of the women-folk, whose feet were pressed by the weight of the heavy, dense, hip-globes as they stepped,
the pair of feet exuded [red dye] at each step, on the pretext of [accidentally] spilled lac-dye. (MŚpv 7.6)

children.text: tava sapadi samīpamānaye tāmahamiti tasya mayāgrato 'bhyadhāyi /
children.translated_text: 'I shall bring her to your presence immediately' — thus he spoke beforehand to me;

children.text: atirabhasākṛtālaghupratijñāmanṛtagiraṃ guṇagauri mā kṛthā mām // MSpv_7.7 //
children.translated_text: 'O fair-of-virtue, do not make me a liar [by going away] — [his was] a promise made hastily and not lightly.' (MŚpv 7.7)

children.text: na ca sutanu na vedmi yanmahīyānasunirasastava niścayaḥ pareṇa /
children.translated_text: 'O slender one, I do know that your resolution [to avoid me], a greater one, which [is made] firmly, with the other [person] —

children.text: vitathayati na jānātu madvaco 'sāviti ca tathāpi sakhīṣu me 'bhimānaḥ // MSpv_7.8 //
children.translated_text: let it not prove false — "let that one not know my word [to be untrue]" — even so, [there is] my pride among my friends.' (MŚpv 7.8)
'The constant not-speaking by me with you has been brought about by you, who show disdain;

children.text: tvayi taditi virodhaniścitāyāṃ bhavati bhavatvasuhṛjjanaḥ sakāmaḥ // MSpv_7.9 //
children.translated_text: since you have resolved upon enmity — let it be, let the circle of friends have their wish.' (MŚpv 7.9)
'Having lost composure, alas, I cannot even sustain [my] breath without a discourse from you, O lady;

children.text: praṇayati yadi na prasādabuddhirbhava mama mānini jīvite dayāluḥ // MSpv_7.10 //
children.translated_text: if there is no gracious disposition in your affection, O proud woman, then be merciful at least toward my life.' (MŚpv 7.10)
Thus, the woman, intensely [recalling] the offense of her beloved, with eyes reddened by anger and remembrance,
from compliance with the words of a friend at [her] feet, somehow — reluctantly — became favorable. (MŚpv 7.11)

children.text: drutapadamiti mā vayasya yāsirnanu sutanuṃ paripālayānuyāntīm /
children.translated_text: 'Do not go with such hasty steps, O friend! Rather, attend to the slender one who follows!

children.text: nahi na viditakhedamedatīyastanajaghanodvahane tavāpi cetaḥ // MSpv_7.12 //
children.translated_text: Surely, your mind too, not unaware of the difficulty, is weary from the burden she bears at breast and hip.' (MŚpv 7.12)
While the group of friends spoke thus, another, out of affection, having waited long for the most beloved,

children.text: tadanugamavaśādanāyatāni nyadhita mimāna ivāvaniṃ padāni // MSpv_7.13 //
children.translated_text: compelled by following her, placed [her] steps — not long ones — as if measuring the earth. (MŚpv 7.13)

children.text: yadi mayi laghimānamāgatāyāṃ tava dhṛtirasti gatāsmi sampratīyam /
children.translated_text: 'If your firmness holds when I, diminished [in your eyes], have departed — I am going now indeed' —

children.text: drutatarapadapātamāpapāta priyamiti kopapadena kāpi saṃkhyā // MSpv_7.14 //
children.translated_text: with these words of anger, a certain woman rushed quickly, with rapid footsteps, [saying] 'O beloved!' (MŚpv 7.14)
With dense goosebumps, as [she] walked alongside, one of the young woman's breasts at each step,

children.text: ghaṭitavighaṭitaḥ priyasya vakṣastaṭabhuvi kandukavibhramaṃ babhāra // MSpv_7.15 //
children.translated_text: joined and disjoined [with the beloved's chest], performed the play of a [bouncing] ball on the surface of the beloved's chest. (MŚpv 7.15)
Clinging tightly to his neck, with one arm firmly embracing the broad outer breast-surface,
with body-hair bristling, she entwined one arm of her husband — soft upon not-soft. (MŚpv 7.16)
Repeatedly churning unevenly, excessively, with the circle of her hips making the girdle-bells resound,
pressing one breast diagonally across the long garland-strand onto the other's chest-surface, she pressed. (MŚpv 7.17)
With the deeply resonant ankle-bells sounding heavily, her left lotus-foot dancing gracefully,
making the other [foot] exceedingly wavering, she went forth with a step languid with love (<s>Manmatha</s>). (MŚpv 7.18)
With light, graceful steps, having placed both sprout-like hands on the pair of his shoulder-platforms, another woman,
with the prodding of her firm breast-tips — the weak one led her beloved playfully. (MŚpv 7.19)
With hips not light, with plump thighs, with difficulty — wearied by the burden of her dense, large buttocks,
a certain [woman] bore [herself], supported by her own arm-creepers hanging from the neck of her most beloved. (MŚpv 7.20)
Another was led by a different [man], of proportionate body, with an arm placed from the arm-root, clasped to the breast by [his] arm,
with teeth-marks placed on [her] cheek, placing [her] uneven [faltering] steps as if by force. (MŚpv 7.21)
Following through the forest, another, [walking] behind the dark-browed [woman], with friends, on her path,
followed, without doubt, matching the fresh love-red line-marks on [her] breast [to his own]. (MŚpv 7.22)
With the navel-pond filled to overflowing with the great flood of love's essence,
those [women], overflowing with the line of body-hair, shone like rivers — with the ornament of swans moving playfully, resounding. (MŚpv 7.23)
Sweet to the ear, the calls of the <s>sārasas</s> (cranes) were heard resounding after them,
producing the suspicion of the twanging of <s>Manmatha</s>'s (Love's) bow — skilled at piercing the heart-arrows of the people. (MŚpv 7.24)
As if calling out like the bride of the crusher of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), the swarms of bees sang eagerly;
the row of forest-creepers enacted the gestures [of that calling], with their new-sprout fingers. (MŚpv 7.25)
Of the trees shaken by the wind, with filaments scattered and blossoming from the loosening of buds not yet fully opened by the bee-clusters,

children.text: marudavaniruhāṃ rajo vadhūbhyaḥ mupaharan vicakāra korakāṇi // MSpv_7.26 //
children.translated_text: the wind presented the pollen to the ladies and broke open [more] buds. (MŚpv 7.26)
By the bees, skilled at following the garden breezes — that which was not attained by the women —
the realm of fragrance of those lofty ones [flowers], in [the bees'] pursuit — indeed, riches stand at the front. (MŚpv 7.27)
The flowers [<s>sumanasas</s>, also 'the well-minded'], their goodwill attained through the interaction with the chariot-wheeled women's lotus-hands,

children.text: jagati sumanasastadādi nūnaṃ dadhati parisphuṭamarthato 'bhidhānam // MSpv_7.28 //
children.translated_text: from that time on, in the world, surely bear their name clearly in its [true] meaning. (MŚpv 7.28)
By the young-shoot-nets of trees falling toward [them], through the excellence of qualities, seizing [them], bearing a blazing subdued pride —
with hand-free [gestures], the women were forcefully led to [playful] breaking. (MŚpv 7.29)
As a woman, joyful with bees, shook the branches with her arm, loosening [and] unchaining the conch-shells,

children.text: taruratiśāyitāparāṅganāyāḥ śirasi mudeva mumoca puṣpavarṣam // MSpv_7.30 //
children.translated_text: the tree — surpassing every other woman — showered flowers upon her head as if with delight. (MŚpv 7.30)
By a young sprout, with unceasing passion, one that shares in affection, [yet] scratched by fingernails and thus praised —

children.text: sapadi taruṇapallavena vadhvā vigatadayaṃ khalu khaṇḍitena mamle // MSpv_7.31 //
children.translated_text: [the sprout], merciless toward the bride, being broken, immediately withered. (MŚpv 7.31)
Of [the beloved] whose arm was raised to pluck flowers — the lovely root of [his arm], adorned with fresh nail-marks — another [woman]
repeatedly concealed [it] with a garment placed by another hand, blocking [the view of] the full breast-slope. (MŚpv 7.32)
With visible pale lines of extended wrinkles, with the row of body-hair vanishing into the other's domain,
though slender, making [her body] slender again — her wide, upward-gazing eyes clinging [to the beloved]. (MŚpv 7.33)
With breast-friends' bonds pressing upward at the chest, with the tie of the upper garment forcefully bursting,
with the silk garment over the belly billowing with breath, the deep root of the navel was faintly visible. (MŚpv 7.34)
Concealed, not recognizing in the colorful ground [her] beloved, who faced her,

children.text: adhiviṭapi salīlamagrapuṣpagrahaṇapadena ciraṃ vilambya kācit // MSpv_7.35 //
children.translated_text: upon a tree, playfully, on the pretext of plucking the topmost flower, a certain [woman] lingered for a long time. (MŚpv 7.35)

children.text: atha kila kathite sakhībhiratra kṣaṇamapareva sasaṃbhramā bhavantī /
children.translated_text: Then, when told by friends 'He is here!' — for a moment, another, becoming flustered,
her flower-filled hand loosening its grip, adjusting her garment to cover her limbs at each step — (MŚpv 7.36)
experiencing a blend of fear and joy, with the lotus-beauty of a face both startled and smiling,

children.text: manasijagurutatkṣaṇopadiṣṭaṃ kimapi rāsena rasantaraṃ bhajantī // MSpv_7.37 //
children.translated_text: assuming at that very instant something — a different emotional state (<s>rasa</s>) — taught by the master of <s>Manasija</s> (Love). (MŚpv 7.37)
With face bowed, the moon-[faced one] seemed to desire, through her unsteady nature, an obstruction from him;

children.text: aharata sutarāmato 'sya cetaḥ sphuṭamabhibhūṣayati striyastrapaiva // MSpv_7.38 //
children.translated_text: she stole his heart all the more by that — truly, modesty itself adorns women. (MŚpv 7.38)
Unspeakable [in words], to be placed only upon the goose-bumped body, on fragments of sprouts —
even the nail-mark-writings, their meaning illuminated, were placed as love-letters by beloveds. (MŚpv 7.39)
Having pushed aside a friend with feigned anger — 'You are clumsy!' — by herself,
toward the desired one, with longing, having revealed the arm-root, she placed a garland on [his] head. (MŚpv 7.40)

children.text: abhimukhamupayāti mā sma kiñcittvamabhidadhāḥ paṭale madhuvratānām /
children.translated_text: 'When he comes toward [you], do not say anything — amid the swarms of bees,
having obtained the fragrance of the honey-scented lotus-face — let [the bee] not fall further from [perching on] your face!' (MŚpv 7.41)
'Disenchanted with the bountiful flower-offerings of trees, full of pollen and honey,
surely this bee abandons the lower [flowers] out of desire to drink the nectar [of your lips].' (MŚpv 7.42)
While the group of friends spoke thus, with eyelashes doubled in density by closing [the eyes in shyness],

children.text: apadatalibhayena bharturaṅgaṃ bhavati hi viklavatā guṇo 'ṅganānām // MSpv_7.43 //
children.translated_text: she clung to the beloved's body from fear that no bee [would sting] — indeed, timidity is a virtue of women. (MŚpv 7.43)
When the youth, raising the lotus-face [of his bride], forcefully kissed the newly-wed bride,

children.text: tadapi na kila bālapallavāgragrahayāparayā vivide vidagdhasakyā // MSpv_7.44 //
children.translated_text: that [act] was not [considered accomplished] by another witty friend — [not] until [she herself could manage] the seizing of the topmost tender sprout. (MŚpv 7.44)
When the young bride was hidden behind dense rows of vines, the beloved [drank] the face of his beloved —
that which he drank from the lower lip — that was revealed by the sound of the bracelet dancing with the gaze's descent. (MŚpv 7.45)
Imitating the play [of the vine] before [her], of a bride of a creeper, mounted on a tree,
before [her] friends, with guilelessness, without the fault of fickleness being perceived, she embraced her lover. (MŚpv 7.46)
One woman, leaning on a friend's shoulder with her hand, her companion having risen with desire for a raised cluster [of flowers],
pressed her breasts with passion upon his chest — those breasts rivaling the frontal globes of a young elephant. // MSpv 7.47 //
Another, unable to bear the weight of her pitcher-like breasts due to her soft, tender foot-soles being unsteady,
fell upon her beloved from above, unsupported, in her desire to reach higher. // MSpv 7.48 //
Another man, greedy for embrace, skillfully attending to the climbing [woman] on the upper branches of trees,

children.text: prathitapṛthupayodharāṃ gṛhāṇa svayamiti mugdhavadhūmudāsa dorbhyām // MSpv_7.49 //
children.translated_text: lifted the naive young wife with his arms, saying 'Take hold!' — she of the prominent, full breasts. // MSpv 7.49 //
Another woman, repeatedly enticing [him] with flowers of the trees, [saying] 'This one! This one!' leading [him] ahead and ahead,

children.text: anurahasamanāyi nāyakena tvarayati rantumaho janaṃ manobhūḥ // MSpv_7.50 //
children.translated_text: was led along by her lover in amorous seclusion — ah, <s>Manobhū</s> (<s>Kāma</s>) urges people to make love in haste! // MSpv 7.50 //

children.text: vijanamiti balādamuṃ gṛhītvā kṣaṇamatha vīkṣya vipakṣamantiko 'nyā /
children.translated_text: Another woman, having forcibly seized him [saying] 'It is secluded!', then glancing for a moment at a rival nearby,
intending to run away, from fear of being seen as fickle, became exceedingly heavy, clinging to her beloved and not releasing [him]. // MSpv 7.51 //

children.text: adhirajani jagāma dhāma tasyāḥ priyatamayeti ruṣā srajāvanaddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: At night, a youth, bound with garlands, having gone to the dwelling of that most beloved woman — in anger [at his infidelity],

children.text: padamapi calituṃ yuvā na sehe kimiva na śaktiharaṃ sasādhvasānāṃ // MSpv_7.52 //
children.translated_text: could not even take a step — what indeed does not drain the strength of those who are apprehensive? // MSpv 7.52 //

children.text: na khalu vayamamuṣya dānayogyāḥ pibati ca pāti ca yāsakau rahastvāṃ /
children.translated_text: 'We are surely not worthy of your gifts! He drinks and protects you in secret, the suitor —

children.text: vraja vicapamamuṃ dadasva tasyai bhavatu yataḥ sadṛśościrāya yogaḥ // MSpv_7.53 //
children.translated_text: go, give him freely to her; let the union of equals last long!' // MSpv 7.53 //
'What use to us, O deceiver, of these vain offerings — tree-leaf and flower ear-ornaments?
Surely our pair of ears is already quite filled with your well-known deceits!' // MSpv 7.54 //
'As if constantly mocked by the cries of crows, why do you bring us this <s>kālikā</s> (dark bud)?

children.text: vasatimupagatena dhāmni tasyāḥ śaṭha kalireṣa mahāṃstvayādya dattaḥ // MSpv_7.55 //
children.translated_text: O rogue, by visiting her dwelling, you have today given us a great quarrel!' // MSpv 7.55 //
Having spoken thus in anger, another [woman] struck her beloved with her eye —

children.text: śravaṇaniyamitena kāntamanyā samamasitāmburuheṇa cakṣuṣā ca // MSpv_7.56 //
children.translated_text: that dark-lotus eye, with trembling, lovely eyelash-tips, restrained by the ear. // MSpv 7.56 //

children.text: vinayati sudṛśo dṛśaḥ parāgaṃ praṇayini kausumamānanānilena /
children.translated_text: The floral pollen from the beautiful eyes of fair women was dispersed by the breeze of their faces, fanning their beloved;
both eyes of that rival woman were constantly filled with the particles of anger. // MSpv 7.57 //
'This very utterance of women about a rival woman is clearly an incantation of sorcery —
for the beautiful-bodied one, summoned by her husband with a soft flower [thrown at her], though struck, swooned!' // MSpv 7.58 //
When a flower was lovingly placed behind the ear of the slender-waisted one by the affectionate [lover],

children.text: vrajadapi laghutāṃ babhūva bhāraḥ sapadi hiraṇmayamaṇḍanaṃ sapatnyāḥ // MSpv_7.59 //
children.translated_text: the golden ornament of her co-wife immediately became a burden, losing its significance. // MSpv 7.59 //
'Your eye has now conquered me!' — as if bowing with modesty,
the ear-lotus of the graceful woman, through the humming of bees, whispered this into her ear. // MSpv 7.60 //
Having gathered flowers, abandoning the creepers, the bee-swarms placed their steps

children.text: padamupadadhire kulānyalīnāṃ na paricayo malinātmanāṃ pradhānam // MSpv_7.61 //
children.translated_text: upon the women who were soft garland-wearers among maidens — for the wicked chiefly seek familiarity. // MSpv 7.61 //
With their shoulder-regions deeply bowed, as if from the weight of loosened hair falling,
with their lotus-faces having closed eyes, as if from the great weight of eyelashes, // MSpv 7.62 //
with their cheeks bearing excessive redness, the rays of the cool-rayed one [moon] expanding and blooming,
the <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) pollen having departed from cheeks experienced in the exertion of kissing, // MSpv 7.63 //
with the graceful play of their arms concluded, with a most delicate, slender pair [of arms],
or with lotus-hands tinted by fresh sprouts — hands of redundant beauty, // MSpv 7.64 //
with their pairs of breasts, exchanging the transferred hue of body-cosmetics with their husbands' chests — [those chests] like the arrows of <s>Kāma</s>,
the breast-pairs, resting upon one another, appeared as if from the abundance of extreme fatigue, // MSpv 7.65 //
with their bodies bent again from the weight of their heavy breasts, bowed by fatigue-born stooping,
their thighs — [thighs] like the trunks of young elephants — bearing the inability to maintain their customary gait, // MSpv 7.66 //
with their lotus-feet, the fresh <s>yāvaka</s> (lac-dye) gone from long walking on the ground, their color having returned —
those feet, trembling, somehow [proceeding], from the intensity of mutual attachment, // MSpv 7.67 //
thus repeatedly, from the passion of forest-sport, at that time exceedingly by those full-hipped women —

children.text: mṛdutaratanavo 'nalasāḥ prakṛtyā ciramapi tāḥ kimuta prayāsabhājaḥ // MSpv_7.68 //
children.translated_text: those women, softer of body and naturally not indolent — how much more so when subjected to exertion! // MSpv 7.68 //
At first, the fatigue-perspiration on their bright cheek-circles was light, like pearls;

children.text: kaṭhinakucataṭāgrapāti paścādatha śatasarkaratāṃ jagāma tāsām // MSpv_7.69 //
children.translated_text: then, falling from the tips of their hard breast-slopes, it attained the quality of hundred-fold sweetness. // MSpv 7.69 //
Even the ample breast-pairs of those women proud with youth shone forth,

children.text: parimalitamapi priyaiḥ prakāmaṃ kucayugamujjvalameṣa kāminīnām // MSpv_7.70 //
children.translated_text: soft with the eruption of dense goosebumps, though fully caressed by their lovers — those breasts of the passionate women, radiant. // MSpv 7.70 //
One woman, from the fatigue of incessant flower-gathering, having placed one creeper-like arm around [his] neck,
hung upon [him], her breasts — broad, without gap — concealing her beloved's chest. // MSpv 7.71 //
Another, with limbs arranged as she desired, raising her breast-pair — that capital of elevation —
the slender one revealed what was longed for, on the pretext of fatigue, with her waving creeper-like arms. // MSpv 7.72 //
A young [groom], bringing drops of perspiration resembling Himalayan dewdrops to the newly-wed bride,
with trembling hands barely managed to touch the pitcher-like nascent breasts. // MSpv 7.73 //
Having reached its crest at the buttock-plain, blocked at the narrow waist-region, flowing past the thigh-trees and creeper-arms toward the deep pool of the full navel,

children.text: ullaṅghyoccaiḥ kucataṭabhuvaṃ plāvayan rokūpān svedapūro yuvatisaritāṃ vyāpa gaṇḍasthalāni // MSpv_7.74 //
children.translated_text: overleaping high the breast-plateau, flooding the lake of the eyes — the flood of perspiration of those river-like women spread across their cheek-surfaces. // MSpv 7.74 //
When the beauty of the perspiration-flow only increased further from the beloved's caressing hand-strokes upon the women's limbs,
then they wished to bathe their bodies with those waters — they whose beauty was unwilted though their bodies were wilted from the fatigue of forest-sport. // MSpv 7.75 //
The group of women, wearied, their breasts heaving audibly from exertion, their lotus-eyes not fully opened,

children.text: abhyambhaḥ kathamapi yoṣitāṃ samūhaistairurvīnihitacalatpadaṃ pracele // MSpv_8.1 //
children.translated_text: somehow moved toward the water, their unsteady feet placed upon the earth by those [lovers]. // MSpv 8.1 //
As the dark-browed women walked together, though the space between their shoulders was ample due to their bowing,

children.text: saṃsaktaivipulatayā mitho nitambaiḥ sambādhaṃ bṛhadapi tadbabhūva vartma // MSpv_8.2 //
children.translated_text: even that broad path became crowded, their hips pressing together from the fullness [of their forms]. // MSpv 8.2 //

children.text: nīrandhradruśiśirāṃ bhuvaṃ vrajantīḥ sāśaṅkaṃ muhuriva kautukātkaraistāḥ /
children.translated_text: As they walked on the densely-shaded, cool ground, the moon [touched them] repeatedly, as if from curiosity, through the gaps
of the wind-agitated branches, with its cool rays, touching those women with its hands for a moment. // MSpv 8.3 //
For one woman scorched by the sun's rays, the moon, bearing at once the nature of both cool and warm covering,
its beauty surpassed by her lotus-face, made service as if to a beloved — [to that beloved] whose passion [like its own radiance] was growing. // MSpv 8.4 //
As she spread her upper garment over [herself] out of coyness, while her lover warded off the heat for her,
the shade of another woman's group of beautiful companions with parasols was greater than hers. // MSpv 8.5 //
As the pleasure of touch pervaded every limb of her whose beloved clung to her palm,

children.text: kauśeyaṃ vrajadapi gāḍhatāmajasraṃ sasraṃse vigalitanīvi nīrajākṣyāḥ // MSpv_8.6 //
