children.translated_text: the silk garment of the lotus-eyed one, though tightly [bound], continuously slipped away, its girdle-knot loosened. // MSpv 8.6 //
Watching those slender women walk languidly, the <s>haṃsīs</s> (female geese), astonished, did not resume their gaits;

children.text: buddhvā vā jitamapareṇa kāmamāṣkurvīta svaguṇamapatrapaḥ ka eva // MSpv_8.7 //
children.translated_text: or perhaps, knowing they were surpassed by another, who would shamelessly display one's own [inferior] qualities? // MSpv 8.7 //
With their glorious hips surpassing [river] sand-banks, with their full, broad buttock-mounds like the climbing <s>mādhavī</s> (spring-jasmine) vines,
swaying from stumbling on stones, they surely went quickly to the inner chambers of the river, out of embarrassment. // MSpv 8.8 //
The women regarded the sandy banks of the rivers — beautiful with pearls released by the water's current from oyster-shells —

children.text: strīlokaḥ parikalayāñcakāra tulyaṃ palyaṅkairvigalitahāracārubhiḥ svaiḥ // MSpv_8.9 //
children.translated_text: as equal to their own couches, beautiful with pearls fallen from their loosened necklaces. // MSpv 8.9 //
The wild flowers could not endure the unceasing, warm breath-exhalations of the women, [mixed with] fatigue-born [sighs], [their fragrance like] a splendid relative;

children.text: āraṇyāḥ sumanasa īṣire na bhṛṅgairaucityaṃ gaṇayati ko viśeṣakāmaḥ // MSpv_8.10 //
children.translated_text: they aspired [instead] for bees — for who considers propriety when desirous of special [pleasure]? // MSpv 8.10 //
Seeing a peacock, suspecting a rival <s>peahen</s> from the weight of its tail-feathers, rushing before [her] as his own woman returned from the forest,

children.text: ālokya vyavadadhataṃ puro mayūraṃ kāminyaḥ śradadhuranārjavaṃ nareṣu // MSpv_8.11 //
children.translated_text: the amorous women confirmed: 'Men are not straightforward.' // MSpv 8.11 //
The flocks of pure-plumed [birds], whose songs rivaled the sweet speech of <s>mādhavī</s> creepers,

children.text: antardhāmupayayurutpalāvalīṣu prāduṣkātka iva jitaḥ puraḥ pareṇa // MSpv_8.12 //
children.translated_text: hid within the lotus-groves — for who appears before [others] when defeated by a superior? // MSpv 8.12 //

children.text: mugdhāyāḥ smaralaliteṣu cakravākyā niśaṅkaṃ dayitatamena cumbitāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Of the naive woman kissed without hesitation by her dearest one, in love-playful [gestures], like a <s>cakravākī</s> (ruddy shelduck) —

children.text: praṇeśānabhi vidadhurvadhūtahastāḥ sītkāraṃ samucitamuttaraṃ taruṇyaḥ // MSpv_8.13 //
children.translated_text: the young women, with hands thrown up [in mock distress], made a suitable rejoinder of hissing sounds toward the lord [husband]. // MSpv 8.13 //
With blooming lotuses raised high as offerings, as if beckoning with affection through bird-songs,

children.text: nārīṇāmatha sarasī saphenahāsā prītyeva vyatanuta pādyamūrmihastaiḥ // MSpv_8.14 //
children.translated_text: the lake, with foam-laughter, joyfully offered foot-washing water to the women with its wave-hands. // MSpv 8.14 //
That [beauty] which they tore away with their hands from the lotus — the eternal beauty of its own abode, through passion —

children.text: vyaktatvaṃ niyatamanena ninyurasyāḥ sāpatnyaṃ kṣitisutavidviṣo mahiṣyaḥ // MSpv_8.15 //
children.translated_text: by this, the queens of the enemy of <s>Kṣitisuta</s> (the earth-goddess's son) clearly expressed their rivalry [with <s>Lakṣmī</s>]. // MSpv 8.15 //

children.text: āskandan kathamapi yoṣito na yāvadbhīmatyaḥ priyakaradhāryamāṇahastāḥ /
children.translated_text: Before the women — fearsome [in their splendor], their hands held by their lovers — could descend upon the water,
that water, from eagerness, rushed swiftly toward them, as if bearing their reflections transferred [into it]. // MSpv 8.16 //

children.text: tāḥ pūrvaṃ sacakitamāgamayya gādhaṃ kṛtvātho mṛdu padamantarāviśantyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those amorous women, first entering the shallows timidly, then gradually stepping softly into the depths,

children.text: kāminyo mana iva kāminaḥ sarāgairaṅgaistajjalamanurañjayāṃbabhū // MSpv_8.18 //
children.translated_text: tinted that water with their passion-flushed limbs, as the mind of a lover [is colored by desire]. // MSpv 8.18 //
As the breast-pair — bearing the beauty of a great elephant's frontal globes — repeatedly churned the water,

children.text: viśleṣaṃ yugamagamadrathāṅganāmnorudvṛttaḥ ka iva sukhāvahaḥ pareṣāṃ // MSpv_8.17 //
children.translated_text: the pair [of breasts and the water] parted momentarily — for who that has risen from others' [embrace] brings happiness? // MSpv 8.17 //

children.text: āsīnā taṭabhuvi sasmitena bhartrā rambhoruvatirutaṃ sarasyanicchuḥ /
children.translated_text: Seated on the bank, she who had broad thighs, not wishing to enter the lake upon her smiling husband's urging,

children.text: dhunvānā karayugamīkṣituṃ vilāsāñśītāluḥ salilagatena sicyate sma // MSpv_8.19 //
children.translated_text: shaking her pair of hands [in refusal], wishing to see his playful [coaxing] — the cold-fearing one was splashed by him from the water. // MSpv 8.19 //

children.text: necchantī samamunā saro 'vagāḍhuṃ rodhastaḥ pratijalamīritā sakhībhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Not wishing to enter the lake together with him, urged by her companions from the bank toward the water,

children.text: āślakṣadbhayacakitekṣaṇaṃ navoḍhā voḍhāraṃ vipadi na dūṣitātibhūmiḥ // MSpv_8.20 //
children.translated_text: the newly-wed bride, with fear-agitated, startled eyes, looked at her husband — she was not [one] to blame [him] in difficulty. // MSpv 8.20 //

children.text: tiṣṭhantaṃ payasi pumāṃsamaṃsamātre taddaghnaṃ tadavayatī kilātmano 'pi /
children.translated_text: Seeing a man standing in water only shoulder-deep, she measured it as [deep enough] even for herself;

children.text: abhyetuṃ sutanurabhīriyeṣa maugdhyādāśleṣi drutamamunā nimajjatīti // MSpv_8.21 //
children.translated_text: the slender one wished to approach fearlessly, in her naivety — [but] he quickly embraced her as she was sinking. // MSpv 8.21 //
When the arched-browed one had entered the lake up to her navel, then playfully, with its wave-hands, the water
climbed up to her breast-pair — but where is steadiness for those who have obtained [even a] touch? // MSpv 8.22 //
Though the <s>kuvalaya</s> (blue lotus) was cast aside by the eyes of the beloved women — 'I alone am not [surpassed] by the beauty of [her] face' —

children.text: saṃharṣādalivirutairitīva gāyallolormau payasi mahotpalaṃ nanarta // MSpv_8.23 //
children.translated_text: in delight, as if singing with the humming of bees, the great lotus danced upon the rolling waves. // MSpv 8.23 //
She who trembled — her thigh struck by the darting <s>śapharī</s> (small fish) — attained an excess of <s>vibhrama</s> (amorous confusion) in her thighs;

children.text: kṣubhyanti pasabhamaho vināpi hetorlīlābhiḥ kimu sati kāraṇe ramaṇyaḥ // MSpv_8.24 //
children.translated_text: alas! beautiful women become agitated in their play even without cause — how much more when a cause exists! // MSpv 8.24 //
Then that water of the lake — the lake of her body's goosebumps — was churned by [her] swiftly moving limbs;
it was agitated by the women's thighs [like] spreading wing-arms, and by their breasts [like] mountain-peaks of their cheeks. // MSpv 8.25 //
Though maintaining depth, the lake was brought to agitation by the women's hip-churning —
that one, with a face like a lotus blooming in the ocean, immediately transgressed the boundary. // MSpv 8.26 //
As if reaching far to seize his beloved, extended by rows of waves,

children.text: kasyāścidvitatacalacchikhāṅgulīko lakṣmīvān sarasi rarāja keśahastaḥ // MSpv_8.27 //
children.translated_text: a certain beautiful hand of hair, with fingers of spread, waving flame-tips, shone in the lake. // MSpv 8.27 //

children.text: unnidrapriyakamanoramaṃ ramaṇyāḥ saṃreje sarasi vapuḥ prakāśameva /
children.translated_text: The beautiful woman's radiant body shone openly in the lake, with awakened <s>priyaka</s> blossoms all around;

children.text: yuktānāṃ vimalatayā tiraskriyāyai nākrāmannapi hi bhavatyalaṃ jalaughaḥ // MSpv_8.28 //
children.translated_text: for a flood of water cannot suffice to conceal the pure, even when it overwhelms them. // MSpv 8.28 //
'Is this a lotus in the lake, or is it a young woman's face that shines?'

children.text: saṃśayya kṣaṇamiti niścikāya kaścidvivyokairbakasahavāsināṃ parokṣaiḥ // MSpv_8.29 //
children.translated_text: Having doubted thus for a moment, someone determined [the answer] by the unseen companions of the cranes co-dwelling [with lotuses]. // MSpv 8.29 //
Drinking-horns blazing with molten gold, fragrances, saffron-dye, garments clinging to the pair of broad breast-vessels,
wine, and the nearest provision—these were the accessories of water-sport for the women. // MSpv 8.30 //
From a high bank, with garments fluttering in the wind, together with the minds of their beloveds who showed fear,
the women, with heavy rows [of ornaments], not slowly leaping, fell more swiftly into the waters. // MSpv 8.31 //
The young women, naive, unacquainted with the stratagems of deception, quickly going to defeat,
played with their lovers a gambling game of splashing, with water sprinkled by their lotus-like hands. // MSpv 8.32 //
One alone performed the great consecration of <s>Kāmadeva</s> (the God of Love)—worthy of the sovereignty of the Love-god, burnt by the flame of the Three-eyed one's (<s>Śiva</s>'s) eye—
upon the moon-face of his beloved, with water raised from her pitcher-like hands. // MSpv 8.33 //
As one woman, tormented by the suffering of <s>Manasija</s> (Love), somehow raised her arm to sprinkle her beloved,
a golden bangle slipped from the tip of her lowering hand—like the remnant of the beauty's grace of that woman. // MSpv 8.34 //

children.text: snihyantī dṛśamaparā nidhāya pūrṇaṃ mūrtena praṇayarasena vāriṇeva /
children.translated_text: Another, placing her loving gaze, full, as if with the very essence of affection embodied in water,
her mind inclined to <s>Kandarpa</s> (Love), under the pretext of wishing to sprinkle her friend, made an offering of joined palms toward the young man. // MSpv 8.35 //

children.text: ānandaṃ dadhati mukhe karodakena śyāmāyā dayitatamena sicyamāne /
children.translated_text: When a dark-complexioned woman's face bore joy while being sprinkled with hand-water by her dearest beloved,
the face of the jealous rival, though unsprinkled, appeared bathed in abundant sweat-water. // MSpv 8.36 //
Looking up at the pair of breasts of another woman, anointed with water-drops dislodged by her lover's bud-like hand,
a wife repeatedly sprinkled her own pair of wide eyes with tears released by indignation. // MSpv 8.37 //
With the very waters by which the playful one sprinkled his beloved, constantly making her face-beauty brilliantly bright,
by those same [waters], clear as moonbeam-streaks, the rival woman's complexion was muddied from afar. // MSpv 8.38 //
Called face-to-face by her lover, his eyes blinded with passion, [but] with a transposition of names,

children.text: māninyā vapuṣi patannisargamando bhindāno hṛdayamasāhi nodavajraḥ // MSpv_8.39 //
children.translated_text: the water, naturally gentle, falling on the body of the offended proud woman, struck her heart like a thunderbolt. // MSpv 8.39 //

children.text: premṇoraḥ praṇayini siñcati priyāyāḥ saṃtāpaṃ navajalavipruṣo gṛhītvā /
children.translated_text: As he lovingly sprinkled the heart of his beloved, relieving her burning, having seized the drops of fresh water,
those [drops], scattered upward by the impact on her firm breast-surface, greatly scorched the rival woman nearby. // MSpv 8.40 //
'The water in the lake will now carry away the body-paint transferred from the beloved's chest to this virtuous woman's [body]';

children.text: tuṣṭvaivaṃ sapadi hṛte 'pi tatra tepe kasyaścitsphuṭanakhalakṣmaṇaḥ sapatnyā // MSpv_8.41 //
children.translated_text: having exulted thus, even when [the paint] was indeed washed away, a certain [rival] with visible nail-marks still burned with jealousy. // MSpv 8.41 //
Of the modest one, called by another name by a friend's lover in return, her moonlike face-beauty fading in the lake—

children.text: antadhiṃ drutamiva kartumaśruvarṣairbhūmānaṃ gamayitumīṣire payāṃsi // MSpv_8.42 //
children.translated_text: the waters seemed to hasten to hide [her] quickly, as if by showers of tears, to bring her to fullness [of concealment]. // MSpv 8.42 //
When a weak woman was first sprinkled briefly and then another was sprinkled by her affectionate [lover]—alas!—

children.text: kālimnā samadhita man.reva vaktraṃ prāpākṣṇorgaladapaśabdamañjanāmbhaḥ // MSpv_8.43 //
children.translated_text: collyrium-water, sliding from her eyes and making a false sound, darkened her face as if with anger's blackness. // MSpv 8.43 //
Unable to bear the golden ornaments, strung with lotus-stalk threads as a substitute,
the young woman's arm, bearing the weight of the side-glances of rival women, became all the heavier. // MSpv 8.44 //
The girdle-string of the women, who constantly plunged into the water, bound with many precious tinkling bells,

children.text: nārāvaṃ vyatanuta mekhalākalāpaḥ kasminvā sajalaguṇe girāṃ paṭutvam // MSpv_8.45 //
children.translated_text: produced a sound—but in what [other] instrument moistened [by water] is there eloquence of voice? // MSpv 8.45 //
When her garment was snatched away in the clear lake, by the waters, the lotus-eyed one, bashful before her master of love-arts,

children.text: suśreṇyā dalavasanena vīcihastanyastena drutamakṛtābjini sakhātvam // MSpv_8.46 //
children.translated_text: was quickly befriended by the lovely lotus-grove, with a petal-garment placed [upon her] by the wave's hand. // MSpv 8.46 //
From the women with heavy hip-surfaces, whose face-beauty surpassed blossoming lotuses,

children.text: lolatvādapaharatāṃ tadaṅgarāgasaṃjajñe sa kaluṣa āśayo jalānām // MSpv_8.47 //
children.translated_text: because of [the water's] fickleness in stealing their body-paint, the depths of the waters became turbid. // MSpv 8.47 //
Though bearing fragrance on account of the women, but having gone far from [matching] the comparison of their faces,

children.text: nedīyo jitamiti lajjayeva tāsāmālole payasi manotpalaṃ mamajja // MSpv_8.48 //
children.translated_text: the blue lotus in the swaying waters submerged, as if from shame at being surpassed by them, too near. // MSpv 8.48 //
The golden ornaments of the brides, hurriedly dropped as they plunged into the water during play, tawny from crushed jasmine,
shone in the lake like fragments of submarine fire's radiance. // MSpv 8.49 //

children.text: āsmākī yuvatidṛśāmasau tanoti cchāyeva śriyamanapāyinīṃ kimebhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This one of ours bestows upon the eyes of young women an imperishable beauty like a shadow—what need of these [ornaments]?'—
thinking thus, the waters, envious of their own beauty being concealed [by the ornaments], washed away the collyrium. // MSpv 8.50 //
When the sandal-paste was washed off by the flood of water, from the pale-complexioned woman whose highest beauty had departed,

children.text: ahnāya stanakalaśadvayādupeye vicchedaḥ sahṛdayayeva hārayaṣṭyā // MSpv_8.51 //
children.translated_text: the necklace-string seemed to separate from the pair of breast-vessels to [seek] the day, as if with sympathy. // MSpv 8.51 //
The lake, possessing the full quality of nectar, adorned with fully blooming radiant lotuses,

children.text: preyobhiḥ saha sarasī niṣevyamāṇā raktatvaṃ vyadhita vadhūdṛśāṃ surā ca // MSpv_8.52 //
children.translated_text: attended by lovers together, and wine too—[both] produced redness in the brides' eyes. // MSpv 8.52 //
The breast-vessels of the bathing beauties, speckled with large, clear water-drops, shone
as if approached on all sides by unstrung beads of necklaces, with the desirability of ornament. // MSpv 8.53 //

children.text: ārūḍhaḥ patita iti svasambhavo 'pi svacchānāṃ pariharaṇīyatāmupaiti /
children.translated_text: Even what is self-born, if risen [to prominence] and then fallen, attains the state of being rejected by the pure;
the dark blue lotuses fallen from the brides' ears were rejected by the waters with waves along the bank. // MSpv 8.54 //
The teeth [brought beauty] to the lower lip's cosmetic, the feet [brought beauty] as fresh foot-ornaments, the nails [brought beauty] to the body as unguent—

children.text: āninyuḥ śriyamadhitoyamaṅganānāṃ śobhāyai vipadi sadāśritā bhavanti // MSpv_8.55 //
children.translated_text: these brought glory to the women above the water; [for] beauties in adversity always remain devoted [to their bearers]. // MSpv 8.55 //
Of a certain woman, following her face with its washed leaf-patterns,
the tip-creepers of her curling locks, hanging heavily with water, variegated within by the mingling of filaments, produced beautiful splendor. // MSpv 8.56 //
The water carried away from the <s>Yādavas</s>' chests their thick body-unguent, and from their heads the chaplets—

children.text: netrāṇāṃ madarucirakṣataiva tasthau cakṣuṣyaḥ khalu mahatāṃ parairalaṅghyaḥ // MSpv_8.57 //
children.translated_text: yet the intoxication-beauty of [their] eyes remained untouched; indeed, what is pleasing to the eye in great men is unassailable by rivals. // MSpv 8.57 //

children.text: yo bāhyaḥ sa khalu jalairnirāsi rāgo yaścitte sa tu tadavastha eva teṣām /
children.translated_text: Whatever passion was external, that indeed was washed away by the waters; but what was in the heart, that remained as it was for them;

children.text: dhīrāṇāṃ vrajati hi sarva eva nāntaḥpātitvādabhibhavanīyatāṃ parasya // MSpv_8.58 //
children.translated_text: for in the steadfast, everything internal indeed becomes unassailable by anything external. // MSpv 8.58 //
Foam played the role of necklace on the breasts, moss [played the role] of garment-beauty on the hips,

children.text: gaṇḍeṣu sphuṭaracanābjapatrtravallī paryāptaṃ payasi vibhūṣaṇaṃ vadhūnām // MSpv_8.59 //
children.translated_text: a lotus-leaf line of clear design [played the role of beauty-mark] on the cheeks—water provided sufficient adornment for the brides. // MSpv 8.59 //
The ornaments falling from the brides' limbs into the water, heavy [as they were], sank as if from shame;

children.text: nirmālyairatha nanṛte 'vadhīritānāmapyuccairbhavati laghīyasāṃ hi dhārṣṭyam // MSpv_8.60 //
children.translated_text: then the discarded [foam and moss] floated high—for indeed, the cast-off lightweights display even greater boldness. // MSpv 8.60 //
Wiped of <s>tilaka</s>-marks' beauty, garlands removed, garment washed colorless, body-paint removed—

children.text: kāmaḥ strīranuśāyavāniva svapakṣavyāghātāditi sutarāṃ cakāra cārūḥ // MSpv_8.61 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kāma</s> (Love), as if repentant, from the ruin of his own party, made the women all the more beautiful thereby. // MSpv 8.61 //
As if the women, their bodies possessing the warmth of fresh youth, had intensely felt the cold from the waters,
a new garment was embraced upon the slopes of their breasts, [anointed] with fresh chilling [sandal-paste]. // MSpv 8.62 //
With water dripping more abundantly from the body-clinging garment-edges—as if grace itself had been liquefied—
the beloved groups then emerged from the lake, practiced in the sport of trembling wave-play. // MSpv 8.63 //
Seeing a certain woman emerging from the water, with beautiful hands [holding] quivering lotuses, creating wonder even among divine [women]—
as if [seeing] <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) herself ascending, <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) remembered the churning of another ocean. // MSpv 8.64 //
The smooth [garment] that was worn by those [women], ostensibly for concealment, clung to their thighs by contact with the water—
the very clear and shining [thighs] of the women [thereby] bore the beauty of silken cloth (<s>dukūla</s>) itself. // MSpv 8.65 //

children.text: vāsāṃsi nyavasata yāni yoṣitastāḥ śubhrābhradyutibhirahāsi tairmudeva /
children.translated_text: The garments in which the women had dressed seemed to laugh with their cloud-bright radiance, as if with joy;

children.text: atyākṣuḥ snapanagalajjalāni yāni sthūlāśrusrutibhirarodiḥ taiḥ śuceva // MSpv_8.66 //
children.translated_text: the waters sliding from the bathing [garments] seemed to weep with streams of large tears, as if with grief. // MSpv 8.66 //
The new lac-dye, even though vigorously shaken off many times, having attained a clinging surpassing [its usual] wetness,

children.text: aṅgebhyaḥ kathamapi vāmalocanāṃ viśleṣo bata navaraktakaiḥ prapede // MSpv_8.67 //
children.translated_text: somehow, alas, achieved separation from the limbs of the lovely-eyed women. // MSpv 8.67 //

children.text: pratyaṃsaṃ vilulitamūrdhajā cirāya snānārdraṃ vapurudavāpayat kilaikā /
children.translated_text: One woman, with hair tossed about on each shoulder, for a long time let her bathing-damp body remain [thus];
she did not recognize [her] desired one nearby—and that again increasingly became a stream of sweat-water. // MSpv 8.68 //
Another, tying her hair-parting with both hands, with the region of her breast-slopes and arm-roots barely visible,

children.text: bhartrānyā muhurabhilaṣyatā nidadhye naivāho viramati kautukaṃ priyebhyaḥ // MSpv_8.69 //
children.translated_text: was repeatedly gazed upon by her longing husband—ah, curiosity from loved ones never ceases! // MSpv 8.69 //
The lips of the playful women, their body-beauty purified by bathing in clear water, bright with <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) luster,

children.text: vāsaśca pratanu viviktamastvitīyānākalpo yadi kusumeṣuṇā na śūnyaḥ // MSpv_8.70 //
children.translated_text: and their garments thin and transparent—these are nothing if not [the work of] the Flower-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>). // MSpv 8.70 //
Thus, having washed away the jealousy of the matrons by immersion in the lake, having attained surpassing beauty with the radiance of spotless limbs—

children.text: avalokya tadaiva yādavānaparavārirāśeḥ śisiretararociṣāpyapāṃ tatiṣu maṅktumīṣe // MSpv_8.71 //
children.translated_text: beholding the <s>Yādavas</s>, even the sun of another ocean, with his cool rays, desired to plunge into the rows of waters. // MSpv 8.71 //
Then the warm-rayed [sun], as if unable to endure the wealth of his own burning heat,
desiring to enter the waters of another ocean, fell upon the western mountain to descend. // MSpv 9.1 //

children.text: gatayā puraḥ pratigavākṣamukhaṃ dadhatī ratena bhṛśamutsukatāṃ /
children.translated_text: A woman, with her gaze fixed before [her] at the window's opening, with great eagerness born of passion,
repeatedly measured with her eye the intervening space between the western mountain and the sun. // MSpv 9.2 //
With faded, thin, cool-bodied radiance, bearing a wan cloud-head all around,

children.text: abhavadgataḥ pariṇatiṃ śithilaḥ paramandasūryanayano divasaḥ // MSpv_9.3 //
children.translated_text: the day became transformed, languid, with the extremely dim sun as its eye. // MSpv 9.3 //
With the afternoon's cooler, gentle breeze swaying the finger-tips of creepers,

children.text: nilayāya śākhina ivāhrayate dudurākulāḥ khagakulāni giraḥ // MSpv_9.4 //
children.translated_text: the trees seemed to invite the bird-flocks, bewildered with cooing, to their dwelling-places. // MSpv 9.4 //
The [sun's] thin [radiance] at dusk remained on the mountain peaks, [just] at that moment of the cool-rayed one's [appearance];
indeed, the station of the virtuous, even at their setting, rises only higher through the net of their rays. // MSpv 9.5 //
When fate turns adverse, even great resourcefulness comes to naught;
even a thousand hands could not support the lord of the day as he was about to fall. // MSpv 9.6 //
With the western direction, whose breast-clouds were red with fresh saffron, grasping a beautiful garment in her own hand,
the cool-rayed [moon] became excessively attached, greatly following [her]. // MSpv 9.7 //
When the sun, whose radiance was like a cluster of <s>japā</s> (hibiscus) blossoms, had gone to [his] descent,
the girdle of the directions appeared as if bound at its middle with a leaf-ornament of thick, passionate <s>kuruvinda</s> (ruby). // MSpv 9.8 //
The body of the radiant one, half-submerged in the water, resembling molten gold,
shone like one half of the great cosmic egg split by the nail of <s>Brahmā</s> // <s>MSpv</s> 9.9 //
Though bearing a form that gives pleasure and inspires love in the eyes, yet causing no heat,
the courtesan of the western quarter expelled the sun, now bereft of wealth, from his sky-abode // <s>MSpv</s> 9.10 //
Gazing long at the hot-rayed one without pause, her eyes wearied from not blinking,
the lotus-pool closed its lotus-eyes, shedding tears of bee-swarms streaming down // <s>MSpv</s> 9.11 //
The sky, with stars invisible, the moon's orb unseen, the sun's light extinguished,
with diminished heat and enveloped in darkness—became as if defective from its very nature; such is the virtue of the flawed // <s>MSpv</s> 9.12 //

children.text: rucidhāmni bhartari bhṛśaṃ vimalāḥ paralokamabhyupagate vivaśuḥ /
children.translated_text: When the radiant lord, most brilliant, departed to the other world, the pure rays grieved exceedingly;

children.text: jvalanaṃ tviṣaḥ kathamitarathā sulabho 'nyajanmani sa eva patiḥ // MSpv_9.13 //
children.translated_text: how indeed could the lights enter fire?—for in another birth, that same lord is easily attained // <s>MSpv</s> 9.13 //
With hands joined in salutation by the multitude, bearing the redness of blossoming safflower,

children.text: ciramujjhitāpi tanuraujjhadasau na pitṛprasūḥ prakṛtimātmabhuvaḥ // MSpv_9.14 //
children.translated_text: even long abandoned, that slender twilight of the self-born one did not forsake her nature // <s>MSpv</s> 9.14 //
Then from the dense twilight-rays reddened, the pair of <s>cakravāka</s> birds of <s>Hari</s>, calling "heti hūti" as they flew,
fell apart separately, as if smeared with heart's blood oozing from hearts split by the pain of separation // <s>MSpv</s> 9.15 //

children.text: nilayaḥ śriyaḥ satatametaditi prathitaṃ yadeva jalajanma tayā /
children.translated_text: That the water-born lotus is always the abode of <s>Śrī</s>—this is well known; yet

children.text: divasātyayāttadapi muktamaho capalājanaṃ prati na codyamadaḥ // MSpv_9.16 //
children.translated_text: she too abandoned it at the day's end; alas, for the fickle, this is no cause for blame // <s>MSpv</s> 9.16 //
"The day has followed its friend to the horizon; what shall I, a weak woman, do here alone?"

children.text: rucibharturasya virahādhigamāditi saṃdhyayāpi sapadi vyagami // MSpv_9.17 //
children.translated_text: —so thinking, the twilight too departed at once, from the grief of separation from its lord of radiance // <s>MSpv</s> 9.17 //
When the sun fell into the ocean, as if enraged by his own reflection in it,
then darkness, murky as herds of wild elephants, spread terror all around the world // <s>MSpv</s> 9.18 //
Issuing forth from mountain caves, dense and dark as thick mud outside,
growing keen at the day's end, darkness, having come out, devoured the caves even more // <s>MSpv</s> 9.19 //
"Does it hang down from the sky attached below? Does it grow upward from the earth's surface?

children.text: visasāra tiryagatha digbhya iti pracurībhavanna niradhāri tamaḥ // MSpv_9.20 //
children.translated_text: Or does it spread sideways from the quarters?"—thus spreading abundantly, darkness could not be ascertained // <s>MSpv</s> 9.20 //
With sky and earth's surface veiled all around, as darkness blinded the eyes of people,

children.text: dadhire rasāñjanamapūrvataḥ priyaveśmavartma sudṛśo dadṛśuḥ // MSpv_9.21 //
children.translated_text: the beautiful-eyed women applied collyrium as if for the first time and beheld the path to their beloved's home // <s>MSpv</s> 9.21 //
Recognizing the gravity of its purpose, the dense darkness within darkness did not become a source of fear;

children.text: sutanoḥ stanau ca dayitopagame tanuromarājipathavepathave // MSpv_9.22 //
children.translated_text: the breasts of the slender one and the trembling on the path of the body's hair-line served the beloved's approach // <s>MSpv</s> 9.22 //

children.text: dadṛśe 'pi bhāskararucāhni na yaḥ sa tamīṃ tamobirabhigamya tatām /
children.translated_text: He who was not seen even by sunlight during the day, having approached that darkness with its darknesses,
seized radiance—the host of planets; the base become manifest through dark surroundings // <s>MSpv</s> 9.23 //
Unguents, flowers, women, those angered at their husbands, lamp-flames—
in that season all alike accomplished the awakening of long-dormant <s>Kāma</s> // <s>MSpv</s> 9.24 //
As if the canopy of the thousand radiances of the hood-gems of the serpent-king had emerged from within the earth,

children.text: sphuradaṃśujālamatha śītarucaḥ kakubhaṃ samaskuruta mādhavanīm // MSpv_9.25 //
children.translated_text: the spreading net of rays of the cool-rayed moon then made the horizon like <s>Mādhava</s>'s abode // <s>MSpv</s> 9.25 //
Encompassed by clear radiance, the form of the moon partly concealed by the eastern mountain appeared;
slowly, like the face of <s>Indra</s>'s quarter, with teeth not yet visible, as if with a coquettish smile // <s>MSpv</s> 9.26 //
With the digit of the frost-rayed moon appearing before it, faintly splitting the matted mass of darkness,

children.text: kṣaṇamabhyapadyata janairna mṛṣā gaganaṃ gaṇādipatimūrtiriti // MSpv_9.27 //
children.translated_text: for a moment the sky was not falsely perceived by people as the form of <s>Gaṇeśa</s> // <s>MSpv</s> 9.27 //
Like a crescent-moon-flower adorning the dark tresses of darkness, moist with sandal paste,

children.text: dadṛśe lalāṭataṭahāri harerharito mukhe tuhinaraśmidalam // MSpv_9.28 //
children.translated_text: the digit of the frost-rayed moon appeared, charming upon the forehead of <s>Hari</s>'s quarter's face // <s>MSpv</s> 9.28 //
First it was a digit, then a half, then the frost-rayed moon rose full and great;

children.text: dadhati dhruvaṃ kramaśa eva na tu dyutiśālino 'pi sahasopacayam // MSpv_9.29 //
children.translated_text: even the radiant ones surely attain growth only gradually, not suddenly // <s>MSpv</s> 9.29 //
The conqueror of <s>Kaiṭabha</s> rose from his couch, with the pale luster of a lotus awakened from sleep—
as if with the moon-face of the first-awakened daughter of the river-king // <s>MSpv</s> 9.30 //
Then the moon, like <s>Rāma</s> son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, having attained the beautiful form of the beloved who had come marked,
leaping across the ocean, surrounded on all sides by hosts of stars, cleft the army of <s>Rākṣasas</s> of darkness // <s>MSpv</s> 9.31 //

children.text: upajīvati sma satataṃ dadhataḥ parimugdhatāṃ vaṇigivoḍupateḥ /
children.translated_text: Continuously supporting, bearing a charming innocence, like the moon-lord of merchants,
having descended into the broad path of the dense sky, his digits served the increase of the waters' treasure // <s>MSpv</s> 9.32 //

children.text: rajanīmavāpya rucamāpa śaśī sapadi vyabhūṣayadasāvapi tām /
children.translated_text: Having attained the night, the moon gained radiance and at once adorned her too;
without delay, alas, such is the conduct of the great—mutual beneficence // <s>MSpv</s> 9.33 //
The day, weeping as it were with incessant cries, beaten by the feet of the intensely hot-rayed one,
the deer-bearing moon repeatedly caressed with its foremost rays and consoled the <s>kumudvatī</s> lotus-maiden // <s>MSpv</s> 9.34 //
The beautiful-eyed women beheld with alarm a moonstone-doll, augmented with sweat-drops born from the heat of love, as a rival wife—
from which water drops trickled under her husband's moon-rays // <s>MSpv</s> 9.35 //
With his nectar-drops the lord of herbs removed from the lotus-eyed women the poison of pride,

children.text: parito visarpi paritāpi bhṛśaṃ vapuṣo 'vatārayati mānaviṣam // MSpv_9.36 //
children.translated_text: spreading all around, burning intensely, expelling it from the body // <s>MSpv</s> 9.36 //
Reflected repeatedly in the spotless mirror-like cheek-surfaces of young women,
the moon spread forth an even denser mass of moonlight, over-illuminating the quarters // <s>MSpv</s> 9.37 //
Embracing the shores with arms of gentle waves, the rivers kissed even the lord of waters;

children.text: rajanīkaraḥ kimiva citramado yadurāgiṇāṃ gaṇamanaṅgalaghum // MSpv_9.38 //
children.translated_text: the night-maker—what wonder is it?—made the host of passionate ones light with lovesickness // <s>MSpv</s> 9.38 //
In the interiors of palaces, languidly reclining with the luster of crystal rods, dim in brightness,
<s>Kāma</s> arose, clinging to the moon-rays that entered through the lattice-windows // <s>MSpv</s> 9.39 //
<s>Kāma</s> too was surely invisible in the darkness, with his domain unperceived at first;

children.text: udite diśaḥ prakaṭayatyamunā yadagharmadhāmni dhanurācakṛṣe // MSpv_9.40 //
children.translated_text: when the hot-rayed one was absent, at the rise of this one who reveals the quarters, he drew his bow // <s>MSpv</s> 9.40 //
When the moon's blooming and rising occurred simultaneously, the arrow-host of the flower-bowed one found

children.text: drutametya puṣpadhanuṣo dhanuṣaḥ kumude 'ṅganāmanasi cāvasaram // MSpv_9.41 //
children.translated_text: an opening quickly, arriving at the night-lotus and at the hearts of women alike // <s>MSpv</s> 9.41 //
Suddenly illuminating the faces of the quarters, producing excessive agitation for lovemaking,
the moon kindled another fire—that born from the eyes of the flower-arrowed <s>Kāma</s> // <s>MSpv</s> 9.42 //
Thus, those women certain of their beloved's arrival, compassionate when the cool-rayed moon appeared,

children.text: pratikarma kartumucakramire samaye hi sarvamupakāri kṛtam // MSpv_9.43 //
children.translated_text: set about performing their toilette; for at the right time, everything done becomes helpful // <s>MSpv</s> 9.43 //
The slender-waisted one's breast-slopes and pearl-necklace bore one and the same ornament;

children.text: ghaṭate hi saṃhatatayā janitāmidameva nirviratāṃ dadhatoḥ // MSpv_9.44 //
children.translated_text: for indeed, what is joined in unity creates this very cessation of distinction between the two that bear it // <s>MSpv</s> 9.44 //
With thighs beautiful as plantain stalks, upon the broad expanse of her hips,
the bride bound with the string of her girdle-cord the elephant of the <s>makara</s>-bannered <s>Kāma</s> // <s>MSpv</s> 9.45 //
<s>Alaktaka</s> (lac-dye) on the lips, <s>lodhra</s> powder pure on the cheek-surface of the beautiful-eyed women,
fresh collyrium on the lotus-eyes—none differed from the water placed in the conch-shell // <s>MSpv</s> 9.46 //
With gleaming radiant lip-petals, with rays of bright teeth all around,
with charming cheek-surfaces held, the women shone with their blossoming face-lotuses // <s>MSpv</s> 9.47 //
One who is excessively defeated goes abroad, or the clever one enters thereafter;
the moon, with a face of bright cheeks, therefore entered the women's homes under the pretext of a reflection // <s>MSpv</s> 9.48 //
Surely <s>Kāma</s>'s arrows met with resistance on the great hard surface of the breasts;
unlike on other limbs, they did not attain slenderness there, though weighed down by heaviness and clinging // <s>MSpv</s> 9.49 //
Even among charming things, the mind of the discerning does not rest without finding special distinction;

children.text: gṛhameṣyati priyatame sudṛśāṃ vasanāṅgarāgasumanaḥsu manaḥ // MSpv_9.50 //
children.translated_text: "My beloved will come home"—the mind of the beautiful-eyed ones dwelt upon garments, body-paint, and flowers // <s>MSpv</s> 9.50 //
The bride did not anoint her body, out of fear that it would obstruct the pleasure of embrace;
this indeed is fitting: that in meetings with the beloved there is no anointing—this is the very proof // <s>MSpv</s> 9.51 //
Another woman, from the breath-exhalations of her face-lotus slipping from the surface of her own hand-petals,
examining slowly, delighted in her mouth-fragrance through the rising scent from her nostrils // <s>MSpv</s> 9.52 //

children.text: vidhṛte divā savayasā ca puraḥ paripūrṇamaṇḍalavikāśabhṛti /
children.translated_text: During the day with her companion, and at night before the full-orbed

children.text: himadhāmni darpaṇatale ca muhuḥ svamukhaśriyaṃ mṛgadṛśo dadṛśuḥ // MSpv_9.53 //
children.translated_text: frost-rayed moon and on the mirror's surface, the doe-eyed women repeatedly beheld the beauty of their own faces // <s>MSpv</s> 9.53 //
Placing her arm upon her knee, with her bent hand-petal resting on her cheek-surface,
eager, near the water, with a sweet-voiced song empty of melody in the throat's turning // <s>MSpv</s> 9.54 //
Sweet, skilled in revealing affection, supremely captivating the hearts of desired ones,

children.text: prajighāya kāntamanu mugdhatarastaruṇījano dṛśa ivātha sakhīḥ // MSpv_9.55 //
children.translated_text: the young woman's company of friends then sent forth glances after the beloved, as if more innocent messengers // <s>MSpv</s> 9.55 //

children.text: na ca me 'vagacchati yathā laghutāṃ karuṇāṃ yathā ca kurute sa mayi /
children.translated_text: "He does not understand my lightness, nor what compassion he shows me—

children.text: nipuṇaṃ tathainamupagamya vaderabhidūti kāciditi saṃdidiśe // MSpv_9.56 //
children.translated_text: go to him skillfully and speak thus, O messenger"—so one woman instructed // <s>MSpv</s> 9.56 //
Even unasked, the friend hastened to the beloved of the proud woman who was with another;

children.text: kimu coditāḥ priyahitārthakṛtaḥ kṛtino bhavanti suhṛdaḥ suhṛdām // MSpv_9.57 //
children.translated_text: what need to be urged?—accomplished friends are self-motivated in working for the welfare of friends // <s>MSpv</s> 9.57 //

children.text: pratibhidya kāntamaparādhakṛtaṃ yadi tāvadasya punareva mayā /
children.translated_text: "If I first rebuff my beloved for his offense, and then

children.text: kriyate 'nuvṛttirucitaiva tataḥ kalayedamānamanasaṃ sakhi mām // MSpv_9.58 //
children.translated_text: once again show him compliance—that is fitting; but, O friend, consider me as one whose pride is intact" // <s>MSpv</s> 9.58 //

children.text: avadhīrya dhairyakalitā dayitaṃ vidadhe virodhamatha tena saha /
children.translated_text: Having spurned her beloved with composure of fortitude, she then made a quarrel with him;

children.text: tava gopyate kimiva kartumidaṃ na sahāsmi sāhasamasāhasikī // MSpv_9.59 //
children.translated_text: "What is concealed from you? I am not bold enough to do this; I am no daring woman" // <s>MSpv</s> 9.59 //

children.text: tadupetya mā sma tamupālabhathāḥ kla doṣamasya na hi vidma vayam /
children.translated_text: "Go to him, do not reproach him—indeed we do not know his fault"—

children.text: iti sampradhārya ramaṇāya vadhūrvihitāgase 'pi visasarja sakhīṃ // MSpv_9.60 //
children.translated_text: thus reflecting, the bride dispatched her friend even to the offending lover // <s>MSpv</s> 9.60 //

children.text: nanu sandiśeti sudṛśoditayā trapayā na kiñcana kilābhidadhe /
children.translated_text: "Send a message then"—told by the beautiful-eyed one, from modesty she uttered nothing at all;

children.text: nijamaikṣi mandamaniśaṃ niśitaiḥ kraśitaṃ śarīramaśīraśaraiḥ // MSpv_9.61 //
children.translated_text: she merely gazed at her own body, constantly wasted by the sharp, cold arrows of <s>Kāma</s> // <s>MSpv</s> 9.61 //
The messenger-women, approaching boldly like another man, spoke words pregnant with deep meaning;
even what seems contrary to nature shines forth for the purpose of a friend's welfare when done by the upright-minded // <s>MSpv</s> 9.62 //
"He who stole my fame of beauty in the world—thereafter this one has entered my heart;"

children.text: tvayi matsarādiva nirastadayaḥ sutarāṃ kṣiṇoti khalu tāṃ madanaḥ // MSpv_9.63 //
children.translated_text: as if from jealousy toward you, he shows no mercy—truly <s>Kāma</s> excessively diminishes her // <s>MSpv</s> 9.63 //

children.text: tava sā kathāsu parighaṭṭayati śravaṇaṃ yadaṅgulimukhena muhuḥ /
children.translated_text: "That she repeatedly presses her ear with her fingertip during conversations about you—

children.text: ghanatāṃ dhruvaṃ nayati tena bhavadguṇapūgapūritamatṛptatayā // MSpv_9.64 //
children.translated_text: she surely makes it denser thereby, unsatisfied, filled with the multitude of your virtues" // <s>MSpv</s> 9.64 //
The dark-lotus-eyed one, tormented by sighs of no small heat,

children.text: dravatāṃ na netumadharaṃ kṣamate navanāgavallidalarāgarasaḥ // MSpv_9.65 //
children.translated_text: the juice of fresh <s>nāgavallī</s> (betel) leaf-color on the lip cannot lead to melting // <s>MSpv</s> 9.65 //
The arrows of the lord of love clearly attain sharpness when they have eyes of <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus) petals;
they pierced even the heart, though shielded by the unbroken, great, hard circle of breasts // <s>MSpv</s> 9.66 //
That the body of the smile-eyed one is more tender than even a flower—not otherwise;

children.text: aniśaṃ nijairakaruṇaḥ karuṇaṃ kusumeṣuruttapāti yadviśikhaiḥ // MSpv_9.67 //
children.translated_text: for the merciless flower-arrowed <s>Kāma</s> constantly burns pitifully with his own arrows // <s>MSpv</s> 9.67 //
It is true that everything approached with wrong conduct assumes the nature of poison;

children.text: amṛtutasru'pi virahādbhavato yadamūṃ dahanti himaraśmirucaḥ // MSpv_9.68 //
children.translated_text: for even the rays of the nectar-rayed [moon], though shedding nectar, burn her due to separation from you. // MSpv_9.68 //

children.text: uditaṃ priyāṃ prati sahārdamiti śradadhīyata priyatamena vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: The words spoken half-earnestly to his beloved were believed by the dearest one,

children.text: viditeṅgite hi pura eva jane sapadīritāḥ khalu laganti giraḥ // MSpv_9.69 //
children.translated_text: for in a person whose gestures are already understood, words spoken with sincerity indeed take hold. // MSpv_9.69 //
With the mind of the young men stolen by their beloveds, as if having first gone into bewilderment,

children.text: udite tataḥ sapadi labdhapadaiḥ kṣaṇadākare 'nupadibhiḥ prayaye // MSpv_9.70 //
children.translated_text: and then suddenly, when the moon rose, finding footing with steps that followed one after another, they set forth. // MSpv_9.70 //
From the ear of the dark-browed one, trembling with excitement, fell a jingling cluster of ornaments,
like a lotus pushed upward by the spreading gaze of the beloved's eyes, blossoming upon seeing [him]. // MSpv_9.71 //
As if to carry her swiftly to the heights of heaven, seized by the pair of her breasts,

children.text: rabhasotthitāmupagataḥ sahasā parirabhya kañcana vadhūmarudhat // MSpv_9.72 //
children.translated_text: a certain [youth], having approached the bride who rose impetuously, suddenly embraced her and made her ascend. // MSpv_9.72 //
A mirror, bearing the heavy reflection of the bridegroom who had come close to her body,

children.text: mukureṇa vepathubhṛto 'tibharāt kathamapyapāti na vadhūkarataḥ // MSpv_9.73 //
children.translated_text: somehow did not fall from the trembling bride's hand, despite the excessive weight. // MSpv_9.73 //
Bending down and tightly embracing her, with her pair of breasts sunk into his chest,
the beloved caused the bride to emit the sound of the small bells and girdle-chains swaying at that moment. // MSpv_9.74 //
When the beloved approached her whose garment-knot was held by his hand, from the one whose seat was not free from haste,
the garment slipped, revealing thighs that shone like a golden slab glimpsed for a moment. // MSpv_9.75 //

children.text: pidadhānamanvagupagamya dṛśau bruvate janāya vada ko 'yamiti /
children.translated_text: Approaching from behind, covering her eyes and saying to the people, 'Tell me, who is this?'

children.text: abhidhātumadhyavasasau na girā pulakaiḥ priyaṃ navavadhūnyagadat // MSpv_9.76 //
children.translated_text: the new bride, unable to speak in words, conveyed her beloved through her horripilation. // MSpv_9.76 //
The body of the beautiful woman — with intense modesty making it excessively trembling, overcome before her husband, distressed with shame —
yet proclaiming the excellence of affection, though bewildered in understanding, became even more [beautiful]. // MSpv_9.77 //
In the ceremony of attending upon their husbands, the women with heavy, rounded hips,
though stumbling at every step, attained the utmost heights of love through their limping gaits. // MSpv_9.78 //

children.text: madhurānnatabhrū lalitaṃ ca dṛśoḥ sakaraprayogacaturaṃ ca vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: A sweet arching of the brow and a charming glance from the eyes, and speech skillful in the art of hand-gestures,
natural yet cleverly learned — such were the playful dance-movements of the slender-bodied one. // MSpv_9.79 //

children.text: tadayuktamaṅga tava viśvasṛjā na kṛtaṃ yadīkṣaṇasahasratayam /
children.translated_text: It was unfitting, O beautiful one, that you were not made thousand-eyed by the creator of the world,

children.text: prakaṭīkṛtā jagati yena khalu sphuṭamindratādya mayi gotrabhidā // MSpv_9.80 //
children.translated_text: whereby the identity of <s>Indra</s> — now clearly revealed in the world by the mountain-splitter — [would be evident] in me today. // MSpv_9.80 //
You do not perceive me, though present before your very eyes, because of your excessive closeness,

children.text: hṛdayasthitāmapi punaḥ paritaḥ kathamīkṣate bahirabhīṣṭatāmām // MSpv_9.81 //
children.translated_text: yet how do you look outward on all sides for the desired one who dwells in your heart? // MSpv_9.81 //
Having said this, wishing to go, [he looked upon her] whose face blossomed with a momentary glance,
and a certain young man, whose beloved's loosened girdle-bells slipped as she released her hold on his hand... // MSpv_9.82 //

children.text: apayāti saroṣayā niraste kṛtakaṃ kāmini cukṣuṣe mṛgākṣyā /
children.translated_text: Dismissed with feigned anger by the deer-eyed one, 'Your love is false, O lover!' —
even so, though pained, he stood still; for who else, tripped by an ill omen, [would not halt]? // MSpv_9.83 //

children.text: ālokya priyatamamaṃśuke vinīvau yattasthe nāmitamukhendu mānavatyā /
children.translated_text: Seeing her dearest one, the proud lady stood with garment-knot [held and] face-moon bent down,
and surely that became the foothold of her pride, which had quickly taken to flight. // MSpv_9.84 //
The breast-burden of the beautiful woman — hot with the warmth of youth, from having been tightly embraced by her beloved who was burning with the heat of passion from separation —

children.text: kathamapyabhavatsmarānaloṣmaṇaḥ stanabhāro na nakhaṃpacaḥ priyasya // MSpv_9.85 //
children.translated_text: somehow did not scald her beloved, though it bore the fire of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love). // MSpv_9.85 //
Bearing a pair of breasts cool as the earth, like <s>Urvaśī</s> herself descended to the surface of the earth,

children.text: babhau mukhenāpratimena kācana śriyādhikā tāṃ prati menakā ca na // MSpv_9.86 //
children.translated_text: a certain woman shone with an incomparable face; in beauty, she surpassed even <s>Menakā</s>. // MSpv_9.86 //

children.text: itthaṃ nārīrghaṭayitumalaṃ kāmibhiḥ kāmamāsan prāleyāṃśoḥ sapadi rucayaḥ śāntamānāntarāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, the rays of the cool-rayed one [the moon], with their obstacles of pride now calmed, were sufficient to unite women with their lovers;

children.text: ācāryatvaṃ ratiṣu vilasanmanmathaśrīvilāsā hrīpratyūhapraśamakuśalāḥ śīdhavaścakrurāsām // MSpv_9.87 //
children.translated_text: and the wines — shining with the splendor of <s>Manmatha</s>'s (the love-god's) beauty, playing the role of teacher in the arts of love, skilled in calming the impediment of modesty — performed [the same] for them. // MSpv_9.87 //
Then, the faces of the young men — fragrant, with eyes blossoming like lotuses,

children.text: āyuṣaḥ śughaṭitāni surāyāḥ pātratāṃ priyatamāvadanāni // MSpv_10.1 //
children.translated_text: well-fashioned by the wine of life — became vessels [worthy of admiration] for their beloveds. // MSpv_10.1 //
With courtesy, with deliberation set aside, with unquenched thirst [expressed] through words of longing,

children.text: te muhūrtamatha mūrtamapīpyan prama mānamavadhūya vadhūḥ svāḥ // MSpv_10.2 //
children.translated_text: they then, for a moment, kissed their brides — embodied [passion], having cast aside pride. // MSpv_10.2 //
In the wine reflecting the beloved and unbeloved faces, with the fragrance of the young mango broken [and mixed in],

children.text: svāduni praṇaditālini śīte nirvivāra madhunīndriyavargaḥ // MSpv_10.3 //
children.translated_text: sweet, with bees humming, and cool — the group of senses found unrestricted [delight]. // MSpv_10.3 //
The six-legged one [bee], intoxicated and whirling about, fragrant with <s>kāpiśāyana</s> (wine), alighted

children.text: phulladṛṣṭi vadanaṃ pramadānāmabjacāru caṣakaṃ ca ṣaḍaṅdhriḥ // MSpv_10.4 //
children.translated_text: equally upon the lotus-beautiful faces of the women and upon the drinking cups with blossoming [reflections]. // MSpv_10.4 //
Knowing that the lotus [reflected] in the cup filled with flowing wine was [merely] a reflection of the young woman's [eye],

children.text: ghrātumakṣi patati bhramaraḥ sma bhrāntibhāji bhavati kva vivekaḥ // MSpv_10.5 //
children.translated_text: the bee nonetheless fell upon it to smell — where indeed is discernment in one subject to delusion? // MSpv_10.5 //
The wine given by the most beloved [wife] indeed attained rich flavor as the husband drank,
since [the cup] was attended upon by the rays of her golden crown, though themselves devoid of consciousness. // MSpv_10.6 //
Through the tasting by the slender-bodied one, the flavor of the [wine at the] lip was experienced without discrimination as something else,

children.text: anyamanyadiva yanmanadhu yūnaḥ svādamiṣṭamataniṣṭa tadeva // MSpv_10.7 //
children.translated_text: for the wine that was sweet and desired by the young man — that very same [thing] was something different, as it were. // MSpv_10.7 //
Bearing excessive sweetness, [the wine and the lips] were drunk simultaneously by the passionate ones;
by faces [blooming] with the sweet flavor and blossoming [lotuses], and by nostrils, the fragrance of the dark lotus [was inhaled]. // MSpv_10.8 //
The faithful wife, in her beloved one's favored [cup], bit the lip-edge [of the cup] that tasted equal to wine;

children.text: labhyate sma pariraktatayātmā yāvakena viyatāpi yuvatyāḥ // MSpv_10.9 //
children.translated_text: and the self of the young woman, though separated by lac-dye, was obtained through her embrace. // MSpv_10.9 //
Of a certain one, deeply engrossed in drinking from the face of his captivating beloved as if it were equal to passion,

children.text: svāditaḥ sakṛdivāsava eva pratyuta kṣaṇavidaṃśapade 'bhūt // MSpv_10.10 //
children.translated_text: the wine, tasted but once, became on the contrary an occasion for biting at every moment. // MSpv_10.10 //
Between the faces of the couples who had drunk sweet and cool wine, [abandoned] within the cups,
the dark lotus descended below, as if weeping with the sounds of bees — out of shame. // MSpv_10.11 //
Among those [women] who had become emboldened by their rival [drink of] <s>trisaraka</s> (triple-distilled wine), there arose charming banter,
delightful with crooked word-play, with laughter that hinted at hidden secrets, among the fair-browed ones. // MSpv_10.12 //

children.text: hāvakāri hasitaṃ vacanānāṃ khauśalaṃ dṛśi vikāraviśeṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Flirtatious laughter, cleverness of speech, special changes in the glance —

children.text: cakire bhṛśamṛjorapi vadhvāḥ kāmineva taruṇena madena // MSpv_10.13 //
children.translated_text: all these were produced in the bride, though naturally straightforward, by the youthful intoxication, as if by a lover. // MSpv_10.13 //
Whether the hearts of the brides — displeased toward the offending husband, ablaze with anger, their composure overthrown —

children.text: kṣālitaṃ nu śamitaṃ nu vadhūnāṃ dravitaṃ nu hṛdayaṃ madhuvāraiḥ // MSpv_10.14 //
children.translated_text: were washed clean, or pacified, or melted by the streams of wine — [who can say]? // MSpv_10.14 //
The intoxication of the women, which had always existed but was unmanifested due to being long-established in their nature, [was now displayed] in [their] radiant limbs,

children.text: vibhramaṃ madhumadaḥ pramadānāṃ dhātulīnamupasarga ivārtham // MSpv_10.15 //
children.translated_text: as the prefix [<s>upasarga</s>] brings forth the meaning that lies latent in the verbal root [<s>dhātu</s>] — so did the wine-intoxication [bring forth] their <s>vibhrama</s> (amorous confusion). // MSpv_10.15 //
Half-spoken words, neglect of garlands and garments and ornaments that had become loose,
rising without reason to walk — all these displayed the amorous confusion born of intoxication in them. // MSpv_10.16 //
By the new bride whose modesty slowly dissolved through drink, with eyes whose lashes were slightly parted,
the face of her lover was gazed upon gradually — though she remained downcast-faced. // MSpv_10.17 //
She who had previously, with difficulty, grown bold toward her beloved only through the words of her friend —

children.text: vrīḍājāḍyamabhajanmadhupā sā svāṃ madātprakṛtimeti hi sarvaḥ // MSpv_10.18 //
children.translated_text: that wine-drinking one abandoned [her] bashful stiffness; for everyone returns to their own nature through intoxication. // MSpv_10.18 //

children.text: chāditaḥ kathamapi trapayayāntaryaḥ priyaṃ prati cirāya ramaṇyāḥ /
children.translated_text: The inner [passion] of the beautiful woman, long concealed by modesty toward her beloved,
now, through the bold advance of wine-intoxication, became as if visible through the eyes, like passion [itself]. // MSpv_10.19 //
For the fair-browed women who wished to send away their beloved ones who had come [back] without heeding their departures,

children.text: prāpi cetasi savipratisāre subhruvāmavasaraḥ sarakeṇa // MSpv_10.20 //
children.translated_text: an opportunity was found by the wine — [entering] their hearts, along with remorse. // MSpv_10.20 //
'Let me not again send away that offending one, bewildered in mind by intoxication' —

children.text: yoṣidityabhilāṣa na hālāṃ dustyajaḥ khalu sukhādapi mānaḥ // MSpv_10.21 //
children.translated_text: [thinking thus,] a woman did not [drink] the wine; for pride is harder to abandon than even pleasure. // MSpv_10.21 //
The wine removed the delusion of modesty from the beloveds and led them nearby for the pleasure of love;

children.text: saprasādamiva sevitamāsītsadya eva phaladaṃ madhu tāsām // MSpv_10.22 //
children.translated_text: the wine, served with grace, became fruit-bearing for them that very day. // MSpv_10.22 //
The wine given by the beloved, pervaded by an exceedingly sharp flavor,

children.text: sasvade mukhasuraṃ pramadābhyo nāma rūḍhamapi ca vyudapādi // MSpv_10.23 //
children.translated_text: tasted like the divine drink to the women — and indeed, even what is well-established [in name] was surpassed. // MSpv_10.23 //
The fragrance — having acquired the quality of sweetness from both the wines and the cup-like faces of the women —
through the mutual combination [sensed by] the delighted bees, attained a transcendent otherness. // MSpv_10.24 //

children.text: mānabhaṅgapacaṭunā suratecchāṃ tanvatā prathayatā dṛśi rāgam /
children.translated_text: By the wine, which was adept at breaking down pride, which extended the desire for love, which spread passion in the eyes,

children.text: lebhire sapadi bhāvayatāntaryoṣitaḥ praṇayineva madena // MSpv_10.25 //
children.translated_text: and which nurtured [feeling] within — the women instantly received [it] as if [it were] a lover. // MSpv_10.25 //
The fair-browed ones, skilled in secret kissing, with fresh <s>yāvaka</s> (lac) color on their lips washed away by drinking,
re-colored their own lower lips with the lip-color-juice of their beloveds. // MSpv_10.26 //
When wine was offered by the beloved to another young woman, calling her by name, even while she was speaking,

children.text: ujjhati sma madamapyapibantī vīkṣya madyamitarā tu mamāda // MSpv_10.27 //
children.translated_text: the other one, [merely] watching the drink, lost even her intoxication — while the first continued to drink. // MSpv_10.27 //
By the woman who suspected that the lord of her heart had his mind gone to another woman,
even though she had drunk much wine, no joy arose — for intoxication is the cause [only] for a happy mind. // MSpv_10.28 //
The angry one, having refused his entreaties, then came [back], her delusion wrought by wine-intoxication,
and, her heart distressed by separation, she herself coaxed the very beloved she had angered. // MSpv_10.29 //
By the intoxication that caused the drooping of limbs and the closing of pairs of eyes, that stilled their speech,

children.text: īrṣyayeva haratā hriyamāsāṃ tadguṇaḥ svayamakāri madena // MSpv_10.30 //

skilled at dispelling the fatigue-sweat from the vigorous love-play of young women intoxicated by the ungovernable passion of blossoming youth. // MSpv_11.19 //
With drooping eye-stars, their faces' moon-orbs wasted, their eyes like blue lotuses languid with sleeplessness,

children.text: timiramiva dadhānāḥ sraṃsinaḥ keśapāśān avanipatigṛhebhyo yāntyamūrvāravadhvaḥ // MSpv_11.20 //
children.translated_text: wearing their loosened tresses like darkness — the courtesans go forth from the kings' palaces. // MSpv_11.20 //
Having kept company with the cool-rayed [moon] at day's end, this night now departs swiftly, fragrant with breath-perfume,

children.text: vrajati rajanireṣā tanmayūkhāṅgarāgaiḥ parimalitamanindyairambarāntaṃ vahantī // MSpv_11.21 //
children.translated_text: carrying to the sky's interior the body-unguent of its [moon's] rays, anointed with blameless [fragrance]. // MSpv_11.21 //
Having stayed awake beyond even the remaining watches in the sport of laughing with the beauty of fresh <s>kumuda</s> (night-lotus) groves,

children.text: ayamaparadiśo 'ṅge muñcati srastahastaḥ śiśayiṣurapi pāṇḍuṃ mlānamātmānaminduḥ // MSpv_11.22 //
children.translated_text: this moon now releases his pale, wilting self upon the body of the western direction, with drooping hand, though still wishing to sleep. // MSpv_11.22 //
That garment which was cast aside throughout the night by the beloved in the impetuosity of passionate embraces —

children.text: vasanamapi niśānte neṣyate tatpradātu rathacaraṇaviśālaśreṇilolekṣaṇena // MSpv_11.23 //
children.translated_text: at night's end, it is brought back to give to the woman by one whose wide, chariot-wheel-row-like rolling eyes [betray desire]. // MSpv_11.23 //

children.text: sapadi kumudinībhirmīlitaṃ hā kṣapāpi kṣayamagamadapetāstārakāstāḥ samastāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Alas, the night too has ended, the <s>kumuda</s>-lotuses have closed, all those stars have departed!' —

children.text: iti dayitakalatraścintayannaṅgamindur vahati kṛśamaśeṣaṃ bhraṣṭaśobhaṃ śuceva // MSpv_11.24 //
children.translated_text: thus thinking of his beloved wives, the moon bears his entire [form] emaciated, fallen from beauty, as if with grief. // MSpv_11.24 //
Before the sun reaches the range of the eyes, all the darkness is already destroyed by <s>Aruṇa</s> (Dawn);

children.text: paraparibhavi tejastanvatāmāśu kartuṃ prabhavati hi vipakṣocchedamagresaro 'pi // MSpv_11.25 //
children.translated_text: for even a forerunner is capable of quickly effecting the destruction of adversaries, for those whose power outshines all rivals. // MSpv_11.25 //

children.text: vigatatimirapaṅgaṃ paśyati vyoma yāvad dhuvati virahakhinnaḥ pakṣatī yāvadeva /
children.translated_text: Just as one sees the sky freed of darkness's veil, just as the love-sick [bird] shakes its wings —
so the <s>cakravākī</s> (ruddy sheldrake hen), driven by eagerness summoned by the sound like chariot-wheels, comes from the far bank of the river. // MSpv_11.26 //
Both equally brought delight to joyful young men's minds at dusk, both were adorned and embellished;
but at dawn, the flower-garlands, beautiful with fragrance, were surpassed by the young women after love-enjoyment — [the garlands] having lost their luster. // MSpv_11.27 //
With tossed lotus-masses, scattered creeper-canopies, shaking all blossoms from every tree in every grove,
this restless wind somewhere attains steadiness within the fragrance-chambers, from crushing the flowers [that adorned] the young women. // MSpv_11.28 //

children.text: nakhapadavalinābhīsandhibhāgeṣu lakṣyaḥ kṣatiṣu ca daśanānāmaṅganāyāḥ saśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Visible in the joints of nail-scratched navel-folds and in the wounds of teeth-marks on the woman's body —

children.text: api rahasi kṛtānāṃ vāgvihīno 'pijātaḥ suratavilasitānāṃ varṇako varṇako 'sau // MSpv_11.29 //
children.translated_text: that [evidence], though wordless, has become a narrator of the secret love-sports — that color [on the body] is itself the describer. // MSpv_11.29 //
This moonlight, with manifestly soiled beauty, its leaf-ornament patterns rubbed off, having acquired the beauty of love-making, bereft of [former] splendor at dawn —

children.text: upahasita ivāsau cāndramāḥ kāminīnāṃ pariṇataśarakāṇḍāpāṇḍubhirgaṇḍabhāgaiḥ // MSpv_11.30 //
children.translated_text: seems mocked by the faces of the amorous women, whose cheek-regions are pale as ripe arrow-reed stalks. // MSpv_11.30 //
Though all the body-paint of the women, wanton with passion, was broken by the tumult of love-play,

children.text: idamatimahadevāścaryamāścaryadhāmnastava khalu mukharāgo yanna bhedaṃ prayātaḥ // MSpv_11.31 //
children.translated_text: this is the supreme wonder of you, O exceedingly wondrous one [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], that your face-color has undergone no change. // MSpv_11.31 //

children.text: prakaṭataramimaṃ mā drākṣuranyā ramaṇyaḥ sphuṭamiti saviśaṅgaṃ kāntayā tulyavarṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Lest other lovely women see this [mark] more clearly' — so, with apprehension, by the beloved who shares your complexion,

children.text: caraṇatalasarojākrāntisaṃkrāntayāsau vapuṣi nakhavilekho lākṣayā rakṣitaste // MSpv_11.32 //
children.translated_text: this nail-scratch on your body from the tread of her lotus-foot-sole has been concealed with lac-dye of the same color. // MSpv_11.32 //
'What you said was indeed true — that you came to my dwelling wearing the garment enjoyed by a beloved woman;

children.text: madadhivasatimāgāḥkāmināṃ maṇḍanaśrīrvrajati hi saphalatvaṃ vallabhālokanena // MSpv_11.33 //
children.translated_text: for indeed the beauty of women's adornment attains its fruition through the beloved's gaze.' // MSpv_11.33 //

children.text: navanakhapadamaṅgaṃ gopayasyaṃśukena sthagayasi punaroṣṭhaṃ pāṇinā dantadaṣṭam /
children.translated_text: 'You conceal the fresh nail-mark on your body with cloth, you cover again with your hand the lip bitten by teeth;

children.text: pratidiśamaparastrīsaṅgaśaṃsī visarpannavaparimalagandhaḥ kena śakyo varītum // MSpv_11.34 //
children.translated_text: but the fragrance of fresh perfume spreading in every direction, betraying union with another woman — by what can that be checked?' // MSpv_11.34 //
Having spoken thus, when a certain [lover], approaching fearfully the one whose tears flow from her eyes, bows at her feet —

children.text: karuṇamapi samarthaṃ mānināṃ mānabhede ruditamuditamastraṃ yoṣitāṃ vigraheṣu // MSpv_11.35 //
children.translated_text: the piteous yet powerful weeping of proud women becomes a mighty weapon for women in quarrels, [bringing] victory even through tears. // MSpv_11.35 //
In the houses where boldness was made manifest by the blossoming intoxication of <s>Madana's</s> (Love's) passion, adorned with ornaments scattered in love-quarrels —

children.text: vidadhati na gṛheṣūtphullapuṣpopahāraṃ viphalavinayayatnāḥ kāminīnāṃ vayasyāḥ // MSpv_11.36 //
children.translated_text: the friends of the amorous women, whose efforts at discipline proved futile, do not offer the fresh flower-oblations. // MSpv_11.36 //
When she angrily suspects from jealousy that the nail-and-teeth marks visible on [his] body were caused by another woman —

children.text: smarasi na khalu dattaṃ mattayaitattvayaiva striyamanunayatītthaṃ vrīḍamānāṃ vilāsī // MSpv_11.37 //
children.translated_text: 'Do you not remember? These were given by you yourself in your intoxication!' — thus the gallant consoles the embarrassed one. // MSpv_11.37 //
When the husband, having embraced her, breaking the heavy pearl-necklace, takes leave to depart while her body goes limp —
the breast-pair of the helpless woman at that moment seems to weep, with drops of large, fresh, loosened pearl-tears. // MSpv_11.38 //

children.text: bahujagadapurastāttasya mattā kilāhaṃ cakara ca kila cāṭu prauḍhayoṣidvadasya /
children.translated_text: 'I indeed was intoxicated before so many people and spoke love-words as a bold woman would to her [lover]' —

children.text: viditamiti sakhībhyo rātrivṛttaṃ vicintya vyapagatamadayāhni vrīḍitaṃ mugdhavadhvā // MSpv_11.39 //
children.translated_text: reflecting thus on the night's events now known to her friends, the innocent bride feels shame in the daytime, her intoxication departed. // MSpv_11.39 //
With hands and foot-tips lovely as rows of red water-[flowers], with eyes like blue lotuses [lined with] abundant dark bee-row kohl,

children.text: anupatati virāvaiḥ patriṇāṃ vyāharantī rajanimacirajātā pūrvasandhyā suteva // MSpv_11.40 //
children.translated_text: speaking with the cries of birds that follow her — the early dawn follows night as if [her] recently-born daughter. // MSpv_11.40 //
At each shelter, by the foremost among priests, who had kindled fires with unextinguished flames, having recited the <s>sāmidhenī</s> (kindling hymns) with libations prescribed by rule,
having performed the destruction of great heaps of sin — the fire, licked by the oblation, was properly consumed with the <s>sāmnāyya</s> (Vedic chant). // MSpv_11.41 //
Of those engaged in their <s>japa</s> (prayer recitation) rituals, the face with its pearl-like teeth [visible] through lip-movements, half-concealed by labial syllables, perceived by others —

children.text: anukṛtimanuvelaṃ ghaṭṭitodghaṭṭitasya vrajati niyamabhājāṃ mugdhamuktāpuṭasya // MSpv_11.42 //
children.translated_text: goes on as an imitation of the constantly opened and closed [lips], like the innocent opening of a pearl-casket of the disciplined ones. // MSpv_11.42 //

children.text: navakanakapiśaṅgaṃ vāsarāṇāṃ vidhātuḥ kakubhi kuliśapāṇerbhāti bhāsāṃ vitānam /
children.translated_text: On the horizon of the maker of days, the canopy of rays shines, fresh-gold-tawny, in the quarter of the thunderbolt-wielder (<s>Indra</s>);
as if the submarine fire's flame, having begun the burning of the world, having consumed the waters, blazes upward from the great ocean. // MSpv_11.43 //
With rays resembling widely spread broad leather straps, like a great pitcher being drawn up by the directions,
with the tumult of cries of restless birds — this sun is being pulled up from the midst of the ocean-waters. // MSpv_11.44 //
[The sun], having been submerged in the ocean's waters at night, constantly heated by the flame of the submarine fire without cease —
that is why this <s>Vivasvān</s> (Sun) now rises, bearing a body pale as the embers of burning <s>khadira</s> (acacia) wood. // MSpv_11.45 //

children.text: atuhinarucināsau kevalaṃ nodayādriḥ kṣaṇamuparigatena kṣmābhṛtaḥ sarva eva /
children.translated_text: Not by the sun alone is this the Rising Mountain — for a moment, with the sun above, every mountain,
with clusters of fresh rays like bunches of <s>bandhūka</s> (scarlet ixora) flowers, seems to bear a crest-jewel. // MSpv_11.46 //
Still prancing on the forecourts of the sunrise-peak's summit, gazed upon by the lotus-pools with smiling lotus-faces,

children.text: vitatamṛdukarāgraḥ śabdayantyā vayobhiḥ paripatati divo 'ṅgake helayā bālasūryaḥ // MSpv_11.47 //
children.translated_text: his soft ray-tips extended, with the flocks of birds making noise — the young sun playfully roams the sky's body. // MSpv_11.47 //
Having sat for a moment with feet placed upon the earth's surface, having observed the world pleased and bowing in reverence before him,
the seven-horsed one [Sun], about to survey the entire surface of the world, rises from the mountain-throne. // MSpv_11.48 //
With the sun's ray-arrows piercing the army of darkness-elephants in all directions, the hue of matured wine —

children.text: rudhiramiva vahantyo bhānti bālātapenacchuritamubhayarodhovāritaṃ vāri nadyaḥ // MSpv_11.49 //
children.translated_text: the rivers shine, bearing reddened water dyed by the early morning glow on both banks, as if carrying blood. // MSpv_11.49 //
The young sun's rays, falling through lattice-windows into the interiors of palaces,

children.text: praṇayiṣu vanitānāṃ prātaricchatsu gantuṃ kupitamadanamuktottaptanārācalīlām // MSpv_11.50 //
children.translated_text: upon the lovers of women who wish to depart at dawn, play the part of burning arrows shot by an angry <s>Madana</s> (Love). // MSpv_11.50 //
The golden goblet, emptied of wine drunk by the brides during the night, [now] with the rising sun's red light of the cool-rayed one penetrating it —
appears even now as if still filled with honey, with its <s>rocanā</s> (yellow pigment)-reddened [interior]. // MSpv_11.51 //
The upper garment left alone on the moonlit bed at night, now showing saffron-like luster from the touch of sunlight —

children.text: nijamiti ratibandhorjānatīmuttarīyaṃ parihasati sakhī strīmādadānāṃ dinādau // MSpv_11.52 //
children.translated_text: when the woman picks it up at day's start, thinking it her own, her friend mocks her, [saying] it belongs to her love-partner. // MSpv_11.52 //
That house, which at night appeared like a silver-crystal royal palace, as if bathed in the moon's rays,
the same house now shines reddened, though not harshly, by the sun's rays, as if bathed in Kashmiri saffron-water. // MSpv_11.53 //
When the lover tenderly loosens the hair [caught] within fresh nail-marks [on the body], the women, radiant,

children.text: vidadhati daśanānāṃ sītkṛtāviṣkṛtānām abhinavaravibhāsaḥ padmarāgānukāram // MSpv_11.54 //
children.translated_text: produce with the revealed hissing of their teeth an imitation of rubies with the luster of fresh passion. // MSpv_11.54 //
With saffron smeared by continuous contact with the beloved's body, its fresh blood-red beauty stirred —

children.text: kanakanikaṣarekhā komalaṃ kāminīnāṃ bhavati vapuravāptacchāyamevātape 'pi // MSpv_11.55 //
children.translated_text: the body of women, delicate as a touchstone-streak of gold, attains shade even in sunlight. // MSpv 11.55 //
Bearing a lotus-forest beauty, of unerring conduct, with a thousand hand-eyes as the cause of the power of sight,

children.text: akhilamatimahimnā lokamākrāntavantaṃ haririva haridaśvaḥ sādhu vṛtraṃ hinasti // MSpv_11.56 //
children.translated_text: pervading the entire world with incomparable greatness—like <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu), the green-horsed one (Sun) thoroughly destroys <s>Vṛtra</s> (darkness). // MSpv 11.56 //
To dispel the designation of darkness, the host of stars, though worthy of being seen, is expelled by the risen radiant one;
those who desire to defeat an enemy but have attained glory through his patronage are themselves on the side to be destroyed. // MSpv 11.57 //
When the cluster of rays is reflected on the silver-bracelet wall, standing opposite, white with dense moonbeams,

children.text: bahirabhihatamadreḥ saṃhataṃ kandarāntargatamapi timiraughaṃ gharmabhānurbhinatti // MSpv_11.58 //
children.translated_text: the sun of burning heat, having struck the external [darkness] of the mountain, splits even the massed darkness inside the caves. // MSpv 11.58 //

children.text: bahirapi vilasantyaḥ kāmamāninyire yad divasakararuco 'ntaṃ dhvāntamantargṛheṣu /
children.translated_text: The fact that the sun's rays, though shining outside, could not penetrate the inner darkness of the inner chambers—
that is the very nature of radiance: though of limited domain in operation, it destroys all opponents with immense power. // MSpv 11.59 //

children.text: ciramatirasalaulyādbandhanaṃ lambhitānāṃ punarayamudayāya prāpya dhāma svameva /
children.translated_text: Of the bees long imprisoned from excessive greed for nectar, now finding their own abode again for their rising—

children.text: dalitadalakapāṭaḥ ṣaṭpadānāṃ saroje sarabhasa iva guptisphoṭamarkaḥ karoti // MSpv_11.60 //
children.translated_text: the sun, splitting open the petal-doors, seems to eagerly break the seal of their confinement in the lotuses. // MSpv 11.60 //
With rays equal in number to his thousand-steeded horses, simultaneously and curiously making thousand-petaled openings,
he seems to gaze lovingly upon <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī), lulled by the songs of bee-swarms, reclining within the lotus-chambers. // MSpv 11.61 //

children.text: adayamiva karāgraireṣa nipīḍya sadyaḥ śaśadharamaharādau rāgavānuṣṇaraśmiḥ /
children.translated_text: This passionate warm-rayed one, as if pitilessly pressing the moon at the beginning of the day with his ray-fingertips,
copiously scatters—the draining of its beauty—into the bellies of white lotuses, pale as water from flowing clouds. // MSpv 11.62 //
As he shines forth for long, illuminating the entire world—as if a second thousand-rayed embodiment were opening its eye—

children.text: sitakaravapuṣāsau lakṣyate saṃprati dyaur vigalitakiraṇena vyaṅgitaikekṣaṇeva // MSpv_11.63 //
children.translated_text: now the sky is seen with the cool-rayed [moon's] body, its rays fading, as if with one eye indicated [while the other is lost]. // MSpv 11.63 //
The <s>kumuda</s> (night-lotus) grove loses its beauty; the day-lotus cluster thrives; the owl abandons joy; the <s>cakravāka</s> (ruddy goose) gains delight;

children.text: udayamahimaraśmiryāti śītāṃśurastaṃ hatavidhilasitānāṃ hī vicitro vipākaḥ // MSpv_11.64 //
children.translated_text: the cool-rayed [moon] of exalted glory rises [while] the warm-rayed [sun] sets—ah, varied indeed is the fruition of those who are destroyed by different fates! // MSpv 11.64 //

children.text: kṣaṇamatuhinadhāmni preṣya bhūyaḥ purastād upagatavati pāṇigrāhavaddigvadhūnām /
children.translated_text: When the cool-rayed [moon], having been sent ahead for a moment, again approaches before [them]—as if a suitor of the direction-brides—

children.text: drutataramupayāti sraṃsamānāṃśuko 'sāv upapātiriti nīcaiḥ paścimāntena candraḥ // MSpv_11.65 //
children.translated_text: this [moon] with loosening garment of rays, goes more swiftly by the western [horizon]—as if thinking, 'Here comes a paramour!' // MSpv 11.65 //
Having brought the entire multitude of stars and worlds to dissolution for the day, bearing an unsurpassed glory of passionate beauty,

children.text: gaganasalilarāśiṃ rātrikalpāvasāne madhuripuriva bhāsvāneṣa eko 'dhiśete // MSpv_11.66 //
children.translated_text: this radiant sun alone presides over the celestial ocean at the end of the night-dissolution, like the enemy of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>). // MSpv 11.66 //
Having awakened the entire world, having dispelled the arising of darkness, having diminished the glory of <s>kumuda</s> lotuses and stars, bringing separation to lovers,

children.text: bahutaraguṇadarśanādabhyupetālpadoṣaḥ kṛtī tava varada karotu suprātamahnāmayaṃ nāyakaḥ // MSpv_11.67 //
children.translated_text: yet with small faults approached due to the perception of far greater virtues—O boon-granting one, may this accomplished leader of days make your dawn auspicious! // MSpv 11.67 //

children.text: itthaṃ rathāśvebhaniṣādināṃ prage gaṇo nṛpāṇāmatha toraṇādbahiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, at dawn, the assembly of kings [gathered] outside the gateway, with the groups of chariots, horses, elephants, and infantry,
and, having spent a moment in preparations of attire fit for the time of departure, beheld <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>). // MSpv 12.1 //
Having mounted <s>Tārkṣya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>), with fine axles, fine wings, blazing with golden splendor, having swiftly surpassed the elephants from on high,

children.text: āruhya tārkṣya nabhasīva bhūtale yayāvanudghātamukhena so 'dhvanā // MSpv_12.2 //
children.translated_text: he proceeded on the road on the earth as if in the sky, without any jolting. // MSpv 12.2 //
Bearing the undivided discus in his hand, the lord of the banner, with <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) resting on his chest,

children.text: satyānuraktaṃ narakasya jiṣṇavo guṇairnṛpāḥ śāṅgiṇamanyayāsiṣuḥ // MSpv_12.3 //
children.translated_text: truly devoted, the conqueror of <s>Naraka</s>—the kings followed the Bow-wielder (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) for his virtues. // MSpv 12.3 //
With the white, star-filled, budding, large lotus-beds of the <s>kumudvatī</s> rivers—

children.text: vyuṣṭaṃ prayāṇaṃ ca viyogavedanāvidūnanārīkamabhūtsamaṃ tadā // MSpv_12.4 //
children.translated_text: dawn and the departure occurred simultaneously then, like the sorrow-of-separation-agitated women. // MSpv 12.4 //
An elephant, with body raised upward, seeming to rival the sky, [about to] leap up to great height—
with curled trunk indicating the measured step, the female elephant bore the mahout upward. // MSpv 12.5 //
With gracefully performed wheelings in front, showing agile feats with flashing hooves,
holding the galloping-rein in one hand, the horsemen mounted their steeds. // MSpv 12.6 //
Until he had not yet created a longer seat-arrangement for the day's further journey—
until then, the chain-bearers (elephants) proceeded unbridled, with irresistible speed. // MSpv 12.7 //
Someone, a skilled charioteer, desiring to attain comfort, yoked his chariot—shining with cheek-glow and brilliant wheel-radiance,

children.text: kaścitsukhaṃ prāptumanāḥ susārathī rathīṃ yuyojādhidhurāṃ vadhūmiva // MSpv_12.8 //
children.translated_text: resplendent with the beauty of a new yoke—to the front axle, like [yoking] a bride. // MSpv 12.8 //
As the camel wished to rise but was held back by the loads, while the burden-bearing apparatus was being placed [upon it],

children.text: ardhojjhitodgāravijharjharasvaraḥ svanāma ninye ravaṇaḥ sphuṭārthatām // MSpv_12.9 //
children.translated_text: the half-suppressed belching-and-gurgling sound made the meaning of his name, '<s>Ravaṇa</s>' (Roarer), clearly evident. // MSpv 12.9 //
The bull, though held by the nose, shaking its pair of horns, whirling its hindquarters with a whistling [sound],

children.text: goṇīṃ janana sma nidhātumuddhṛtāmanukṣaṇaṃ nokṣataraḥ pratīcchati // MSpv_12.10 //
children.translated_text: repeatedly refused to accept the sack lifted to be placed [on it]. // MSpv 12.10 //
The ocean of the army, with variously manifested, unceasing sounds of many kinds, of a thousand paths, difficult to master by the restless,

children.text: gāndharvabhūyṣṭhatayā samānatāṃ sa sāmavedasya dadhau balodadhiḥ // MSpv_12.11 //
children.translated_text: by the predominance of the <s>Gāndharva</s> [musical mode], attained similarity to the <s>Sāmaveda</s>. // MSpv 12.11 //
