With a swaying mahout, rejecting his blunted [goad], wielding another goad against every rival elephant,
the elephant was restrained by the rider, shaking its head with its high-arching tusk-circle. // MSpv 12.12 //
The sound of the kettledrum surged with the unbridled conch-blast, when the Bow-wielder (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) departed;

children.text: svānininye nitarāṃ mahāntyapi vyathāṃ dvayeṣāmapi medinīghṛtām // MSpv_12.13 //
children.translated_text: the sounds brought great anguish, borne by the earth, to both of them [the drum and the earth]. // MSpv 12.13 //
Scattering the beauty of <s>kālīyaka</s> (dark aloewood) paste-anointing in every direction, with radiance of flashing rays,

children.text: khātaṃ khuraimudgabhujāṃ vipaprate gireradhaḥ kāñcanabhūmijaṃ rajaḥ // MSpv_12.14 //
children.translated_text: the golden dust, born of the earth, dug up by the hooves of the horses, spread beneath the mountain. // MSpv 12.14 //
The deep [sounds] of the elephants and the sounds of the chariot-wheels concealed the very same trumpet;
the high-pitched, clear neighing of horses among them arose, having gained the upper hand. // MSpv 12.15 //
Wishing to follow, despising the goad's grasp, carrying his head high with the goad [still on it], hidden,
with trunk-tip reaching forward, the elephant approached through the dense [throng] a nearby female elephant. // MSpv 12.16 //
Going as if not touching the earth with their feet, with scattered sparks flying about from their speed,

children.text: adyāpi senāturagāḥ savismayairalūnapakṣā iva menire janaiḥ // MSpv_12.17 //
children.translated_text: the horses of the army were even now regarded with wonder by the people, as if they were wingless [birds]. // MSpv 12.17 //
With straight, outstretched necks, with swaying topknots, with gurgling throat-sounds,
even the great earth was traversed in a moment by the camels, with unhesitating steps. // MSpv 12.18 //
The pair of mules, driven at speed by the guide calling out loudly, urged on the road,
ran as if in fear of the heap of dense earth-dust [produced by their] own rim-scars [on the ground]. // MSpv 12.19 //
With all the army-followers turning their faces back, their faces seen for a moment as they marched,
the harem-women of the horsemen departed, their bouncing heavy breast-trembling bodices [visible]. // MSpv 12.20 //

children.text: pādaiḥ puraḥ kūbariṇāṃ vidāritāḥ prakāmamākrāntatalāstato gajaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The paths, torn in front by the feet of the pole-horses, fully trampled thereafter by the elephants,
with broken heights and subsequently filled hollows, appeared as if plowed and leveled. // MSpv 12.21 //
People watched, with cries of 'Alas! Alas!', a horse that had thrown its rider, the untamable one set loose,
galloping swiftly in one direction, its trappings slipping, its breast-strap hanging. // MSpv 12.22 //
The rivers—even when unobstructed by mountains, even deep, even broad—

children.text: anvarthasaṃjñayaiva paraṃ trimārgagā yayāvasaṃkhyaiḥ pathibhiścamūrasau // MSpv_12.23 //
children.translated_text: were crossed by that army with innumerable paths, as the name 'Tri-mārgagā' (going by three paths) was truly justified. // MSpv 12.23 //
Two young camels, frightened by the trumpeting of a nearby female elephant, when the driver had confusedly released the reins,

children.text: kṣiptāvarodhāṅganamutpathena gāṃ vilaṅghya laghvīṃ karabhau babhañjatuḥ // MSpv_12.24 //
children.translated_text: having thrown off the harem-women, crossed the light [shallow] ground by a wrong path and broke [free]. // MSpv 12.24 //

children.text: srastāṅgasandhau vigatāśāpāṭave rujā nikāmaṃ vikalīkṛte rathe /
children.translated_text: When the chariot's joints had loosened and the side-beam had come apart and it was utterly disabled by damage,

children.text: āptena tatkṣaṇā bhiṣajeva tatkṣaṇaṃ pracakrame laṅghanapūrvakaḥ kramaḥ // MSpv_12.25 //
children.translated_text: an expert, like a physician at that very moment, immediately undertook the treatment beginning with a jump [to repair it]. // MSpv 12.25 //
When the she-camel's lip was split from the jolt of the pole-breaking, and on the far road awash with flowing ichor,

children.text: sthāṇau niṣaṅgiṇyanasi kṣaṇaṃ puraḥ śuśoca lābhāya kṛtakrayo vaṇik // MSpv_12.26 //
children.translated_text: a merchant, pausing a moment before a pillar [where stood] a quiver-bearing [soldier], grieved—for the price he had paid for [his] gain. // MSpv 12.26 //
With drums calling out to the great cave-mouths of the mountain, with flag-cloths threatening the <s>kandalī</s> (plantain) groves,

children.text: uttaṅgamātaṅgajitālaghūpalo balaiḥ sa paścātkiyate sma bhūdharaḥ // MSpv_12.27 //
children.translated_text: with tall elephants conquering its light boulders—that mountain was being diminished from behind by the forces. // MSpv 12.27 //
The fierce elephants, made ferocious by the scent of wild elephant-ichor carried by the wind, angered by the felling of trees,
maddened, were somehow led away from afar by their drivers through detour. // MSpv 12.28 //
By those [armies], with rows of great elephants rivaling the rows of <s>Jayantī</s> trees of the mountain,
many intervening stretches of land, with hundreds of rivers of flowing people, were traversed. // MSpv 12.29 //

children.text: tasthemuhūrta hariṇīvilocanaiḥ sadṛśi dṛṣṭvā nayanāni yoṣitām /
children.translated_text: Deer paused for a moment, seeing in the eyes of the women [resemblances to] their own doe-eyes;
then they fled, with many startled, fearful, and coquettish movements. // MSpv 12.30 //

children.text: nimnāni duḥkhādavatārya sādibhiḥ sayatnamākṛṣṭakaśāḥ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Descending into hollows with difficulty, pulled by riders carefully tugging the reins, slowly, slowly,
the herds of horses crossed upward, swiftly, with loud hoof-clatter, with loosened bridles. // MSpv 12.31 //
As if someone had mounted [ahead] on the road, keeping [hold], repeatedly restraining the crowd—

children.text: dākṣyaṃ hi sadyaḥ phaladaṃ yadagrataścakhāda dāserayuvā vanāvalīḥ // MSpv_12.32 //
children.translated_text: a young attendant ate the roadside fruit-groves—for skill that bears immediate fruit [prevails] when one is in front. // MSpv 12.32 //
With groups of kings, subdued by <s>Śauri</s>'s (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s) valor, gathered from here and there, with forms bowed in humility,
the army became [united] under one parasol—by the very fewness of parasols of [the other] kings. // MSpv 12.33 //
Hearing the sound from the cheek-bells of a following elephant, the army-followers with agitated limbs,
turning their burden-animals far aside, quickly withdrew from the road. // MSpv 12.34 //
With powerful, lustrous color, brilliant, of noble conduct, gracious, not abandoning awareness of [their] lineage,

children.text: ślokānupendrasya puraḥ sma bhūyaso guṇānsamuddiśya paṭhanti vandinaḥ // MSpv_12.35 //
children.translated_text: the bards before <s>Upendra</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) repeatedly recited verses, pointing out [his] many virtues. // MSpv 12.35 //
Even the ocean, whose surface is completely covered by waters, overflows when agitated;

children.text: grāmeṣu sainyairakarodavāritaiḥ kimavyavasthāṃ calito 'pi keśavaḥ // MSpv_12.36 //
children.translated_text: how then could <s>Keśava</s>, even when [merely] set in motion, [not] create disorder in the villages with his unrestrained troops? // MSpv 12.36 //
The village brides, with faces beautiful as gourd-flowers and <s>guluccha</s> (cluster) blossoms, with eyes terrible as wide-open arrows,
gazed for a long time upon the dead [animals trampled along the way], unnoticed by [other] people. // MSpv 12.37 //
In the cattle-pens, the villagers, seated in circles for assembly, rising suddenly with a shout, repeatedly prancing—
he saw [them], tawny, thirsty, their spirits animated by the chanting of their own clan-names. // MSpv 12.38 //

children.text: paśyankṛtārthairapi vallavījano janādhināthaṃ na yayau vitṛṣṇatām /
children.translated_text: Even the cowherd-folk, though their purposes were fulfilled, seeing the lord of men, did not attain indifference;
[they watched] with eyes of well-known wide [beauty], with charms not understood due to utter innocence. // MSpv 12.39 //
A milker, lovingly licking the suckling calves, holding the pail between both knees,

children.text: vardhiṣṇudhārādhvani rohiṇīḥ payaściraṃ nidadhau duhataḥ sa goduhaḥ // MSpv_12.40 //
children.translated_text: for a long time placed the milk of the cows he was milking into the growing-stream path. // MSpv 12.40 //
As he approached, the calves that had come eagerly ran ahead; wishing to milk the cow herd with the hand at departure,
the foe of <s>Madhu</s> beheld the row of cow-pens on the bank of the <s>Gomatī</s>, beautiful with the lowing of cows // <s>MSpv</s> 12.41 //
He watched with amusement the cowherd-women all around, agitated—while parrots had gone to drive away the rice,

children.text: kaidārikāṇāmabhitaḥ samākulāḥ sahāsamālokayati sma gopikāḥ // MSpv_12.42 //
children.translated_text: deer meanwhile ravaged the beauty of the <s>kaidārikā</s> fields // <s>MSpv</s> 12.42 //
Hearing a cowherd-girl's songs to the effect that "he stirs to drive us away, our life-breaths depart before that from inattention,"

children.text: gītāni gopyāḥ kalamaṃ mṛgavrajo na nūnamattīti harivyalokayat // MSpv_12.43 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> observed a herd of deer that surely did not flee from there // <s>MSpv</s> 12.43 //
Soft with the sound of tinkling anklets slipping from the playfully moving feet of women, interspersed with the sound of red lotuses,
the cry of intoxicated <s>sārasa</s> cranes from the marshlands captivated the mind of <s>Śauri</s> // <s>MSpv</s> 12.44 //
The great dust-mass of the army, risen high, unfaltering and immense, visible even from afar as he advanced—
some bore it on their heads as the dust-load of kings; others bore it as mountains bear the earth // <s>MSpv</s> 12.45 //

children.text: prāyeṇa nīcānapi medinībhṛto janaḥ samenaiva pathādhirohati /
children.translated_text: Generally, people ascend even lowly rulers by the same path;

children.text: senā murāreḥ patha eva sā punarmahāmahīdhrānparito 'dhyarohayat // MSpv_12.46 //
children.translated_text: but the army of <s>Murāri</s>, on that very path, made even the great mountains climb all around // <s>MSpv</s> 12.46 //
With their tusk-tips splitting clouds, facing upward, the greater elephants ascended the mountain ranges,
with rivers of rut-water flowing sideways from their temples, filling the hollows of their ears // <s>MSpv</s> 12.47 //
By some elephant, enormous, dripping drops of rut-water, with the splendor of a cluster of storm-clouds,
the road was blocked on high, by the one endowed with massive tusks // <s>MSpv</s> 12.48 //
Breaking trees, they made the directions from here and there agitated with fluttering banners;
the elephants, crushing mountain-ridges with their speed, made the grounds impassable with their swaying massive bodies // <s>MSpv</s> 12.49 //
<s>Hari</s> beheld the elephant-troops in hundreds ascending the mountains,
like great boulders falling from the slopes against contrary storm-winds // <s>MSpv</s> 12.50 //
Mountain women, clinging to the <s>āmalakī</s> groves, with breasts thrust upward from the exertion of the mountain climb,
gazed upon him with eyes wide open with blooming, flirtatious wonder // <s>MSpv</s> 12.51 //

children.text: sāvajñamunmīlya vilocane sakṛtkṣaṇaṃ mṛjendreṇa suṣupsunā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: A king of lions, having contemptuously opened his eyes once, wishing to sleep again,

children.text: sainyānna yātaḥ samayāpi vivyathe kathaṃ surājaṃbhavamanmathāthavā // MSpv_12.52 //
children.translated_text: was not disturbed even at the time from the armies—was it the yawn of the gods, or love? // <s>MSpv</s> 12.52 //
With banners shaking the great trees uprooted by their height, with the momentum of elephants unchecked by the crowd of people,
with elephants hurling great boulders repeatedly, the army rose above those mountains // <s>MSpv</s> 12.53 //

children.text: śmaśrūyamāṇe maghujālake tarorgajena gaṇḍaṃ kaṣatā vidhūnite /
children.translated_text: When the tree's creepers were being sheared and the cheek was being scratched by a tusked elephant, shaking it,
bees ran in agitation, smaller ones even more, being bitten by the fleeing people // <s>MSpv</s> 12.54 //
When a <s>palāśa</s> tree was felled as if it were a body by a war-elephant of tireless deeds,

children.text: saṃcerurātmāna ivāparaṃ kṣaṇātkṣamāruhaṃ dehamiva plavaṃgamāḥ // MSpv_12.55 //
children.translated_text: monkeys moved in an instant to another earth-tree, like souls to another body // <s>MSpv</s> 12.55 //
In some places bowing humbly, in some places ascending boldly, through open spaces and through caverns too,
the army of <s>Hari</s> then crossed over even the weighty mountains, treating them as equals left behind // <s>MSpv</s> 12.56 //

children.text: sa vyāptavatyā parito 'pathānyapi svasenayā sarvapathīnayā tayā /
children.translated_text: He, with his all-traversing army spread around even over trackless regions,

children.text: ambhobhirullaṅghita tuṅgarodhasaḥ pratīpanāmnīḥ kurute sma nimnagāḥ // MSpv_12.57 //
children.translated_text: made the rivers run backward, like waters overflowing their high banks, their names reversed // <s>MSpv</s> 12.57 //
As long as the elephant squadrons had not waded in, until then the dust raised by the hooves of horses,

children.text: kṣiptaṃ samīraiḥ saritāṃ puraḥ patajjalānyanaiṣīdraja eva paṅkatām // MSpv_12.58 //
children.translated_text: falling before the rivers, blown by the winds, brought the water to the state of mud // <s>MSpv</s> 12.58 //
Repeatedly going forth in delight to sport, intoxicated with rut, on slopes with high broken banks,
stripping away garments of moss with their trunks, they produced the appearance of rivers going to the ocean // <s>MSpv</s> 12.59 //
Breaking their great banks and filling them with water, leveling the ancient rivers with the flat ground,
the elephants, with their rut-waters, set in motion other new rivers with bank-touching currents // <s>MSpv</s> 12.60 //
The rivers, deprived of lotuses that matched the luster of women's faces, bereft of geese bearing the beauty of parasols,
were far diminished as the army passed, with mountain-like elephants that had surpassed the lotus-groves // <s>MSpv</s> 12.61 //
With the unbroken ranks of elephants, their bodies dark as smooth collyrium, towering high,

children.text: senā sudhākṣālitasaudhasaṃpadāṃ purāṃ bahūnāṃ parabhāgamāpa sā // MSpv_12.62 //
children.translated_text: that army attained superiority over many cities whose mansion-wealth was washed white as nectar // <s>MSpv</s> 12.62 //
Along the way, the lord's dwellings were tent-pavilions that rivaled the splendor of palaces;

children.text: nūnaṃ sahānena viyogaviklavā puraḥ puraśrīrapi niryayau tadā // MSpv_12.63 //
children.translated_text: surely the beauty of each city, distressed at separation from him, also came out before it then // <s>MSpv</s> 12.63 //
The towering bodies of elephants, trumpeting loudly, revealed from afar to the forest-dwellers
their homes: shelters in the tree-trunks dripping with rut-water flowing from the rubbing of their temple-surfaces // <s>MSpv</s> 12.64 //
With hundreds of elephant squadrons, tall and extended, surpassing the battlements in height,

children.text: dūṣyairjitodagragṛhāṇi sā camūratītya bhūyāṃsi purāṇyavartata // MSpv_12.65 //
children.translated_text: with canopies that conquered the foremost houses, that army passed through many cities and moved on // <s>MSpv</s> 12.65 //
The dust, raised high by the army's rays, heated by the proximity of the sun,

children.text: āhlādikahlārasamīraṇāhate puraḥ papātāmbhasi yamune rajaḥ // MSpv_12.66 //
children.translated_text: struck by the delightful lotus-bearing breeze, fell into the water of the <s>Yamunā</s> ahead // <s>MSpv</s> 12.66 //

children.text: yā gharmabhānostanayāpi śītalaiḥ svasā yamasyāpi janasya jīvanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: She who, though daughter of the hot-rayed sun, is cool; though sister of <s>Yama</s>, gives life to people;

children.text: kṛṣṇāpi śuddheradhikaṃ vidhātṛbhirvihantumahāṃsi jalaiḥ paṭīyasī // MSpv_12.67 //
children.translated_text: though dark, is more adept than the pure at washing away sins with her waters by the creators // <s>MSpv</s> 12.67 //

children.text: yasyā mahānīlataṭīriva drutāḥ prayānti pītvā himapiṇḍapāṇḍurāḥ /
children.translated_text: Whose banks are like great sapphire cliffs, from which the clouds, white as snowballs, having drunk, depart swiftly,
tinged as if by <s>kālī</s> vines, like broken sticks of collyrium in an instant // <s>MSpv</s> 12.68 //

children.text: vyaktaṃ balīyān yadi heturāgamādapūrayatsā jaladhiṃ na jāhnavī /
children.translated_text: Clearly, if the cause were stronger than tradition, the <s>Ganges</s> would not have filled the ocean;
how else could the ocean's water be of the same color as <s>Śambhu</s>'s throat scorched by the <s>Ganges</s>-flood? // <s>MSpv</s> 12.69 //

children.text: abhyudyatasya kramituṃ javena gāṃ tamālanīlā girāṃ dhṛtāyatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Of him who had risen to cross the earth swiftly, dark as a <s>tamāla</s> tree, with extended dimensions,

children.text: sīmeva sā tasya puraḥ kṣaṇaṃ babhau balāmburāśermahato mahāpagā // MSpv_12.70 //
children.translated_text: that great river appeared before him for a moment like a boundary-line, a force of the great ocean // <s>MSpv</s> 12.70 //
With rocking oars like feet on all sides, with river-folk in boats rapidly crossing,
with women clinging to them, eyes closed from the dizziness produced by the whirling of the rafts // <s>MSpv</s> 12.71 //

children.text: tatpūrvamaṃsadvayasaṃ dvipādhipāḥ kṣaṇaṃ sahelāḥ parito jagāhire /
children.translated_text: The lordly elephants, shoulder-deep at first, playfully plunged all around for a moment;
their water was immediately augmented by the rut-water ceaselessly streaming from them in gift // <s>MSpv</s> 12.72 //
With horses facing forward, their nostrils flaring with audible snorting, their long tails spread out,
ears pricked up, necks held firm and high, they crossed ahead, their gaze fixed on the far bank // <s>MSpv</s> 12.73 //

children.text: tīrtvā janenaiva nitāntadustarāṃ nadīṃ pratijñāmiva tāṃ garīyasīm /
children.translated_text: Having crossed that river, most difficult to ford by ordinary means, as if a great vow fulfilled,
the lowing of the humped cattle shone forth loudly, scattering from the peaks of the great bank-cliffs // <s>MSpv</s> 12.74 //
The river, being parted by the forces of the <s>Yadu</s> king, shone with a dark luster from the fords,
marked with many <s>sindūra</s>-reddened bangles, like an elongated braid of the earth // <s>MSpv</s> 12.75 //
With unobstructed swift motion, risen high, without abandoning their great speed,
some crossed the navigable waters with their arms alone, throwing waves as if others were throwing waves at them // <s>MSpv</s> 12.76 //
Splitting the great banks by the goring of bulls' horns, with crocodiles dragged out by their powerful feet, with intoxicated traders,

children.text: sapadi saritaṃ sā śrībharturbṛhadrathamaṇḍalaskhalilamullaṅghyaināṃ jagāma varūthinī // MSpv_12.77 //
children.translated_text: the army of <s>Śrī</s>'s lord, suddenly crossing that river, stumbling over the great circles of chariot-wheels, marched on // <s>MSpv</s> 12.77 //
Then <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, the son of austerity, heard that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> had crossed the <s>Yamunā</s>;

children.text: sa yadācalannijapurādaharniśaṃ nṛpatestadādi samacāri vārtayā // MSpv_13.1 //
children.translated_text: from the time he had departed from his own city, day and night, news had been continuously reported to the king // <s>MSpv</s> 13.1 //
In the great city, as if unable to contain the joy born from the approach of the <s>Yadu</s> lord,
suddenly then, accompanied by his brothers, the king of the earth went forth to meet him // <s>MSpv</s> 13.2 //
With the hearing of the people deafened by the sounds of the <s>Kuru</s> wheel-drums set in rapid motion,
the speakers completed the remainder of desired conversations with hand-gestures // <s>MSpv</s> 13.3 //
Without any gap on all sides, the ground of earth—with golden-rimmed wheels spinning rapidly in flight,
the bannered warriors had garments of earth-dust that resembled each other, stirred by the swift winds // <s>MSpv</s> 13.4 //
The earth, struck by horse-hooves, sounded rapidly overhead like hand-drums;
and peacocks danced, their cries joyfully matching the deep sounds of cloud-like mighty elephants // <s>MSpv</s> 13.5 //
Even as the armies of the foe of the <s>Asuras</s> and the <s>Pāṇḍu</s> sons marched together in unity born of affection,

children.text: raruṣe viṣāṇibhiranukṣaṇaṃmitho madamūḍhabuddhiṣu vivekitā kutaḥ? // MSpv_13.6 //
children.translated_text: the tusked elephants clashed with each other at every moment—where is discernment in those whose minds are dulled by rut? // <s>MSpv</s> 13.6 //

children.text: avaloka eva nṛpateḥ sma dūrato rabhasādrathādavatarītumicchataḥ /
children.translated_text: At the very sight of the king from afar, eagerly wishing to descend from his chariot,

children.text: avatīrṇavānprathamamātmanā harirvinayaṃ viśeṣayati sambhrameṇa saḥ // MSpv_13.7 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> himself descended first—he distinguished his humility by his eagerness // <s>MSpv</s> 13.7 //
The <s>Purāṇa Puruṣa</s> (ancient being), before him on the ground, his body adorned with the broad necklace being arranged,

children.text: bhuvanairnato 'pi vihitāttmagauravaḥ praṇanāma nāma tanayaṃ pitṛṣvasuḥ // MSpv_13.8 //
children.translated_text: though bowed to by the worlds, himself maintaining self-dignity, bowed in name to the son of his father's sister // <s>MSpv</s> 13.8 //

children.text: mukuṭāṃśurañjitaparāgamagrataḥ sa na yāvadāpa śirasā mahītalam /
children.translated_text: Before he could touch the ground with his head, reddened by the dust colored by his crown-rays,
the king seized him eagerly with the cage of his arms, disregarding all protocol // <s>MSpv</s> 13.9 //

children.text: na mamau kapāṭataṭavistṛtaṃ tanau muravairimavakṣa urasi kṣamābhujaḥ /
children.translated_text: The chest of the foe of <s>Mura</s>, broad as a door-panel, could not be contained on the breast of the lord of earth;
yet with his pair of long arms, extended wide, he embraced him all around // <s>MSpv</s> 13.10 //
<s>Śrī</s>, whose constant dwelling was upon the chest of the enemy of <s>Mura</s>, having released her lotus down to the navel,
rose to his face from fear of being crushed in the merciless embrace of the osprey-like king // <s>MSpv</s> 13.11 //

children.text: śirasi sma jighrati surāribandhane chalavāmanaṃ vinayavāmanaṃ tadā /
children.translated_text: The king smelled the head of the subduer of the foe of the gods, who was deceptively small as <s>Vāmana</s> yet small in humility,
whose head-hair was perfumed with the flowers of the celestial tree won by the valor of his glory // <s>MSpv</s> 13.12 //
Even when the son of <s>Vasudeva</s> was released, his body thrilling with goose-bumps from the sensation of joy,
the beauty of the lord of the <s>Kurus</s> was not abandoned by his vine-like limbs, lovely as blossoming <s>kadamba</s> clusters // <s>MSpv</s> 13.13 //
The other kings too, his kinsmen, delighted with eyes blooming with joy,
he honored appropriately, he who was worthy of the honor of all people, he who had forcibly uplifted the assembly of the gods // <s>MSpv</s> 13.14 //
Meeting their equals of equal glory, with arms longer than the broad sides of boulders,

children.text: pariśiśliṣuḥ kṣitipatīnkṣitīśvarāḥ kuliśātpareṇa girayo girīniva // MSpv_13.15 //
children.translated_text: the kings embraced the kings, like mountains embracing mountains with something harder than thunderbolts // <s>MSpv</s> 13.15 //
With mutual elephant-hump-high hard breasts keeping their stomachs far apart,
with full blooming cheek-surfaces, the women of the <s>Kukura</s> and <s>Kaurava</s> clans embraced each other // <s>MSpv</s> 13.16 //
The two contingents—confused with chariots, horses, foot-soldiers, and female elephants—met each other face to face;

children.text: dadhire pṛthakkariṇa eva dūrato mahatāṃ hi sarvamathavā janātigam // MSpv_13.17 //
children.translated_text: the great elephants alone stood apart at a distance—for everything belonging to the great is indeed beyond common people // <s>MSpv</s> 13.17 //
"Let him mount"—thus addressed by the king, <s>Hari</s>, placing his hand in that of the <s>Kapi</s>-bannered one, ascended the chariot;

children.text: avalambitailavilapāṇipallavaḥ śrayati sma meghamiva meghavāhanaḥ // MSpv_13.18 //
children.translated_text: with his hanging hand-petal grasping the edge of the canopy, he mounted it like <s>Indra</s> mounting a cloud // <s>MSpv</s> 13.18 //
And of him who stood upon his chariot, advancing against the cities of the enemy like the cities of old — of the foe of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Muradviṣ</s>),

children.text: atha dharmamūrtiranurāgabhāvitaḥ svayamādita pravayaṇaṃ prajāpatiḥ // MSpv_13.19 //
children.translated_text: then <s>Prajāpati</s> (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>), the embodiment of <s>Dharma</s>, imbued with affection, himself came forth first in a carriage. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.19 //
Then slowly, from between the fine meshwork of his [hair], flickering like the digit of the night-maker (moon) — its luster [resembling]
the broad foam-crest of the lord of rivers, the son of the wind (<s>Bhīma</s>), like <s>Raghu</s>, scattered [a radiance]. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.20 //
With the splendor of blossoming <s>kalāya</s> flowers — dark, not pale — moon-white, of the lord of all beings,
outshining in radiance the circle of geese upon the lake of the <s>Yamunā</s> — <s>Jiṣṇu</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>) bore the parasol that wards off heat. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.21 //
With the discus-bearer (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), resplendent, stationed between the son of the wind (<s>Bhīma</s>) and the son of <s>Indra</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>),
he shone as if bearing a conjunction — hard to sustain, named after two planets — with the moon stationed between the two planetary nodes. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.22 //

children.text: vaśinaṃ kṣiterayanayāviveśvaraṃ niyamo yamaśca niyataṃ yatiṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: The master of the earth (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>), lord of the two solstice-paths, self-controlled — restraint and discipline [followed] the steadfast ascetic, as it were;
then the two sons of the <s>Aśvins</s> (<s>Nakula</s> and <s>Sahadeva</s>) followed him, as if attended by the splendor of victory, like the sun and the wind. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.23 //
By the joyful ones — enemies of the <s>Daitya</s>-born — who had approached with devotion blossoming from unhesitating enthusiasm,
as if by instructors, he was surrounded by those who chastise the unchastened — themselves disciplined and humble. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.24 //
Then, as if [there were] no difference in the movement of those two armies — like the waters of the sun-born (<s>Tāpī</s>) and <s>Jāhnavī</s> (<s>Gaṅgā</s>),
with the celestial chariots resounding with echoing pride, [they] thundered exceedingly with the greatest joy. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.25 //
Of the kings who had come to attend the sacrifice, their encampments arranged all around outside,

children.text: uparudhyamānamiva bhūbhṛtāṃ balaiḥ puṭabhedanaṃ danusutāriraikṣata // MSpv_13.26 //
children.translated_text: the enemy of the sons of <s>Danu</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) saw the breaching of the enclosures [of the city] by the armies of the kings. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.26 //
Filling the regions with echoes, that ocean of armies, descending toward the city gate,

children.text: ruruce himācalaguhāmukhonmukhaḥ payasāṃ pravāha iva saurasaindhavaḥ // MSpv_13.27 //
children.translated_text: shone like the current of the heavenly river (<s>Gaṅgā</s>) facing the cave-mouth of the <s>Himālaya</s>. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.27 //
He who had assumed many bodily forms time and again — that <s>Puruṣa</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), divided among the nine city-gates,

children.text: puruṣaḥ puraṃ praviśati sma pañcabhiḥ samamindriyairiva narendrasūnubhiḥ // MSpv_13.28 //
children.translated_text: entered the city through five [gates] with the five princes, as if with the five senses. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.28 //
Where the men shone not with bodies whose radiance [resembled] the form of <s>Smara</s> (Love), as if gazed upon by the three-eyed one (<s>Śiva</s>) [and burned],

children.text: pramadāśca yatra khalu rājayakṣmaṇaḥ parato niśākaramanoramairmukhaiḥ // MSpv_13.29 //
children.translated_text: and the women, with faces as lovely as the moon, [shone] from afar — surely [afflicting others] with the royal disease (love-sickness). // <s>MSpv</s> 13.29 //
Summoned by the proclamation of drums, to behold the enemy of the foes of the gods (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),
the women of the city rushed to every main street, abandoning all other tasks with eagerness. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.30 //
The women, hastily adorning themselves, with garments slipping from hips barely held by their hands,
stationed upon the walls — the rows of mansions assumed a loud burst of laughter, as it were, from the reverberations of drums. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.31 //
With necklaces, anklets, tooth-ornaments and golden girdles [misplaced], with ear-ornaments set upon their heads instead of in the hair,
with pairs of garments reversed — the women came rushing, with ear-flowers turned into bracelets. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.32 //
A certain one, extending her foot from the hand-petal of a maidservant [applying lac-dye], leaving involuntarily through passion,

children.text: drutayāvakaikapadacitritāvaniṃ padavīṃ gateva girijā harārdhatām // MSpv_13.33 //
children.translated_text: marking the ground with the imprint of a single foot [dyed with] wet <s>yāvaka</s> (lac) — went forth like <s>Girijā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>) [going] to share half of <s>Hara</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) body. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.33 //
With girdle-bells clanging as they slipped on the summit of their broad, massive hip-surfaces, in a flurry,
the women [crossed] the mansions on lofty golden walkways, their golden anklets tinkling at each step. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.34 //
Peering out from the window of a golden mansion, longing to see the slayer of <s>Mura</s>,
the full-moon disk of [her] face-lotus shone like the moon [peering] from the mouth of a cave on the eastern mountain. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.35 //
By one [woman] who had climbed high upon her own dwelling, her garment-end blown by the wind,

children.text: vihitopaśobhamupayāti mādhave nagaraṃ vyarocata patākayeva tat // MSpv_13.36 //
children.translated_text: as <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) approached, the city was adorned — shining as if with a banner. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.36 //
With handfuls of parched rice and flowers released from lotus-bud hands, at every house the women showered [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>],
like clusters of pearls freed from split-open oyster shells, [those] women [greeted] the beloved of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, who bears the <s>cakravāka</s>-emblem. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.37 //
Radiant as the moon freed from frost, bearing a lotus, causing birds to rejoice and fish-bannered <s>Kāma</s> to arise,

children.text: abhavatprasāditasuro mahotsavaḥ pramadājanasya sa cirāya mādhavaḥ // MSpv_13.38 //
children.translated_text: that <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), having propitiated the gods, became a long-awaited great festival for the women-folk. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.38 //
He whose glance alone plainly is not equal [to behold], the lord of both refuge-paths of the earth-upholder — the ill-eyed [man] does not see clearly;

children.text: madanenavītabhayamityadhiṣṭhitāḥ kṣaṇamīkṣate sma sa purovilāsinīḥ // MSpv_13.39 //
children.translated_text: "Fear has been overcome by <s>Madana</s> (Love)" — thus emboldened, he gazed for a moment at the city's playful women. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.39 //

children.text: vipulena sāgaraśayasyakukṣiṇā bhuvanāni yasya papire yugakṣaye /
children.translated_text: He by whose expansive belly the worlds were drunk at the end of the age — the one who reclines on the ocean —

children.text: madavibhramāsakalayā pape punaḥ sa purastriyaikatamayaikayā dṛśā // MSpv_13.40 //
children.translated_text: he in turn was drunk by the city women, intoxicated with love's rapture, with a single sidelong glance of one [woman]. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.40 //
Repeatedly lifting with effort [her garment over] a breast that was lofty, massive, and close-pressing, with peacock-feather and conch-shell [ornaments] swaying and sounding,
a certain [woman] quickly scratched one ear-hole with her fingertip, gazing toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.41 //
With a hand whose finger-sprouts, beautiful as pink lotus petals, moved repeatedly,
another, with trembling head, invited the enemy of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) with a gesture pregnant with suppressed meaning. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.42 //
Another, covering her beautiful face with one hand possessing the beauty of a sprout placed near a lotus,
with teeth-rays sparkling through the gaps of her trembling fingers — stifled a yawn. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.43 //
With [her] slender line of body-hair made dense by the radiance of a great dark sapphire set in a bracelet,
another held her slipping garment with her sprout-hand, her eyes [open only for] the moment of seeing <s>Hari</s>. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.44 //
With sweat washed away by the fan-breeze of bee-wings whirring about, drawn by her own fragrance,

children.text: abhiśauri kācidanimeṣadṛṣṭinā puradevateva vapuṣā vyabhāvyata // MSpv_13.45 //
children.translated_text: a certain [woman] appeared toward <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) with unblinking gaze, like a presiding city-goddess in bodily form. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.45 //

children.text: abhiyāti naḥ satṛṣa eva cakṣuṣo harirityakhidyata nitambinījanaḥ /
children.translated_text: "<s>Hari</s> approaches us, yet our eyes remain ever thirsty" — the broad-hipped women were distressed;

children.text: na viveda yaḥ satatamenamīkṣate na vitṛṣṇatāṃ vrajati khalvasāvapi // MSpv_13.46 //
children.translated_text: she who gazes at him constantly does not know [satisfaction], nor indeed does that [gaze] ever reach freedom from thirst. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.46 //
Showing no regard for returning to their own homes, the women-folk stood still for a moment as if drawn by a painter's brush,

children.text: gatamacyutena saha śūnyatāṃ gataḥ pratipālayanmana ivāṅganājanaḥ // MSpv_13.47 //
children.translated_text: gazing after [him who had] departed with <s>Acyuta</s>, [their world] gone to emptiness — as if minds awaiting [his return]. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.47 //

children.text: alasairmadena sudṛśaḥ śarīrakaiḥ svagṛhānprati pratiyayuḥ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With bodies languid from intoxication [of love], the beautiful-eyed women slowly, slowly returned to their homes,
with widely outstretched gaze-offering bowls, overflowing with the hastily drunk nectar of <s>Mādhava</s>'s (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s) beauty. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.48 //
Sprinkled in front with fresh scented water, with the illusion of dust [created] by dense incense-smoke,
with garments hanging from tall, raised flagstaffs — the city streets were then traversed by <s>Hari</s>. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.49 //

children.text: upanīya bindusaraso mayena yā maṇidāru cāru kila vārṣaparvaṇam /
children.translated_text: The assembly-hall that <s>Maya</s> had built [using resources] brought from Lake <s>Bindu</s>, of wondrous gem-and-wood [construction], for the season of rains,

children.text: vidadhe 'vadhūtasurasadmasampadaṃ samupāsadatsapadi saṃsadaṃ sa tām // MSpv_13.50 //
children.translated_text: which shamed the splendor of the celestial mansions — he (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) at once approached that assembly. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.50 //
Where at night the rays of the moon, falling on the lustre of mansions [built] of gold-washed stone,
seemed again, as it were, to fall into the milk-ocean — the cool-rayed one [seeming] to resume his momentary dwelling there. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.51 //
In its chambers, floors made of red gold, with interiors turned green by the rays of sapphire gems,

children.text: jamadagnisūnupitṛtarpaṇīrapovahati sma yā viralaśaivalā iva // MSpv_13.52 //
children.translated_text: bore waters — sparse in moss — as if flowing for the ancestral libations of the son of <s>Jamadagni</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>). // <s>MSpv</s> 13.52 //

children.text: viśadāśmakūṭaghaṭitāḥ kṣapākṛtaḥ kṣaṇadāsu yatra ca rucekatāṃ gatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Where at night, rows of houses built with crystalline stone-peaks, having attained oneness with the night,
were passed through by people for a long time as if in darkness, identified only by touch of the hand. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.53 //
In dwellings at night, with heaps of dark stones — [whose darkness] is a manifest offense against the lotus-maiden (lotus beauty),

children.text: muharatrasadbhirapi yatra gauravācchaśalāñchanāṃśava upāṃśu jadhnire // MSpv_13.54 //
children.translated_text: the rays of the hare-marked [moon], even when truly present, out of respect, struck [there] only faintly. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.54 //
Where, within the gem-[inlaid] walls of houses, the happy ones faced reflections [in the polished surfaces],
and lovers, even when turning away in bashful modesty, bore delight through new embraces with their beloveds. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.55 //
Where in the mansions [built] of green stone, <s>Hari</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) beheld [horses] with repeatedly lowered faces, desiring grass,
appearing as if deer seizing mouthfuls, with tips of rays sprouting at the edge of the halter. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.56 //
In the precincts of the <s>Yadus</s>, the trees shone with their own reflections mirrored in the water held in the broad basins around them,

children.text: yadupāntikeṣu dadhato mahīruhaḥ sapalāśarāśimiva mūlasaṃhatim // MSpv_13.57 //
children.translated_text: bearing the appearance of a mass of leaves and branches [extending] even at the root-cluster. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.57 //
In the courtyards of the <s>Yadu</s> [city], with rumblings of clouds constantly rising above [drawn by] the proximity of gems on serpent-lords' crests,
the ground sprouted fresh <s>vālavāyaja</s> gem-stalks, as if breathing [new life]. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.58 //

children.text: nalinī nigūḍhasalilā ca yatra sā sthalamityadhaḥ patati yā suyodhane /
children.translated_text: And there was that lotus-pool, its water concealed [by crystal floors] — that very one into which <s>Suyodhana</s> (<s>Duryodhana</s>) fell thinking it solid ground —
which became the cause of the destruction of all kings, troubled by the laughter of the son of the wind (<s>Bhīma</s>). // <s>MSpv</s> 13.59 //
Where, out of suspicion of water [on the sapphire floor] gleaming all around with a tender, sword-like luster, disregarding [the floor] to be laughed at by others,

children.text: udakarṣi yatra jalaśaṅkayā janairmuhurindranīlabhuvi dūramambaram // MSpv_13.60 //
children.translated_text: people repeatedly lifted their garments high on the indigo-stoned ground, far [from actual water]. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.60 //
Then, from the chariot, <s>Hari</s> and the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>), their bodies gleaming like spotless orbs of light, descended into the assembly,
delighting the eyes — like the Moon and <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Venus</s>) [descending] from the rising mountain into the sky. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.61 //
Then, when the king said "This way, this way!" respectfully, to him [whose way was obscured] by the invisible gem-inlaid walls,
he (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) slowly entered the assembly, its doorways indistinguishable amid the mass of white crystal rays. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.62 //

children.text: navahāṭakeṣṭakacitaṃ dadarśa sa kṣitipasya pastyamatha tatra saṃsadi /
children.translated_text: There, in that assembly, he saw the court of the king, paved with fresh golden bricks,

children.text: gaganaspṛśāṃ maṇirucāṃ cayena yatsadanānyudayasmayata nākināmapi // MSpv_13.63 //
children.translated_text: whose mansions, with clusters of gem-radiances touching the sky, aroused envy even in the celestials. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.63 //
Bearing a radiance as of the sun-lord and the full moon rising simultaneously upon the peak of the eastern mountain,

children.text: rucimāsane ruciradhāmni bibhratāvalaghunyatha nyaṣadatāṃ nṛpācyutau // MSpv_13.64 //
children.translated_text: the king (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>) and <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) then sat, not lightly, upon a splendid, brilliant throne. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.64 //
With the supremely comfortable [breeze] dispelling all fatigue, like the wind [itself] soothing the body,

children.text: yadunandanena tadudanvataḥ payaḥ śasineva rājakulamāpa nandathum // MSpv_13.65 //
children.translated_text: by the delight of the <s>Yadu</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) — like the moon [delighting] the ocean — the royal family attained joy. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.65 //
Graceful dancing accompanied by faultless music with proper rhythm, and tender new songs achieving a novelty beyond the familiar,
with vivid <s>sāttvika</s> and <s>āṅgika</s> [expressions] — the brilliant dance — performed by playful, charming courtesans. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.66 //

children.text: sakale ca tatra gṛhamāgate harau nagare 'pyakālamahamādideśa saḥ /
children.translated_text: And when <s>Hari</s> had arrived at the residence, throughout the city he (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>) proclaimed an untimely festival;

children.text: satatotsavaṃ taditi nūnanmunmudo rabhasena vismṛtamabhūnmahībhṛtaḥ // MSpv_13.67 //
children.translated_text: "That city is in perpetual festival" — this [saying], surely, in his ecstasy, the king had forgotten in his excitement. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.67 //
<s>Hari</s>, who knows all names from infancy onward, inquired about the welfare of each of his kinsmen;

children.text: mahatīmapi śriyamavāpya vismayaḥ sujano na vismarati jātu kiñcana // MSpv_13.68 //
children.translated_text: even upon attaining great prosperity, a noble person never forgets anyone. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.68 //
Having attained a joy hard to obtain in the mortal world, surpassing [all] by [its] excess, bearing an unmatched novelty,
the lord of <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) and the lord of the earth (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>) — both relished the nectar of mutual conversation for a long time. // <s>MSpv</s> 13.69 //
The king (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>) addressed him with words as if pouring forth [his feelings], with a gaze radiant with affection,

children.text: yajñakarmaṇi manaḥ samādadhadvāgvidāṃ varamakamadvado nṛpaḥ // MSpv_14.1 //
children.translated_text: fixing his mind on the matter of the sacrifice — the foremost of the eloquent spoke without jealousy. // <s>MSpv</s> 14.1 //

children.text: lajjate na gaditaḥ priyaṃ paro vaktureva bhavati trapādhikā /
children.translated_text: "The other to whom a pleasant [truth] is spoken does not feel ashamed; rather, it is the speaker who bears the greater embarrassment;

children.text: vrīḍametina tava priyaṃ vadanhrīmatātrabhavataiva bhūyate // MSpv_14.2 //
children.translated_text: in speaking what is dear to you, the modesty is mine — indeed, by such a modest one as yourself, it is borne. // <s>MSpv</s> 14.2 //

children.text: toṣameti vitathaiḥ stavaiḥ paraste ca tasya sulabhāḥ śarīribhiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Others are gratified by false praises, and those [flatterers] are easily found among living beings;

children.text: asti na stutivaco 'nṛtaṃ tava stotrayogyana ca tena tuṣyasi // MSpv_14.3 //
children.translated_text: but no word of praise addressed to you is untrue, nor are you, worthy of hymns, pleased even by that. // <s>MSpv</s> 14.3 //

children.text: bahvapi priyamayaṃ tava bruvanna vrajatyanṛtavāditāṃ janaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Though this person speaks many pleasant things about you, he does not incur the charge of speaking falsehood;
that all perfections of every virtue arise in you who are unstained by any fault. // MSpv 14.4 //

children.text: sā vibhūtiranubhāva sampadāṃ bhūyasī tava yadāyatāyati /
children.translated_text: That glory of yours is the splendor of [your] majestic powers; that it extends ever further —

children.text: etadūḍhagurubhāra bhārataṃ varṣamadya mama vartate vaśe // MSpv_14.5 //
children.translated_text: [is proven by] this <s>Bhārata</s> land, bearing a great heavy burden, which now stands under my command. // MSpv 14.5 //
For one desiring to attain the sevenfold [ritual] thread, grant your favor by your permission, O Lord;

children.text: mūlatāmupagate prabho tvayi prāpi dharmamayavṛkṣatā mayā // MSpv_14.6 //
children.translated_text: with you as root, the tree-nature of <s>dharma</s> has been attained by me. // MSpv 14.6 //
By me who desires to perform the pure sacrifice with all implements gathered,

children.text: tvaṃ samīraṇa iva pratīkṣitaḥ karṣakeṇa valajānpupūṣatā // MSpv_14.7 //
children.translated_text: you have been awaited like the wind by a farmer wishing to fill the threshing-floors. // MSpv 14.7 //
My sacrifice, consecrated by your sinless presence, is now free from obstacles;
who is able to destroy the splendor of the day when the cool-rayed one [the moon] has risen at its rising? // MSpv 14.8 //
The patrimony I obtained by right, which I guarded and increased —

children.text: tīrthagāmī karavai vidhānatastajjuṣasva juhavāni cānale // MSpv_14.9 //
children.translated_text: going on pilgrimage, I shall offer it ritually; let me pour libations into the fire as ordained. // MSpv 14.9 //

children.text: pūrvamaṅga juhudhi tvameva vā snātavatyavabhṛthe tatastvayi /
children.translated_text: First, do you yourself offer the preliminary oblation; then, when you have bathed in the <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath),
as the <s>Soma</s>-drinker, the <s>Rājasūya</s> shall be performed by me, who desires the highest canopy of the sacrifice. // MSpv 14.10 //
What need of this wealth of possessions, won by your grace? Let it be employed!

children.text: śādhi śāsaka jagattrayasya māmāśravo 'smi bhavataḥ sahānujaḥ // MSpv_14.11 //
children.translated_text: Command me, O ruler of the three worlds! I am obedient to you, together with my younger brothers.' // MSpv 14.11 //
To him thus speaking, <s>Viṣṭaraśravas</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), then making all the kings hear,
spoke — his body dappled with circles of tooth-lustre rays that seemed to laugh. // MSpv 14.12 //
'Having subdued all kings, your great splendor now shines indeed through the wealth of your own statecraft;

children.text: kiṃ parasya sa guṇaḥ samaśnute pathyavṛttirapi yadyarogitām // MSpv_14.13 //
children.translated_text: what virtue does another's [contribution] achieve? Even wholesome conduct [independently] attains good health. // MSpv 14.13 //

children.text: tatsurājñi bhavati sthite punaḥ kaḥ kratuṃ yajatu rājalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: With that divine king (<s>Indra</s>) established [in his place], who else should perform the sacrifice that bears the mark of kingship?

children.text: uddhṛtau bhavati kasya vā bhuvaḥ śrīvarāhamapahāya yogyatā // MSpv_14.14 //
children.translated_text: Except for <s>Śrīvarāha</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s> in the Boar form), who has the capacity to raise up the earth? // MSpv 14.14 //

children.text: śāsane 'pi guruṇi vyavasthitaṃ kṛtyavastuṣu niyuṅkṣva kāmataḥ /
children.translated_text: One who is established even in the weighty commandment — employ him at will in matters of duty;

children.text: tvatprayojanaghanaṃ dhanañjayādanya eva iti māṃ ca māvagāḥ // MSpv_14.15 //
children.translated_text: and do not think that someone other than <s>Dhanañjaya</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>) is more devoted to your purposes — including me! // MSpv 14.15 //

children.text: yastaveha savane na bhūpatiḥ karma karmakaravatkariṣyati /
children.translated_text: Whatever king does not perform his ritual duty at your sacrifice like a laborer —

children.text: tasya neṣyati vapuḥ kabandhatāṃ bandhureva jagatāṃ sudarśanaḥ // MSpv_14.16 //
children.translated_text: his body shall be reduced to a headless trunk by <s>Sudarśana</s> [the discus], the kinsman of all beings. // MSpv 14.16 //'

children.text: ityudīritagiraṃ nṛpastvayi śreyasi sthitavati sthirā mama /
children.translated_text: When <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) had thus spoken and had taken his stand in what was auspicious, the king said:
'Firm is my every prosperity' — and, bearing joy, he rose up for the sacrifice. // MSpv 14.17 //
Bearing a digit of the moon on his face, his body of <s>Kāma</s> (Love) destroyed by [mere] sight,
he [<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>], bathed in pure waters, became an eighth form — [he] who bore the form of the eight-formed Lord [<s>Śiva</s>]. // MSpv 14.18 //

children.text: tasya sāṃkhyapuruṣeṇa tulyatāṃ bibhrataḥ svayamakurvataḥ kriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: He, bearing equality with the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Self) of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, not himself performing actions,
attained agency [only] through the perception thereof — in the functioning instrument [the priest], just as in the officiating priest. // MSpv 14.19 //
With the <s>anuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse), pronounced without error, clearly and loudly, those knowers of sentence-characteristics,
the ritual performers, with the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse), offered the material substance, designating the deity. // MSpv 14.20 //
The <s>Sāma</s>-chanters sang the <s>Sāman</s> unstintingly, with tones arranged by the sevenfold division of notes;
there, the learned ones of truthful speech chanted the holy <s>Ṛk</s>-<s>Yajus</s> texts in between. // MSpv 14.21 //
The oblations, beheld by the sacrificer's wife wearing a girdle of <s>darbha</s> grass,
consecrated with the placing-ceremony and other rites, were poured into the kindled fire by them. // MSpv 14.22 //
Not easily expressible through inflections and all the [grammatical] forms in tradition,

children.text: tatra karmaṇi viparyaṇīnaman mantramūhakuśalaḥ prayogiṇaḥ // MSpv_14.23 //
children.translated_text: in that ritual, the skilled practitioners, expert at pondering mantras, bent [them] correctly into [proper] utterance. // MSpv 14.23 //

children.text: saṃśayāya dadhatoḥ sarūpatā dūrabhinnaphalayoḥ kriyāṃ prati /
children.translated_text: Of two compounds, bearing identical form yet yielding vastly different results with respect to ritual action,

children.text: śabdaśāsanavidaḥ samāsayorvigrahaṃ vyavasasuḥ svareṇa te // MSpv_14.24 //
children.translated_text: those versed in the science of grammar resolved the dissolution [of the compound] by means of accent. // MSpv 14.24 //
The fire, blazing, as if laughing with the circle of radiance from hundreds of flickering flame-tongues,
licked up the abundant clarified butter offered repeatedly with the exclamation '<s>vaṣaṭ</s>!', with a clean lapping. // MSpv 14.25 //

children.text: tatra mantrapavitaṃ haviḥ kratāvaśnato na vapureva kevalam /
children.translated_text: There, the fire did not consume merely the body of the oblation purified by mantras in the sacrifice;
bearing an exceedingly clear splendor of color, with a blazing name [<s>Havirbhuj</s>, 'oblation-eater'], he became radiant. // MSpv 14.26 //

children.text: sparśamuṣṇamucitaṃ dadhacchikhī yaddadāha haviradbhutaṃ na tat /
children.translated_text: That the fire, bearing appropriate hot touch, burned the oblation is no wonder;
by the fragrance too, born of the offered oblation, it burned the mass of sins of embodied beings. // MSpv 14.27 //
Rising up suddenly, making the directions smoky, growing dense, pushing down the clouds,

children.text: dyāmiyāya dahanasya ketanaḥ kīrtayanniva divaukasāṃ priyam // MSpv_14.28 //
children.translated_text: the banner of the fire went up to the sky, as if proclaiming tidings dear to the gods. // MSpv 14.28 //
The immortal nectar, surpassing the flowing essence of all the herbs of every great ocean, was celebrated;

children.text: nākinaḥ kathamapi pratīkṣituṃ hūyamānamanale viṣehire // MSpv_14.29 //
children.translated_text: the gods somehow could not wait to watch [it] being poured into the fire. // MSpv 14.29 //
There, when the husbands — constantly invited by the ritual invocations — had departed [to the sacrifice],
the divine women wore braids on their heads, not garlands of fully blooming celestial trees. // MSpv 14.30 //
Because they [the gods] quickly consumed the oblation-food there, through that they attained long immortality;

children.text: uddhatānadhika medhitaujaso dānavāṃśca vibudhāḥ vijigyire // MSpv_14.31 //
children.translated_text: and the gods, with their power increased and strengthened by the sacrificial nourishment, also conquered the <s>Dānavas</s> (demons). // MSpv 14.31 //
No transgression occurred — not the slightest error in any ritual act; every implement was perfectly accomplished;

children.text: atyaśerata parasparaṃ dhiyaḥ sattriṇāṃ narapateścasaṃpadaḥ // MSpv_14.32 //
children.translated_text: the intellects of the sacrificial participants and the wealth of the king mutually surpassed each other. // MSpv 14.32 //
Then, recognizing the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> host — purifying in rows — as worthy of <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fees),
the gracious king distributed the <s>Rājasūya</s> fees in the assembly, row by row. // MSpv 14.33 //
In the field-lands of the twice-born, where all rites preceded by water-offering had attained purity,

children.text: bhāvi bibhrati phalaṃ mahaddvijakṣetrabhūmiṣu narādhipo 'vapat // MSpv_14.34 //
children.translated_text: the king sowed wealth like seeds, which would bear great future fruit. // MSpv 14.34 //
What wonder that the king upon the sacrificial altar was praised while gratifying the assemblies of twice-born?

children.text: rājataḥ pupuvire nirenasaḥ prāpya te 'pi vimalaṃ pratigraham // MSpv_14.35 //
children.translated_text: Even they were purified of blemish, having received from him the spotless gift-acceptance. // MSpv 14.35 //
He, whose decrees bore the mark of his own hand, whose governance equaled <s>Pākaśāsana</s>'s (<s>Indra</s>'s) rule,
bestowed abundant lands extending to the directions, the sun, and the ocean, pleasing the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. // MSpv 14.36 //
He repeatedly listened to the assemblies of the twice-born reciting the scriptures — pure, free of contradictions to the <s>Śruti</s> —
together with their books, radiant with the intermixture of bright letters. // MSpv 14.37 //
For the first-born [<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>] who had come with devoted minds to witness the oblation-fire,
that lordly one, the teacher of the hermitage, unrestricted in hospitality, did not grow weary in performing host-duties. // MSpv 14.38 //
Having himself brought forth and offered abundant precious [gifts] — [gifts] that were hard to obtain even when sought —
the kings, sitting outside awaiting their turn, received his jewels as gifts. // MSpv 14.39 //

children.text: eka eva vasu yaddadau nṛpastatsamāpakamatarkyata kratoḥ /
children.translated_text: The wealth that one king alone gave was thought to suffice for the completion of the sacrifice;

children.text: tyāgaśālini tapaḥsute yayuḥ sarvapārthivadhanānyapi kṣayam // MSpv_14.40 //
children.translated_text: in the presence of that generous son of austerity, the riches of all other kings came to naught. // MSpv 14.40 //
Such was his delight in giving that the kings, wishing to please him,
derived even greater joy from the gifts they had touched and deposited at his dwelling, than [from keeping them]. // MSpv 14.41 //
He whom [the king] blessed — even in a minor task — reducing [the pupil's] faults, [treating him] as a disciple,
that other king was looked upon with envy by other kings — and he was highly esteemed. // MSpv 14.42 //
The directions divided among themselves the earth — [that earth] weighed down like the primeval boar, made to tremble repeatedly by earthquakes —

children.text: vāciropitavatāmunā mahīṃ rājakāya viṣayā vibhejire // MSpv_14.43 //
children.translated_text: not of such [poor quality] in herself — [all this occurred] because he placed [his authority] upon speech. // MSpv 14.43 //
With a resolute mind that had arrived, his consciousness unperturbed by the wealth of <s>sattva</s> (goodness),

children.text: tatra nābhavadasau mahāhave śātravādiva parāṅmukho 'rthinaḥ // MSpv_14.44 //
children.translated_text: he was never there in the great assembly — never turned his face away from the supplicant, as from an enemy. // MSpv 14.44 //
He never looked upon a supplicant with contempt; when asked, he did not delay;

children.text: nāditālpamatha na vyakatthayaddattamiṣṭamapi nānvaśeta saḥ // MSpv_14.45 //
children.translated_text: he did not give a pittance; nor did he boast; even having given the desired [gift], he did not follow up [expecting gratitude]. // MSpv 14.45 //
Even one devoid of virtues was not turned away from the king's presence — [that king] whose mind was passionate for giving;
is the rain-cloud that has risen to pour water to be avoided by barren land? // MSpv 14.46 //

children.text: prema tasya na guṇeṣu nādhikaṃ na sma veda na guṇāntaraṃ ca saḥ /
children.translated_text: His affection was not [only] for the virtuous, nor was it greater [for them]; nor was he ignorant of [their] different virtues;

children.text: ditsayā tadapi pārthivo 'rthinaṃ guṇyaguṇya iti na vyajīgaṇat // MSpv_14.47 //
children.translated_text: but the king, from his desire to give, did not discriminate among supplicants as 'worthy' or 'unworthy.' // MSpv 14.47 //
Immediately upon seeing the mendicant people, [his wealth] went to them of its own accord willingly;
thus the word 'Let it be given!' became free of the purpose of requesting — [it became] superfluous at the distribution. // MSpv 14.48 //
No one who had not obtained wealth departed with desire for wealth; no sick person left with his disease undiagnosed;

children.text: icchatāśitumanāśuṣā na ca pratyagāmi tadupeyuṣā sadaḥ // MSpv_14.49 //
children.translated_text: and no one who desired to eat departed unfed, having approached his assembly. // MSpv 14.49 //
Relishing the flavors of foods — variously prepared, natural, served without mixing of vessels —

children.text: bhāvaśuddhisahitairmudaṃ jano nāṭakairiva babhāra bhojanaiḥ // MSpv_14.50 //
children.translated_text: the people bore delight through the meals, accompanied by purity of sentiment, as if through dramas. // MSpv 14.50 //

children.text: rakṣitāramiti tatra karmaṇi nyasya duṣṭadamanakṣamaṃ harim /
children.translated_text: Having appointed <s>Hari</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) as the protector in that ritual — [<s>Hari</s>] who was capable of subduing the wicked —
the king then completed without flaw the rites of gift-giving, fire-offerings, and worship. // MSpv 14.51 //
'This <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) alone is the excellent companion of those who press the <s>Soma</s>!' — as if acting out [this truth] loudly,
the sacrificial post, beautiful as a pillar of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s arm, bore a ring comparable to a finger-ring. // MSpv 14.52 //

children.text: itthamatra vitatakrame kratau vīkṣya dharmamatha gharmajanmanā /
children.translated_text: Thus, when the sacrifice was in extended progress, then <s>Dharmarāja</s> (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>), beholding <s>dharma</s>, the son of heat [<s>Bhīṣma</s>],

children.text: arghadānamanucodito vacaḥ sabhyamabhyadhita śantanoḥ sutaḥ // MSpv_14.53 //
children.translated_text: prompted to offer the <s>arghya</s> (guest-offering), spoke these words befitting the assembly, the son of <s>Śantanu</s>: // MSpv 14.53 //

children.text: ātmanaiva guṇadoṣakovidaḥ kiṃ na vetsi karaṇīyavastuṣu /
children.translated_text: 'You yourself, O knower of virtues and faults — what do you not know regarding what must be done?

children.text: yattathāpi na gurūnnapṛcchasi tvaṃ kramo 'yamiti tatra kāraṇam // MSpv_14.54 //
children.translated_text: That nevertheless you do not ask elders — the reason for that is: this is the proper procedure.' // MSpv 14.54 //

children.text: snātakaṃ gurumabhīṣṭamṛtvijaṃ saṃyujā ca saha medinīpatim /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>snātaka</s> (graduate), the preceptor, the desired <s>ṛtvij</s> (priest), the ally, and the king —

children.text: arghabhāja iti kīrtayanti ṣaṭ te ca te yugapadāgatāḥ sadaḥ // MSpv_14.55 //
children.translated_text: these six are declared the recipients of <s>arghya</s>; and they have all come together to the assembly.' // MSpv 14.55 //
'The self-existent [<s>Brahmā</s>-descended <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>], born at the face of your sacrifice, whose calamities are averted by the power of mantras, shine all around — mighty;
and the kings too, conquering the other world. // MSpv 14.56 //'
'The virtuous ones individually receive genuine honor, O son of <s>Pṛthā</s>;

children.text: eka eva guṇavattamo 'thavāpūjya ityayamapīṣyate vidhiḥ // MSpv_14.57 //
children.translated_text: but this rule also is desired: that one alone, the most virtuous of all, should be worshipped.' // MSpv 14.57 //
'And here in this entire [assembly], there shines one who is endowed with every virtue, worthy before me —
<s>Hari</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), the enemy of the former demons, deserves the honor in the confluence of earthly, human, and celestial gods.' // MSpv 14.58 //
'If you considered him as merely mortal — [him] before whom the subdued <s>Daityas</s> and <s>Dānavas</s> bow —

children.text: aṃśa eṣa janatātivartino vedhasaḥ pratijanaṃ kṛtasthiteḥ // MSpv_14.59 //
children.translated_text: he is a portion of the Creator who transcends all beings, who has established order for each creature.' // MSpv 14.59 //
'The sole object of meditation, stationed beyond the path of the intellect,
the supreme object of praise, beyond the reach of speech — him whom the <s>yogins</s> worship with devotion, though he dwells exceedingly far.' // MSpv 14.60 //

children.text: padmabhūriti sṛjañjagadrajaḥ satvamacyuta iti sthitiṃ nayan /
children.translated_text: 'As <s>Padmabhū</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), creating the world with <s>rajas</s>; as <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), guiding [it] in sustenance through <s>sattva</s>;

children.text: saṃharanhara iti śritastamasraidhameṣa bhajati tribhirguṇaiḥ // MSpv_14.61 //
children.translated_text: as <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), destroying [it], resort of <s>tamas</s> — this one manifests through three <s>guṇas</s>.' // MSpv 14.61 //
'All-knowing, beginningless, having assumed a body out of desire to favor embodied beings,
free from afflictions, <s>karma</s>, and the experience of [their] fruits — they know this supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> as <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord).' // MSpv 14.62 //
'The devoted ones, in this world, devoted to the one who loves devotees, their sins destroyed by constant remembrance,
attain the culmination of the one who fashions the drama-like mockery of worldly suffering — [they attain] his [abode].' // MSpv 14.63 //
'Those desiring to abandon the worldly condition, with minds fallen upon the path of <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: durgamekamapunarnivṛttaye yaṃ viśanti vaśinaṃ mumukṣavaḥ // MSpv_14.64 //
children.translated_text: enter that self-mastered one — difficult to reach — for the sake of non-return, those seekers of liberation.' // MSpv 14.64 //
He holds the beginning for the birth of embodied beings, and also their end, imperishable;

children.text: bibhrate bhuvamadhaḥ sadātha ca brahmaṇo 'pyupari tiṣṭhate namaḥ // MSpv_14.65 //
children.translated_text: He bears the earth below, and stands above even <s>Brahmā</s>—salutation [to Him]! // MSpv 14.65 //

children.text: kevalaṃ dadhati kartṛvācinaḥ pratyayāniha na jātu karmaṇi /
children.translated_text: The verbal roots that bear agent-signifying suffixes never [bear suffixes] in the object-sense here;
the roots 'to create' and 'to destroy'—in their case, the praise [of Him] has reversed grammatical relations. // MSpv 14.66 //
This one, it is said, first created the waters and placed in them His irresistible virility;
and that became the golden cause—from <s>Brahmā</s> this world was created, as was not [directly] by Him. // MSpv 14.67 //
Like two bedbugs formerly swimming about on the ocean-lord's couch where He reclined,

children.text: gacchataḥ sma madhukaiṭabhau vibhoryasya naidrasukhavighnatāṃ kṣaṇam // MSpv_14.68 //
children.translated_text: <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s> went to momentarily disturb the slumber-pleasure of the all-pervading Lord. // MSpv 14.68 //
Near the moon-face of <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī), there shines the lotus of His navel-lake,
radiant, containing the six-footed bee of <s>Brahmā</s>, skilled in sweet song on the path of the <s>Śruti</s> (Vedas). // MSpv 14.69 //
Though truthful in conduct, He is called a magician; though ancient, He is an infant of appropriate slumber;

children.text: janma bibhratamajaṃ navaṃ budhā yaṃ purāṇapuruṣaṃ pracakṣate // MSpv_14.70 //
children.translated_text: though bearing birth, He is unborn; though ever new, the wise proclaim Him the Primeval Person. // MSpv 14.70 //
With filament-mane scattering great floods of ocean-water by the shaking of His shoulders,
He beheld the earth, with broad-nosed body, lifted up as if for a moment. // MSpv 14.71 //
This one, in His divine leonine form, the enemy of the gods [i.e., the demon] finding no rest even from weapons,
tore open the chest with His soft nails, [satisfying] the irresistible battle-itch. // MSpv 14.72 //
As His beautiful shell-like nails struck the faces of the directional elephants, like wave-fingertips of the ocean,
they bore the radiance of clusters of shining pearls. // MSpv 14.73 //
This one, whose radiance surpassed <s>Virocana</s> (the Sun), desiring the earth from the son of <s>Virocana</s> (<s>Bali</s>)—
the Self-born one, the younger brother of the lord of heaven, whose every offspring is unexcelled, attained the status of <s>Indra</s>'s younger brother. // MSpv 14.74 //

children.text: kiṃ kramiṣyati kilaiṣa vāmano yāvaditthamahasanna dānavāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'How far will this <s>Vāmana</s> (Dwarf) step?'—thus the demons laughed;

children.text: tāvadasya na mamau nabhastale laṅghitārkaśaśimaṇḍalaḥ kramaḥ // MSpv_14.75 //
children.translated_text: but then His stride, surpassing the orbs of the sun and moon, could not be measured in the sky. // MSpv 14.75 //
Even as He strode to the very summit of the sky, with His foot heavier than mountains,
<s>Bali</s>, the powerless one, as if with neck trampled, came under the bondage of the lord of heaven. // MSpv 14.76 //
At will, the heaven-dwellers beheld His thigh, far-reaching, dark-blue, extensive,
in the sky, as if a stream of the celestial river <s>Yamunā</s> had risen in rivalry with the heavenly river. // MSpv 14.77 //
Unable to do the slightest [harm] to Him, <s>Rāhu</s>, who has assumed a body through bodily penance,
the skillful one, afflicts the moon, which resembles the face of His beloved. // MSpv 14.78 //
With imperishable form, with unobstructed memory, [born] to remember the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedas) that had come
to destruction through the lapse of traditional transmission—He became [the sage] named <s>Datta</s>, born in the lineage of <s>Atri</s>. // MSpv 14.79 //
Having assumed the form of the son of <s>Reṇukā</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>), having mowed down the thick multitude of leaves (arms),
this one made the <s>Arjuna</s> (Kṣatriya) forest shade-less, with its many branch-arms lopped off. // MSpv 14.80 //
This one, having become the son of <s>Daśaratha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>), having destroyed the arrogant ten-faced one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) and his people,
made the city of the <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons) protected—with its populace guarded—by [installing] one more terrible in splendor than <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>. // MSpv 14.81 //
Entreated by <s>Svayambhū</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) himself to thoroughly destroy the enemies of the lord of the gods,

children.text: samprati śrayati sūnutāmayaṃ kaśyapasya vasudevarūpiṇaḥ // MSpv_14.82 //
children.translated_text: He now assumes the sonship of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, in the form of <s>Vasudeva</s> [i.e., as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>]. // MSpv 14.82 //
'Father, we are unable to undertake the churning of the ocean without you'—

children.text: yaḥ surairiti suraughavallabho ballavaiśca jagade jagatpatiḥ // MSpv_14.83 //
children.translated_text: thus He, the beloved of the host of gods, was addressed by the gods, and the lord of the world [was also addressed thus] by the cowherds. // MSpv 14.83 //
He who uprooted from heaven the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree—whose fragrance was not endured, being dispelled by enemies,
and whose shade removed the weariness of the gods—[uprooted it] as if [uprooting] the pride of the enemy of <s>Vṛtra</s> (<s>Indra</s>). // MSpv 14.84 //

children.text: yaṃ sametya ca lalāṭalekhayā bibhrataḥ sapadi śaṃbhuvibhramam /
children.translated_text: When the bull (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) approached him, bearing suddenly the movements of <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva) on its forehead-mark,
the eye of <s>Cedipa</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>) [was extinguished] like a lamp by a violent wind, as if by the fierce gale. // MSpv 14.85 //

children.text: yaḥ kolatāṃ ballavatāṃ ca bibhraddaṃṣṭrāmudasyāśu bhujāṃ ca gurvīm /
children.translated_text: He who, bearing the nature of a boar and of a mighty one, raising a tusk and also a heavy arm,

children.text: magnasya toyāpadi dustarāyāṃ gomaṇḍalasyoddharaṇaṃ cakāra // MSpv_14.86 //
children.translated_text: accomplished the upliftment of the circle of cows (the earth), sunk in the impassable flood of waters. // MSpv 14.86 //

children.text: dhanyo 'si yasya harireṣa samakṣa eva dūrādapi kratuṣu yajvabhirijyate yaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Blessed are you, in whose very presence is <s>Hari</s>, who is worshipped from afar in sacrifices by those who perform rituals;
having offered <s>arghya</s> (water of welcome) to Him here, may you obtain praise from the good throughout the worlds, as long as the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> revolves!' // MSpv 14.87 //

children.text: bhīṣmoktaṃ taditi vaco niśamya samyak sāmrājyaśriyamadhigacchatā nṛpeṇa /
children.translated_text: Upon hearing that speech of <s>Bhīṣma</s>, by the king who was attaining the glory of universal sovereignty,

children.text: datter'dhe mahati mahībhṛtāṃ puro 'pi trailokye madhubhidabhūdanargha eva // MSpv_14.88 //
children.translated_text: at the great occasion of the offering, even before the other kings, the enemy of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) became priceless throughout the three worlds. // MSpv 14.88 //
Then, the honor shown to the enemy of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) in that assembly by the son of <s>Pṛthā</s> (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>)

children.text: mānamasahata na cedipatiḥ paravṛddhimatsari mano hi māninām // MSpv_15.1 //
children.translated_text: was not tolerated by the king of <s>Cedi</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>)—for the minds of the proud are envious of another's advancement. // MSpv 15.1 //

children.text: pura eva śārṅgiṇi savairamatha punaramuṃ tadarcayā /
children.translated_text: Already hostile toward the Bow-wielder (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), now again through this worship of him,

children.text: manyurabhajadavagāḍhataraḥ samadoṣakāla iva dehinaṃ jvaraḥ // MSpv_15.2 //
children.translated_text: a deeper anger seized [<s>Śiśupāla</s>], like a fever seizing an embodied being when the [three] humors are simultaneously vitiated. // MSpv 15.2 //
As if threatening the entire assembly of kings, he shook,
his head, with crown-jewel rays flickering, slowly and slowly—[he] who shook the three worlds. // MSpv 15.3 //
He, shedding tears of rage, with the broad surface of his cheeks streaming with profuse heat,
shone with sweat-drop-terrible hands, as if a triply-split elephant in rut. // MSpv 15.4 //
He, intensely heated, frequently shaking off the royal [emblems] like a honey-bee [shaking off pollen],
his body scattering copious water-drops, [appeared] like the primeval <s>Varāha</s> (Boar) risen from the ocean of dissolution. // MSpv 15.5 //
For a moment he embraced a pillar, his shoulder-ornaments hard as joined mountain-peaks—
he, upon whom [excessive] agitation was placed, shook the entire assembly exceedingly. // MSpv 15.6 //
The circle of his arms, turned tawny by the radiance of his golden armlets,
appeared surrounded by arrays of fire-flames of his anger. // MSpv 15.7 //
As if a third eye had been brought into proximity again, on his [face],
his face became cruel, with curved eyebrows and forehead furrowed by heavy frowns. // MSpv 15.8 //
Having attained a state of extreme passion, with mind resolved on aggression,
his gaze, disregarding the fear of the sword, clung to [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] as if embracing a fearful companion. // MSpv 15.9 //
With his fist-bud he struck his own thigh, harsh as a great thunderbolt of rock,
loudly, producing a terrifying sound heard by the startled, trembling, fleeing people. // MSpv 15.10 //

children.text: iti cakrudhe bhṛśamanena nanu mahadavāpya vipriyam /
children.translated_text: Thus he raged violently—for indeed, having suffered a great displeasure,

children.text: yāti vikṛtimapi saṃvṛtimatkimu yannisarganiravagrahaṃ manaḥ // MSpv_15.11 //
children.translated_text: even a disciplined mind undergoes transformation—what then of one that is by nature unrestrained? // MSpv 15.11 //
First, through the bud-clenching caused by the bodily transformation of agitation, without [visible] suffering,
he then opened the anger-blossom, the fruit-product of an inherent quarrel, through speech. // MSpv 15.12 //
Then, resounding through the assembly with a voice deep as the rumble of a water-laden cloud, fearless,
he spoke words excessively harsh with clearly articulated syllables, from the force of extreme anger. // MSpv 15.13 //
'That you have worshipped here, O <s>Pārtha</s>, the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, while he is unhonored by the good—

children.text: prema vilasati mahattadaho dayitaṃ janaḥ khalu guṇīti manyate // MSpv_15.14 //
children.translated_text: ah, love is merely playful in the great! People consider the beloved one as virtuous, indeed! // MSpv 15.14 //
That this <s>arghya</s> (welcome-offering), fit for a king, has been offered here to the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, who is no king—

children.text: grāmyamṛga iva havistadayaṃ bhajate jvalatsu na mahīśavahniṣu // MSpv_15.15 //
children.translated_text: this one receives the oblation like a village beast, while the fires of the earth's lords are blazing. // MSpv 15.15 //

children.text: anṛtāṃ giraṃ na gadasīti jagati paṭahairvighuṣyase /
children.translated_text: You are proclaimed throughout the world with drums as "one who does not speak falsehood";

children.text: nindyamatha ca harimarcayatastava karmaṇaiva vikasatyasatyatā // MSpv_15.16 //
children.translated_text: but your falsity blossoms forth through the very act of worshipping the blameworthy <s>Hari</s>. // MSpv 15.16 //

children.text: tava dharmarāja iti nāma kathamidamapaṣṭhu paṭhyate /
children.translated_text: How is this name "<s>Dharmarāja</s>" (King of Righteousness) inappositely applied to you?
Or rather, people do call even the most inauspicious [Tuesday] '<s>Maṅgala</s>' (Auspicious). // MSpv 15.17 //

children.text: yadi vārcanīyatama eṣa kimapi bhavatāṃ pṛthāsutāḥ /
children.translated_text: If this <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) is indeed the most worship-worthy of all for you, O sons of <s>Pṛthā</s>,
then why were all the kings invited here—for the purpose of insulting [them]? // MSpv 15.18 //
Or rather, you fools, who do not understand <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) in a time of difficult comprehension,
this son of the river (<s>Bhīṣma</s>), dim-witted and inattentive, has been uselessly maintained here for nothing. // MSpv 15.19 //
You yourself, O son of <s>Śantanu</s> (<s>Bhīṣma</s>), placed this one also in the group [deserving] <s>arghya</s>;

children.text: tatra muraripurayaṃ katamo yamanindyabandivadabhiṣṭuṣe vṛthā // MSpv_15.20 //
children.translated_text: among them, who is this slayer of <s>Mura</s>, whom you pointlessly praise, like a degraded panegyrist of <s>Yama</s>? // MSpv 15.20 //
Passing over the assembly of exalted kings, O exceedingly dull one,

children.text: nīci niyatamiha yaccapalo nirataḥ sphuṭaṃ bhavasi nimnagāsutaḥ // MSpv_15.21 //
children.translated_text: you are clearly fickle and devoted to the low, O base one—you are certainly the son of a river! // MSpv 15.21 //

children.text: pratipattumaṅga ghaṭate ca na tava nṛpayogyamarhaṇam /
children.translated_text: And the honor worthy of a king does not befit you to receive, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;

children.text: kṛṣṇa kalaya nanu ko 'hamiti sphuṭamāpadāṃ padamanātmaveditā // MSpv_15.22 //
children.translated_text: "Consider—who am I?"—one who does not know himself is clearly a vessel for calamities. // MSpv 15.22 //

children.text: asurastvayā nyavadhi ko 'pi madhuriti kathaṃ pratīyate /
children.translated_text: 'You have slain some demon called <s>Madhu</s>'—how is that to be believed?
Having crushed a swarm of bees (also <s>madhu</s>) with a stick, you are famed as '<s>Madhusūdana</s>' (Slayer of Madhu), [merely] killing honey! // MSpv 15.23 //
You who took refuge in the bed of <s>Mucukunda</s>, whose power was depleted by the king of <s>Magadha</s>—
your strength, O weakling, is proven merely from the companionship of the son of <s>Rohiṇī</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>)! // MSpv 15.24 //
Deceiving people with falsehood, clever in trickery, a conjurer—

children.text: prītimanubhavasi nagnajitaḥ sutayeṣṭasatya iti sampratīyase // MSpv_15.25 //
children.translated_text: you enjoy pleasure with the daughter of <s>Nagnajit</s>—and [so] you are believed to be 'a lover of truth'! // MSpv 15.25 //
You did not wield your discus in battle, frightened by the fear of the enemy's discus;

children.text: cakradhara iti rathāṅgamadaḥ satataṃ bibharṣi bhuvaneṣu rūḍhaye // MSpv_15.26 //
children.translated_text: yet you constantly bear in the world the boast of being '<s>Cakradhara</s>' (Discus-bearer), from [merely holding] a chariot-wheel! // MSpv 15.26 //
Though you were devoid of <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) in the world, because you married the daughter of the ocean (<s>Satyabhāmā</s>),

children.text: jñātijanajanitanāmapadāṃ tvamataḥ śriyaḥ patiriti prathāmagāḥ // MSpv_15.27 //
children.translated_text: and because of the title given by kinsmen, you have thus attained the fame of being 'Lord of <s>Śrī</s>'! // MSpv 15.27 //
Though you never displayed valor against an enemy in battle,

children.text: vyomni kathamapi cakartha padaṃ vyapadiśyate jagati vikramītyataḥ // MSpv_15.28 //
children.translated_text: because you somehow made a step in the sky, you are called '<s>Vikramin</s>' (The Valiant Strider) in the world! // MSpv 15.28 //

children.text: pṛthivīṃ bibhartha yadi pūrvamidamapi guṇāya vartate /
children.translated_text: If you bore the earth formerly, this too serves as a virtue;
but you, whose earth has been stolen by others, how else can you be called '<s>Bhūmibhṛt</s>' (Earth-bearer) by people? // MSpv 15.29 //
This too is your good fortune—that even though compared with all kings for a moment,
with a wearied palm holding up a mountain, you are called 'one who weighed the mountains' on the surface of the earth. // MSpv 15.30 //
You, incapable, not engaged in auspicious deeds, of impure intellect, unable to conquer <s>Naraka</s> (Hell), terrible in fruition—
for glory, you conquered the son of the Earth (<s>Naraka</s> the demon), [thus gaining fame] in the world beyond. // MSpv 15.31 //
This body of yours, endowed with all faults, [merely] praised with [supposed] qualities—
O quality-less one, why do you vainly undertake the effort of abandoning the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities [of prakṛti])? // MSpv 15.32 //

children.text: tvayi pūjanaṃ jagati jālma kṛtamidamapākṛte guṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: This worship done to you, O wretch, in the world—you who are devoid of virtues—
provokes excessive laughter, like combing [applied to] a bald head! // MSpv 15.33 //
