That this honor was made, before the very eyes of the sons of <s>Pṛthā</s>, as if to a lion among animals—

children.text: asya vanaśuna ivāpacitiḥ paribhāva eva bhavatāṃ bhuvo 'dhipāḥ // MSpv_15.34 //
children.translated_text: it is like [honoring] a village dog—it is the very insult of you [all], O lords of the earth! // MSpv 15.34 //

children.text: avadhījjanaṅgama ivaiṣa yadi hatavṛṣo vṛṣaṃ nanu /
children.translated_text: If this one, like a wandering <s>Jaina</s> ascetic, indeed killed the [sacred] bull (<s>Ariṣṭa</s>),

children.text: sparśamaśucivapurarhati na pratimānanāṃ tu nitarāṃ nṛpocitām // MSpv_15.35 //
children.translated_text: with an impure body he deserves no touch—much less the honor worthy of kings! // MSpv 15.35 //

children.text: yadi nāṅganeti matirasya mṛdurajani pūtanāṃ prati /
children.translated_text: If his mind did not consider her a woman, in the case of <s>Pūtanā</s>,

children.text: stanyamaghṛṇamanasaḥ pibataḥ kila dharmato bhavati sā jananyapi // MSpv_15.36 //
children.translated_text: then by <s>dharma</s>, since he drank the breast-milk of the merciless one, she indeed becomes his mother! // MSpv 15.36 //
The overturning of the cart, the breaking of the tree, the lifting of the mountain, and the like—

children.text: karma yadayamakarottaralaḥ sthiracetasāṃ ka iva tena vismayaḥ // MSpv_15.37 //
children.translated_text: this deed performed by the restless one—for the steadfast, what wonder is there in that? // MSpv 15.37 //
This one, [being the servant] of the son of <s>Ugrasena</s>, tended other kings' animals like cattle—

children.text: svamivadhamasukaraṃ puruṣaiḥ kurute sma yatparamametadadbhutam // MSpv_15.38 //
children.translated_text: that he makes the killing of his own lord, so difficult for [other] men, seem easy — this is the most supreme wonder! // MSpv_15.38 //
Having uttered this arrogant speech at once, together with <s>Veṇudārin</s>,
he who bore the weight of the enemy's strength, unable to endure [further], laughed aloud with a clap of his hands. // MSpv_15.39 //
Even by the harsh words of <s>Caidya</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>), <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) underwent no change;

children.text: satyaniyatavacasaṃ vacasā sujanaṃ janāścalayituṃ ka īśate // MSpv_15.40 //
children.translated_text: who is able to move with words a good man whose speech is bound to truth? // MSpv_15.40 //

children.text: na cataṃ tadeti śapamānamapi yadunṛpāḥ pracukrudhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor did the <s>Yadu</s> kings grow angry at the one cursing thus;
their minds were restrained by <s>Śauri's</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>) command — for people follow the will of the master. // MSpv_15.41 //
Of the repeated offender, unrestrained, bound only by the rope of his own words —

children.text: tasya katitha iti tatprathamaṃ manasā samākhyadaparādhamacyutaḥ // MSpv_15.42 //
children.translated_text: 'How many [offenses] is that now?' — thus <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) first counted the transgressions mentally. // MSpv_15.42 //
Not the entire catalogue of his enemy's misdeeds came upon the path of his memory;

children.text: smartumadhigataguṇasmaraṇāḥ paṭavo na doṣamakhilaṃ khalūttamāḥ // MSpv_15.43 //
children.translated_text: for the noble, who have mastered the remembrance of virtues, are indeed not skilled in remembering all faults. // MSpv_15.43 //
When the king was reviling <s>Śauri</s>, then the son of the celestial river (<s>Bhīṣma</s>) spoke words

children.text: smāha calayati bhuvaṃ maruti kṣubhitasya nādamanukurvadambudheḥ // MSpv_15.44 //
children.translated_text: echoing the roar of the agitated ocean when the storm-wind shakes the earth. // MSpv_15.44 //
Then, not counting his own insult through reverence [for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>],

children.text: prāha murariputiraskaraṇakṣubhitaḥ sma vācamiti jāhnavīsutaḥ // MSpv_15.45 //
children.translated_text: the son of <s>Jāhnavī</s> (<s>Bhīṣma</s>), agitated by the dishonoring of <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), spoke this speech: // MSpv_15.45 //
'The worship of <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) performed by me today in this assembly has been tolerated;

children.text: yasya namayatu sa cāpamayaṃ caraṇaḥ kṛtaḥ śirasi sarvabhūbhṛtām // MSpv_15.46 //
children.translated_text: let him who [objects] bend his bow — this foot has been placed on the heads of all earth-lords.' // MSpv_15.46 //
At these words spoken by <s>Bhīṣma</s>, as if understanding their meaning in an instant,
the group of kings on <s>Śiśupāla's</s> side became exceedingly agitated. // MSpv_15.47 //
The face of <s>Bāṇa</s>, with dark pupils surrounded by coppery eyes reddened with anger,

children.text: bāṇavadanamudadīpi bhiye jagataḥ sakīlamiva sūryamaṇḍalam // MSpv_15.48 //
children.translated_text: blazed forth to terrify the world — like the sun's disc with its corona. // MSpv_15.48 //
Blazing with the brilliant flower-like splendor of his extremely fierce coppery eyes torn wide open, flashing,
<s>Druma</s> appeared like another venomous tree — his body coppery-red as the dawn-tinted moon. // MSpv_15.49 //
By the son of <s>Naraka</s>, whose internal moisture had been dried up by the unceasing fire of enmity,

children.text: kopamarudabhihitena bhṛśaṃ narakātmajena taruṇeva jajvale // MSpv_15.50 //
children.translated_text: struck hard by the wind of anger — [rage] blazed forth as if from fresh [kindling]. // MSpv_15.50 //
Of <s>Uttamauja</s>, wishing to say something, his face appeared distorted like <s>Rāhu's</s> —
with the row of white teeth gleaming within, like [the face swallowing] the moon. // MSpv_15.51 //
First, a laugh faintly indicated the angry form [to come];
then <s>Dantavakra's</s> terrifying [rage], with the thundering sound of a mountain-slope split by a thunderbolt, [was revealed] by the whirling of his fists. // MSpv_15.52 //
Hostility, coming from somewhere, took shelter in the group of kings;

children.text: jāmiharaṇajanitānuśayaḥ samudācacāra nija eva rukmiṇaḥ // MSpv_15.53 //
children.translated_text: in <s>Rukmin</s> himself, the resentment born from the abduction of his sister arose anew. // MSpv_15.53 //
<s>Śubala</s> stamped his foot upon the earth, its mountain-bonds loosened,
its shore-waters trembling in waves, the coiled hoods of serpents beneath broken. // MSpv_15.54 //
Though the kings were angered, <s>Āhuki</s> (<s>Akrūra</s>), whose mind had anticipated the outbreak of quarrel,
took even greater delight through the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> chariot-wheel-hands. // MSpv_15.55 //
Of the raging <s>Yavana</s>, whose steps were checked by intense anger, who had come through calamities — his ferocity,
his terrifying mouth-cavity gaping as if to devour the entire world, wishing to speak — // MSpv_15.56 //
With his massive exposed arm-clubs, rushing forward impetuously, intending to slay all the kings,

children.text: hantumakhilanṛpatīnvasunā vasane vilambini nije vicaskhale // MSpv_15.57 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vasu</s> stumbled on his own trailing garment. // MSpv_15.57 //
Thus the assembly of kings, assuming frightful forms one after another, took on a terrible aspect against him whose mind was undisturbed —
like <s>Māra's</s> army [arrayed] against the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Hari</s>. // MSpv_15.58 //
Then the kings rose for battle, desiring combat, free of improper fear,
with dense crystal-like flashes leaping from their crown-rays, in the assembly. // MSpv_15.59 //
With blossoming eye-petal and lip-petal [faces] borne on the tree-like feet of the earth-lords,
the assembly, as they shook their broad arm-creepers and moved — had the appearance of a forest disturbed by a fierce wind. // MSpv_15.60 //
They deemed even <s>Hari</s> as [worthless as] grass and did not count the <s>Kuru</s>-king either;
those kings, whose pride weighed against the three worlds, did not even fear the son of the River (<s>Bhīṣma</s>). // MSpv_15.61 //
Then the <s>Cedi</s> king, breathing heavily, his body trembling and unsteady, his words venomous,
scattering fire-sparks of teeth-rays — like a hooded serpent, released [his venom]: // MSpv_15.62 //
'Why, O kings, do you not strike together with me this slave, along with his five mendicant sons —

children.text: vadhyamabhihata bhujiṣyamamuṃ saha cānayā sthavirarājakanyayā // MSpv_15.63 //
children.translated_text: and this elderly princess too, who is their common wife?' // MSpv_15.63 //
'Or rather, you yourselves [are enough] — you, of disregarded storm-force!

children.text: vastu kiyadidamayaṃ na mṛdhe mama kevalamasya mukhamīkṣituṃ kṣamaḥ // MSpv_15.64 //
children.translated_text: What is this [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>]? He alone in battle is not even able to look upon my face.' // MSpv_15.64 //
'Let the son of the river (<s>Bhīṣma</s>) and the son of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>) know the rest in this assembly of all;

children.text: yātu nikaṣamadhiyuddhamasau vacanena kiṃ bhavatu sādhvasādhu vā // MSpv_15.65 //
children.translated_text: let him come near for combat — what use are words? Let there be what is right or wrong.' // MSpv_15.65 //
'Shortly, when the foe of the serpent (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) has gone to battle with me,
let the earth, together with the falling heaps, drink the blood sucked by the sharp arrow-tips.' // MSpv_15.66 //

children.text: abhidhāya rūkṣamiti mā sma gama iti pṛthāsuteritām /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus harshly, disregarding the conciliatory words uttered by the son of <s>Pṛthā</s> (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>) — 'Do not go!' —

children.text: vācamanunayaparāṃ sa tataḥ sahasāvakarṇya niriyāya saṃsadaḥ // MSpv_15.67 //
children.translated_text: he then suddenly departed from the assembly. // MSpv_15.67 //
The <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, naturally gracious, with compassionate and patient minds,
did not grow angry with him who came home — the son of their mother's sister. // MSpv_15.68 //
He departed from the sacrifice-ground of the king, his desire unchecked;
then quickly the sons of the earth-lords followed the son of <s>Damaghoṣa</s>, as if they too hastened [to war]. // MSpv_15.69 //
He swiftly crossed the intervals between streets with fast horses;
the women, thrown [aside] by his violent speed, could not gaze upon him — [he] left them with unsatisfied hearts. // MSpv_15.70 //

children.text: kṣaṇamīkṣataḥ pathi janena kimidamiti jalpatā mithaḥ /
children.translated_text: The people on the road looked for a moment, saying to each other 'What is this?'
Reaching his camp with fearless mind, he hastily assembled his army. // MSpv_15.71 //
Filled by the wind of the hurrying conch-blower's cheeks swelling with force,
his battle-conch resounded, its echo splitting the walls of mountain-slopes. // MSpv_15.72 //
His war-trumpet sounded to the end — emitting dire, uneven sounds like those uttered at the world's destruction,
its steady own-echo merged into the deep grave reverberations. // MSpv_15.73 //
Then suddenly, his location became confused with all the people bewildered and agitated,
and took on the appearance of a heaven with its star-disc displaced. // MSpv_15.74 //
Bearing fearful swiftness and attaining similarity
to a mountain veiled in a curtain of smoke, the kings quickly donned their armor. // MSpv_15.75 //
The armor, brought with great difficulty after a long time by the bewildered attendants,
the other [king] crushed to fine powder with his two palms, regarding it with contemptuous gaze. // MSpv_15.76 //
In [the camp] made clamorous with the rising tumult of battle-frenzy,

children.text: śārimaśakadhiropayituṃ dvirade madacyuti janaḥ kathañcana // MSpv_15.77 //
children.translated_text: the men somehow managed to mount the war-elephant from whose temples the rut-fluid was streaming. // MSpv_15.77 //
All around, with polished golden face-guards gleaming with moonlike bright discs,

children.text: tenuratanuvapuṣaḥ pṛthivīṃ sphuṭalakṣyatejasa ivātmajāḥ śriyaḥ // MSpv_15.78 //
children.translated_text: the slender-bodied [warriors] spread across the earth — as if the sons of <s>Śrī</s> herself, their radiance clearly visible. // MSpv_15.78 //
The chariots, situated within dense dust-halos raised from the wheel-rims,
fell [upon the ground] as if like thunderbolts, the creatures terrified by their heavy rumbling. // MSpv_15.79 //
Bearing bodies with gleaming chest-armor bright as the rabbit-marked moon,

children.text: cakruratha saha purandhijanairayathārthasiddhiṃ sarakaṃ mahībhṛtaḥ // MSpv_15.80 //
children.translated_text: the kings, together with their noble women, performed the farewell rite — [yet] with its purpose unfulfilled. // MSpv_15.80 //
The golden goblet, laden with falling lotus-petals heavy with bees,
fell from the hand of the distressed queen, [intended] for her departing beloved. // MSpv_15.81 //
The women's eyes, greatly weakened with bodily fatigue, [showing] compassion on their cheeks,
abandoning incomplete words and intoxication, produced grief that partook of his [husband's] virtue. // MSpv_15.82 //
The fair-eyed women then attempted to speak to the young [warriors] departing for battle —
their voices choked in their throats by grief, only tear-water as their answer, swift in coming. // MSpv_15.83 //
The women, [embracing] their beloveds who were about to march to the vast mountain-grounds,
clasped their chests with the crushing of their full breast-slopes, tears falling like showers of love's arrows. // MSpv_15.84 //
The graceful woman did not release her tears, desiring the auspicious victory-blessing for her beloved;
nor did she notice the bracelet slipping from the wasting arms of the departing one. // MSpv_15.85 //
Upon the departing most beloved, the beautiful woman cast the gaze of both her eyes like fetters —
with the beauty of dark blue lotus-petal garlands, [binding] the pair of his feet. // MSpv_15.86 //
'Where are you going, father? O brave one!' — thus a child, understanding the familiar meaning though indistinctly,
spoke [words of] courage — whose anger was increased by the mother's rebuke. // MSpv_15.87 //
'Rogue! You wish to sport endlessly with the heavenly women!
That is why you are joyful!' — thus another woman, with jealousy, addressed her battle-eager husband. // MSpv_15.88 //
Though the tears were held back, they flowed when the beloved departed, from the bent-browed women;
this indeed is fitting for those of excessively innocent hearts, who bear affection of undissembled essence. // MSpv_15.89 //
Together with the kohl, the stream of tear-water from the lotus-eyes [flowed]
on all sides of the cheek-surfaces of the fair-bodied woman — like the dark track of grief's path. // MSpv_15.90 //
The beloved, departing just a few steps, restrained for but a moment by the bent-browed one —
the sound of bracelets slipping from her drooping arm-pair was heard, as if a muffled sneeze. // MSpv_15.91 //
On the path of her most beloved, a certain woman, rushing with eagerness, her spotless long garment slipping,

children.text: bhūminabhasi rabhasena yatī virarāja kācana samaṃ maholkayā // MSpv_15.92 //
children.translated_text: shone between earth and sky — like a great meteor. // MSpv_15.92 //
Even when the assembly of kings was battle-ready, the warrior-folk, with minds fixed singly on following [their lords] to death,

children.text: dīnaparijanakṛtāśrujalo na bhaṭījanaḥ sthiramanāḥ vicaklame // MSpv_15.93 //
children.translated_text: did not waver in firm resolve, though the pitiable servants shed tears. // MSpv_15.93 //
As if knowing that the sight of him would be exceedingly difficult to obtain again, the young wife,

children.text: yāntamanimiṣamatṛptamanāḥ patimīkṣate sma bhṛśayā dṛśaḥ pathaḥ // MSpv_15.94 //
children.translated_text: insatiate in mind, gazed upon her departing husband with unblinking eyes, straining the path of her gaze. // MSpv_15.94 //
'Return safely soon, O warrior, from battle!' — this fond blessing uttered by her husband,

children.text: sadyaḥ prasahya dvitayena netrayoḥ pratyācacakṣe galatā bhaṭastriyāḥ // MSpv_15.95 //
children.translated_text: was immediately contradicted by both eyes of the soldier's wife, overflowing with streaming tears. // MSpv_15.95 //

children.text: kācitkīrṇā rajobhirdivamanuvidadhe bhinnavaktrendulakṣmīr aśrīkāḥ kāścidantardiśa iva dadhire dāhamudbhrāntasatvāḥ /
children.translated_text: Some [women] were covered with dust and showed broken moon-beauty of their faces to the sky; some held burning [anguish] within like the directions, their beings bewildered, bereft of beauty;

children.text: bhremurvātyā ivānyāḥ pratipadamaparā bhūmivatkampamāpuḥ prasthāne pārthivānāmaśivamiti puro bhāvi nāryaḥ śaśaṃsuḥ // MSpv_15.96 //
children.translated_text: others whirled like whirlwinds; another trembled like the earth — the women foretold inauspicious [omens] at the departure of the kings. // MSpv_15.96 //
Then a certain eloquent man, left behind by the son of <s>Damaghoṣa</s>,
approaching <s>Hari</s>, spoke words of clearly ambiguous meaning in the assembly: // MSpv_16.1 //

children.text: abhidhāya tadā tadapriyaṃ śiśupālo 'nuśayaṃ paraṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having spoken that displeasure then, <s>Śiśupāla</s> has gone into extreme remorse;

children.text: bhavato 'bhimanāḥ samīhate saruṣaḥ kartumupetya mānanām // MSpv_16.2 //
children.translated_text: full of regard for you, he wishes, approaching angrily, to perform salutation.' // MSpv_16.2 //
'Exceedingly agitated, let him come with great joy, pressing hard mercilessly,

children.text: pracurādhigatāṅganirvṛtiṃ paritastvāṃ khalu vigraheṇa saḥ // MSpv_16.3 //
children.translated_text: having attained full satisfaction of all his limbs — indeed, he [wishes] to wrestle with you.' // MSpv_16.3 //

children.text: praṇataḥ śirasā kariṣyate sakalairetya samaṃ dharādhipaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He will bow with his head, coming together with all the earth-lords —'

children.text: tava śāsanamāśu bhūpatiḥ paravānadya yatastvayaiva saḥ // MSpv_16.4 //
children.translated_text: The king shall swiftly carry out your command; being now subordinate, he depends upon you alone // <s>MSpv</s> 16.4 //
Of you who surpass fire and moth in splendor, who are of controlled mind and capable deeds,

children.text: tava sarvavidheyavartinaḥ praṇatiṃ bibhrati kena bhūbhṛtaḥ // MSpv_16.5 //
children.translated_text: in whose command all things move—by what means do kings bear obeisance to you? // <s>MSpv</s> 16.5 //
Since you support a populace oppressed by enemies, with a mind free from fear,

children.text: tava kṛṣṇa guṇāstato narairasamānasya dadhatyagaṇyatām // MSpv_16.6 //
children.translated_text: therefore, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, your virtues, unequaled among men, attain incalculability // <s>MSpv</s> 16.6 //
Shameless before the wicked, trembling before those who bow, motherless, fearless, an atheist—
endowed with your kind of courtesy, where is another like you, virtuous and without arrogance? // <s>MSpv</s> 16.7 //
Even now, for you who killed the cowherd women's lover and the bull in dreadful <s>Naraka</s>,
the conduct that has humbled the sinful is well praised by the people // <s>MSpv</s> 16.8 //
Having performed worship of kings, having terrified enemies with your forces,
be you, with your retinue, higher even than the highest of mountains and earth-bearers // <s>MSpv</s> 16.9 //
Impregnable on all sides, with your elephant-herds dense as cloud-masses,

children.text: nagareṣu bhavantu vīthayaḥ parikīrṇā vanajairmṛgādibhiḥ // MSpv_16.10 //
children.translated_text: may your city streets be strewn with forest-born animals like deer // <s>MSpv</s> 16.10 //
May your enemy, his own prowess wholly concealed, his rise brought about only by your constant calamity,
be an everlasting disease to your lofty and steadfast spirit // <s>MSpv</s> 16.11 //
O bull of the <s>Yadus</s>, of you with eyes lovely as blooming blue lotuses, having joined battle with <s>Caidya</s>,

children.text: yadupuṅgava bandhusauhṛdāttvayi pātā sasuro navāsavaḥ // MSpv_16.12 //
children.translated_text: may your father-in-law, out of kinship-affection, be a protector, fresh as new wine // <s>MSpv</s> 16.12 //

children.text: calitānakadundubhiḥ puraḥ sabalastvaṃ saha sāraṇena tam /
children.translated_text: With <s>Anakadundubhi</s> preceding, you together with <s>Sāraṇa</s>, along with your army,
having approached the battle impetuously, with mace in hand, should deign to receive him // <s>MSpv</s> 16.13 //
Having met with <s>Śiśupāla</s> who strikes down enemies in battles,
be long at ease, together with all the <s>Sātvatas</s>, with your women confident and delighted // <s>MSpv</s> 16.14 //
Let the king, joyful, having conquered anger, behold you, the enemy of the great kings,

children.text: asakṛjjitasaṃyataṃ puro muditaḥ sapramadaṃ mahīpatiḥ // MSpv_16.15 //
children.translated_text: one who has been repeatedly conquered and restrained, now before him, with delight and with joy // <s>MSpv</s> 16.15 //

children.text: iti joṣamavasthitaṃ dviṣaḥ praṇidhiṃ gāmabhidhāya sātyakiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus addressed the enemy's spy who stood in silence, <s>Sātyaki</s>

children.text: vadati sma vaco 'tha coditaścalitaikabhrū rathāṅgapāṇinā // MSpv_16.16 //
children.translated_text: then spoke these words, prompted by the discus-wielding one, with one eyebrow raised // <s>MSpv</s> 16.16 //
"Your speech, sweet on the outside and unpleasant within, is such that though made by a skilled speaker,
when perceived in its full meaning, it is seen as pleasant outside but unpleasant within" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.17 //
"Exceedingly soft on one side, on the other harsh as the stalk of a fresh lotus,

children.text: vahati sphuṭamekameva te vacanaṃ śākapalāśadeśyatām // MSpv_16.18 //
children.translated_text: your single utterance clearly bears the character of the <s>śāka</s>-leaf and the <s>palāśa</s>" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.18 //

children.text: prakaṭaṃ mṛdu nāma jalpataḥ paruṣaṃ sūcayatorthamantarā /
children.translated_text: "Of one who speaks openly what is soft in name but suggests harshness of meaning within—
from such harshness one should recoil, as wayfarers do from a harsh-voiced bird of omen" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.19 //
"If the king has honored <s>Hari</s>, what jealousy is there for your king?
Who resents the placing on one's head of a sweet-smelling flower, for its repose?" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.20 //
"Ah, how delicate is the heart of the petty—since whatever unpleasant thing enters it

children.text: sahasaiva samudgirantyamī jarayantyeva hi tanmanīṣiṇaḥ // MSpv_16.21 //
children.translated_text: they blurt out at once; indeed, the wise merely let such things age within" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.21 //
"The good person is by nature always devoted to benefiting all people;
yet alas, even so, the eminence of the good constantly produces a serious heart-disease in the wicked" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.22 //
"The best person is never tormented; the middling one, even if tormented, is well-concealed;
the lowest, afflicted by others' prosperity, is openly burst with his vile intentions" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.23 //
"The wickedness of the wicked, barren as it is, undiminished in its ascetic affliction, abandoned by flowers—

children.text: khalatāṃ khalatāmivāsatīṃ pratipadyeta kathaṃ budho janaḥ // MSpv_16.24 //
children.translated_text: like a barren and vile woman—how could a wise person resort to it?" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.24 //
<s>Keśava</s> gave no reply to the cursing king of <s>Cedi</s>;

children.text: anuhuṅkurute ghanadhvaniṃ na hi gomāyurutāni kesarī // MSpv_16.25 //
children.translated_text: a lion does not echo back the cries of jackals along with the rumble of thunder // <s>MSpv</s> 16.25 //
"The great-minded ones have conquered the current of anger; the base person is immediately conquered by wrath;

children.text: vijitena jitasya durmatermatimadbhiḥ saha kā virodhitā // MSpv_16.26 //
children.translated_text: what rivalry can the evil-minded, conquered by the already-conquered, have with the wise?" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.26 //

children.text: vacanairasatāṃ mahīyaso na khalu vyeti gurutvamuddhataiḥ /
children.translated_text: "The dignity of the great is not diminished by the insolent words of the base;
is the great value of a gem diminished when scattered with dust from the earth?" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.27 //

children.text: paritoṣayitā na kaścana svagato yasya guṇo 'sti dehinaḥ /
children.translated_text: "No embodied being whose virtue is innate has anyone who can fully gratify him;
a petty person seeks to gratify his own people with stories of others' faults" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.28 //
"Congenitally blind to their own misdeeds, divinely clear-sighted in seeing others' faults,
loud-voiced about their own virtues, observing ascetic vows—the wicked are experts at seizing others' merits" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.29 //
"To conceal for long even the manifest faults of others is great skill;
to reveal one's own virtues is extreme lack of skill for noble minds" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.30 //
"What magnanimous person recounts his own virtue, even when celebrated by the entire world?

children.text: vaditā na laghīyaso 'paraḥ svaguṇaṃ tena vadatyasau svayam // MSpv_16.31 //
children.translated_text: Since no lesser person will speak his virtue for him, he must therefore speak it himself" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.31 //
"Some men, without boasting, release anger like venomous serpents;
others, holding an inner nature of hollowness, are like drums—all sound, no substance" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.32 //
"This <s>Cedi</s> king whom fate has destined to behold the slayer of <s>Naraka</s>—

children.text: drutametu na hāpayiṣyate sadṛśaṃ tasya vidhātumuttaram // MSpv_16.33 //
children.translated_text: let him come quickly; he will not be denied a fitting reply" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.33 //
"Is the king armed? Or does he wish to make a treaty with this one?

children.text: harirākramaṇena saṃnati kila vibhrati bhiyetyasaṃbhavaḥ // MSpv_16.34 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> showing submission through retreat—this is indeed an impossibility" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.34 //
"The evil-minded one, violently overstepping the great, perishes by his own fault;

children.text: kurute na khalu svayecchayā śalabhānindhanamiddhadīdhitiḥ // MSpv_16.35 //
children.translated_text: the blazing fire does not of its own will make moths its fuel" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.35 //

children.text: yadapūri purā mahīpatirna mukhena svayamagasā śatam /
children.translated_text: "The king's hundred insults, which he formerly did not fill with his own mouth,

children.text: atha saṃprati paryapūpurattadasau dūtamukhena śārṅgiṇaḥ // MSpv_16.36 //
children.translated_text: he now completes through the messenger's mouth, against the wielder of <s>Śārṅga</s>" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.36 //
"If from this city with its gates flung open you will say anything further displeasing,

children.text: vivariṣyati taccirasya naḥ samayodvīkṣaṇarakṣitāṃ krudham // MSpv_16.37 //
children.translated_text: that will open up in a moment our anger, restrained until now by waiting for the proper occasion" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.37 //
Hearing that mighty speech of <s>Śini</s>'s grandson, who was not one to incur sins,

children.text: punarujjhitasādhvaso dviṣāmabhidhatte sma vaco vacoharaḥ // MSpv_16.38 //
children.translated_text: the spokesman, fearless again before the enemies, spoke these words, a stealer of speech // <s>MSpv</s> 16.38 //

children.text: vivinakti na buddhidurvidhaḥ svayameva svahitaṃ pṛthagjanaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The common man, evil in judgment, does not discern by himself what is beneficial to him;

children.text: yadudīritamapyadaḥ parairna vijānāti tadadbhutaṃ mahat // MSpv_16.39 //
children.translated_text: that he does not comprehend even what is stated by others—this great wonder" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.39 //
"The wise perceive danger to themselves from afar, or trust what comes from others;

children.text: na paropahitaṃ na ca svataḥ pramimīte 'nubhavādṛte 'lpadhīḥ // MSpv_16.40 //
children.translated_text: the dull-witted neither measures what is done by others nor by himself, without direct experience" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.40 //

children.text: kuśalaṃ khalu tubhyameva tadvacanaṃ kṛṣṇa yadabhyadhāmaham /
children.translated_text: "That speech which I uttered was indeed for your own welfare, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;
the virtuous are devoted to instructing even those who face their own destruction" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.41 //
"Both what I said at once in haste—the conciliatory and the other, to you—

children.text: pravibhajya pṛthaṅmanīṣayā svaguṇaṃ yatkila tatkariṣyasi // MSpv_16.42 //
children.translated_text: separating them distinctly with your intellect, you will surely do what is your own merit" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.42 //
"Or rather, good speech goes to futility upon those of fixed prejudice,
like the net of rays of the cool-rayed moon upon lotus-pools when the sun is absent" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.43 //
"Disregarding merit and demerit, a person follows only his own inclination with certainty;

children.text: apahāya mahīśamarcicatsadati tvāṃ nanu bhīmapūrvajaḥ // MSpv_16.44 //
children.translated_text: abandoning a great king to worship you—did not the elder brother of <s>Bhīma</s> do just that?" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.44 //

children.text: tvayi bhaktimatā na satkṛtaḥ kururājā gurureva cedipaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The <s>Kuru</s> king, devoted to you, was not honored; the <s>Cedi</s> lord indeed is the elder;
is a gem born from an elephant's forehead blameworthy if abandoned by a lion fond of flesh?" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.45 //
"The white is indeed made prominent by the white on high, and by the dark below;
<s>Śaṅkara</s> bore the celestial river on his head, while the slayer of <s>Madhu</s> bore it on his foot" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.46 //

children.text: abudhaiḥ kṛtamānasamvidastava pārthaiḥ kuta eva yogyatā /
children.translated_text: "Of the <s>Pārthas</s>, who have made you their idol without wisdom, where is the fitness?

children.text: sahasi plavagairupāsitaṃ na hi guñjāphalameti soṣmatām // MSpv_16.47 //
children.translated_text: A <s>guñjā</s> berry worshipped by monkeys does not attain the value of a gem" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.47 //
"The king, tolerant of a hundred offenses, surpasses you in forbearance alone;

children.text: hṛtavatyapi bhīṣmakātmajāṃ tvayi cakṣāma samartha eva yat // MSpv_16.48 //
children.translated_text: even when you abducted the daughter of <s>Bhīṣmaka</s>, we tolerated it—for indeed the powerful can" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.48 //
"Having stolen a bride bestowed by elders, from the family of a king,

children.text: janako 'si janārdana sphuṭaṃ hatadharmārthatayā manobhuvaḥ // MSpv_16.49 //
children.translated_text: you are clearly, O <s>Janārdana</s>, the father of <s>Kāma</s>, by having slain the purpose of <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s>" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.49 //
Of you whose beauty is indescribable, or whose hue is borrowed from another's plumage,

children.text: tava sarvagatasya saṃprati kṣitipaḥ kṣipnurabhīśumāniva // MSpv_16.50 //
children.translated_text: the king is now everywhere diminishing you, like the sun diminishing the frost-rayed moon // <s>MSpv</s> 16.50 //
"My proposal of peace to you, O agitated king, is in vain;

children.text: pralayollasitasya vāridheḥ parivāho jagataḥ karoti kim // MSpv_16.51 //
children.translated_text: what can a dam do for the world when the ocean overflows at the dissolution?" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.51 //
"I was sent by the king to summon <s>Mādhava</s> to battle;

children.text: na pareṣu mahaujasaśchalādapakurvanti malimlucā iva // MSpv_16.52 //
children.translated_text: those of great strength do not act through deception against others, like thieves" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.52 //

children.text: tadayaṃ samupaiti bhūpatiḥ payasāṃ pūra ivānivāritaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Therefore this king approaches like an unrestrained flood of waters;

children.text: avilambitamedhi vetasastaruvanmādhava mā sma bhajyathāḥ // MSpv_16.53 //
children.translated_text: without delay take your stand, O <s>Mādhava</s>—like a cane-tree, do not be broken" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.53 //

children.text: paripāti sa kevalaṃ śiśūniti tannāmani mā sma viśvasīḥ /
children.translated_text: "He protects merely children"—do not trust that name alone;

children.text: taruṇānapi rakṣati kṣamī sa śaraṇyaḥ śaraṇāgatāndviṣaḥ // MSpv_16.54 //
children.translated_text: the forbearing one, as a refuge, protects even young warriors who come seeking shelter, though they be enemies // <s>MSpv</s> 16.54 //

children.text: na vidadhyuraśaṅkamapriyaṃ mahataḥ svārthaparāḥ pare katham /
children.translated_text: "How could those devoted to self-interest do harm fearlessly to the great?
Even when angered, the noble-minded one accepts reconciliation with a mere bow" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.55 //

children.text: hitamapriyamicchasi śrutaṃ yadi saṃdhatsva purā na naśyasi /
children.translated_text: "If you wish to hear what is beneficial though unpleasant, make peace before you perish;
but if you are satisfied with pleasant falsehoods—may you conquer, live, and be lord of the earth" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.56 //
"Even though a conqueror of adversaries, you will undoubtedly be defeated in battle by <s>Caidya</s>;

children.text: grasate hi tamopahaṃ muhurnanu rāhvāhvamaharpatiṃ tamaḥ // MSpv_16.57 //
children.translated_text: does not darkness called <s>Rāhu</s> repeatedly swallow the lord of day, the destroyer of darkness?" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.57 //
"Having recently conquered the fish-bannered one, resplendent, honored by the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> hosts,

children.text: kṣitipaḥ kṣayitoddhatāntako haralīlāṃ sa viḍambayiṣyati // MSpv_16.58 //
children.translated_text: the king, who has destroyed the arrogant <s>Antaka</s> (death), will imitate the sport of <s>Hara</s>" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.58 //
"Of him who holds abundant fame earned step by step, having slain the intoxicated wicked elephant,

children.text: na bibheti raṇe harerapi kṣitipaḥ kā gaṇanāsya vṛṣṇiṣu // MSpv_16.59 //
children.translated_text: the king does not fear even <s>Hari</s> in battle—what account does he make of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>?" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.59 //

children.text: na tadadbhutamasya yanmukhaṃ yudhi paśyanti bhiyā na śatravaḥ /
children.translated_text: "It is no wonder that his enemies do not behold his face in battle from fear;

children.text: dravatāṃ nanu pṛṣṭhamīkṣate vadanaṃ so 'pi na jātu vidviṣām // MSpv_16.60 //
children.translated_text: surely he too never sees the face of his fleeing foes—only their backs" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.60 //
"If the rain-clouds, with briefly flickering thin radiance, reaching autumn, with weapons shattered,

children.text: dadhate 'ribhirasya tulyatāṃ yadi nāsārabhṛtaḥ payobhṛtaḥ // MSpv_16.61 //
children.translated_text: attain equality with his enemies—then not!" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.61 //
"His pair of feet, repeatedly soiled by battle-dust from enemies, washed by the tears of their women,
is then anointed with the ray-colors of the crown-jewels of kings" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.62 //
"His bow, which when drawn to full tension for a moment in battle becomes exceedingly hard,
together with the bow causes the families of enemies to assume a submission that fears destruction" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.63 //
"His friends consider this cold-rayed moon to be hot-rayed; his adversaries

children.text: kṛtibhiḥ kṛtadṛṣṭivibhramāḥ srajameke bhujagaṃ yathāpare // MSpv_16.64 //
children.translated_text: see a garland where the skilled see a snake—like some seeing ornaments where others see serpents" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.64 //
"Of him whose death is unapproachable, whose body is singularly superhuman,

children.text: bhuvi samprati na pratiṣṭhitāḥ sadṛśā yasya surairarātayaḥ // MSpv_16.65 //
children.translated_text: his enemies, equal to gods, are not now established on earth" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.65 //
"Of this king of exceedingly wondrous deeds, whatever opposes him—
this son of the <s>Yadu</s> leads the family of enemies to an inexhaustible destruction" // <s>MSpv</s> 16.66 //
With the wealth of headless trunks rising high, the paths blocked by the <s>makara</s> formation
he repeatedly crossed, by the strength of his own arms, the great oceans of battle. // <s>MSpv</s> 16.67 //

children.text: na cikīrṣati yaḥ smayoddhato nṛpatittaccaraṇopapagaṃ śiraḥ /
children.translated_text: He who, puffed up with pride, does not bow his head to that one's feet —

children.text: caraṇaṃ kurute gatasmayaḥ smasāveva tadīyamūrdhani // MSpv_16.68 //
children.translated_text: that very one, his pride gone, [finds that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s] foot is placed upon his own head. // <s>MSpv</s> 16.68 //
With only his two arms as weapons, setting aside the four-fold army,

children.text: bahuśaḥ saha śakradantinā sa caturdantamagacchadāhavam // MSpv_16.69 //
children.translated_text: he went many times to battle against four-tusked [elephants], together with <s>Indra</s>'s elephant (<s>Airāvata</s>). // <s>MSpv</s> 16.69 //
Of you two, both embraced by <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), whose beautiful discuses remain unshaken, [united] by affection —

children.text: yuvayoridameva bhidyate yadupendrastvamatīndra eva saḥ // MSpv_16.70 //
children.translated_text: only this difference exists: that you are subordinate to <s>Indra</s> (<s>Upendra</s>), while he indeed surpasses <s>Indra</s>. // <s>MSpv</s> 16.70 //
Though the unborn [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], whose share of enjoyment is abundant in worldly prosperity, has conquered many cities of enemies,
this king, whose radiance is that of the full moon, produces [only] the beauty of a crescent moon [in comparison]. // <s>MSpv</s> 16.71 //
He who, seized by his rising, swiftly brings to ruin — whose rise is itself unbreakable —
causes another, whose arm-branches tremble on the earth's surface, to attain great elevation. // <s>MSpv</s> 16.72 //
And finding a gap in between, causing a breach in [the enemy's] circle from another direction,

children.text: khanati kṣatasaṃhati kṣaṇādapi mūlāni mahānti kasyacit // MSpv_16.73 //
children.translated_text: he digs up even the great roots of someone, shattering the compact mass in an instant. // <s>MSpv</s> 16.73 //
He swiftly uproots some followers bearing thick leaves [dense armies] and makes them his own;

children.text: dṛḍhamapyaparaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ pratikūlaṃ nitarāṃ nirasyati // MSpv_16.74 //
children.translated_text: even one firmly established, [if] hostile, he completely casts down. // <s>MSpv</s> 16.74 //

children.text: iti pūra ivodakasya yaḥ saritāṃ prāvṛṣijas taṭadrumaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, like a flood of river-waters in the rainy season with [uprooted] bank-trees,

children.text: kvacanāpi mahānakhaṇḍitaprasaraḥ krīḍati bhūbhṛtāṃ gaṇaiḥ // MSpv_16.75 //
children.translated_text: he, the great one, whose advance is nowhere checked, sports with the hosts of kings. // <s>MSpv</s> 16.75 //
Possessing rows of heavy stones, blocking the uninterrupted sky all around,

children.text: adhirūḍhanitambabhūmayo na vimuñcanti cirāya mekhalāḥ // MSpv_16.76 //
children.translated_text: having scaled the hip-regions — the girdles do not release [the mountains] for a long time. // <s>MSpv</s> 16.76 //
With beautiful arms [adorned] by fresh pearl ornaments, they embrace the bracelets;

children.text: niyataṃ dadhate ca citrakairaviyogaṃ pṛthugaṇḍaśailataḥ // MSpv_16.77 //
children.translated_text: and they constantly maintain, through varied [adornments], inseparability from the broad cheek-surface of cliffs. // <s>MSpv</s> 16.77 //
Thus, the splendors that the women of enemies formerly obtained in their homes —
all of that now plainly [rests] upon the mountain-summits, through [his] calamitous [conquest]. // <s>MSpv</s> 16.78 //
Burning even the great trees of the <s>Kukura</s> and <s>Andhaka</s> clans excessively, like a forest-fire,
most wondrous is this — that the king will not make the earth dark [i.e., <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-less]. // <s>MSpv</s> 16.79 //

children.text: paritaḥ pramitākṣarāpi sarvaṃ viṣayaṃ vyāptavatī gatā pratiṣṭhām /
children.translated_text: Though measured in its syllables, [his] command, pervading every domain, has attained authority;

children.text: na khalu pratihanyate kutaścitparibhāṣeva garīyasī yadājñā // MSpv_16.80 //
children.translated_text: the weighty decree of a <s>Yadu</s> [lord] is never obstructed from any quarter — like a sovereign edict. // <s>MSpv</s> 16.80 //
The earth (<s>bhū</s>), whom the ancient <s>Puruṣa</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), having assumed the <s>Varāha</s> (Boar) form, once uplifted for a moment —

children.text: tenohyate sāṃpratamakṣataiva kṣatāriṇā samyagasau punarbhūḥ // MSpv_16.81 //
children.translated_text: that same earth is now again properly borne by him, the destroyer of enemies (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), undiminished — a wife [re-]married. // <s>MSpv</s> 16.81 //

children.text: bhūyāṃsa kvacidapi kāmamaskhalantastuṅgatvaṃ dadhati ca yadyapi dvaye 'pi /
children.translated_text: "Though the waves of the ocean are more numerous, stumble nowhere as they wish, and attain height in both —

children.text: kallolāḥ salilanidheravāpya pāraṃ śīryante na guṇamahormayastadīyāḥ // MSpv_16.82 //
children.translated_text: upon reaching the shore they shatter; but the great waves of his virtues do not. // <s>MSpv</s> 16.82 //

children.text: lokālokavyāhataṃ gharmaraśmeḥ śālīnaṃ vā dhāma nālaṃ prasartum /
children.translated_text: "The light of the sun, blocked by [Mount] <s>Lokāloka</s>, or the modest flame — [neither] is able to spread forth;

children.text: lokasyāgre paśyato dhṛṣṭamāśu krāmatyuccairbhūbhṛto yasya tejaḥ // MSpv_16.83 //
children.translated_text: but his splendor boldly strides forth swiftly, before the watching world, over the kings. // <s>MSpv</s> 16.83 //

children.text: vicchittirnavacandanena vapuṣo bhinno 'dharo 'laktakair acchācche patitāñjane ca nayane śroṇyo 'lasanmekhalāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Sandalwood-paste adorning the body, lower lip colored with <s>alaktaka</s> (lac-dye), clear eyes touched with collyrium, hips [swaying] with languid girdles,

children.text: prāpto mauktikahāramunnatakucābhogastadīyadviṣām itthaṃ nityavibhūṣaṇā yuvatayaḥ saṃpatsu cāpatsvapi // MSpv_16.84 //
children.translated_text: lofty breast-slopes adorned with pearl necklaces — thus his enemies' wives are eternally adorned, both in prosperity and in adversity. // <s>MSpv</s> 16.84 //
"Having slain you, the mighty one, in battle — [making] the name '<s>Śiśupāla</s>' ('child-protector') literally true —
he will show tender-heartedness toward the weeping troops of your women." // <s>MSpv</s> 16.85 //
When this speech, as weighty as the winds at the end of a cosmic age, was uttered by that eloquent one (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>),

children.text: pracakṣubhe sapadi tadamburāśinā samaṃ mahāpralayasamudyataṃ sadaḥ // MSpv_17.1 //
children.translated_text: the assembly at once became agitated — together with that ocean — as if the great dissolution had commenced. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.1 //
With passionate [fury], streaming with copious hot sweat, slapping broad thigh-platforms loudly,

children.text: muhurmuhurdaśanavikhaṇḍitoṣṭhayā ruṣā nṛpāḥ priyatamayeva bhejire // MSpv_17.2 //
children.translated_text: biting their lips with their teeth again and again — the kings were seized by anger, as if by a most beloved [mistress]. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.2 //
On the mace (<s>gada</s>) — whose arm-ornament was shattered in an instant — placed on [his] own shoulder by his palm,
with sparkling reddish gems [loosened from the armlet], the fire of rage was clearly visible as if [emitting] sparks. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.3 //
When <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) laughed aloud in contempt, with the circle of his gleaming teeth radiating,

children.text: ruṣāruṇīkṛtamapi tena tatkṣaṇaṃ nijaṃ vapuḥ punarayannijāṃ rucim // MSpv_17.4 //
children.translated_text: his own body, though already reddened by anger, at that very moment recovered its [natural white] luster again. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.4 //
When [<s>Balarāma</s>] leaped up, his broad necklace-circle whirling, and his firebrand revolving rapidly,
[and] struck the hard stone floor with his broad shoulder — thereupon the entire assembly seemed to spin. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.5 //
Of <s>Yudhājit</s>, who was raging, his lotus-face sweated again profusely,
fanned hastily [yet in vain] — by the hot winds of his garment-ends [blown by] the gusts of his breathing. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.6 //
Risen for the destruction of <s>Prajāpati</s>'s (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>'s) sacrifice — like a terrible, raging fever —

children.text: samudyataṃ sapadi vadhāya vidviṣāmatikrudhaṃ niṣadhamanauṣadhaṃ janaḥ // MSpv_17.7 //
children.translated_text: the people perceived him, the <s>Niṣadha</s> [king], rising suddenly for the slaughter of enemies, furiously enraged, without remedy. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.7 //
Of <s>Sudhanvan</s>, mutually enraged, crushing [his palms together] — [his] pair of hands muddied with golden dust from [his] wound-bracelets,
were washed at once by his own tears ceaselessly streaming. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.8 //
<s>Āhuki</s> [raised] his forefinger — elongated, blazing with fire-flame-radiance at the nail-tip's halo of splendor,
resembling a whirling firebrand not yet spinning — as if to burn the world. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.9 //
<s>Manmatha</s> (Love) assumed a terrible-to-behold [aspect], just as formerly, accustomed to the audacity of burning —

children.text: dhruvaṃ puraḥ saśaramamuṃ tṛtīyayā haro 'pi na vyasahata vīkṣituṃ dṛśā // MSpv_17.10 //
children.translated_text: surely even <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) could not have endured to look at him with his third eye, [if he stood] before [<s>Āhuki</s>] holding his arrow. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.10 //
<s>Pṛthu</s> (<s>Pṛthurāja</s>), contemplating with relish the approaching battle, with body-hair bristling on his chest, stroked with his forehand
his broad [chest], hard as the breast-surface of a cruel, unyielding mistress — its sandal-paste [already] rubbed away. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.11 //
Seeing the breach of decorum, when even the weighty son of <s>Gāndinī</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) was [challenged] by the enemy's harsh speech —
the people then perceived the mountain-lords as if overturned by the winds of a cosmic age-cycle. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.12 //
Rolling his eyes muddied with intoxication [of rage], making a terrifying roar by striking the ground with his hands,
<s>Prasenajit</s> assumed a deeply reddened body from fury — like a rouge-red elephant. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.13 //
<s>Gaveṣaṇa</s>, with saffron-tinged, dense, unspaced water-drops — reddened as ripe pomegranate —

children.text: sa matsarasphuṭitavapurviniḥsṛtairbabhau ciraṃ nicita ivāsṛjāṃ lavaiḥ // MSpv_17.14 //
children.translated_text: his body burst open [as it were] with jealous rage, shone for a long time as if heaped with drops of blood. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.14 //
With feet stamping in agitation, splitting the ground and opening up subterranean passages,
<s>Śini</s>'s [descendant] exposed the nether world (<s>Rasātala</s>) — its serpents tormented by the sun's rays to which they were unaccustomed. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.15 //

children.text: pratikṣaṇaṃ vidhuvati śāraṇe śiraḥ śikhidyutaḥ kanakakirīṭaraśmayaḥ /
children.translated_text: As [<s>Śāraṇa</s>] shook his head constantly, the rays of his golden crown, [blazing like] a peacock's radiance,

children.text: aśaṅkitaṃ yudhamadhunā viśantvamī kṣamāpatīniti nirarājayanniva // MSpv_17.16 //
children.translated_text: seemed to consecrate the kings [for war] — as if [saying] 'Enter battle now without fear!' // <s>MSpv</s> 17.16 //
<s>Vidūratha</s>, his broad tongue quivering with desire to speak, his wide arm-creepers extended,

children.text: vidūrathaḥ pratibhayamāsyakandaraṃ calatphaṇādharamiva koṭaraṃ taruḥ // MSpv_17.17 //
children.translated_text: held open his fearsome mouth-cavern — like a tree [whose] hollow [has] a swaying serpent-hood below. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.17 //

children.text: samākule sadasi tathāpi vikriyāṃ mano 'gamanna murabhidaḥ paroditaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Even in the tumultuous assembly, the mind of the slayer of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) underwent no agitation from the provocations of others;

children.text: ghanāmbubhirbahulitanimnagājalairjalaṃ na hi vrajati vikāramambudheḥ // MSpv_17.18 //
children.translated_text: the ocean does not undergo change from the waters of rivers swollen with abundant cloud-waters. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.18 //

children.text: parānamī yadapavadanta ātmanaḥ stuvanti ca sthitirasatāmasāviti /
children.translated_text: That those who bowed praised [themselves], and those who defamed him were [merely showing] the nature of the unreal — [knowing] this,

children.text: nināya no vikṛtimavismitaḥ smitaṃ mukhaṃ śaracchaśadharamugdhamuddhavaḥ // MSpv_17.19 //
children.translated_text: <s>Uddhava</s> did not undergo any change — unastonished, [wearing] a smile, his face [radiant as] the autumn moon, innocent. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.19 //

children.text: nirākṛte yadubhiriti prakopibhiḥ spaśe śanairgatavati tatra vidviṣām /
children.translated_text: When a spy of the enemies slowly entered that [assembly], while the <s>Yadus</s> had been insulted — provoking rage —

children.text: muradviṣaḥ svanitabhayānakānakaṃ balaṃ kṣaṇādatha samanahyatājaye // MSpv_17.20 //
children.translated_text: the army of the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, with its terrifyingly resounding weapons, at once prepared for battle. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.20 //
In battle, repeatedly striking back the weapons of enemies, with dense, mountain-firm hip-armor,
biting [their lips] — not devoid of the bite of valor — [they said] 'Lead on these forces!' — the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> kings [commanded]. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.21 //
Hard to bear [for others], yet in that interval the armors of the great, glory-bearing kings

children.text: mahībhujāṃ mahimabhṛtāṃ na saṃmamurmudo 'ntarāvapuṣi bahiśca kañcukāḥ // MSpv_17.22 //
children.translated_text: did not contain their joy from the report of battle — [bursting] both within the body and on the outer cuirass. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.22 //
Marshalling the elephant-corps, infantry, foot-soldiers, and harnessing the horses of victory,

children.text: tvarāyujaḥ svayamapi kurvato nṛpāḥ punaḥ punastadadhikṛtānatatvaran // MSpv_17.23 //
children.translated_text: while the kings themselves, yoked with speed, were acting [in haste], they urged their officers again and again. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.23 //
To the elephant-squadrons accompanied by warriors, with firmly bound girths, humming with swarms of bees attracted [by their rut],

children.text: adīyata dvipaghaṭayā savāribhiḥ karodaraiḥ svayamatha dānamakṣayam // MSpv_17.24 //
children.translated_text: imperishable gifts were then bestowed by their own hollow hands [i.e., generous patrons] — for [the sake of] battle with the enemies. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.24 //
With fine girdles, charming white teeth, the splendor of garments adorning their slender bodies,

children.text: raṇaiṣiṇāṃ pulakabhṛto 'dhikandharaṃ lalambire sadasilatāḥ priyā iva // MSpv_17.25 //
children.translated_text: the beloved [wives], their body-hair bristling, clung to the necks of [their husbands] eager for battle — like creeper-vines in the assembly. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.25 //
Captivating by nature with attractive forms, yet terrifying in battle with fearsome appearances —
the weapons of the slayer of <s>Mura</s> were ever-attended, inseparable, accompanied by their deities — like his own limbs. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.26 //
Unrestricted, he went abundantly among both [sides] and even into the intervals between the encampments of kings;

children.text: muhuryudhi kṣatasuraśatruśoṇitaplutapradhiṃ rathamadhirohati sma saḥ // MSpv_17.27 //
children.translated_text: and repeatedly in battle he mounted his chariot, its axle drenched with the blood of slain enemies of the gods. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.27 //
And approaching [the chariot], his own lordly bird (<s>Garuḍa</s>) — whose wings' wind made the sky tawny from its radiance in all directions —

children.text: prakampitasthiratarayaṣṭi tatkṣaṇaṃ patatpatiḥ padamadhiketanaṃ dadhau // MSpv_17.28 //
children.translated_text: that lord of birds, shaking the firm flagstaff, at that moment planted his foot on the banner. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.28 //
With a resonance that surpassed the deep drum-sound, with a vocal splendor that destroyed the joy of enemy-swans (<s>haṃsas</s>),

children.text: pramodayannatha mukharānkalāpinaḥ pratiṣṭhate navaghanavadrathaḥ sma saḥ // MSpv_17.29 //
children.translated_text: delighting the vocal peacocks — his chariot then advanced, like a fresh rain-cloud. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.29 //
Then, beholding the army surging forth, blocking the regions without gap, the people
became filled with wonder — as if in a great natural flood, with the waters of the unleashed ocean. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.30 //
The elephant-lords trumpeted, the great drums resounded, the victorious horses neighed;

children.text: asaṃbhavadgirivaragahvarairabhūttadā ravairdalita iva sva āśrayaḥ // MSpv_17.31 //
children.translated_text: then, with those sounds echoing [as if] from mountain-caves, their very abode seemed to be shattered. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.31 //

children.text: anārataṃ rasati jayāya dundubhau madhudviṣaḥ phaladalaghupratisvanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: As the war-drum resounded ceaselessly for the victory of the foe of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), with echoes [rolling like] unripe fruit,
the mountains too burst with joy, [spewing] lions from their cave-mouths [as if] laughing. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.32 //
When the army's roar, stunning the hearing of the celestials, entered the caves of the gods' mountain (<s>Meru</s>),
the skills of the coy, experienced courtesans' love-play rattling and tinkling became purposeless. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.33 //
The celestial courtesans, hearing the sounds of battle-drums, eager to reclaim [their] comrades slain by enemies in battle,

children.text: akurvata prathamasamāgamocitaṃ cirojjhitaṃ suragaṇikāḥ prasādhanam // MSpv_17.34 //
children.translated_text: began their toilette befitting the first meeting — long since abandoned. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.34 //
Urged by mahouts expert in accustomed tasks, trained in the skillful use of the goad,
the elephants, struck once on the temple-lobes by their [mahouts'] palms, came with their bells clanging repeatedly. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.35 //

children.text: savikramakramaṇacalairitastataḥ prakīrṇakaiḥ kṣipata iva kṣite rajaḥ /
children.translated_text: With [horses'] spirited prancing steps scattering dust from the ground here and there,
the horses, bearing fresh caparisons, did not allow the gazes of the people to rest. // <s>MSpv</s> 17.36 //
With sprout-like trembling fingers, with raised hands, she danced — clearly keeping time with her ears —
was sung melodiously by swarms of bees clinging to the walls dripping with rut-fluid. // MSpv 17.37 //
The earth was sprinkled by the rut-waters of [elephants] that suppressed [its] dust, [the earth] bearing freshly filled water-pots;
and music was sounded, pleasing to the ear, heavy with the deep resonance of the rising breast-like drums, with upturned faces. // MSpv 17.38 //
Banners, sky-licking, with garments fluttered by the wind, rose here and there;

children.text: yataḥ puraḥ pratiripu śārṅgiṇaḥ svayaṃ vyadhīyata dvipaghaṭayeti maṅgalam // MSpv_17.39 //
children.translated_text: while before [him], facing the enemy, the bearer of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow himself arranged the elephant-formations as an auspicious [omen]. // MSpv 17.39 //

children.text: na śūnyatāmagamadasau niveśabhūḥ prabhūtatāṃ dadhati bale calatyapi /
children.translated_text: The encampment did not become empty, maintaining its abundance even as the army moved out;

children.text: payasyabhidravati bhuvaṃ yugāvadhau saritpatirna hi samupaiti riktatām // MSpv_17.40 //
children.translated_text: for the lord of rivers [the ocean] does not become depleted when the waters rush upon the earth at the end of the age. // MSpv 17.40 //
The people then beheld the direction — gray as an aging buffalo's horn — which the slayer of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) desired to reach, [the direction indicated by] the sun,
and in front of which fell a garland of the enemy army's dust — as if [the direction were] fumigated. // MSpv 17.41 //
The echo of the spirited warriors, swelling and weighty, was heard — but not their own drum-sounds;
for the sounds of the enemy army's tethering-posts, raised before them, drew the mind more. // MSpv 17.42 //

children.text: yathā yathā paṭaharavaḥ samīpatāmupāgamatsa harivarāgrataḥ saraḥ /
children.translated_text: As the drumbeats drew nearer and nearer to the foremost excellent army's lake [that army being like a lake],

children.text: tathā tathā hṛṣitavapurmudākulā dviṣāṃ camūrajani janīva cetasā // MSpv_17.43 //
children.translated_text: so more and more did the enemy army arise — bristling, agitated with excitement — as if born in the mind. // MSpv 17.43 //
Then, as the sky spread open, the row of the enemy's banners, soiled by wind-whirled pollen-dust,
appeared from afar in the form of the dissolution-born dark goddess [<s>Kālikā</s>]. // MSpv 17.44 //
And in an instant — hard to look upon, with the flash of swords reflecting the fierce sun-rays face-to-face —

children.text: bhayaṅkarā bhṛśamapi darśanīyatāṃ yayāvasāvasuracamūśca bhūbhṛtām // MSpv_17.45 //
children.translated_text: that terrifying demon-army of kings also became exceedingly spectacular. // MSpv 17.45 //

children.text: payomucāmabhipatatāṃ divi drutaṃ viparyayaḥ parita ivātapasya saḥ /
children.translated_text: Like a reversal of sunlight from the rain-clouds rushing down from the sky swiftly,
that flood-like army, advancing simultaneously on even and uneven [ground], filled the earth's surface in a moment. // MSpv 17.46 //

children.text: mamau puraḥ kṣaṇamiva paśyato mahattanūdarasthitabhuvanatrayasya tat /
children.translated_text: That great army of the enemies appeared for a moment as if measured before the eyes of the slayer of <s>Madhu</s>, within whose slender belly the three worlds reside;

children.text: viśālatāṃ dadhati nitāntamāyate balaṃ dviṣāṃ madhumathanasya cakṣuṣi // MSpv_17.47 //
children.translated_text: as it assumed exceeding vastness and expanded, [it appeared thus] in the eyes of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. // MSpv 17.47 //
Profusely sweating, their bodies bristling with goosebumps, with valor fixed in their overflowing hearts,

children.text: mukhe yudhaḥ sapadi raterivābhavansasambhramāḥ kṣitipacamūvadhūgaṇāḥ // MSpv_17.48 //
children.translated_text: the armies of the kings' women became, at the face of battle, suddenly agitated — as if at the face of love-making. // MSpv 17.48 //
With banner-cloths spread by the steady favorable wind, as if making forcible invitations,

children.text: yadūnabhi drutataramudyatāyudhāḥ krudhā paraṃ rayamarayaḥ prapedire // MSpv_17.49 //
children.translated_text: the enemies, with weapons raised, rushed toward the <s>Yādavas</s> with extreme speed, propelled by rage. // MSpv 17.49 //
The army commanders of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) also set forth to engage the enemy forces;

children.text: vilambituṃ na khalu sahā manasvino vidhitsataḥ kalahamavekṣya vidviṣaḥ // MSpv_17.50 //
children.translated_text: for the spirited cannot bear to delay when they see hostile adversaries rising for battle. // MSpv 17.50 //
With wind-proof armor fitted on their bodies, with rays of light streaming from gleaming jewels like needles,

children.text: nirantaraṃ narapatayo raṇājire rarājire śaranikarācitā iva // MSpv_17.51 //
children.translated_text: the kings on the battlefield shone splendidly without interruption, as if studded with showers of arrows. // MSpv 17.51 //
Then, exceedingly high, [rising] with a pallid glow like the scattered body-hairs of an old pigeon's neck,
the dust of the earth rose up in waves — with rattling wealth-chains shaking from the moving hooves. // MSpv 17.52 //
In places, the dust-clouds, blocked from rising by the entangling horses pressing against one another overhead,
struck at every step by the hooves of the restless [horses], wandered for a long time below only. // MSpv 17.53 //
The dust of the vast, many-fronted, passionate [army] became thick, obscuring the creatures —

children.text: sisṛkṣataḥ sarasijajanmano jagadbalasya tu kṣayamapanetumicchataḥ // MSpv_17.54 //
children.translated_text: [like the dust] of <s>Padmaja</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) who desires to create the world, but of the army [of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] who desires to remove destruction. // MSpv 17.54 //

children.text: purā śarakṣatijanitāni saṃyuge nayanti naḥ prasabhamasṛñji paṅkatām /
children.translated_text: 'Before the sword-wound-generated [bloods] reduce our blood-smeared limbs to a pulpy mass in battle —'

children.text: iti dhruvaṃ vyalagiṣurāttabhītayaḥ khamuccakairanalasakhasya ketavaḥ // MSpv_17.55 //
children.translated_text: thus resolved, the banners of the friend of fire [the wind] rose high into the sky, having assumed fearfulness. // MSpv 17.55 //
Here mottled with masses of dense cloud-clusters, there golden-yellow with heaps of golden particles,
elsewhere pale as fragments of the autumn moon — the dust rose from the hoof-scarred surface of the earth. // MSpv 17.56 //
In the great dust of the vast army of the directional elephants, clinging to [their] faces,
the rut-streaked elephants abandoned the appearance of a scattered row of cuckoos — [looking instead] dark like clouds in the rainy season. // MSpv 17.57 //

children.text: śiroruhairalikulakomalairamī mudhā mṛdhe mṛṣata yuvāna eva mā /
children.translated_text: 'These youths with hair soft as bee-swarms must not vainly think themselves [still young] in battle —'

children.text: baloddhataṃ dhavalitamūrdhajāniti dhruvaṃ janāñjarata ivākarodrajaḥ // MSpv_17.58 //
children.translated_text: truly, the dust, having whitened their hair, made people appear as if aged — though raised by force [of the army]. // MSpv 17.58 //

children.text: susaṃhatairdadhadapi dhāma nīyate tiraskṛtiṃ bahubhirasaṃśayaṃ paraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Though bearing luster compactly united, [the sun] is certainly eclipsed by many others [dust-particles] combined;
for the minute constituent parts of the earth covered even the body of the treasury of radiance [the sun]. // MSpv 17.59 //
The world, veiled by the thick dust rising and flashing from the earth's surface scarred by the swiftly running chariot-wheels,
appeared submerged, as if in the waters of the ocean at the unrestrained moment of the age's destruction. // MSpv 17.60 //
The direction-women, dusty, their sky-beauty rubbed away, their faces' beauty [obscured] by the rising sun's shining countenance,

children.text: digaṅganāḥ kṣaṇamavilokanakṣamāḥ śarīriṇāṃ pariharaṇīyatāṃ yayuḥ // MSpv_17.61 //
children.translated_text: became for a moment impossible to look upon — and thus became objects to be avoided by embodied beings. // MSpv 17.61 //
The dust, meeting [the gods] in the sky who had gathered from curiosity to watch the valor of the kings at the battle-front,
was fled from by the hosts of gods — [that dust] causing the anguish of the unblinking lotus-eyes [of the gods]. // MSpv 17.62 //
As the dust — clinging at every step, quickly diminishing in luster, marked by the wind — was absorbing the moisture,
the rain-clouds gradually grew heavy with accumulated mud-weight and departed, their rains spent. // MSpv 17.63 //
The directional elephants, sky-roaming, their forms washed by the mingling of celestial rivers,
obtained the unprecedented pleasures of bathing in the earth-dust rising and flying from the hooves of the moving army's horses. // MSpv 17.64 //
When the earth, bending down from the weight of the advancing elephant-herds, consumed the nether world entirely,

children.text: nabhastalaṃ bhahulatareṇa reṇunā tato 'gamattrijagadivaikatāṃ sphuṭam // MSpv_17.65 //
children.translated_text: the sky was [filled] with the even greater dust — thus clearly the three worlds became as one. // MSpv 17.65 //
The great caves [of mountains], filled by the dust of the kings' armies that leveled all their openings,
became useful to the sky-dwelling beings who desired secluded retreats — disturbed and whirling with seekers. // MSpv 17.66 //

children.text: gate mukhacchadapaṭasādṛśīṃ dṛśaḥ pathasthiro dadhati ghane rajasyapi /
children.translated_text: Even though the dense dust maintained a face-veil-like [screen] steadily upon the path of sight,
the elephants rushed toward [other] elephants with speed — [guided] by the rut-scented breezes, fragrant with the mango-like [scent] of their rut. // MSpv 17.67 //
The elephant named <s>Añjana</s>, having settled the dust-heaps below with his rut-water dripping in seven streams,
looked upward at the thick dust-circles remaining above — as if at canopy-pavilions of stretched cloth. // MSpv 17.68 //
Neither too low nor too high, exceedingly broad, bearing the majesty of mountains, resembling golden rows with their lightning-garland chains,

children.text: varṣantaḥ śamamānayannupalasacchṛṅgāralekhāyudhāḥ kāle kāliyakāyakālavapuṣaḥ pāṃsūngajāmbhomucaḥ // MSpv_17.69 //
children.translated_text: raining [rut-fluid], bringing calm, with their tusks as weapons [like] visible ornamental streaks — black-bodied like the body of <s>Kāliya</s> [the serpent] in due season — the elephant-clouds [scattered] dust. // MSpv 17.69 //
The two army-oceans, deep-sounding, not looking to retreat, came together with force —

children.text: pakṣacchedātpūrvamekatra deśe vāñchantau vā vindhyasahyau niletum // MSpv_18.1 //
children.translated_text: as if <s>Vindhya</s> and <s>Sahya</s>, before their wings were clipped, desired to settle in one place. // MSpv 18.1 //

children.text: pattiḥ pattiṃ vāhameyāya vājī nāgaṃ nāgaḥ syandanastho rathastham /
children.translated_text: Foot-soldier met foot-soldier, horseman met horseman, elephant met elephant, charioteer met charioteer;

children.text: itthaṃ senā vallabhasyeva rāgādaṅgenāṅgaṃ pratyanīkasya bheje // MSpv_18.2 //
children.translated_text: thus the army engaged the rival army limb for limb, as a beloved [embraces] with passion. // MSpv 18.2 //
The rumble of chariots, the trumpeting of elephants, the neighing of horses —
merging together, the pervading, continuous roar of drums became indistinct, like the [cosmic] ruler's cry. // MSpv 18.3 //
Of the foot-soldiers advancing against the enemy in a rush of anger, their thick arms raised high as banner-poles,
the long, transverse sword-lines gleamed like victory-pennants. // MSpv 18.4 //
The golden armor-plates of the horsemen — strapped with leather thongs, galloping at speed — rising high, swaying,

children.text: raukmā rejuḥ sthāsakā mūrtibhājo darpasyeva vyāptadehasyaśeṣāḥ // MSpv_18.5 //
children.translated_text: shone as if embodied forms of pride — [pride] that had pervaded the entire body, complete. // MSpv 18.5 //
With dense hide-coverings, bark-clinging flanks, assuming a fourth bodily splendor,
the elephants, driven by the wind as at the end of a <s>kalpa</s> (age), charged fiercely — like cheek-boulders [rolling from mountains]. // MSpv 18.6 //
Sporting, the chariot-axles of the swift chariots — their fronts rising from the steeds urged forward with passion —

children.text: raṃhobhājāmakṣadhūḥ syandanānāṃ hāhākāraṃ prājituḥ pratyanandat // MSpv_18.7 //
children.translated_text: bearing speed, greeted the war-cry 'Hāhā!' with delight, traversing the superhuman path. // MSpv 18.7 //
Of [the banners] that obstruct death in battle — for the sweeping away of enemies' abundant dust —

children.text: sammārjanyo nūnamuddhūyamānā bhānti smoccaiḥ ketanānāṃ patākā // MSpv_18.8 //
children.translated_text: the raised pennants of the banner-staffs, to be swept away [by the enemy], shone high — as brooms [sweeping]. // MSpv 18.8 //
Drawn to their full circle by the archers, producing a rising sound, the bows — thick, harsh —

children.text: āsphālyante kārmukāṇi sma kāmaṃ hastyārohaiḥ kuñjarāṇāṃ śirāṃsi // MSpv_18.9 //
children.translated_text: were slapped at will by the elephant-riders upon the elephants' heads. // MSpv 18.9 //
The clanging of bells, the sound of small drums, the jingling of neck-chains, the trumpeting —
as if echoing in agreement, the elephants answered the encouraging words of the mahout. // MSpv 18.10 //
Going forth with the fourfold division of weapons and other distinctions, with unimpeded elegance and lightness,
the warriors displayed the power of their training by striking with weapons both hurled and hand-held. // MSpv 18.11 //
Some two, from a rush of anger, approaching face-to-face with sheer speed as if for a [bride's] hand-grasping,

children.text: hitvā hetīrmallavanmuṣṭighātaṃ ghnantau bāhūbāhavi vyāsṛjetām // MSpv_18.12 //
children.translated_text: abandoning weapons, like wrestlers, striking with fist-blows, released [their] arms in arm-to-arm [combat]. // MSpv 18.12 //

children.text: śuddhāḥ saṅgaṃ na kaucitprāptavanto dūrānmuktā śīghratāṃ darśayantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Pure [in aim], not reaching any obstacle, shot from afar, displaying swiftness,

children.text: antaḥsenaṃ vidviṣāmāviśanto yuktaṃ cakruḥ sāyakā vājitāyāḥ // MSpv_18.13 //
children.translated_text: the arrows, entering the interior of the enemy army, made fitting [proof] of the bowstring's [worth]. // MSpv 18.13 //
Scaling the foremost shoulder [of the elephant] from behind, then standing fearlessly upon its head,

children.text: helālolā vartma gatvātimartyaṃ dyāmārohanmānabhājaḥ sukhena // MSpv_18.14 //
children.translated_text: playfully casual, having traversed the superhuman path, the honored ones easily ascended toward the sky. // MSpv 18.14 //
Penetrating the wound-openings, reaching the interior of the body through the restless movable [arrows], the fixed [arrow-heads] —

children.text: kecitgurvīmetya saṃyanniṣadyāṃ krīṇanti sma prāṇamūlyairyaśāṃsi // MSpv_18.15 //
children.translated_text: some, attaining the weighty seat of battle, purchased glory at the price of their lives. // MSpv 18.15 //
Having performed a valorous deed in the battle-vanguard, praiseworthy of courage and spirit, shaming the proud —

children.text: ajñātānāṃ śatrubhiryuktamuccaiḥ śrīmannāma śrāvayanti sma nagnāḥ // MSpv_18.16 //
children.translated_text: those unknown [warriors], stripped [of armor], loudly proclaimed their glorious names to the enemies, fittingly. // MSpv 18.16 //
Others, rushing face-to-face against those who held sharp swords of various kinds held by yet others,
blinded by rage, entered the [enemy's] shields with their own chest-platforms [their bare chests]. // MSpv 18.17 //
Even when the two armies there had become intermingled, this distinction was mostly clear:

children.text: ātmīyāste ye parāñcaḥ purastādabhyāvartī saṃmukho yaḥ paro 'sau // MSpv_18.18 //
children.translated_text: those facing away [from you] were your own; the one facing toward [you] was the enemy. // MSpv 18.18 //
From a good lineage, brought to bodily intimacy at will, bound with respect,

children.text: nītā hastaṃ vañcayitvā pareṇa drohaṃ cakre kasyacitsvā kṛpāṇī // MSpv_18.19 //
children.translated_text: taken into the hand, then treacherously deceived by the other — a certain man's own sword committed treachery. // MSpv 18.19 //
When the other's [armor] — resembling a cloud — was split by the blow of a washed [bright] blade,

children.text: sāsṛgrājistīkṣṇamārgasya mārgo vidyuddīptaḥ kaṅkaṭe lakṣyate sma // MSpv_18.20 //
children.translated_text: the sharp path's track — bloody-streaked — was seen on the coat of mail, lit up like lightning. // MSpv 18.20 //
When the arm was stitched from root to tip by a long arrow, [the arm] of one whose fist gripped a frog-shaped [mace],
though enduring unbearable pain, with fortitude destroyed, the shield did not fall from the other hand. // MSpv 18.21 //
Piercing the nose, [passing] upward to the chest with effort, shot with a vulture-feathered [arrow] into the back of the neck,

children.text: śikṣāhetorgāḍharajjveva baddho hartuṃ vaktraṃ nāśakaddurmukho 'pi // MSpv_18.22 //
children.translated_text: bound as if by a tight rope for the purpose of training — even the foul-faced one could not remove [it] from his face. // MSpv 18.22 //
A thoroughbred horse, desired by a lance-bearing rider to kill from on high, did not shrink from elephants;

children.text: karmodāraṃ kīrtaye kartukāmānkiṃvā jātyāḥ svāminohrepayanti // MSpv_18.23 //
children.translated_text: need I praise those noble breeds whose valorous deeds put their masters to shame? // MSpv 18.23 //

children.text: jetuṃ jaitrāḥ śekire nārisainyaiḥ paśyanto 'dho lokamasteṣujālāḥ /
children.translated_text: Invincible warriors mounted on elephants, looking down upon the world through arrow-nets, could not be conquered by the hostile forces;

children.text: nāgārūḍhāḥ pārvatāni śrayanto durgāṇīva trāsahīnāstrasāni // MSpv_18.24 //
children.translated_text: taking refuge on mountain-dwelling [elephants], like impregnable fortresses, they were fearless yet fearsome. // MSpv 18.24 //
Scattering the army-waves in all directions, the <s>Āvanti</s> kings—somewhere one who had gone far,

children.text: babhrāmaikobandhumiṣṭaṃ didṛkṣuḥ sindhau vādyo maṇḍalaṃ gorvarāhaḥ // MSpv_18.25 //
children.translated_text: alone, wandering, wishing to see a dear kinsman—like a boar [circling] in the ocean, [made] a circle. // MSpv 18.25 //

children.text: yāvaccakre nāñjanaṃ bodhanāya vyutthānajño hasticārī madasya /
children.translated_text: Until the elephant-trainer, skilled in rousing from torpor, applied <s>añjana</s> (collyrium) for awakening,
the thick streams of ichor flowed by themselves from the elephants' own temple-glands, from the scent of the army. // MSpv 18.26 //
An elephant, enraged by the scent, charging at a rival elephant from afar, despising the rider who was trying to mount, shaking his head,

children.text: ghorārāvadhvanitāśeṣadikke viṣke nāgaḥ paryāṇaṃsītsva eva // MSpv_18.27 //
children.translated_text: with his terrible roar filling all the directions, severed his own trappings. // MSpv 18.27 //

children.text: pratyāsanne dantini prātipakṣe yantrā nāgaḥ prāstavaktracchado 'pi /
children.translated_text: When the enemy elephant drew near, an elephant, though his face-guard had been removed by the driver,

children.text: krodhākrāntaḥ krūranirdāritākṣaḥ prekṣāṃcakre naiva kiñcinmadāndhaḥ // MSpv_18.28 //
children.translated_text: seized by rage, with eyes cruelly torn wide, blinded by rut, did not look at anything. // MSpv 18.28 //
Before the mahout could swiftly remove the eye-cloth, the covering of the elephant's vision,
another elephant, mounted [by a warrior], was already slashing with single blows of the betel-nut [shaped mace], with clusters [of strikes]. // MSpv 18.29 //

children.text: āsthaddṛṣṭerācchadaṃ ca pramatto yantā yātuḥ pratyarībhaṃ dvipasya /
children.translated_text: The driver of the maddened elephant going to meet the rival placed the eye-screen,

children.text: bhagnasyoccairbarhabhāreṇa śaṅkoravavrāte vīkṣaṇe ca kṣaṇena // MSpv_18.30 //
children.translated_text: but [the elephant,] his peacock-feather-weighted [head-ornament] broken, in a moment, obtained both sight and [the opportunity] of the goad. // MSpv 18.30 //
One, by carefully protecting, attained imperishability through firmness; another, having determined with concentrated mind,
maintained the desired passion, or the wealth of calamity—the use appropriate for the time of the final moment. // MSpv 18.31 //
Touching each other's trunks, with tails bent upward from the breaking of ichor,
with heads raised, meeting [head-on] with their frontal [bosses], they fought, with the sound of tusks clearly audible. // MSpv 18.32 //
The tusks of the elephants, longer, massed, possessing firmness, beautiful, sharp, and not abandoning their keenness,

children.text: dantā dantairāhatāḥ sāmajānāṃ bhaṅgaṃ jagmurna svayaṃ sāmajātāḥ // MSpv_18.33 //
children.translated_text: when struck by tusks, themselves broke—not of their own accord, but born together [with them]. // MSpv 18.33 //
The fire born from the clash of elephants' tusks, with flickering tips resembling the reflection of cut gold,

children.text: lagno 'pyagniścāmareṣu prakāmaṃ māñjiṣṭheṣu vyajyate na sma sainyaiḥ // MSpv_18.34 //
children.translated_text: though clinging to the <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks), madder-red, was not noticed by the troops. // MSpv 18.34 //
The garland of stars high in the sky above the elephants' heads [appeared] to burn—
either from the fire born of the friction of the earth-growing [tusks], envy-born wind embracing [them], or from the conjunction-ending fires. // MSpv 18.35 //

children.text: sāndrāṇbhodaśyāmale sāmajānāṃ vṛnde nītāḥ śoṇitaiḥ śoṇimānam /
children.translated_text: The tusks, brought to redness by blood among the dense cloud-dark elephant herds,

children.text: dantāḥ śobhāmāpurambhonidhīnāṃ kandodbhedā vaidrumā vāriṇīva // MSpv_18.36 //
children.translated_text: attained the beauty of coral sprouts bursting forth from the oceans' [depths], as if underwater. // MSpv 18.36 //
With trembling banner-tips, approaching the fray with high, piercing throat-cries,

children.text: magnānaṅge gāḍhamanyadvipānāṃ dantānduḥkhāduttkhananti sma nāgāḥ // MSpv_18.37 //
children.translated_text: the elephants painfully uprooted the tusks of rival elephants, deeply embedded in their flanks. // MSpv 18.37 //
A mighty elephant, lifting up with its tusks a thrashing enemy elephant high,
clearly attained the resemblance of a mountain with a rainy-season cloud impaled on its horn. // MSpv 18.38 //

children.text: bhagne 'pībhe sve parāvartya dehaṃ yoddhrā sārdhaṃ vrīḍayā muñcateṣūn /
children.translated_text: Even when his own elephant was broken, a warrior, turning his body, releasing arrows together with shame,

children.text: sākaṃ yantuḥ saṃmadenānubandhī dūno 'bhīkṣṇaṃ vāraṇaḥ pratyarodhi // MSpv_18.39 //
children.translated_text: along with his driver, the afflicted elephant, stubbornly pursuing due to rut, repeatedly blocked [the enemy]. // MSpv 18.39 //
A steady, superior elephant, reaching with determination the army's midst, filled with the world, with retreat hard to gain,

children.text: senāmadhyaṃ gāhate vāraṇaḥ sma brahmaiva prāgādidevodarāntaḥ // MSpv_18.40 //
children.translated_text: plunged into the army's center, just as <s>Brahmā</s> formerly [entered] the interior of the primeval god's belly. // MSpv 18.40 //
With his body pierced without gap by arrows, dark-rayed like rows of black bees,
the elephant, fearless and wishing to be struck in battle, rejoicing with bristling hair, shone forth. // MSpv 18.41 //
When an arrow was swiftly extracted from the reddish temple-region of the elephant-king by the front-stationed [mahout],

children.text: niścyotantī nāgarājasya jajñe dānasyāho lohitasyeva dhārā // MSpv_18.42 //
children.translated_text: a stream was born—whether of ichor or of blood—dripping from the elephant-lord. // MSpv 18.42 //
Climbing the tusks of an elephant with daring, the two poles of Death's bedstead—
another was immediately suspected by the troops, mounted halfway to heaven on high, [of being about to die]. // MSpv 18.43 //
Making the sky resemble the star-studded [heavens] with drops of moonlight-like pearls,
a mass of scattering pearls shone from an elephant's frontal globe, split by sword-blows. // MSpv 18.44 //

children.text: dūrotkṣiptakṣipracakreṇa kṛttaṃ matto hastaṃ hastirājaḥ svameva /
children.translated_text: A maddened elephant-king, with his own trunk cut off by a discus hurled from afar,

children.text: bhīmaṃ bhūmau lolamānaṃ saroṣaḥ pādenāsṛkpaṅkapeṣaṃ pipeṣa // MSpv_18.45 //
children.translated_text: in rage crushed that terrible [trunk], writhing on the ground, with his foot into a paste of blood-mud. // MSpv 18.45 //
An elephant, its body hewn away from the impact, falling to the ground without support, face downward—

children.text: labdhāyāmaṃ dantayoryugmameva svaṃ nāgasya prāpaduttambhanatvam // MSpv_18.46 //
children.translated_text: having obtained the width between its two tusks alone, its own pair of tusks became its props. // MSpv 18.46 //
