Having obtained contact with the ground, standing steadily for a moment in the gap between the tusks—
another instantly conquered and rose above that elephant, entering through its tusks cut by the upward half of a sword. // MSpv 18.47 //
An elephant, seizing some fearless warrior with its trunk-tip, hurled him upward on high;

children.text: āsīnānāṃ vyomni tasyaiva hetoḥ svargastrīṇāmarpayāmāsa nūnam // MSpv_18.48 //
children.translated_text: surely it was delivering him to the celestial women, seated in the sky on his very account. // MSpv 18.48 //
One [warrior], pierced from afar by a firmly-driven long lance, with an interior wound,
though reached by the elephant's trunk before him, there was no power in the elephant to seize [him]. // MSpv 18.49 //

children.text: tanvāḥ puṃso nanda gopātmajāyāḥ kaṃseneva sphoṭitāyāḥ gajena /
children.translated_text: Of a slender woman, the cowherd <s>Nanda</s>'s daughter-in-law, crushed by an elephant as by <s>Kaṃsa</s>,
her divine form, rising skyward through the sky, was beheld with wonder—like <s>Caṇḍikā</s>. // MSpv 18.50 //
Stepping on one's leg with his forefoot, lifting another's high with his trunk,
the cruel-natured elephant tore someone apart from the middle, as if [splitting] a piece of wood. // MSpv 18.51 //

children.text: śocitvāgre bhṛtyayormṛtyubhājoraryaḥ premṇā no tathā vallabhasya /
children.translated_text: An enemy grieved first for two of his servants who met death—not so for his beloved;

children.text: pūrvaṃ kṛtvā netarasya prasādaṃ paścāttāpādāpa dāhaṃ yathāntaḥ // MSpv_18.52 //
children.translated_text: having first shown favor to one [servant] and not the other, he suffered inner burning from subsequent remorse. // MSpv 18.52 //
Leaping from afar, when the face of another [warrior] was cut by a half-moon [arrow], his lip and teeth bitten in rage,

children.text: sainyaiḥ kaṇṭhacchedalīne kabandhādbhūyo bibhye valgataḥ sāsipāṇeḥ // MSpv_18.53 //
children.translated_text: the troops feared even more the still-prancing, sword-in-hand headless trunk (<s>kabandha</s>), merging with the [severed] neck. // MSpv 18.53 //
With trumpet-sounds providing high, palm-tree-like rhythm, with <s>kāhala</s> (war-trumpet) horns singing <s>kāhala</s>,
performing in the dance blind-handed gestures of the body, some headless trunk laughed aloud with gurgling. // MSpv 18.54 //

children.text: pratyāvṛttaṃ bhaṅgabhāji svasainye tulyaṃ muktairākiranti sma kaścit /
children.translated_text: When their own army turned in defeat, some warriors showered [the fleeing enemy] simultaneously with arrows

children.text: ekaughena svarṇapuṅkhairdviṣantaḥ siddhāḥ mālyaiḥ sādhuvādairdvaye 'pi // MSpv_18.55 //
children.translated_text: in a single volley—gold-feathered [arrows against] enemies, garlands of accomplishment, and words of praise upon both sides. // MSpv 18.55 //
Of elephants whose riders had been shot off by arrows, leaving empty seats, proceeding to be seized by enemy troops,

children.text: saṃrabdhānāṃ bhrāmyatāmājibhūmau vārī vāraiḥ sasmare vāraṇānām // MSpv_18.56 //
children.translated_text: the furious ones, wandering on the battlefield, repeatedly recalled the water—the [familiar] bathing-waters. // MSpv 18.56 //
An elephant-lord, maddened by the repeatedly [encountered] scent of blood, trampling in anger the world of the battlefield,
dragged from the ground a long garland-like [chain of corpses] caught at his feet. // MSpv 18.57 //
One warrior, having fallen unconscious from a hard blow, sprinkled with the cool spray of an elephant,

children.text: ucchvāsa prasthitā taṃ jighṛkṣurvyarthākūtā nākanārī mumūrccha // MSpv_18.58 //
children.translated_text: as he began to breathe—a celestial woman wishing to seize him, her purpose frustrated, fainted [herself]. // MSpv 18.58 //
From another whose neck was severed by a scimitar, whose face was about to fly up very high into the sky,
the naive celestial women trembled at the <s>Rāhu</s>-like, terrible form—with the moons of the <s>apsaras</s>' faces [reflected in it]. // MSpv 18.59 //

children.text: vṛttaṃ yuddhe śūramāśliṣya kācidrantuṃ tūrṇaṃ merukuñjaṃ jagāma /
children.translated_text: One <s>apsaras</s>, having embraced a hero fallen in battle, quickly went to the bower of <s>Meru</s> to sport;

children.text: tyaktvā nāgnau dehameti sma yāvatpatnī sadyastadviyogāsamarthā // MSpv_18.60 //
children.translated_text: as long as his wife, unable to bear his separation, had not yet cast off her body in the fire. // MSpv 18.60 //

children.text: tyaktaprāṇaṃ saṃyuge hastinīsthā vīkṣya premṇā tatkṣaṇādudgatāsu /
children.translated_text: A certain faithful wife, seeing from atop a female elephant her beloved slain in battle, having instantly departed from life,

children.text: prāpyākhaṇḍaṃ devabhūyaṃ satītvādāśiśleṣa svaiva kañcitpurandhrī // MSpv_18.61 //
children.translated_text: attaining complete divinity through her virtue, embraced [him] herself [in heaven]. // MSpv 18.61 //

children.text: svargevāsaṃ kārayantyā cirāya pratyagratvaṃ pratyahaṃ dhārayantyā /
children.translated_text: Granting residence in heaven for a long time, maintaining precedence every day—

children.text: kaścidbheje divyanāryā parasmiṃlloke lokaṃ prīṇayantyeha kīrtyā // MSpv_18.62 //
children.translated_text: one [hero] was won by a divine woman; in the next world, he gladdened the world here through fame. // MSpv 18.62 //

children.text: gatvā nūnaṃ vaibudhaṃ sadma ramyaṃ mūcchābhājāmājagāmāntarātmā /
children.translated_text: Having surely gone to the beautiful celestial abode, the inner spirit of those who had fainted returned;

children.text: bhūyo dṛṣṭapratyayāḥ prāptasaṃjñāḥ sādhīyaste yadraṇāyādriyante // MSpv_18.63 //
children.translated_text: again having direct perception, having regained consciousness, they became all the more valiant, for they devoted themselves to battle. // MSpv 18.63 //
One, bewildered by a weapon-blow, but having again obtained consciousness, turned back to battle,

children.text: vyāvartiṣṭa krośataḥ sakhyuruccaistyaktaścātmā kā ca lokānuvṛttiḥ // MSpv_18.64 //
children.translated_text: even as his friend cried out loudly—for abandoned was the self's [interest], and what indeed is conformity to the world? // MSpv 18.64 //
Two [warriors], both with chests pierced, each dragging the other from afar with a single arrow's proximity,
by the power of their mutual steadfastness, went to heaven together, still upright. // MSpv 18.65 //
Others, restraining their own party from killing the well-born [enemies] who were struck by weapons, deluded, wavering,

children.text: jīvagrāhaṃ grāhayāmāsuranye yogyenārthāḥ kasya na syājjanena // MSpv_18.66 //
children.translated_text: captured them alive—for with the right person, what purposes cannot be achieved? // MSpv 18.66 //
Parasols with broken staves, fallen to the ground, with the full brilliance of the moon,

children.text: āhārāya pretarājasya raupyasthālānīva sthāpitāni sma bhānti // MSpv_18.67 //
children.translated_text: shone as if they were silver plates placed out for the food of the King of the Dead (<s>Yama</s>). // MSpv 18.67 //

children.text: rejurbhraṣṭā vakṣasaḥ kuṅkumāṅkā muktāhārāḥ pārthivānāṃ vyasūnām /
children.translated_text: Pearl necklaces fallen from the chests of dead kings, marked with saffron stains,

children.text: hāsāllakṣyāḥ pūrṇakāmasya manye mṛtyordantāḥ pītaraktāsavasya // MSpv_18.68 //
children.translated_text: I think were the teeth of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), his desires fulfilled, visible through [his] laughter—yellow and blood-stained. // MSpv 18.68 //
The blood, pooled in the hollows, that shone on the earth from those whose bodies were wounded by weapons—

children.text: rāgārthaṃ tatkiṃ nu kausumbhamambhaḥ saṃvyānānāmantakāntaḥ purasya // MSpv_18.69 //
children.translated_text: was that saffron-water for dyeing the shrouds of <s>Antaka</s>'s (Death's) inner city? // MSpv 18.69 //

children.text: rāmeṇa triḥsaptakṛtvo hradānāṃ citraṃ cakre pañcakaṃ kṣatriyāstraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Wonderfully, just as <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) made five pools thrice-seven times with the blood of <s>Kṣatriyas</s>,
in that battle, innumerable island-bearing rivers immediately flowed with blood-red waters. // MSpv 18.70 //
Elephants, pierced downward from the howdah by weapon-trained archers, with limbs severed by hundred-edged [weapons],
their feet [submerged] in blood-rivers, attained the likeness of tortoises among inter-flowing [streams]. // MSpv 18.71 //
With warrior-faces in lotus-shapes, with <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks) fallen from elephant-ears serving as swans,
the blood-watered rivers flowed fully equipped, with waves splashing high. // MSpv 18.72 //
Above the departed [warriors], for [their] flesh, feathered ones circled through the sky;

children.text: mūrtāḥ prāṇāḥ nūnamadyāpyavekṣāmāsuḥ kāyaṃ tyajitāḥ dāruṇāstraiḥ // MSpv_18.73 //
children.translated_text: they were surely the embodied vital breaths, even now watching over the body, cast out by terrible weapons. // MSpv 18.73 //
Stretching their wing-tip sounds across the directions, arriving swiftly from afar with sharp beak-tips—
first the blood of the dead soldiers was drunk, then later [their flesh] by the flocks of vultures. // MSpv 18.74 //
Surely the battlefield, taking forcibly the splendor together with the bodies of the vigorous ones standing in battle,
under the pretext of flames, vomiting that inner radiance, cried aloud with blazing tongues. // MSpv 18.75 //
Through the unbroken space between severed bodies, with the cry of the flame of the hard-to-satiate [fire],
having kindled the flesh of a warrior pierced by arrows, [the fire] savored an unprecedented taste of cooking, with the jackals. // MSpv 18.76 //
A jackal, having drunk blood—the <s>ariṣṭa</s> (liquor) dispelling weariness, for rousing hunger, with the remnant of drying indigestion—

children.text: svāduṃkāraṃ kālakhaṇḍopadaṃśaṃ kroṣṭā ḍimbaṃ vyaṣvaṇadvyasvanañca // MSpv_18.77 //
children.translated_text: made a sweet sound, with a morsel of dark-sugar as accompaniment, and howled and cried out. // MSpv 18.77 //
The lotus-like [faces] of the dead, torn open by flocks of carrion-eaters with hopes of fat—

children.text: ābhīlāni prāṇinaḥ pratyavasyankālo nūnaṃ vyadadāvānanāni // MSpv_18.78 //
children.translated_text: surely <s>Kāla</s> (Time/Death) had given terrifying mouths for the living beings [to behold]. // MSpv 18.78 //

children.text: kīrṇā reje sājibhūmiḥ samantādaprāṇadbhiḥ prāṇabhājāṃ pratīkaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The battlefield shone, strewn all around with lifeless bodies of the living,
or with the half-completed forms of many beginnings—like the workshop of creation of the Creator // <s>MSpv</s> 18.79 //
Of the royal armies approaching ceaselessly with their swift currents, thus with the weighty forces of <s>Śrī</s>'s lord, wave-like,
there was a swaying battle with the rivers flowing repeatedly into the great ocean, making a tremendous roar, possessed of violence // <s>MSpv</s> 18.80 //
Then there arose in the forest of battle, by one who splits the bamboo of unfriendly foes,
from the friction of the host of kings' feet, a fire, like a bamboo-splitter // <s>MSpv</s> 19.1 //
As the enemy rushed from afar, <s>Bala</s>, whose valor had put distance between himself and others,
watched him approach as a lion watches an elephant // <s>MSpv</s> 19.2 //
The victorious warrior, born to conquer, beyond all measure of speed, rushed forth to battle him;
bearing a splendor that overwhelmed the burden of the earth, the enemy of enemies roared // <s>MSpv</s> 19.3 //
His chariot, existing for the welfare of the worlds, causing the great earth to tremble,
fell upon the foe like a thunderclap, terrible with its battle-cries // <s>MSpv</s> 19.4 //
Against the enemy <s>Rāma</s>, a great archer skilled in the battle of arrows,

children.text: kopādathainaṃ śitamā maheṣvā sa vicakṣaṇe // MSpv_19.5 //
children.translated_text: then in anger the great archer struck him with a sharp-tipped shaft, the discerning one // <s>MSpv</s> 19.5 //
Like the sun carried to the direction opposite to the west, he removed the one fallen into a swoon;
the charioteer swiftly carried away from the battlefield that one of feeble prowess // <s>MSpv</s> 19.6 //
Having rendered the army of <s>Śālva</s> powerless through the might of <s>Śini</s>'s descendant,
he uttered with his mouth words of majestic power, radiant as blooming lotuses // <s>MSpv</s> 19.7 //
Like a firebrand reaching a tree and making its foliage shrink,
he blazed with terror, scattering his splendor in all directions // <s>MSpv</s> 19.8 //
<s>Rukmin</s>, overseeing the vast army of <s>Pṛthu</s>, raised his bow and weapons,
and with that very speech requesting departure, he raised his bow and weapons // <s>MSpv</s> 19.9 //
The armies of kings attacking simultaneously from all directions equally,
the son of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> received them alone, like rivers flowing into <s>Sarasvatī</s> // <s>MSpv</s> 19.10 //
By those bearing the likeness of clouds with their gleaming iron-tipped arrows,

children.text: tatra kāñcanasacchāyā sasṛje taiḥ śarāśaniḥ // MSpv_19.11 //
children.translated_text: a golden-hued thunderbolt of arrows was discharged there // <s>MSpv</s> 19.11 //
He shone brilliantly on high, like a tree with its clusters of nail-ray blossoms scattered,
with his trembling bow-branch mounted with buzzing arrow-bees // <s>MSpv</s> 19.12 //
Reaching the terrible battle, showing nobility to those who bowed,
striking but not releasing the enemies—the destroyer of enemy hosts—with his arrows // <s>MSpv</s> 19.13 //
Of the one who had achieved victory, with the aspiration of victory first against all kings,
he accomplished the shattering of the many arrows of <s>Bāṇa</s> with his own arrows // <s>MSpv</s> 19.14 //
The army that bore many magical illusions and great restlessness,
he, drawing his bow, free from illusion, advanced against that army // <s>MSpv</s> 19.15 //
He of great energy, having instantly subdued the vigor of the supreme warriors,
achieving the foremost position among the goat-bannered ones, scorned the claim to pre-eminence // <s>MSpv</s> 19.16 //

children.text: dūrādeva camūrbhallaiḥ kumāro hanti sa sma yāḥ /
children.translated_text: The armies which the prince destroyed from afar with his crescent-tipped arrows—

children.text: na punaḥ sāṃyugīṃ tāḥ sma kumāro hanti sasmayāḥ // MSpv_19.17 //
children.translated_text: those battle-hosts the prince slew with a smile, not again // <s>MSpv</s> 19.17 //
Released by him with force and compressed with desire without regard,
the arrows caused the enemies to attain bewilderment, not the arrow-tips themselves // <s>MSpv</s> 19.18 //
His exploits in battle, which suddenly caused horripilation,

children.text: surairaśaṃsi vyomasthaiḥ saha sāro maharṣibhiḥ // MSpv_19.19 //
children.translated_text: were praised by the gods stationed in the sky, along with the great sages, as having true substance // <s>MSpv</s> 19.19 //
Perfuming the directions, a pure, unfading flower from heaven
fell abundantly there; from that, his fame ascended to heaven // <s>MSpv</s> 19.20 //
His enemies were unable to endure the battle, nor were they a barrier to its fierceness;
and his fame spread across the sky, a cloudless canopy // <s>MSpv</s> 19.21 //
Of the battle, whose tresses were the abundant hair-like multitude, there was adorned
a crest, as it were, with a blooming wreath bearing the mark of flowers // <s>MSpv</s> 19.22 //
Even though fighting respectfully, the army, diminishing, was led by him to flee,

children.text: sā daraṃ pṛtanā ninye hīyamānā rasādaram // MSpv_19.23 //
children.translated_text: showing contempt for other men's valor, and taken to the breaking point // <s>MSpv</s> 19.23 //
Thus, seeing the fish-bannered <s>Kāma</s> embraced by the goddess of victory,

children.text: kruddhayeva krudhā sadyaḥ prapede cedibhūpatiḥ // MSpv_19.24 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Cedi</s> king was seized at once by anger, as if by an angered one // <s>MSpv</s> 19.24 //
Against his foes, the proud one with his four-limbed army
advanced with the gait of a young elephant, with four-limbed equal force // <s>MSpv</s> 19.25 //
Then with the reverberating, roaring sounds of bowstring-twanging from all sides,
with martial instruments imitating the turbulent ocean at the end of an age // <s>MSpv</s> 19.26 //
[This is a palindromic verse:] Arrows flew, bodies fell, weapons clashed, and battle-cries resounded,
the tumult of war thundered, and drums beat with their booming sounds // <s>MSpv</s> 19.27 //
Like the very sister of <s>Yama</s> herself, surrounded by swarms of <s>Kālī</s>ya's serpents,
dark with gleaming iron armor, wishing to render assistance // <s>MSpv</s> 19.28 //
[Palindrome:] She was tireless with passion at the onset of her army's advance,
intoxicated by the loud cries of the people, marching with the gait of a majestic elephant, free from illness // <s>MSpv</s> 19.29 //
The commanders, with their pure intentions shaken, as the earth-bearers took their positions—
she was indeed the touchstone of courage and passion for those who lived by the occasion // <s>MSpv</s> 19.30 //
Who, wishing to go to heaven through battle, bearing a wealth of soft and spotless glory,
while wielding a sword-vine, bore a spotless, pure abundance? // <s>MSpv</s> 19.31 //
Soldiers simultaneously sought to conquer with fierce speed
the enemy side with iron-bar arms and shanks, each against the other // <s>MSpv</s> 19.32 //
[Palindrome:] The sound of people arose then from the vehicles in the lake of pride,
of the intoxicated lordly elephants, the finest among them, a heavy burden of cries // <s>MSpv</s> 19.33 //
[Palindrome:] Darkness from the essence of passion was assumed by the splendor of the swift-striking warriors;
the army was a battle of proud warriors, equal in force, spreading in extent // <s>MSpv</s> 19.34 //
Of unbroken conduct, forcibly drawn by those intoxicated with youth,
the bow-vines, with middles graspable by a fist, cried out loudly // <s>MSpv</s> 19.35 //
Many elephants were crushed, dust arose, bells rang in thousands;

children.text: kareṇuḥ śīkaro jajñe reṇustena śamaṃ yayau // MSpv_19.36 //
children.translated_text: female elephants produced a shower-spray, and by that the dust was settled // <s>MSpv</s> 19.36 //
Though the elephants bore the freshly-assumed ornament of passion's <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment),

children.text: saroṣasambhramairbarbhre raudra eva raṇe rasaḥ // MSpv_19.37 //
children.translated_text: only the <s>raudra</s> (furious) <s>rasa</s> (sentiment) was borne on the battlefield, with agitation and anger // <s>MSpv</s> 19.37 //
Fear did not remain in the hearts of those seeking to repay the honor received from their lord

children.text: raṇaikasargeṣu bhayaṃ mānasaṃ prati pattiṣu // MSpv_19.38 //
children.translated_text: in the single-creation of battle, among the foot-soldiers // <s>MSpv</s> 19.38 //
With archer-trees whose hollows were quivers filled with arrows placed by bowmen,
whose branch-arms were clasped with finger-guard lizards—the forest of battle became terrible // <s>MSpv</s> 19.39 //
[Palindrome:] That army, destroying enemies here, endowed with the dense force of a flood of warriors,
scorning various battles, was attended by its own extended strength // <s>MSpv</s> 19.40 //
With <s>viṣama</s> (uneven), <s>sarvatobhadra</s> (universally auspicious), <s>cakra</s> (wheel), <s>gomūtrikā</s> (cow-urine pattern), and other formations,
like a great poem with its stanzas, that army took shape in battle arrays // <s>MSpv</s> 19.41 //
Having united, the <s>Sātvata</s> army, with its brilliant force, against <s>Caidya</s>,
marshalled itself to fight, arising in matched counterpart formations // <s>MSpv</s> 19.42 //
Extended in length, with restless multitudes filling every gap,

children.text: narendramārgaṃ rathyeva papāta dviṣatāṃ balam // MSpv_19.43 //
children.translated_text: the army of the enemies fell upon the king's path like a chariot on a main road // <s>MSpv</s> 19.43 //
[Palindrome:] Deep as elephants, with a tumultuous roar of troops, finely tempered,
that army caused the slaughter of enemies and could not be repelled, blocking the foes // <s>MSpv</s> 19.44 //
Under the elephants, swift, beautiful with their outspread plumes,
peacock-like arrows fell, deadly and life-stealing // <s>MSpv</s> 19.45 //
In the battle that commenced with resounding noise, with non-poisonous means of accomplishment,
the tusked elephants rained freely their copious rut-fluid in battle // <s>MSpv</s> 19.46 //
That battle, ignited by the infantry deployed in front, those of proven purity,
blazed like <s>Gāndharva</s> music with its <s>ālāpa</s> preludes // <s>MSpv</s> 19.47 //
With his own sword, someone's striking of the circular edges of others' shields was found blameless;
it attained the fame-flooded earth, and the circular edge-striking was deemed faultless // <s>MSpv</s> 19.48 //
Sharp in destroying enemies, equally from a well-compacted
retinue, someone separated both his sword and his self // <s>MSpv</s> 19.49 //
By another, wielding with excessive grace and exuberance,
with his upraised sword swiftly creating excessive turbidity in the army // <s>MSpv</s> 19.50 //
Some warrior, fulfilling a thousand, cut off the heads of enemies with his sword,
and then upward itself the headless trunk performed its dancing act // <s>MSpv</s> 19.51 //
Another, adorned with ornaments that were the beauty of weapon-wounds on the battlefield,
was seen like <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, adorned with ornamental decoration // <s>MSpv</s> 19.52 //
Another, deprived of both thighs by the enemy's severing and slashing blows,
and sprinkled with weapons on both sides, became a figure of crimson // <s>MSpv</s> 19.53 //
Another attained terribleness in the great battle equal to the ocean;

children.text: dākṣe kopaḥ śivasyeva samedhitamahā have // MSpv_19.54 //
children.translated_text: his wrath, like that of <s>Śiva</s> in <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice, swelled to great proportions // <s>MSpv</s> 19.54 //
The foot-soldiers, their sword-blades severed by the enemy's broadswords,
bit down in rage with their teeth at the foe, like elephants // <s>MSpv</s> 19.55 //
In the battle, when the elephants' bodies burst open with blooming gore,

children.text: na tatra gatabhīḥ kaścidvipapāṭa vikāsini // MSpv_19.56 //
children.translated_text: no one there who had abandoned fear was shattered or blossomed // <s>MSpv</s> 19.56 //
As long as life was not abandoned by those desiring to repay the debt of their lord's affection, properly honored,
until then it was not abandoned in battle by others motivated by indignation // <s>MSpv</s> 19.57 //
[Yamaka:] Fearful of the infamy hard to look upon, except in the abode of rage and death,
infamy is hard to attain in the world for those who dispense anger and honor death // <s>MSpv</s> 19.58 //
The spear, never stumbling anywhere due to its sharpness, bearing fruit of success,

children.text: amoci śaktiḥ śaktikairlohajā na śarīrajā // MSpv_19.59 //
children.translated_text: was released by the spear-wielder—it was born of iron, not of the body // <s>MSpv</s> 19.59 //
Kings fought with their strategies engaged; with that divine army

children.text: āpa divyā pṛtanayā vismayaṃ janatā yathā // MSpv_19.60 //
children.translated_text: the people attained amazement, just as the army attained it // <s>MSpv</s> 19.60 //
Like courtesans who attract with their own qualities until the fruit is obtained,
they suddenly released their arrows, discarding their lovers as it were // <s>MSpv</s> 19.61 //
The horses of the enemy army, horses freshly joined in battle,
and arrows too—all entered the middle of the swift-horsed ones // <s>MSpv</s> 19.62 //
With well-feathered arrows, having good wing-support and being fruitful at the front,
because of being well-notched, they attained their mark quickly through those seekers // <s>MSpv</s> 19.63 //
One archer, uttering the hymn of blood-flow like a red <s>japā</s> flower, among the enemy's rivals,
inflicted a wound in battle with his arrows, going forward with the passion of battle // <s>MSpv</s> 19.64 //
Two warriors, eager for battle, approaching from afar with great speed,
the elephant that died between them became like a camel // <s>MSpv</s> 19.65 //
[Alliterative verse:] The elephants, heavy with the earth's burden, terrible and massive, clashed with elephants,
fearless elephants roared against elephants like cloud-like, tremendous drums // <s>MSpv</s> 19.66 //
Elephants fighting with their tusks broken, their trunks severed by sharp sword-blades,
did not attain helplessness as much when fighting with tusks as when those were broken // <s>MSpv</s> 19.67 //
From the mutual pressing, rut-water flowed ceaselessly,
and from the impetuous clash of the elephant-bodies, it streamed forth on all sides // <s>MSpv</s> 19.68 //
The battlefield, flooded with rut-water like a lake,
the elephant churned up the hundred-petaled lotuses dragged by its broad trunk // <s>MSpv</s> 19.69 //
When the elephant, wounded by arrows, was distressed by bees on the poisoned wound,
there was weeping under the pretext of crying out, as it sank further // <s>MSpv</s> 19.70 //
There, on the broad bed of <s>Antaka</s> (Death) as it were, in that great battle,
the elephants attained the state of bed-bugs, from their addiction to biting // <s>MSpv</s> 19.71 //
[Palindromic citrakāvya verse:] In the repeatedly kindled destruction of the fearful, the joyful one's annihilation,
the shining army, desiring fulfillment, slowly longed for love // <s>MSpv</s> 19.72 //
Even though bearing a terrible and demonic aspect in battle repeatedly,
those slain by the enemy while facing forward attained the state of gods // <s>MSpv</s> 19.73 //
He whose body was marked with wounds, equal to the immortals by his luster,
attained equality with the immortals, through his sword and his splendor // <s>MSpv</s> 19.74 //
That battlefield, where friends, lords, paternal uncles, brothers, and maternal uncles had been felled,
was observed by the wise as if it were <s>Pāṇini</s>'s grammar [with its fallen suffixes] // <s>MSpv</s> 19.75 //
It came to resemble the twilight-red clouds with its river of blood-water

children.text: hṛte yoddhuṃ janaḥ pāṃśau sa dṛgrudhi rato yathā // MSpv_19.76 //
children.translated_text: the people, eager to fight in dust, were as if devoted to the sport of eyes [i.e., blind with battle-fury]. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.76 //
Strewn with bursting lotuses, turbulent with falling conch-shells,
with leaf-chariots [floating corpses] drifting — the rivers flowed with blood-red waters. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.77 //
The blood of men, the wounds from weapons, the sinking of the proud [warriors] —
the <s>Rākṣasas</s> and <s>Piśācas</s> rejoiced [in] the fresh [feast of] sinking of the proud. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.78 //
Wondrous — with bows whose strings had departed, [the battlefield] flashing with hundreds of blood-streams,
that [spectacle] shone like a mass of clouds — [proclaiming] the heroic hopes [of warriors]. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.79 //
When a kinsman fell [in battle], many a man near him in the army

children.text: aśoci sainye ghaṇṭābhirna reṇe hatadantike // MSpv_19.80 //
children.translated_text: lamented; the bells of the slain elephant's [harness] did not ring at the trunk's side. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.80 //

children.text: kṛttaiḥ kīrṇā mahī reje dantairgātraiśca dantinām /
children.translated_text: The earth shone, strewn with severed tusks, limbs, and bodies of elephants,
as if with the mortars and pestles of Death, who crushes the lives of the world. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.81 //
Thus, the battle raging — with shaken pride — having gone beyond fear,
the <s>Caidya</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>) vanquished the enemies through the application of human [valor]. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.82 //
Then, with a yellow garment shimmering with the reflected radiance of the chest-gem,
[he shone] like a flash of lightning pierced by a sparkling rainbow — [he embodied] lightning itself. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.83 //
With a dark-blue [body like] a dense, still lotus-entwined, bee-swarming, playfully swaying,
a fondling, abundantly playful, embracing [lover] — // <s>MSpv</s> 19.84 //
as if by the unprecedented, passionately longing <s>Vijayaśrī</s> (Goddess of Victory), desirous of union at that very moment,
with sidelong glances — O king, beholding his form — // <s>MSpv</s> 19.85 //

children.text: vibhāvī vibhavī bhābho vibhābhāvī vivo vibhīḥ /
children.translated_text: The radiant one, the powerful one, the effulgent one, the splendid lord, the luminous one, the fearsome one,

children.text: bhavābhibhāvī bhāvāvo bhavābhāvo bhuvo vibhuḥ // MSpv_19.86 //
children.translated_text: the subduer of existence, the essence of being, the destroyer of worldly existence, the lord of the earth — // <s>MSpv</s> 19.86 //
by the supreme <s>yogins</s>, resolved [in their purpose], desiring to reach the far shore [of liberation],
striving through the abandonment of the body — the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> was beheld. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.87 //
Him who was attended by <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), dense in radiance, by her who is the essence [of all],
by her who went swiftly — beautiful, [bearing] a sinless son — attended [by her]. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.88 //
Seeing [him approach] the enemies — who felt no enmity [toward him] — nevertheless the sinless ones [recognized him],
like medicine that is unpleasant but cures disease — by its very nature. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.89 //

children.text: viditaṃ divi ke 'nīke taṃ yātaṃ nijitājini /
children.translated_text: "Who in heaven's army knows him who has gone forth victorious in battle?"

children.text: vigadaṃ gavi roddhāro yoddhā yo natimeti naḥ // MSpv_19.90 //
children.translated_text: "The warrior who bows to us — free from disease, a defender of cows — is a fighter without words." // <s>MSpv</s> 19.90 //
Being engaged in the most weighty task ahead,
the bow, upon which many a great quality was strung, bent [respectfully] before the master. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.91 //
There, arrows — harsh and beautiful — were fitted [to the bow];
for the enemies, the harshness of [those arrows] drawn [on the string] was unbearable; for him, [they were] lovely. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.92 //
Even of those [arrows] made [to fly] after [the enemy], like men bearing feathers [wings],

children.text: yoyo guṇena saṃyuktaḥ sa sa karṇāntamāyayau // MSpv_19.93 //
children.translated_text: each one that was endowed with a [bow]string came [all the way] to the ear. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.93 //

children.text: prape rūpī purārepāḥ paripūrī paraḥ paraiḥ /
children.translated_text: The resplendent one, formerly the destroyer of enemies, complete in fullness, supreme among the highest,
with immeasurable strikes, from above, filled [the field] again with other [arrows]. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.94 //
Pervading the quarters, sharp, piercing, striking the vital spots,
he discharged in a single instant arrows both innumerable and unerring. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.95 //
Showering arrows, thundering loudly, with his flashing bow as his banner,
he, of dark complexion (<s>Keśava</s>), shone like a moving rain-cloud. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.96 //
Not only was his bow, drawn with light touch, seen by people as [spinning in] a circle;
even the army of the enemies perceived [only its] power from beginning to end. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.97 //
[He was] the world-illuminator, the timeless one, stainless, enveloped in the mass of bee-dark [arrows as] locks,
Death [itself], undiminished, without strife, in due time — a playful [destroyer], a sportive slayer, indeed. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.98 //
He pierced the enemies, [though] thin-armored, in [their] unimpaired eyes;

children.text: dāneṣu sthūlalakṣyatvaṃ na hi tasya śarāsane // MSpv_19.99 //
children.translated_text: for in his archery, there was no such thing as a large target — [even] in generous [giving]. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.99 //
The excellent one, without gaps [in defense], the dispeller of enmity, [his bow-]sound like roaring waters,

children.text: vivavāra varo vairaṃ vīro ravirivaurvaraḥ // MSpv_19.100 //
children.translated_text: the best of heroes warded off enmity — heroic like the sun, like the submarine fire. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.100 //
His bow, which released many arrows at once, robbed the life-breath of the greater number of enemies;

children.text: tadīyaṃ dhanuranyasya na hi sehe sajīvatām // MSpv_19.101 //
children.translated_text: it did not tolerate the survival of any other [foe]. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.101 //
The row of kings was routed; the unborn, undecaying, dustless [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] shone;
the enemy kings were crushed, thundering, battered, and shattered. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.102 //
Of the proud enemies [whom] he struck down, two things resulted:

children.text: pānārthe rudhiraṃ dhātau rakṣārthe bhuvanaṃ śarāḥ // MSpv_19.103 //
children.translated_text: their blood went to the [earth for] drinking; their arrows [went] to the world for protection. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.103 //
The crusher of cruel enemies, the doer of terrible deeds, the maker of battle-cries,
the hail-like striker with bud-like [arrow-]hands, the thorn-remover, the harsh, fierce destroyer — // <s>MSpv</s> 19.104 //
though he had descended [to earth] to reduce its burden,
he made the earth heavier by creating numerous masses of slain enemies. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.105 //
The splitter [of enemy ranks], terror to terrifying foes, generous like a mountain, the demolisher from afar,
far from cruelty [to the good], [yet] from afar the giver of fear, the uprooter, the forceful, the respectful dispenser — // <s>MSpv</s> 19.106 //
Splitting enemies massed together with a single arrow, like trees,
he made himself the equal of <s>Rāma</s> of a former birth. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.107 //
The valorous <s>Śauri</s>, with his hot, swift arrows [raining] across the quarters — the lord of hosts,
the arrow-eager one, the lord of <s>Śrī</s>'s body — pierced the heads of enemies with arrows. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.108 //
The arrows that belonged to those [enemies] who were slain by that foe-destroyer —

children.text: manohṛto 'pi hṛdaye legureṣāṃ na patriṇaḥ // MSpv_19.109 //
children.translated_text: though they robbed [their] hearts, those feathered [shafts] did not cling to their hearts. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.109 //
"Let there be no staining of the syllables of [their wives'] names" — hence, manifestly,
his arrows did not seize the lives [and] garland-strings of the enemies' wives. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.110 //
Having seized the entire life-wealth of the warrior-caravan, the swift-flying [arrows],
like house-breakers, vanished from sight far away upon the earth. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.111 //
Of his army with fearsome weapon-lines, with rows of banners,
the arrows created terrible battles and made the earth blood-soaked — [those] victors. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.112 //
With faces fit for the butcher's [trade], rendering the enemy army inert and void,
his arrows pervaded the sky like <s>śakuntī</s> (vulture-feathered) birds. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.113 //
The giver of gifts, the giver who gave generously, the roaring giver, the giver [who gave] to both givers' arms,
he gave the gift of [battle-]giving in the tumult; the giver who gave [to] givers — the non-giver [received nothing]. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.114 //
He set in motion rivers of blood, born from heart-wounds,
overflowing from the chest-pots of the [slain] elephants — [rivers] of both his enemies and their women [i.e., tears]. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.115 //
Mostly attended by the ever-intoxicated army, his <s>rasa</s> (essence/valor) fully drawn forth, he shone —
of proven valor, O glorious one — <s>Hari</s> [shone] like another <s>Hari</s> (lion). // <s>MSpv</s> 19.116 //

children.text: dvidhā tridhā caturdhā ca tamekamapi śatravaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing him — one [alone] — in two, three, and four [forms simultaneously], the enemies,

children.text: paśyantaḥ spardhayā sadyaḥ svayaṃ pañcatvamāyayuḥ // MSpv_19.117 //
children.translated_text: in [vain] rivalry, themselves at once attained the five-fold state [death]. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.117 //
Always endowed with a perfect body in battles where divine endowments fill [the scene],

children.text: maho dadhe 'stāri mahānitāntaṃ mahodadhestārimahā nitāntam // MSpv_19.118 //
children.translated_text: he held a glory exceedingly vast — destroying the enemies, [like] the great [fire] of the great ocean, utterly. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.118 //

children.text: iṣṭaṃ kṛtvārthaṃ patriṇaḥ śārṅgapāṇer etyādhomukhyaṃ praviśanbhūmimāśu /
children.translated_text: Having accomplished their purpose, the arrows of the wielder of <s>Śārṅga</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), entering the ground face-down swiftly —

children.text: śuddhayā yuktānāṃ vairivargasya madhye bhartrā kṣiptānāmetadevānurūpam // MSpv_19.119 //
children.translated_text: this alone was fitting for those flung by [their] master into the midst of the enemy host, joined with purity. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.119 //
Seizing with battle-fury a distinguished being of valor, radiant before [all], having attained the purification of sin-destruction, with the higher <s>Śrīvatsa</s>-mark upon his chest, in joy,

children.text: muktvā kāmamapāstabhīḥ paramṛgavyādhaḥ sa nādaṃ harer ekaughaiḥ samakālamabhramudayī ropaistadā tastare // MSpv_19.120 //
children.translated_text: having released [arrows] at will, fearless — that supreme hunter (<s>Mṛgavyādha</s>) uttered <s>Hari</s>'s cry; with single floods [of arrows], rising without confusion, with strikes, he then spread out. // <s>MSpv</s> 19.120 //
Bearing a face lofty with three gleaming lines [of frown], terrifying with an eyebrow-pair hard to break,
unable to endure the valor [of the other] in battle, the fearless [<s>Śiśupāla</s>] challenged the lord of <s>Cedi</s> against the foe of <s>Mura</s>. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.1 //

children.text: śitacakranipātasaṃpratīkṣyaṃ vahataḥ skandhagataṃ ca tasya mṛtyum /
children.translated_text: Bearing death seated on his shoulder — [death] awaiting the fall of the sharp discus —

children.text: abhiśauri ratho 'thanoditāśvaḥ prayayau sārathirūpayā niyatyā // MSpv_20.2 //
children.translated_text: toward <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), his chariot, its horses urged forward, sped — with Fate itself as his charioteer. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.2 //
The chariot of <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) also advanced against the <s>Caidya</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>),
smearing the ground with the coppery blood flowing from corpses crushed under its heavy wheel-rims — [blood red as] <s>jāguḍa</s>-lac and saffron. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.3 //
He, with extended banner-cloth-tips, with softly tinkling, fearsome small bells,

children.text: virarāja ripukṣayapratijñāmukharo muktaśikhaḥ svayaṃ nu mṛtyuḥ // MSpv_20.4 //
children.translated_text: shone — as if Death himself, clamoring the vow of the enemy's destruction, his crest-flame released. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.4 //
The sound of his chariot, imitating the roar of rain-laden clouds, filling all the quarters,
was heard attentively by the peacocks (<s>śitikaṇṭhas</s>) with raised necks, their crests straightened. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.5 //
Seeing on <s>Acyuta</s>'s (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s) chest the saffron-mark from the breasts of the princess of <s>Vidarbha</s> (<s>Rukmiṇī</s>),

children.text: cirasevitayāpi cedirājaḥ sahasāvāpa ruṣā tadaiva yogam // MSpv_20.6 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Cedi</s> king, though [he himself had] long served [that mark], suddenly attained union with fury at that very instant. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.6 //
Twanged aloud by the king, creating the suspicion of thunderbolt-sound,
the bow's string flashed [like] the crest-flames of the world-ending fire driven by a restless wind. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.7 //
Then, with simultaneous fitting, drawing, and releasing — as if [occurring] at the same instant —

children.text: atha sābhisāraṃ śaraistarasvī sa tiraskartumupendramadhyavarṣat // MSpv_20.8 //
children.translated_text: the impetuous [<s>Śiśupāla</s>] showered arrows to overwhelm <s>Upendra</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), eagerly. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.8 //
The union of the arrows — partaking of rectitude, proper application, and purity, supported by a weighty side [feathering] —

children.text: guṇinā natimāgatena sandhiḥ saha cāpena samañjaso babhūva // MSpv_20.9 //
children.translated_text: with the bow, through the [bow-]string, properly bent in salutation — was fitting and harmonious. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.9 //
By the <s>Cedi</s> king, appointed to the most unbearable task, the master [of the bow] —
the bow resounded aloud, with its firmly drawn [string] causing the life [of enemies] to tremble from the forceful pulling, [inflicting] hard anguish. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.10 //
Falling in continuous succession, bearing sharpness, carrying purity, having taken [their] side —

children.text: vadanādiva vādino 'tha śabdāḥ kṣitibharturdhanuṣaḥ śarāḥ prasasruḥ // MSpv_20.11 //
children.translated_text: like words from the mouth of a speaker, the arrows issued forth from the king's bow. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.11 //
His bow, dark-lustred as a buffalo, positioned in the midst, bearing the nose-[shape] of terrible extended arm-shafts,
was seen by the people with a fearsome appearance — [like] the eyebrow-pair of enraged Death rising up. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.12 //
With arrows golden-shafted [bright as] flashing lightning, dark-faced, resounding,

children.text: jaladairiva raṃhasā patadbhiḥ pidadhe saṃhatiśālibhiḥ śaraughaiḥ // MSpv_20.13 //
children.translated_text: falling with the speed of rain-clouds — he covered [the sky] with compact, dense masses of arrow-floods. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.13 //
With sharp lance-pointed [arrows] splitting the clouds and causing water to stream, [inflicting] manifest, intense pain,
the golden-shafted [arrows] were like the weeping horizon-circle of the quarters, streaming with tears. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.14 //

children.text: amanoramatāṃ yatī janasya kṣaṇamālokapathānnabhaḥ sadāṃ vā /
children.translated_text: For a moment, [the sky] yielded unpleasantness to the sight-path of the people — the sky of the assemblies, or [both] —
was blocked: the sun's radiance concealed, the steadfast earth hidden — covered by arrows. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.15 //
For the entire army of the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, a single [canopy] blocking the sun's heat,

children.text: śarajālamayaṃ samaṃ samantāduru sadmeva narādhipena tene // MSpv_20.16 //
children.translated_text: the king provided, as it were, a vast house made of arrow-nets — equally on all sides. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.16 //
Thus, at that time, by the <s>Cedi</s> king, the army of the slayer of <s>Danu</s>'s sons (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)
was surrounded on all sides — like a bird [caught] in a net of snares, rendered helpless. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.17 //
The many arrow-showers discharged by the solitary enemy — <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) then, with his own pointed shafts,

children.text: atha vādikṛtaṃ pramāṇamanyaiḥ prativādīva nirākarotpramāṇaiḥ // MSpv_20.18 //
children.translated_text: as a debater [refutes] arguments established as proofs by others — refuted [them all] with counter-proofs. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.18 //
By him, with elbow bent back, drawing the bowstring to the vicinity of the ear,
his bow sounded aloud — imitating the copious cries of <s>krauñca</s> (curlew) birds maddened by the dense [rain]-clouds. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.19 //
With broad chest, shoulders lowered, head crowned with a peacock-[feather crest], at that moment

children.text: kṣaṇamālikhito nu sauṣṭhavena sthirapūrvāparamuṣṭirābabhau vā // MSpv_20.20 //
children.translated_text: he appeared as if drawn [by an artist] with elegance — [or rather] shone with both fists firmly set, front and back. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.20 //
From the resounding bow, with great force — heavy — the innumerable arrows, with lightning-like quivering bowstrings,
fell swiftly with sound — like rain-showers from a thundercloud. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.21 //
With shoulder-platforms harsh and elevated at their peaks, blocking many a quarter with his extended reach,
his single arm, once stretched out, was perceived as if it were the king of the earth with [all] his armies. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.22 //
The arrows of the <s>Garuḍa</s>-bannered one (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), with unblunted tips, splitting the arrow-volley discharged by the enemy,
shattered [it and] brought the king's case [to naught] — like the true-worded [counselors] of a leader [defeating] the faction of wrongful [claimants]. // <s>MSpv</s> 20.23 //
Like betrayed beloveds, the arrows of the foe of <s>Mura</s>, with bright limb-lines facing [the enemy] directly —

children.text: laghimānamupeyuṣī pṛthivyāṃ viphalā śatruśarāvaliḥ papāta // MSpv_20.24 //
children.translated_text: having attained lightness upon the earth, the fruitless volley of the enemy's arrows fell. // MSpv 20.24 //
And the feathered [arrows] struck in front, [discharged] forcibly with the calf-like teeth [of the bow-string] released by <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),

children.text: paripūrṇataraṃ bhuvo gatāyāḥ parataḥ kātaravatpratīpamīyuḥ // MSpv_20.25 //
children.translated_text: having gone beyond the more completely [filled ranks of the] earth, turned back timidly, as if retreating. // MSpv 20.25 //
Fire born from the mutual collision, scattering sparks from the clashing of [arrow-]throats,
momentarily blazed, licking the layers of clouds against the others. // MSpv 20.26 //
When the cloud-net of the enemy's arrows was split by the Lord, brilliant with arrow-beauty, as in autumn [when clouds are dispersed],

children.text: vikasanmukhavārijāḥ prakāmaṃ babhurāśā iva yādavadhvajinyaḥ // MSpv_20.27 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Yādava</s> women, their lotus-faces blooming, shone like the directions themselves. // MSpv 20.27 //
He covered the sky with volleys of arrows, making circles of fierce radiance disappear;

children.text: dadṛśe 'tha ca tasya cāpayaṣṭyāmiṣurekaiva janai sakṛdvisṛṣṭā // MSpv_20.28 //
children.translated_text: and then from the staff of his bow, only a single arrow was seen by the people, discharged once. // MSpv 20.28 //

children.text: bhavati sphuṭamāgato vipakṣānna sapakṣo 'pi hi nirvṛtervidhātā /
children.translated_text: Clearly, [the arrow] came from the enemy's side — for even one's own ally is not a creator of joy;

children.text: śiśupālabalāni kṛṣṇamuktaḥ sutarāṃ tena tatāpa tomaraughaḥ // MSpv_20.29 //
children.translated_text: the volley of lances released by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> greatly tormented <s>Śiśupāla</s>'s forces. // MSpv 20.29 //
The arrows, golden-tawny in luster, with feathers roaring from their great velocity,

children.text: vinatāsutavattalaṃ bhuvaḥ sma vyathitabhrāntabhujaṅgamaṃ viśanti // MSpv_20.30 //
children.translated_text: entered the earth's surface like [<s>Garuḍa</s>], the son of <s>Vinatā</s>, where the serpents were agitated and fleeing in distress. // MSpv 20.30 //

children.text: śataśaḥ paruṣāḥ puro viśaṅkaṃ śiśupālena śilīmukhāḥ prayuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: Hundreds of sharp arrows, discharged fearlessly by <s>Śiśupāla</s> in front,

children.text: paramarmabhido 'pi dānavāreraparādhā iva na vyathāṃ vitenuḥ // MSpv_20.31 //
children.translated_text: even though they pierced vital points, caused no pain to the enemy of the <s>Dānavas</s> [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] — as if they were non-offenses. // MSpv 20.31 //
Wishing to create wonder by fashioning a marvelous world-creation through <s>māyā</s> (illusion) against the slayer of <s>Mura</s>,
the king discharged the <s>svāpana</s> (sleep-inducing) missile — [invoking <s>Yoganidrā</s>], the <s>yoga</s>-sleep of the time of the world's destruction. // MSpv 20.32 //
Dark as the body of the water-moist boar [<s>Varāha</s>], rendering the sun meaningless in name [i.e., darkening it],
the darkness made the [enemy] army [have] trembling, wide lotus-eyes [from fear]. // MSpv 20.33 //

children.text: guravo 'pi niṣadya yannidadrurdhanuṣi kṣmāpatayo na vācyametat /
children.translated_text: That even the mighty kings sat down and fell asleep upon their bows — this need not be said;

children.text: kṣayitāpadi jāgrato 'pi nityaṃ nanu tatraiva hi te 'bhavanniṣaṇṇāḥ // MSpv_20.34 //
children.translated_text: for those always awake even in diminished calamity — surely they were always seated there [on their bows]. // MSpv 20.34 //
As the enemies thus went slack, abandoning their own capacity to hold [weapons],
even the well-grasped weapon fell from their hands — like scripture from the hand of the heedless. // MSpv 20.35 //
Though accustomed to sleeping on the [cosmic] ocean, the Supreme Being, situated amidst his own army-ocean,

children.text: bhuvanatrayakāryajāgarūkaḥ sa paraṃ tatra paraḥ pumānajāgaḥ // MSpv_20.36 //
children.translated_text: being awake to the duty of the three worlds, that transcendent <s>Puruṣa</s> alone stayed awake there. // MSpv 20.36 //
Then, when his gaze — like the sun's rays — fell upon the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem [upon his chest, becoming] a mirror,

children.text: paṭuḥ dhāma tato na cādbhutaṃ tadvibhurindvarkavilocanaḥ kilāsau // MSpv_20.37 //
children.translated_text: the keen [radiance] went forth from it — and this is no wonder, for that Lord has the moon and sun as his eyes. // MSpv 20.37 //

children.text: mahataḥ praṇateṣviva prasādaḥ sa maṇeraṃśucayaḥ kakuṃmukheṣu /
children.translated_text: The ray-clusters of that [<s>Kaustubha</s>] jewel, like the grace of the great upon those who bow,
expanded from his blossoming eyes toward the faces of the directions, giving unclouded light to the armies. // MSpv 20.38 //

children.text: prakṛtiṃ pratipādukaiśca pādaiścakḷṣe bhānumataḥ punaḥ prasartum /
children.translated_text: The world of the living, setting aside its swoon from the dominion of darkness,
was drawn by the light-bearing one's feet [with their] soles, back to [its] natural state — to spread forth again, reviving suddenly. // MSpv 20.39 //
The enemies were greatly harassed in battle again by the <s>Yadu</s> warriors [who came forth] from the dense darkness;

children.text: nanu vāridharoparodhamuktaḥ sutarāmuttapate patiḥ prabhāṇām // MSpv_20.40 //
children.translated_text: indeed, released from the obstruction of rain-clouds, the lord of rays [the sun] blazes forth all the more! // MSpv 20.40 //
Then, when the light had conquered the darkness — like a lawsuit defeating a false charge —

children.text: ripurulbaṇabhīmabhogabhājāṃ bhujagānāṃ jananīṃ jajāpa vidyām // MSpv_20.41 //
children.translated_text: the enemy muttered the incantation for serpents, the offspring of those possessed of terrible, dreadful coils. // MSpv 20.41 //
Then, great serpent-kings, bearing broad hoods, incessantly spewing their poisonous hissing,
appeared with both corners of their mouths licked by their flickering forked tongues. // MSpv 20.42 //
The sons of <s>Kadrū</s>, born at the tip of immortality [<s>Amṛta</s>], desiring victory at that very moment through deception,

children.text: amṛtāgrabhuvaḥ pureva pucchaṃ baḍavābharturavāri kādraveyaiḥ // MSpv_20.43 //
children.translated_text: with mock-hair imitations [swaying hoods], [drank] the tailless waters of the submarine fire's lord [the ocean], as before. // MSpv 20.43 //
Broad [serpents], with unprecedentedly deep hissing, appeared at the face — those of the ear-and-eye [ones];
like dramatic spectacles composed by a poet versed in the canons of drama, marked with acts. // MSpv 20.44 //
The body of the fierce-rayed [sun], its rays dimmed by the intervening dense smoke of the poisonous breath of the serpents,
assumed the appearance of a copper disc — as if undergoing an eclipse. // MSpv 20.45 //
With peacock-feather-made banner-crests, their coils momentarily turning in apprehension,
the flickering-tongued [serpents] fell upon the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> host — like <s>Yama</s>'s noose, for the swift binding [of lives]. // MSpv 20.46 //
Amid the serpent-bodies, the banner-cloths, white as the canopy of foam

children.text: dadhati sma bhujaṅgamāṅgamadhye navanirmokaruciṃ dhvajāṃśukāni // MSpv_20.47 //
children.translated_text: gleaming within the circles of vast ocean-waves, bore the beauty of fresh sloughed skin. // MSpv 20.47 //
With the coiling serpent-coils, forming circular bonds, blazing, hanging down upon the chest,
the people shone — as if bearing garlands of crushed blue lotuses. // MSpv 20.48 //
And the men, their bodies entwined from the base by serpents — with hood-tops bearing gem-flowers —
bore the likeness of great trees enwrapped by extended creepers. // MSpv 20.49 //
The serpents, dark-lustred as the thick collyrium-mud paste, wearying the body here and there,
displayed upon the horses the play of clearly-[visible] saddle-bound leather straps. // MSpv 20.50 //
The long, graceful body of the great serpent, iron-dark, forcefully wrapping around at every step,
made the elephant motionless — like an elephant-fetter. // MSpv 20.51 //
Then, by <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), with a contemptuous glance accompanied by a smile, one eyebrow raised,
myriads of bird-kings [<s>Garuḍas</s>] flew forth from <s>Suparṇa</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) perched atop his own banner. // MSpv 20.52 //
The birds, golden-lustred, flying up from the bird-king with a loud cry of no small power,
were watched momentarily from high by the armies — like sparks from the blazing seven-rayed [sun]. // MSpv 20.53 //
The noble-born <s>Garuḍas</s>, earth-bearing [in power], found their simile in the fish of the sky-ocean around [Mount] <s>Sumeru</s>,
with their fluttering wings momentarily tossing aside the great cloud-masses. // MSpv 20.54 //
From the falling [<s>Garuḍas</s>] all around, with their blazing rays making the faces of the directions tawny,
the sun became even harder to look at — as if mirroring itself through those rays. // MSpv 20.55 //
The hood-bearing [serpents'] gems — split by the radiance of the blazing descending <s>Vainateyas</s> (<s>Garuḍas</s>) —
bore the luster of the bile of the weary serpent-king born from the churning of the great ocean-mountain. // MSpv 20.56 //
A wind born from the wings of the enemies of serpents [<s>Garuḍas</s>], with the deep sound of agitated oceans on all sides,
uprooting entire masses of trees, generated the fear of cosmic dissolution. // MSpv 20.57 //
By the paths cleared by the forcefully uprooted mountains from the wind of the rushing wings of the bird-king,
the terrified serpents, helpless, quickly entered their own dwelling [the netherworld]. // MSpv 20.58 //
When, by the sky-going [<s>Garuḍas</s>], destruction was brought upon the undying serpent-army — as good deeds bring destruction upon evil —
the enemy, burning with rage as if with an odd-eyed [<s>Rudra</s>'s] fire, then invoked the fire-missile. // MSpv 20.59 //
Bearing the beauty of a loud, raised burst of laughter, its sound terrifying all creatures,
fire then sprang up high — like a <s>vetāla</s> (vampire-demon), with sky-reaching weapon-arms. // MSpv 20.60 //
That [fire], with its rising, billowing smoke-banner stirred by impetuosity, red-horsed [<s>Rohitāśva</s>] and sky-ascending,
the crested one, with the swift wind as charioteer, beautiful as a golden chariot, advanced. // MSpv 20.61 //
The fire-born one [<s>Jātavedas</s>] burned the entire [universe] high — with the blazing sky's hollow interior,
its smoke bound by thick, moist cloud-leaves, its tall wood-pieces kindled — like a tree. // MSpv 20.62 //
The rain-clouds, white from the drying of their waters by the intense heat, tawny for a moment with clinging thin fire-glow,
then becoming ash from their own insubstantiality, [ultimately] regained their [cloud] form. // MSpv 20.63 //
The banner-flags, with their foliage-tips blazing with kindled fire, their glow golden as the shining wings of spiders [fireflies],
existing for but a moment in the time of destruction, attained as it were an even longer future. // MSpv 20.64 //
Then the slayer of <s>Mura</s> recalled the cloud-producing missile [<s>meghaṅkara</s>] — capable of counter-striking the fire-weapon —
as [the fire] was making the entire sky assume the beauty of molten gold for a long time. // MSpv 20.65 //
From the hair of the three-radiant [<s>Viṣṇu</s>], whose body was of the nature of water, with the four oceans in the depths of his vast belly,
with all rivers concealed at [his body's] junctures, cloud-formations arose. // MSpv 20.66 //
Covering the directions with resounding noise, screening the curtains of sunlight,
masses of clouds rose up — instantly bringing a dark hue. // MSpv 20.67 //
The sky became pale-golden as a streak of refined gold, with loud laughter of towering, flashing lightning,
accompanied by the thunderous tumult of rising, billowing rain-clouds. // MSpv 20.68 //
The clouds, blazing all around, shining high, with rays scornful of the sun's,
long-anointed with the hue of dark elephants' bodies, fashioned as it were a banner for the comet [<s>Dhūmaketu</s>]. // MSpv 20.69 //
The rain-bearing clouds, thundering like bulls, displaying as if the deluge of dissolution to quench the blazing, multicolored fire,
rained — raising the water of rivers above their banks. // MSpv 20.70 //

children.text: madhurairapi bhūyasā sa medhyaiḥ prathamaṃ pratyuta vāribhirdidīpe /
children.translated_text: At first, even by the abundant, pure, sweet waters, that friend of the wind [fire] was [only] kindled further;
then gradually, like affectionate anger [that subsides] through disputes, it was extinguished. // MSpv 20.71 //
Forcibly driven all around by volleys of arrows, his hopes taking refuge in the end,

children.text: prabaleṣu kṛtī cakāra vidyudvyapadeśena ghaneṣvanupraveśam // MSpv_20.72 //
children.translated_text: the skillful one [<s>Śiśupāla</s>] made his entry into the dense [clouds], on the pretext of [becoming] lightning. // MSpv 20.72 //
Somewhere, a carefully aimed [flame] of the quenched fire was seen — its root-flame released,
like a single feather from the wing of a bird-king, severed by the blow of a weapon hurled by <s>Balabhit</s> (<s>Indra</s>). // MSpv 20.73 //
The dense clouds, having quenched the crested one [fire], departed swiftly from the faces of the directions;

children.text: upakṛtyanisargataḥ pareṣāmuparodhaṃ na hi kurvate mahāntaḥ // MSpv_20.74 //
children.translated_text: for the great, having rendered help by nature, do not create obstruction for others. // MSpv 20.74 //
The sky, which had been burned by the flames of the fire and repeatedly sprinkled with fresh water,
attained the appearance of a wounded, heated-and-irrigated cloud — [a sky] bearing the beauty of the scorched and cooled. // MSpv 20.75 //

children.text: iti narapatirastraṃ yadyadāviścakāra prakupita iva rogaḥ kṣiprakārī vikāram /
children.translated_text: Thus, whatever missile the king deployed, the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, like a physician against a virulent disease's swift progression,

children.text: bhiṣagiva gurudoṣacchedinopakrameṇa kramavidatha murāriḥ pratyahaṃstattadāśu // MSpv_20.76 //
children.translated_text: versed in sequence, immediately countered each and every one with an incisive remedy. // MSpv 20.76 //
Finding him unconquered even by arrows that had attained purity [of aim] — straight, not striking vital points —

children.text: marmātigairanṛjubhirnitarāmaśuddhair vāksāyakairatha tutoda tadā vipakṣaḥ // MSpv_20.77 //
children.translated_text: the enemy then pierced [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] with crooked, exceedingly impure word-arrows [insults] that penetrated beyond vital points. // MSpv 20.77 //
<s>Rāhu</s> [had been] rendered [headless], his beauty of slack-embracing dalliance with his two wives made vain —

children.text: tenākrośata eva tasya murajittatkālalolānalajvālāpallavitena mūrdhavikalaṃ cakreṇa cakre vapuḥ // MSpv_20.78 //
children.translated_text: by that same [<s>Viṣṇu</s>], who, while [<s>Śiśupāla</s>] was still hurling abuse, made the slayer of <s>Mura</s>'s disc — adorned with flickering fire-flame-petals of that moment — render [<s>Śiśupāla</s>'s] body headless. // MSpv 20.78 //

children.text: śriyā juṣṭaṃ divyaiḥ sapaṭaharavairanvitaṃ puṣpavarṣair vapuṣṭacaidyasya kṣaṇamṛṣigaṇaiḥ stūyamānaṃ nirīya /
children.translated_text: The body of that <s>Caidya</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>), attended by <s>Śrī</s> (splendor), accompanied by divine drum-sounds and showers of flowers, praised momentarily by hosts of sages — having issued forth,

children.text: prakāśenākāśe dinakarakarānvikṣipadvismitākṣair narendrairaupendraṃ vapuratha viśaddhāma vīkṣāṃbabhūve // MSpv_20.79 //
children.translated_text: in the sky, with radiant brilliance, casting aside the sun's rays, while the kings watched with astonished eyes, it became merged with the body of the son of <s>Upendra</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) — [that body of] pure radiance. // MSpv 20.79 //
